in writing. − i consider that the reform of the dangerous preparations directive (1999/45/ec) is necessary to ensure greater clarity and precision of the rules in force as of 1 december 2010. the directive is of particular importance for regulating the classification, packaging and labelling of dangerous substances and mixtures, including the un global harmonized system as of 20 january 2009. all the adaptations and amendments proposed by the commission are justified by the need to update the directive in the light of the provisions recently introduced by the treaty of lisbon or adopted under the reach regulation.
in writing. − as the advisory working party has unanimously concluded that the present proposal does not contain any substantive amendments other than those identified as such in the proposal or in this opinion, i believe that the recommendations of the advisory working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission should be taken into account.
in writing. − the reform of directive 1999/45/ec is necessary for two reasons: - to update the proposal under the lisbon treaty, to replace the old provisions, which have become obsolete, with new ones; - the adoption of the reach regulation, which codifies directive 199/45/ec to ensure clarity and precision in the applicable rules. one of the most important changes seems to me to be that in the consolidated version there are numerous references to part a of annex v to directive 67/548/ec, concerning test methods. i consider that, in order to ensure uniform conditions for the implementation of this directive, implementing powers should be conferred on the commission.
in writing. − i voted to update the provisions on the classification, packaging, and labelling of dangerous preparations, in order to align the old directive to the lisbon treaty. this confirms the powers of the commission and parliament respectively regarding implementation of these important safety regulations
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the classification, packaging and labelling of dangerous preparations. the reform of the dangerous preparations directive (1999/45/ec) is proposed in order to codify the acts amending and aligning the provisions concerning the commission's power to adopt delegated and implementing acts to the treaty of lisbon. the dangerous preparations directive (dpd) regulates the classification, packaging and labelling of preparations, i.e. mixtures or solutions consisting of two or more substances (chemical elements and their compounds). it remains applicable until 1 june 2015 and is the new eu system for the classification and labelling of dangerous substances and mixtures, including the un global harmonized system. the reform of directive 1999/45/ec is justified either by the need to update the proposal in line with the lisbon treaty or by the adoption of the reach regulation and other changes introduced by it, which require a codification of directive 1999/45/ec to ensure the clarity and precision of the applicable rules. the reform proposal did not include political choices, substantial changes resulting from the treaties or new eu legislation on the subject.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the current system of fishing quotas has brought the short-term concerns of the states to the fore. the sustainability of the fisheries sector has thus been put on the back burner. some 60% of european fish stocks are exploited beyond the maximum sustainable yield. as in many other parts of europe, the mediterranean is overfished. the commission has therefore decided to extend the scope of the current regulation to cover the whole of the north sea. the commission must initiate long-term plans which take account of the needs of the member states on the one hand and the need to preserve fish stocks on the other. member states will also have to show greater responsibility in the future.
in writing. − i welcome and support the rapporteur's wish to improve the state of implementation of regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 and believe that member states must step up their efforts to implement this regulation. it hopes that, together with the reform of the common fisheries policy, a new regional framework will allow the rapid identification of appropriate regulatory solutions for the mediterranean sea, which will be accepted by all stakeholders, while effectively ensuring the sustainability of fisheries and the protection of resources and the environment.
in writing. − i hope that, together with the reform of the common fisheries policy, a new regional framework will allow for the rapid development of appropriate regulatory solutions for the mediterranean sea, which will be accepted by the member states and the interested parties, taking into account the specificities of this sea basin, while effectively ensuring the sustainability of fisheries and the protection of resources and the environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the present report, which identifies the delegated powers of the commission in council regulation (ec) no 1967/2006. this will enable the alignment of the regulation i just mentioned with the provisions introduced by the treaty on the functioning of the european union and in particular regarding resorting to delegated acts. empowering the commission to adopt, by way of delegated acts, amendments on non-essential elements of the regulation will improve our rapidity of reaction to new situations. however, i agree with the rapporteur that the annexes in fact constitute an essential part of regulation (ec) no 1967/2006. therefore i believe that in this case, delegated acts are not appropriate. annexes should be amended only by the european parliament and the council together, according to the ordinary legislative procedure.
in writing. − no debate on the management of mediterranean fisheries resources can ignore the fact that the problems of the black sea fisheries are currently being managed in a bizarre way by the general commission for the mediterranean. a whole series of problems are caused by this measure, which has no justification (legal, geographical, economic). the establishment of a black sea commission and the clarification of competences are necessary and urgent. the question of clarifying legislative cooperation between parliament and the council in the context of the treaty also remains.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on management measures for the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources in the mediterranean sea. conservation of fisheries resources is of paramount importance. in order to counterbalance the negative connotations of the term 'exploitation', it is appropriate to indicate that regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 also aims at the conservation of fishery resources in the mediterranean sea. i voted for the inclusion of this objective both in the title of regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 and in the text of the regulation. regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 is one of the first acts in the fisheries sector to be aligned to the new system of delegated and implementing acts. it is therefore of particular importance to find a very well-founded solution from a legal point of view, which protects the rights of parliament which were introduced by the treaty of lisbon. in this respect, i voted in favour of limiting the power of the commission to adopt delegated acts for a period of three years from the date of entry into force of this regulation, in order to allow for a regular evaluation of them. i also voted that the annexes should be amended only by co-legislators.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation because i too welcome the rapid ratification of the nagoya-kuala lumpur additional protocol on liability and compensation. i believe that it will contribute greatly to the achievement of the objectives of the convention on biological diversity and the cartagena protocol on biological diversity. i welcome the fact that the additional protocol will deal specifically with liability and compensation for damage to biodiversity caused by living modified organisms (lmos). in view of the potential damage that lmo can cause, it is important to focus mainly on the procedures and administrative requirements related to the measures to be taken in response to damage. in doing so, we must take into account adverse effects on the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity and risks to human health.
in writing. − the nagoya-kuala lumpur additional protocol on liability and reparation of damage emphasises the responsibility that all countries must have for the environment and i am convinced that it will make a major contribution to the achievement of the objectives of the convention on biological diversity and the cartagena protocol on biological diversity. the additional protocol complements existing legislation with international rules and procedures on liability and redress for damage to biodiversity caused by living modified organisms (lmos) that have adverse effects on the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity, taking also into account risks to human health. most member states have signed this additional protocol and will ratify it shortly. in the european union, the provisions of the cartagena protocol on biosecurity are governed by european biosecurity legislation, which remains an essential cornerstone of the precautionary principle.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the council decision on the signing, on behalf of the eu, of the nagoya-kuala lumpur additional protocol on liability and reparation to the cartagena protocol on biosafety. the cartagena protocol on biological diversity is an international treaty that regulates the movement of living modified organisms (lmo) resulting from modern biotechnology from one country to another. it establishes a prior informed consent procedure to provide countries with the information necessary to make informed decisions before approving the import of such organisms. the protocol refers to the precautionary approach. to this end, a biosafety clearing-house is hereby established to facilitate the exchange of information on lmos and to support countries in the implementation of this protocol. the nagoya-kuala lumpur additional protocol provides for international rules and procedures on liability and compensation for damage to biodiversity caused by lmos. in the eu, the provisions of the cartagena protocol are governed by european biosecurity legislation. the liability provisions of the nagoya-kuala lumpur additional protocol are governed by directive 2004/35/ec on environmental liability with regard to the prevention and remedying of environmental damage. it establishes a framework based on the 'polluter pays' principle, whereby the polluter pays if environmental damage has been caused.
mr president, i voted for this report, considering that an increase of two percentage points in the government debt-to-gdp ratio in the eurozone in only one year is a warning that we should concentrate on credible long-term strategies for budgetary consolidation. however, member states are not all in the same situation; they have particular economic and social conditions. therefore i call on the commission to facilitate the implementation of differentiated fiscal strategies, adapted to the particular microfinancial risk of each country. consistent and common efforts on structural reforms are needed for our goal for a solid economic and monetary union in the long term.
i voted in favour of this report because the problems in the public finance sector continue to have a negative impact on socioeconomic development and political stability, both in the euro area and in the rest of the union. given the high levels of public and private debt and public deficits in some member states, we need credible long-term strategies. i too support the report's proposals and would like to stress the need to constantly support public and private investment, which is crucial for job creation. moreover, it is essential that proportionality be taken into account in public finance decisions. when it is recommended to reduce wages and social spending, other options, such as taxes on real estate or on polluting activities, must be considered as well.
in writing. − the current european economic and political context continues to be marked by the major effects of the economic, financial and banking crisis. the economic and institutional stability of the member states remains a key priority of governance within the european union. the high level of unemployment in the member states, together with the high share of public debt in gdp, calls for measures to complement recent reforms in the euro area and the union as a whole. as the report's conclusions show, beyond the concrete institutional measures we must take into account, the credibility and legitimacy of the european construction are also at stake in the current dynamics. the european union can only overcome the crisis by increasing transparency and creating public mechanisms capable of assuming maximum responsibility in the economic field. at the same time, i support the report's position that the process of strategic consolidation of public finances in european countries should continue, given the scale of public debts and deficits.
in writing. − considering that the current economic, financial and banking crisis is not abating and that public finance problems are having a negative impact on economic development and political stability, and taking into account that member states are not all in the same situation, it is necessary to apply strategies for sustainable economic growth, differentiated according to the specific recommendations adopted by the council for each country. i believe that credible long-term fiscal consolidation strategies are still needed and that member states should pursue growth-oriented policies and reforms in line with the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on public finances in emu 2011 and 2012. i believe that the budget of the european union can play an important role in reducing macroeconomic and social imbalances across the union. the european parliament takes note of the commission's current forecast for negative gdp growth for the emu as a whole in 2013. the european parliament calls on the member states to implement growth-oriented policies and reforms in line with the europe 2020 strategy, taking into account social protection, social inclusion and public investment. the long-term sustainability of public and private finances is a key condition for economic growth and for maintaining public spending, including investment, at an appropriate level. high youth unemployment will also affect future economic development. we call on the member states to take concrete measures to reduce youth unemployment. parliament welcomes the new emphasis on budgetary decentralisation in the commission's report on public finances in emu in 2012 and suggests that a chapter on local and regional public finances should always be included in future editions.
mr president, through their notation, credit rating agencies have a substantial impact on the financial economy of any country and definitely on the daily life of citizens. the 2008 subprime crisis, together with the bankruptcy of enron, revealed the severe weaknesses existing within credit rating agencies in terms of transparency and conflict of interest. i welcome the measures put forward by the report to guarantee the independence of the credit rating agencies. i commend the limits introduced on cross-shareholdings and especially the fact that a member or shareholder of a credit rating agency must publicly declare any share he or she holds in another agency, that these shares cannot exceed 5 % and that credit rating agencies are not allowed to hold a stake of more than 10 % in any entity that they rate. these are promising steps for greater transparency within these institutions.
i voted in favour of this report because i believe that excessive reliance on credit ratings must be curbed. through the information they provide, credit rating agencies play an important role in financial markets. however, they do not provide characteristics of a security, such as liquidity risk or price volatility. therefore, the information provided by them should not be regarded as the sole criteria for assessing credit risk. i think if financial market participants would evaluate the opinions of credit rating agencies before making decisions, the failure rate in the markets would go down considerably. balanced confidence in credit ratings will contribute to a more effective protection of investors and european financial markets and reduce the risk of unfair practices.
in writing. − the activities of credit rating agencies have a very high impact on economic and financial actors and on public institutions. it is therefore essential that they operate within a regulatory framework that is as rigorous as possible and adapted to recent developments in financial markets. i believe that the commission's proposal has the potential to address the dependence of credit institutions and investment firms on the external ratings of credit rating agencies by encouraging the creation of internal risk assessment models and imposing due diligence obligations. welcomes the introduction of rules aimed at resolving conflicts of interest that could affect the quality of proposed ratings, thereby ensuring the independence of rating agencies. i voted in favor of this resolution.
in writing. − credit rating agencies have a major impact on the interest rates at which public authorities and different economic actors borrow, so better regulation in this area is absolutely necessary. i voted in favour of this report because it will ensure greater independence for the rating agencies by clarifying and sanctioning situations of conflict of interest.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on credit rating agencies because there is a need for stricter regulation of these companies. the measures we voted for are designed to combat oligopoly and conflict of interest and to limit the influence of these institutions on political decisions which should be the result of a democratic process. agencies will have to present a fixed timetable for the publication of country assessments and will no longer be able to issue policy recommendations. investors will also be able to sue credit rating agencies if they breach the rules laid down by this regulation.
in writing. − i consider it useful to establish an internal control structure within credit rating agencies, which would allow the prevention and control of possible conflicts of interest and ensure the independence of the ratings of these agencies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1060/2009 on credit rating agencies. the regulation on credit rating agencies has been amended as regards: the scope, the use of credit ratings, the independence of credit rating agencies, the publication of information on credit rating agency methodologies, credit ratings and rating outlooks, the comparability of credit ratings and the fees charged for credit ratings, and the civil liability of credit rating agencies towards investors. we voted to increase competition in a market dominated by three credit rating agencies and to take steps to encourage the use of smaller credit rating agencies. the commission should submit a report to the european parliament and the council analysing the appropriateness of setting up a european public credit rating agency to assess the solvency of the sovereign debt of member states and the ways in which this support can be provided and/or of setting up a european credit rating foundation to carry out all other types of ratings.
mr president, i voted in favour of the report to acknowledge the need to reduce the risk of managers of undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities and of alternative investment funds relying overly on credit ratings. while we cannot deny the importance of credit ratings for assessing financial markets and credit risks, we should not consider them as the only arbiters of credit risk. therefore i welcome the set of measures to reduce reliance on ratings and improve the agencies’ credibility. i commend in particular the fact that regulated financial institutions are encouraged to develop their own rating capacities while being required not to sell assets automatically in the event of a downgrade of their creditworthiness by an external credit rating agency.
i voted in favour of this report because in 2008 we all witnessed the influence of international rating agencies on the world economy. their contribution to the financial crisis clearly demonstrates the importance of regulation in this area. i think it is useful to launch a debate which will allow different points of view to be presented and which will define more precisely the role of the rating agencies. they should not enjoy a special status or automatically influence the activities of economic and financial operators. they should be a credible source of information and the way they are communicated should no longer be decided unilaterally by credit rating agencies alone.
in writing. − i believe that credit rating agencies carry out research, provide forward-looking opinions on credit risk and play an important role in financial markets. investors in undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) and alternative investment funds (aifs) should themselves assess the opinions issued by credit rating agencies and should carry out their own credit risk assessment. therefore, i believe that the internal risk management processes and systems used by ucits managers and aifs should be strengthened and the general principle of avoiding excessive reliance on external credit ratings adopted.
in writing. − i voted for the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive amending directive 2009/65/ec on the coordination of laws, regulations and administrative provisions relating to undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) and directive 2011/61/eu on alternative investment fund managers as regards excessive reliance on credit ratings. directive 2003/41/ec provides for the regulation of institutions for occupational retirement provision (iorps) at union level. directive 2009/65/ec provides for the regulation of undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) at union level. directive 2011/61/eu provides for the regulation at union level of alternative investment fund managers (aifs). one of the effects of the financial crisis is that investors, including iorps, ucits managers and aifs, rely excessively on credit ratings to invest in debt instruments without assessing themselves the creditworthiness of the issuers of such instruments. in order to improve the quality of investments made by iorps, ucits managers and aifs and thereby protect investors in those funds, it is provided that iorps, ucits managers and aifs should avoid relying exclusively and automatically on external credit ratings or using them as the sole parameter when assessing the risks involved in investments made.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that certain provisions of the regulation establishing a multiannual plan for cod stocks in the baltic sea and for the fisheries exploiting those stocks, as proposed earlier, should be amended. as this act was adopted before the entry into force of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), i consider this amendment to be essential for the plan to function effectively in the new decision-making framework established by the treaty of lisbon. the basic objective of the plan should be to ensure that the exploitation of cod stocks in the baltic sea can be carried out under economically, environmentally and socially sustainable conditions, and the commission should be given the appropriate powers.
in writing. − i consider that the proposed provision determines whether certain fishing restrictions apply in certain geographical areas, but does not establish uniform conditions. for that reason, i believe that the use of implementing acts in this case would not be in accordance with the treaty, but the conditions for the use of delegated acts are fulfilled.
in writing. − i voted in favour of amending regulation (ec) no 1098/2007 establishing a multiannual plan for cod stocks in the baltic sea and for the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the regulation aims to ensure that cod stocks in the baltic sea are exploited under sustainable economic, ecological and social conditions. to achieve this objective, rules are established for the establishment of annual fishing opportunities for this stock. these rules use certain technical parameters to determine the state of conservation of the stock. i voted that if the fishing mortality rate for one of the cod stocks concerned has been estimated to be at least 10% above the target fishing mortality rate, the total number of fishing days (with the gear referred to in paragraph 1) shall be reduced by 10% of the total number of days permitted in the current year. every five years, starting from 18 september 2007, the commission shall evaluate the functioning and results of the multiannual plan. for the purpose of carrying out this assessment, the commission shall seek recommendations from stecf and the baltic sea regional advisory council. if necessary, the commission shall make appropriate proposals for amending the multiannual plan.
in writing. − while a period of transitional measures is still needed in view of the ongoing reform of the common fisheries policy, we must not deviate from the ultimate objective of establishing a clear and balanced legal framework that ensures a suitable living environment for fishermen while protecting fish stocks. fisheries must be conducted in a responsible manner. in the black sea, fish species have already disappeared and will continue to disappear unless we manage biological resources in a sustainable way; a key step in this direction is the completion of the cfp reform.
in writing. − i support this project because i believe that a regionalised approach to fisheries management is indispensable. these technical conservation measures will allow the specific designation of fishing areas and gears to protect the marine environment and the ecosystems in which fish live. i also support the observance of these rules by all fishermen.
in writing. - i voted for the postponement of the vote on this report, to send a signal to the council that it refuses to accept the new powers of the european parliament in the fisheries sector after the adoption of the treaty of lisbon. last year, the council went so far as to adopt unilaterally the multiannual plan for the code. this attitude of the council cannot be tolerated by the european parliament. the european commission, as guardian of the treaties, has an obligation to take a firm stand on this matter.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that parliament's rules of procedure must ensure the most efficient functioning of the institution. therefore, i think it is only right that if the number of candidates for the office of vice-president is equal to the number of vacancies, then the choice of candidates should be by acclamation. i also think it would be beneficial to introduce a secret ballot to establish the precedence of each vice president. this gives the vice-presidents more legitimacy and responds to the concerns of the political groups about this procedure. last but not least, the order of precedence by vote will reflect the distribution of seats to each political group in parliament.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it will improve the way in which the vice-presidents of the european parliament are elected and clarify the order of precedence.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report amending the rules of procedure of parliament as regards the order of precedence of the vice-presidents elected by acclamation. article 13 (1) of the rules of procedure provides that the president, the vice-presidents and the quaestors shall be elected by secret ballot. however, if the number of applications does not exceed the number of seats to be filled, the candidates may be elected by acclamation. i voted for the amendment which states that if the election is by acclamation, the order of precedence is determined by secret ballot. i also voted against the amendment which removes the requirement that the election of the president, vice-presidents and quaestors must take account of an overall fair representation of member states and political tendencies. the reason why the amendment of the rules of procedure was requested is that the political groups eventually reach agreement on the persons appointed as vice-presidents, but never on the order of precedence. if the political groups cannot agree on the persons to be elected or if there are 'independent' candidates, a vote is taken and the order of precedence is determined according to the order in which the candidates were elected.
in view of the alarming situation of young europeans, urgent measures such as the youth guarantee are a priority for securing the future of the european union. economic change must be accompanied by efforts to create jobs, focused on the young workforce, and i believe that these guarantees will only have the desired effect if they are accompanied by a link between community employment strategies and the future needs of the european economy, by new programmes to provide young people with high-performing technological education and, not least, by support for the development of entrepreneurship among young people through increased access to european funds and business advice.
i support the establishment of the youth guarantee. they have intellectual capital and work capacity that needs to be expressed and harnessed to the fullest capacity, as much as possible, for themselves first and for society. of course, investing in the private system to create jobs is vital and this should be the priority of every european union government. in particular, i ask the commission to pay greater attention to young people from vulnerable groups and those from disadvantaged categories who experience social exclusion, such as those affected by poverty or disability, or those from minority or migrant groups. these young people must have financial, human and social support and full information on their employment opportunities.
i voted for this resolution. the introduction of the youth guarantee can help to reduce unemployment, but only if additional funding is secured. the national authorities must implement as soon as possible the measures to facilitate the introduction of this guarantee. first, an assessment and a personalised employment plan will be needed, followed by the application of the guarantee. public employment services will have to provide personalised assistance, given that there are various reasons behind the difficulties young people face in making the transition from school to their first job. but long-term measures will also be needed. states must adapt their education provision to the requirements of the labour market. therefore, romania is focusing on reopening vocational and apprenticeship schools, without neglecting higher education.
in writing. − youth unemployment is probably the phenomenon with the most damaging impact on european societies. although the statistical category of young people is not a homogeneous group but a body of citizens with undeniably different interests and problems, the fact that young europeans are facing increasing difficulties in finding a job raises numerous questions about the soundness of european economies and societies. moreover, this is becoming a chronic problem at member state level and calls into question the eu's major objective of promoting a sustainable, smart and inclusive growth model. i support the proposal to introduce a youth guarantee, which offers the prospect of continuing training or education for young europeans, alongside the acquisition of skills required by the labour market, as one of the most appropriate responses to current challenges. however, it must be borne in mind that the process can only bring about the desired changes in the medium term if there is close cooperation between the european and national authorities. it is equally important that this be supported by appropriate funding, within the limits of the budgetary constraints existing both for the member states and for the european authorities. i voted for the resolution.
in writing. − i mention that i support the commission's initiative to propose a council recommendation on youth guarantee schemes, as this is not a homogeneous group and should be given financial and social support. this support should benefit all categories of young people, who should first receive a personalised assessment of their needs, followed by the creation of services specifically tailored to those needs.
in writing. − the current financial and economic crisis in europe has led to an increase in youth unemployment to 22.8%, leaving 5.5 million young people unemployed. the introduction of a youth guarantee at member state level - giving every young eu citizen the chance to work or to be enrolled in an education or vocational training programme within four months of becoming unemployed or completing a form of education - will be of paramount importance in addressing this situation. the epsco council of february 2013 should present a recommendation aimed at implementing youth guarantee schemes in all member states, providing every young person with an opportunity to work, education or vocational training programmes. youth guarantee schemes should effectively improve the labour market situation of young people by providing adequate pay, working conditions and health and safety standards. youth guarantee schemes should also be eligible for the different specific forms of european funding, in particular in the member states with the highest rates of youth unemployment.
in writing. − in the current social, financial and economic context, where the global youth unemployment rate has reached an unprecedented level, it is imperative to implement mechanisms to match labour market demands and offers with those in the education system. the european union and the member states must step up their efforts to increase employment, which is why i support the european parliament's resolution on the establishment of a youth guarantee.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the establishment of youth guarantees in all eu member states, because i believe we have a duty to make every effort to encourage young people to take up employment. the current youth unemployment rate of 23.4% is worrying. i therefore welcome the idea of creating a tool through which young people under 25 or graduates under 30 will be guaranteed a good quality job offer, further education or a traineeship contract within four months of finishing their studies or becoming unemployed.
in writing. − the european union's concern to reduce youth unemployment will be reflected in the implementation of youth guarantee schemes in all member states, involving all social partners, local and regional authorities and local and regional education and training institutions. it is beneficial that at least 25% of the structural funds will be allocated to the youth guarantee, to which amounts must be added to the member states' funding to support the programme.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the establishment of a youth guarantee, as i believe that a european approach is needed to the growing problem of youth unemployment, which affects almost a quarter of young people. in line with the europe 2020 strategy, which sets ambitious targets for both employment and school drop-out rates, the youth guarantee could be a concrete measure to support all young people under 25 and recent graduates to either find a job in line with their skills or to continue their education or apprenticeship. this requires determination and political will, not only on the part of the european parliament but above all on the part of the member states, to adopt such a youth guarantee as soon as possible.
in writing. − i supported this resolution and its call to the council to make a positive recommendation on the youth guarantee next month. the economic crisis has affected young people disproportionately, and an offer of employment, education or an apprenticeship would bring considerable benefits to young people and make a positive impact in these difficult times.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the establishment of a youth guarantee, given that in november 2012 5.799 million young people under 25 were unemployed, an increase of 329 000 compared to november 2011. the youth guarantee will be a tool to ensure that all young people under 25 and recent graduates under 30 receive a good quality job offer or continue their education or apprenticeship within four months of becoming unemployed or leaving school. i am in favour of youth guarantee schemes being eligible for specific forms of european funding, particularly in the member states with the highest unemployment rates. i believe that close cooperation between the commission and the member states and, at national level, between the social partners (sectoral), local and regional authorities, public and private employment services and local and regional education and training institutions is essential for the effective implementation of youth guarantee schemes. youth guarantee schemes should also be accompanied by a quality framework to ensure that the education, training and jobs provided include adequate remuneration, working conditions and health and safety standards.
the european union must act as soon as possible to secure its energy future and protect its interests in this area, and the role of cohesion policy is crucial to this end. i believe that for the next programming period, additional attention should be paid to the regions on the external borders of the european union and, through well-funded projects from the cohesion and energy funds, an integrated and interconnected energy system should be developed with partner third countries. i believe that we must also encourage the regions and local representatives to include in the operational programmes the guidelines set by the european union on the development of energy systems and on energy efficiency, which is the most important aspect and would ensure sustainable development, but more than that, would ensure a significant reduction of costs in this area by about 25%.
investment in renewable energy is vital, now more than ever. i therefore ask the commission to ask the member states to simplify the rules and procedures for accessing structural funds in the field of energy policy and to support them in this respect, because complicated, interpretable, long and non-transparent procedures are the source of failure, including corruption and fraud in accessing these funds. the commission also needs to review its procedures and rules for accessing funds and must focus on regions. the use of renewable energy across regions will reduce inequalities between them, inequalities between the way people live and will increase the rate of uptake, to the benefit of european citizens.
i voted in favour of this report because the cohesion fund will play a very important role in achieving the europe 2020 energy efficiency objectives. my country has set itself a target of reducing primary energy consumption by 19% by 2020. but the target is very ambitious and at the same time very difficult to achieve. the main lines of action are to improve the efficiency of the energy production and distribution system and to inform the population. i believe that priority access should continue to be given to renewable energy and investment in this area. romania is increasingly encouraging this type of energy and is looking to continue promoting renewable energy sources, and the use of the cohesion funds as an additional source of funding for energy projects can contribute to this objective.
in writing. − the correlation between cohesion policy and a possible new european union energy initiative is a step forward for the member states and the citizens of the union. the achievement of an institutional link between two european union policies offers the possibility of taking on the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, especially with regard to greenhouse gas emissions, and increasing energy efficiency. the correlation of the two policies of the european union can lead to the achievement of its objectives of reducing the development gap between the different regions of the european union. the launch of regional or crossborder energy projects can help to support the process of sustainable, smart and inclusive growth, which the european union has set itself as the key objective of the next decade. last but not least, another important aspect of the coordination between the two european union initiatives should be highlighted. in addition to avoiding duplication of union efforts, this process can ensure, while promoting the development of energy infrastructure, job creation at a time when more and more european citizens are facing the problem of unemployment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is necessary and important that cohesion policy is linked to the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy in order to achieve sustainable and inclusive growth and to support the move towards a low-carbon and energy-efficient economy in all sectors. in this respect, i believe that coherent rules at european level and a mechanism allowing the authorities to access information from across the union are necessary to fully understand the evolution of the energy market. another important aspect seems to me to be the need to increase energy efficiency and the development of renewable energy in rural areas.
in writing. − the common objectives of european energy policy are security of supply, sustainability and competitiveness. european energy policy should ensure the security of energy resources, diversification of supply and affordable prices for final consumers. the main objectives of eu cohesion policy are the economic, social and territorial cohesion of europe's regions, achievable through investment in growth and jobs. energy policy should promote growth and job creation at local level in all regions, while ensuring sustainable energy sources and guaranteeing the security of energy supply throughout the union. investments in energy infrastructure and energy efficiency in the construction and transport sectors will directly lead to the creation of new jobs. exchanges of good practice across the eu should therefore be encouraged to monitor the impact of energy policies on energy poverty. the need for energy efficiency and renewable energy development in rural areas is also important and the growing potential for energy saving in rural households, which could require innovative financing schemes, should be highlighted as these communities do not have the necessary financial institutions to support such projects.
in writing. − the european union needs a new policy on security and diversification of energy supply. cohesion policy-supported energy investment is also driving local economic growth and creating new jobs. in order to have a competitive economy, i believe that the european union must invest in the development of renewable energy. cohesion funds could help many regions in europe to improve their energy consumption and build energy storage and transport infrastructure.
in writing. − i welcome the possibility of improving the flexibility of the use of the structural funds and the cohesion fund, in particular to encourage project submissions by those who need it most, but also to achieve the european union's objective of reducing carbon emissions and increasing energy efficiency in all sectors.
in writing. − as rapporteur for the itre commission opinion on the report on the role of eu cohesion policy and its actors in the implementation of the new european energy policy, i voted in favour of it, as i consider that the structural and cohesion funds have a very high potential to support important energy projects such as investments in energy efficiency, including housing. it is important that the available funds are made available to beneficiaries in the form of easily accessible financial instruments and, to this end, it is essential that excessive red tape at both national and european level is eliminated. at the same time, it is important that cohesion policy financial instruments are used in coordination with other funds specifically intended for energy projects, such as the connecting europe facility, in such a way as to create benefits of scale.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the role of eu cohesion policy and its actors in implementing the new european energy policy, because for the coming programming period, member states need strong eu support to promote smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, while taking into account national, local and regional specificities. in the current programming period, unfortunately, excessive bureaucracy and a lack of procedural clarity have made it difficult to access the structural funds and the cohesion fund, thus discouraging potential beneficiaries from making progress in this direction. with today's vote, we have removed the restrictions on funding for renewable energy sources and local and regional authorities will continue to benefit from funding for renewable energy projects. by using community funds wisely for the next programming period, it will be possible to achieve the 20% target for energy efficiency and, by implication, the sustainability and competitiveness objectives in the european union. last but not least, cohesion policy funds should also be available for the information and training of local and regional authorities, smes and potential beneficiaries on national renewable energy schemes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the role of cohesion policy in implementing the new european energy policy. we voted for a new regional development plan, which will lead to the minimization of differences between regions and to a more effective protection of vulnerable consumers. these consumers should benefit the most from energy efficiency improvements, but efficient use of structural funds and funds from the eib and other public financial institutions, as well as good coordination between union and national funds, is needed. we also voted to establish energy efficiency funds at national, regional or local level. these funds could play a fundamental role in job creation, the development of smes and companies providing energy efficiency services. the specific needs of the different regions must be taken into account. investments are needed either in the renovation of buildings or in the power transmission networks. all types of projects should take into account the connecting regions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution and support in particular the paragraph on making investments in energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy, particularly in the housing sector. by contributing from various european funds to the thermal rehabilitation of collective housing, together with funding from the member states, significant amounts of energy could be saved, especially in eastern european states such as romania. the ratio of investments made to savings made is an important argument in favour of such allocations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the role of eu cohesion policy and its actors in implementing the new european energy policy. i believe that european energy projects could contribute to regional development and enhance cross-border cooperation by helping regions to improve their capacity to manage energy resources. investments in renewable and low-carbon energy sources and energy efficiency can also support regional growth and job creation. i support the need to promote and use the jessica and elena financial instruments for investments in sustainable energy at local level to support cities and regions in launching viable investment projects in the field of energy efficiency, the use of renewable energy sources and sustainable urban transport. i voted for the revision of vat directive 2006/112/ec to allow for a reduction in the vat rate applied to regional, local and cross-border projects aimed at improving energy efficiency and purchasing products in the highest energy efficiency class, under directive 2010/30/eu. i believe that the modernisation of district heating networks, cogeneration plants and distribution networks and the creation of new high-efficiency plants should be encouraged and supported by cohesion policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the introduction of the debt securities. the pooling of public debts at the level of euro area countries will bring more stability to financial markets, demonstrate commitment to the single currency and a common desire to overcome the current crisis through solidarity measures, and strengthen the status of the euro at global level. eurobonds can also be a step towards federalisation.
in writing. − in the current economic and financial crisis, stabilising sovereign debt markets is necessary for all banks in the eu. i support the rapporteur's view that eurobonds are not a 'magic bullet' but their launch will have a positive impact on the market in the long term and on risk management.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that there is a further need to deepen and strengthen economic and monetary governance in the european union, which can be achieved, inter alia, by issuing euro bonds that help to restore long-term confidence and improve de facto economic solidarity within the union. the roadmap proposed in this report is very ambitious, proposing the issuance of medium-term european bonds that can finance major european projects such as energy or research.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the feasibility of introducing stability bonds. the issuance of sovereign bonds in the euro area is currently carried out by the member states in a decentralised manner using various issuance procedures. the introduction of jointly issued stability bonds would require the joint issuance of sovereign bonds by member states and the sharing of associated revenue streams and debt servicing costs. i believe that action is urgently needed to support a long-term strategy for the euro area, ensuring sound public finances, sustainable growth, social cohesion and high levels of employment. any move towards a joint bond issue should take full account of the single market perspective, ensuring that no obstacles or unnecessary imbalances are created between participating and non-participating member states. i believe that in order to maintain the integrity of economic and monetary union, alternative ways of maintaining access to markets or reducing the cost of borrowing for member states must be sought. these alternative solutions should not rely exclusively on rescue mechanisms such as the european stability mechanism (esm) and the european financial stability facility (efsf).
in writing. – the situation in syria is a slap in the face of the international community. there have been situations before this which were less tragic but which mobilised the international community in curtailing human tragedy, even without the un’s blessing. sadly, not this time. the official explanation for inaction is the russian and chinese veto in the security council, preventing any legitimate action in that country. the truth is that, after afghanistan and iraq, there is not much stomach for another intervention with a doubtful ending. moreover, one does not know whether the end result will not prove worse than the initial situation. in the meantime, the syrians will continue to suffer and die. and, when everything is over, they will be entitled to look into our eyes and ask: where were you when we needed you most?
from the views of my colleagues so far, it would seem that we should not discuss this partnership and cooperation agreement. but my view is that these agreements give the european union the opportunity to be a relevant political actor, to enter the political arena and not just to show off its right to sit in the gallery and criticize, because you are just as guilty when you criticize without offering solutions. this partnership and cooperation agreement gives the european union the chance to get involved in finding solutions to the situation in iraq. the european union must take some responsibility for this. let us not forget the events of ten years ago and how readily we supported the united states in this war. but i think this partnership and cooperation agreement is very important from a security point of view. what do we want? do we want an iraq that we all know is torn by ethnic conflict, an iraq that can de-state and end up in a syrian-style civil war? do we have the capacity, as the european union, to find solutions for peace in the region? we have that capability, to the extent that we're politically involved. and this treaty and this agreement give the european union the opportunity to get involved. the partnership is mutually beneficial: to us because, we must admit, it has an important economic component; iraq benefits because, in my view, we can export our democratic know-how and we can support democratic institutions in strengthening them. on one condition: that there are not many who are interested in taking the resources of those who have a problem of survival at the moment, actually stealing those resources. the iraqi government must be careful to manage iraqi resources, and for that to happen, the european union must give the people a chance, not the government.
mr president, i will start with the conclusion. the agreement will be approved. this is my opinion. the real question is: to what extent does the agreement represent an effective instrument permitting the eu to support the reintegration of a democratic iraq into the international community and its institutions, including the wto? iraq, however, is still facing formidable challenges both internally and externally. internally – with my romanian experience in mind – the main challenge to the iraqi authorities is to provide their citizens with basic services, such as decent living conditions, health and education and above all security. the iraqi citizens should be convinced that their life is now better than how it was under saddam, otherwise all sacrifices would seem to have been in vain and the momentum for change will fade away. the iraqi authorities still have a long way to go in order to reconcile the old traditions with their new democracy and respect for law and human rights – above all the right of minorities to live – and with having a federalist state organisation. the external challenges are also impressive. in that respect, there is no secret that with regard to syria iraq does not share the eu’s perceptions and positions, where it is quietly supporting the assad regime, sometimes in apparent conjunction with iran. however, such differences do not annul the value of the present agreement which will hopefully provide the framework for their discussion.
mr president, eur 120 billion is the estimated amount of money lost to corruption in europe per year. in 2011 over one thousand irregularities, accounting for a total of eur 400 million, were reported as illegal activities. corruption distorts competition and the market. it decreases the level of investments, reduces public financing and undermines citizens’ trust in institutions. the 2012 eu barometer on corruption shows that 74% of europeans believe that corruption is a major problem in their country and also shows that 57% believe that national politicians awarding public tenders are involved in corruption; 47% believe that national officials awarding public tenders are involved in corruption. fraud, tax evasion, money laundering and corruption all contributed to the economic crisis and have slowed down the recovery. we must act now. first we need a full and tough implementation of national anti-corruption legislation. in many eu countries anti-corruption laws are not implemented. political will is often lacking. where national politicians or officials are involved in corruption and fraud, one should not be naive and expect them to impose strict anti-corruption measures and sanctions. this is why eu direct anti-corruption legislation is a must. the reporting mechanism we have in the union should be a step forward to anti-corruption legislation at union level. another vital element is the freezing and confiscation of the means and proceeds of crime. these should be frozen and confiscated in both criminal and civil proceedings. if we do not do this, all our talk, laws or actions against corruption and organised crime are useless and, at the very least, naive. our laws and practice must be based on the principles ‘follow the money’ and ‘follow the money across borders’. the fight against corruption and organised crime must involve strong support – including financial support – for investigative journalism. independent investigative reporting is vital in exposing organised crime and corruption within a country or across the world. look at the websites of the investigative dashboard or the rise project and see what valuable work has been done by independent reporters in exposing cross-border organised crime. once again, corruption costs money and is more expensive than the instruments to fight it. therefore i say once again, do not bet on corruption.

in writing. corruption continues to be a widespread phenomenon throughout the european union. most polls show that european citizens regard corruption as a real problem, regardless of their country of origin. the fight against corruption must be a strategic priority, both at union level and in the member states. among the main problems identified by citizens are public procurement procedures. this requires greater transparency and closer scrutiny of contracts awarded. the rules on procurement need to be better applied, especially where the beneficiaries are public authorities. i therefore believe that, although most member states have adopted the necessary legislation to combat corruption effectively, implementation still lacks. therefore, if the application of anti-corruption legislation at national level does not produce results, then concrete steps should be taken towards the adoption of such legislation at community level. this will ensure more efficient and transparent spending of public money and increase citizens' confidence in national decision-making.
i would like to express my disappointment for the cancellation of the conference, but unfortunately the situation in the region does not allow for the best conditions for such an event. the creation of a nuclear-weapon-free zone in the middle east can be a solution for stability in the region. however, such an initiative should be regional and not external. the states in the area must first consider whether such a measure would ensure their security. and for such an initiative to work, i believe that peace must be established before any decision is made. at the same time, trust between the countries of the region must be increased in order to revive dialogue. and now, major efforts are needed to restore trust between the states in the region.
i believe that the conclusion of an interim agreement between the union and the states of eastern and southern africa is the solution to minimize any possible disruption to trade with these partners. the countries concerned will thus gradually open their markets to european exports over the next 15 years, to the benefit of both parties. and the inclusion of rules of origin, development cooperation and trade protection instruments in the agreement will bring mutual benefits. on the other hand, the agreement's correlation with the cotonou agreement in terms of good governance, democracy and human rights will be important. and here i am referring specifically to the situation in zimbabwe, which, according to a recent report by human rights watch, has failed to make the necessary reforms to ensure free and fair elections this year.
the adoption of the community customs code has consolidated and simplified the union's customs legislation. the customs code is currently being modernised to facilitate trade while ensuring a high level of border security. one of the efforts made in this direction by the world trade organization is to harmonize the non-preferential origin of goods. the commission has developed various mandatory rules of origin. although the commission believes that the new rules will lead to increased legal certainty regarding imports, it remains unclear how the future provisions will be monitored and implemented. an impact assessment on all parties involved is indispensable. the ultimate objective of the modernisation of the community customs code should be to facilitate import and export procedures. special attention should be paid to smes so that their work is not affected.
european citizens who travel frequently within the eu may find that some airlines apply unfair restrictions to the baggage that passengers can take on board. i am talking about the size and weight of the permitted items, as well as the items that passengers are allowed to carry. i understand and respect the constraints of on-board security and the pressure of storage space, but i believe that measures should be taken at european level to avoid abuses by airlines and excessive charges on baggage. checking frames for baggage that do not match the dimensions displayed and the imposition of a maximum weight of 7 kg are situations that create a lot of inconvenience. i ask the european commission to look into these problems in detail and to take measures to ensure that the hand luggage regime is fairly regulated and that passengers' rights are respected.
over the last ten years, passenger traffic on international routes served by regional airports has increased by 84%. the european airport network is composed of 90% regional airports, the role and relevance of which have expanded significantly over the last ten years. we call on the commission to take firm action to limit the aggressive and abusive practices of some air carriers on the single baggage rule. we ask the commission to propose a timetable of measures to harmonize commercial practice in respect of hand luggage. these measures are necessary to protect passengers against excessive restrictive practices and to allow them to bring hand luggage on board in a reasonable manner. the single baggage rule and other restrictions on hand baggage imposed by certain companies are a violation of competition. we call on the commission to investigate the practice of baggage registration fees, which often appear disproportionately high and which violate the fair and transparent pricing practices and policy of the european union.

mercosur is the eighth largest trading partner of the european union. exports to the region have increased significantly in recent years, with the union ranking first in 2010 both among the region's trading partners and among foreign investors. the conclusion of a balanced and fair trade agreement with the area, synonymous with better economic integration and conducive to the conclusion of the association agreement, represents an opportunity for both regions. in this context, the relaunch in may 2010 of negotiations for the establishment of a free trade area was welcomed. however, these have made limited progress, reflecting the protectionist measures that some countries in the region have decided to apply. i hope that the meeting next week in santiago de chile, which you are attending, commissioner, will be marked by dialogue and will allow a rapid compromise to be found on the trade pillar of the agreement.

in writing. − the political and trade provisions of the partnership and cooperation agreement will provide the basis for a more intensive political dialogue on a range of issues of bilateral, regional and global importance. i also believe that trade relations between iraq and the eu will improve, by supporting iraq's development and reform efforts to facilitate its integration into the world economy. an important point in the dialogue between the eu and the iraqi authorities is the respect for human rights and fundamental civil and individual freedoms, with a particular focus on cases of human rights violations. in my view, it is important that the eu delegation in baghdad is fully operational to enable the eu to play a meaningful role in the transition in iraq.

mr president, i would like to refer to the eu’s financial contribution to iraq. the eu is a major financial donor and has systematically contributed to the country’s progress. eujust lex- iraq has been present on the ground since 2005, and its mandate has been extended until the end of the year. however, the situation in the middle east continues to be volatile. there are 34 000 syrian refugees reported in kurdistan. iraq is struggling with internal problems of its own: youth unemployment at 30%, rising ethnic and religious tensions, fights between political parties. money, if well channelled, can make a difference in these difficult times. the pca with iraq is the first building block of good partnership. the next step, however, should involve not only financial assistance but more expertise and knowledge-sharing, particularly in areas such as human rights, transparency, anti-corruption and the rule of law.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this legislative resolution because i believe that the european union can contribute, through cooperation with the republic of iraq, to combating poverty and to facilitating and improving services that meet the basic needs of iraqi citizens, such as health and education. the eu can also facilitate iraq's democratic transition by creating a cooperation council characterised by regular meetings at ministerial level. last but not least, as rapporteur for monitoring eu-iraq relations, i support this move to deepen the trade agreement with iraq, placing it in the sphere of 'partnership and cooperation' agreements.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion of an eu-iraq partnership and cooperation agreement. the aim of this agreement, concluded for a period of 10 years, renewable, is to create a solid basis for strengthening the ties between iraq and the eu. the political part of the agreement involves the introduction of an annual ministerial and senior official dialogue on peace, foreign and security policy, dialogue and national reconciliation, democracy, the rule of law, human rights, good governance and regional stability and integration. we recommend that the respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, including with regard to religious and ethnic minorities and vulnerable parts of iraqi society such as women, refugees and displaced persons, be emphasised in bilateral discussions with the iraqi authorities. as regards trade and investment, the non-preferential agreement incorporated the fundamental rules of the wto, although iraq is not a member of the wto. the agreement contains preferential elements, notably in public procurement, services and investment. the partnership and cooperation agreement demonstrates the eu's determination to play a major role in iraq's transition process.
mr president, i voted in favour of this resolution. 2013 is a key election year for zimbabwe which will test the strength of its democracy and constitutional order. the latest human rights watch report, published on 10 january, expressed concerns about the current political situation. there are disagreements between president mugabe and the prime minister over the election date, and therefore many fear a repetition of the past violence. the political agreement signed in 2008 between zimbabwe’s two main parties did not foster much-needed legislative and electoral reforms. therefore the signing of an epi with the eu comes at a crucial moment for zimbabwe. i believe that this agreement could be a step towards more political engagement for the eu. the union must support more effectively reforms, fair elections and the pluralistic political system. it is true that trade can fight poverty, but not in the absence of functioning democratic institutions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the implementation of the interim economic partnership agreement (epa) between the european union and the states of eastern and southern africa in the context of the current situation in zimbabwe. the eu must promote fair trade with developing countries, based on full respect for ilo standards and labour conditions, and ensure that social and environmental standards are applied at the highest possible level. we regret the lack of a robust human rights clause in the epa and reiterate the call for binding, non-negotiable human rights clauses in eu trade agreements. we also regret the omission of a chapter on sustainable development and a requirement to comply with international labour and environmental standards. the provisional entry into force of the epa is an important step towards strengthening the partnership between the eu and the four african countries concerned (seychelles, madagascar, mauritius and zimbabwe) in a stable legal framework. we stress the importance of continuing negotiations to reach a full agreement aimed at fostering increasingly open and fair trade, investment and regional integration.
mr president, i welcome an agreement which promotes economic cooperation between countries in eastern and southern africa on the one hand and the european union on the other. we must ensure that countries signing economic partnership agreements with the eu are offered a fair deal. we also must ensure that in these countries, in addition to the trade we can help to foster, there is a stable and well-functioning democracy. we must ensure that money does not go into private pockets; we must ensure that money really produces progress and is not subject to corruption or fraud. i support the idea that economic partnerships with african countries are a good policy for the union. we should recall, however, the conditionality criteria used for our neighbourhood partners. some of these – deeper democracy, fair elections, impartial justice, anti-corruption measures and anti-fraud measures – could and should be included in future epas.
in writing. − the economic partnership agreement between the eastern and southern african states and the european community and its member states (esa) is a necessary step towards sustainable growth in the region and highlights the importance of continuing negotiations towards a comprehensive agreement that will encourage trade, investment and regional integration in the region. the agreement contains provisions on rules of origin, development cooperation, fisheries, trade defence instruments and dispute settlement. in 2010, total eu imports from the whole of the eastern and southern africa (esa) group reached eur 2.88 billion, or 0.2% of total eu imports, comprising mainly processed tuna, coffee, sugar cane sugar, tobacco, cut flowers and pig iron. eu exports to the aes, consisting primarily of machinery, vehicles, pharmaceuticals and chemicals, reached approximately eur 3.99 billion in the same year. the eu contributes to regional integration through measures such as the exclusion of acp trade from the most favoured nation clause and by allowing the efta states to maintain regional preferences. as an awepa member, i believe that development cooperation also needs to aim at preparing businesses for international competition and supporting exporters to meet eu import standards.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of the interim agreement establishing a framework for an economic partnership agreement between the eastern and southern african states and the european union and its member states. in 2010, total eu imports from the whole of the eastern and southern africa (esa) group reached eur 2.88 billion, or 0.2% of total eu imports, comprising mainly processed tuna, coffee, sugar cane sugar, tobacco, cut flowers and ferroalloys. imports from the eea countries initiating interim agreements accounted for around 70% of eu imports from the eea region. eu exports to the aes, consisting primarily of machinery, vehicles, pharmaceuticals and chemicals, reached approximately eur 3.99 billion in the same year. the interim agreement provides for duty-free and quota-free access to the eu market for exports from mauritius, madagascar, the seychelles and zimbabwe. these countries will gradually open their markets to european exports over the next 15 years, with exceptions (maximum 20% of eu imports) for certain products considered sensitive by these countries. these excluded products vary from country to country, but mainly include agricultural products. the agreement contains provisions on rules of origin, development cooperation, fisheries, trade defence instruments and dispute settlement.
mr president, i voted in favour of the present motion for a resolution to acknowledge a possible distortion effect of state aids on competition in the internal market. for instance 40% of the cases of state aid granted under the block exemption regulations are reported as possibly problematic. the state aid regulations had to be modernised and this is what happened with this package. however, i regret that parliament is only given a consultative role in this crucial reform. state-aid-related reforms should be brought in line with other areas of market integration and economic regulation where codecision is the rule. therefore i call for the establishment of interinstitutional arrangements to overcome this deficit.
i voted in favour of the resolution because the modernisation of state aid is necessary to stimulate economic growth and improve the fiscal position of the member states. in my view, the reform proposed by the european commission is aimed at achieving the common objective of inclusive and sustainable economic growth, and state aid control is essential to ensure the proper functioning of the single market. i also believe that resources should be directed in a balanced way to both high-impact and low-impact cases. the lack of involvement of the european parliament in the decision-making process is, in my view, a gap in the reform. there are good reasons for parliament to exercise its right of democratic oversight over state aid monitoring acts. i therefore believe that parliament's opinion on this matter should be taken into account.
in writing. − the european commission has embarked on a complex process of modernising state aid rules to take account of recent developments in the eu's internal market. i support the european executive's efforts in this regard and stress that the new legislative framework should aim to provide more targeted state aid with less public expenditure. i encourage the timely implementation of measures on the modernisation of state aid, as the proper use and monitoring of such aid will play an important role in achieving the objectives of the eu 2020 growth strategy. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the modernisation of state aid. we welcome the commission communication on the modernisation of state aid and the new commission proposals for regulations. the commission must ensure that stimulating growth, as one of the overall objectives of this reform, will not lead to a further increase in public debt. i voted for the amendment which stresses the need for better targeted state aid, which implies less public spending and does not distort competition, while supporting the transition to a knowledge-based economy. i also voted to delete from the same paragraph the reference calling for less state aid. we stress that state aid must be designed to promote the development of services, knowledge and infrastructure itself and not to support specific companies. i voted against the last part of paragraph 10, which calls on the commission to guarantee a long-term reduction in the level of state aid. we request further clarification on the 40% of state aid cases granted under the block exemption regulations, which could be problematic. this is a problem for new entrants and for small and medium-sized enterprises, with a distorting effect on competition.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the indication of the country of origin of certain products imported into the eu from third countries. the eu does not apply harmonised rules on the indication of the origin of imported products, except in certain cases in the agricultural sector. some wto but non-eu countries, such as brazil, canada, china and the usa, have introduced mandatory origin indication mechanisms for certain products. we therefore need common provisions to increase competitiveness among wto member countries and to ensure a level playing field with producers in the main eu partner countries that have implemented indication of origin. we regret the commission's intention to withdraw the proposal for a regulation on the indication of the origin of certain products imported from third countries, adopted by parliament at first reading, without informing parliament in good time and without giving its colleagues a detailed explanation of its intention before taking this decision. we invite the commission to inform parliament of the timetable for the future measures needed to relaunch the legislative process and overcome the current impasse. we also call on the commission to undertake a comparative study of the legal rules on indication of origin in force and implemented in each wto member country.
