we all know that small and mediumsized enterprises are the main components of the economic system of the european union, and the development of employment depends to a large extent on the situation of these enterprises. however, because of the financial crisis, they are the ones most affected by the decline in lending and the general uncertainty in the economy. however, the financing problems are only part of the negative trends affecting smes, as many member states are making their situation more difficult by introducing additional measures. some governments, in order to reduce deficits and increase budget revenues, impose additional taxes on this sector. the new romanian government, which has just taken office, is doing the same, with the approval of the international monetary fund. the new tax measures of the government of victor ponta smes will be obliged to pay tax on their income rather than on their profits industry experts believe that they could lead to the bankruptcy of thousands of small businesses. this could not only lead to higher unemployment and lower consumption, but also delay the start of economic expansion.

mr president, owing to their size and geographical situation, smaller aegean islands face obstacles to supply and trade. they also suffer from inadequate, ageing and expensive transport networks. article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union draws attention to the importance of strengthening the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the european union. this provision is relevant in the case of the smaller aegean islands. local production on those islands should receive adequate funding. therefore i share the view that increased budget appropriations for the special supply arrangements should not be made at their expense. in addition, specific support should be devoted to the maintenance and promotion of traditional agricultural products.
i voted in favour of the report because the large number of islands in the aegean sea is a challenge to the territorial cohesion of the union. their position within the archipelago is an obstacle to supply and trade, leading to very high transport costs, especially for producers. measures should be introduced to improve the transport of processed agricultural products to the aegean islands. the financing of their supply of basic products is not sufficient as long as funds are not also provided for the subsequent transport of the resulting products. a clear strategy is also needed to address the existing structural problems of agriculture in the area. on the other hand, farms must not affect the natural and cultural resources of the islands, given that tourism is the main source of income in the region.
in writing. − these outermost regions are generally small territories with difficult climatic conditions. because of this, there are difficulties for the agricultural development of these areas. the objective of this regulation is to mitigate the additional costs associated with supply and agricultural activity. certain agricultural products, which are considered essential for human or animal consumption or for the manufacture of other agricultural products, are included in a specific supply scheme. under this scheme, limited quantities of the products concerned may be imported by the eu with aid covering part of the additional costs caused by the outermost region or by third countries without import duties being applied.
in writing. − due to their geographical location at the extreme periphery, the small aegean islands have great problems in terms of trade with the rest of europe. this is having a negative impact on local production, holding back the development potential of the islands. if we also consider that transport networks are outdated and impose extremely high supply costs on local producers, the islands seem to be doomed either to 'economic death' or to an even greater dependence on tourism revenues, which, in times of global economic recession, decline. i therefore consider the adoption of this report to be essential in ensuring the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the european union.

in writing. climate change is undeniably real and represents the greatest environmental threat facing humanity. the doha climate change conference did not lead to a new agreement on the fight against climate change. the negotiations have led to the extension of the kyoto agreement and an agreement on financial aid for the countries of the south, but these results are not a solution to slowing down global warming. the next conference of the parties to the united nations framework convention on climate change (cop 19) in warsaw in november-december 2013 is of particular importance as an intermediate preparatory stage for the next major international meeting to be held in 2015 in paris, the aim of which is to conclude an international agreement on greenhouse gas reductions involving all countries, including the biggest polluters: china and the united states. such an agreement is imperative to slow global warming. member states must reach a clear, firm and united position so that the european union can play a stronger and more influential role in international climate change negotiations.
in writing. despite strict international controls on the ivory trade, the african elephant population continues to be threatened by the flourishing illegal trade. recently, the amount of ivory seized has increased dramatically. there is evidence that enforcement has not improved considerably, especially in countries with a large ivory market, where elephant slaughter and illegal trade are common. we must not allow trade to take place under these conditions. i welcome the withdrawal of the proposal made to the cites conference this year for a one-off sale of ivory from tanzania. the impact of similar sales in the past to china and japan has not yet been assessed, although it is suspected to have been extremely harmful, with legal sales helping to mask illegal operations. although i referred in my message to the theme of elephants and ivory, the problem goes beyond one species or another. it's affecting biodiversity as a whole, and all the benefits that it provides us, from water purification and carbon sequestration to soil fertility. african countries must be supported in their fight to halt the decimation of endangered species and to promote the sustainable use of their increasingly limited natural resources.
we are in a difficult period in terms of public debt and investment prospects. however, there is a continuous effort to consolidate national budgets. i therefore support the report's proposals and believe that the european parliament and all the union institutions should show solidarity with the difficult economic and budgetary conditions in the member states. institutions must continue to demonstrate a high degree of accountability and control. they also support the continuation of structural reforms to ensure that the institutions function more effectively. at european level, the main objective is to have flexible but effective institutions. but in some member states, such as romania, the number of government institutions has increased since the left-wing coalition took power, which is not in the interest of the taxpayer.
i would also like to begin by congratulating my colleague, mr baldassarre, on his report. in recent years, corporate social responsibility has become a topic of increasing attention in the private sector, in public authorities and in society. i believe that if properly applied and practised, csr can make a major contribution to restoring lost trust in the union. i support the introduction of the new definition proposed by the commission. csr should be mainly driven by enterprises on the basis of their own capabilities, supported by public authorities. in romania, as in most emerging economies, csr is still in its infancy. however, many of the leading companies in this field understand the value of a robust csr strategy.
42% of consumers believe that a company should be partly or fully responsible for solving the social problems of the community in which it operates, and 49% of consumers take environmental aspects into account when buying a product. businesses need to take these aspects into account and behave responsibly towards people, the planet and profits, but also address social measures such as vocational training, reconciling family and professional life and appropriate working conditions. i believe that csr is and must remain an important element of strategic development, but also a priority in the growth process of companies, regardless of their size and type of activity. on the other hand, standards and models of social responsibility could be a solution to the problems faced by smes.
in writing. european businesses are currently facing tough challenges due to the crisis, accelerating globalisation and climate change. responding to these challenges requires focusing efforts on increasing corporate social responsibility in terms of their impact on society. through social responsibility, companies seek to build sustainable relationships with employees and customers to develop long-term business models. the social partnership created implies rights and obligations for both parties. companies focus on respecting the collective rights of employees and contribute to the inclusion of vulnerable groups by insisting on the training and specialisation of workers. social responsibility also has a bottom-up approach. employees and consumers defend the interests of companies, combat discrimination and undeclared work and are responsible for their working environment. i would like to highlight an example that is becoming increasingly common in eu companies, whereby workers give up hours of work to save their colleagues from being laid off. at present, smes are underrepresented in public works. the social responsibility of public authorities, however, is to support these enterprises, respecting the principles of transparency, non-discrimination and equal treatment.
motorised transport is one of the main sources of noise pollution. the number of cardiovascular diseases, cognitive disorders, sleep disturbances can increase as a result of prolonged exposure to high noise levels. i therefore consider this report to be an important step forward in tackling the effects of vehicle noise on human health and the environment. my country is interested in the proposed changes, as dacia has become a major european car manufacturer in recent years. i also believe that noise reduction should not be done only at the level of motor vehicles. the quality of the road surface also strongly influences the noise emissions generated by the rolling of vehicle tyres. consumers need clear and transparent information on vehicle noise emissions to make informed purchases.
it is clear that the member states have the right to determine their contribution to the union budget, but it is equally clear that the same member states have the obligation to respect the provisions of the lisbon treaty and the commitments they have made in relation to european policies. member states who think they will gain by reducing the national contribution are wrong. the european budget is 95% investment budget. its decline will reduce investment and, by implication, jobs across europe, and the effects will be felt in all member states. the negative consequences will outweigh the relatively positive consequences of the decrease in the national contribution. a budget smaller than the present one would be a step backwards, a failure of the union. there will be other effects besides the direct financial ones; it will be a win for the eurosceptics, for the populists, it will constitute a negative signal for the financial markets and it will cause uncertainties in the chancelleries of third countries. parliament has to vote on an opinion on the mff. the outcome of this vote is not certain at this time. moreover, over 60 legislative proposals are under way under the codecision procedure, where parliament has equal powers with the council. we need to get agreement in these negotiations, otherwise we will be in a situation where we are applying in 2014 policies that were established in 2006. the european council must think before it decides, because a disagreement on the budget leads us to apply, in 2014 and in the years to come, the budgetary ceiling of 2013, which is much better. mr. president, mr. farage was referring to the movement of labor, the romanians and the bulgarians. i would ask him to stop making such populist judgments and to turn more to the internal situation of great britain. it is not the free movement of labour and membership of the union that has created the situation in britain today. answer to the blue card. it is clear that a multiannual budget is much better than an annual budget, but it depends on the value of the budget, because if we have a multiannual budget smaller than the current financial framework, i do not think it is in the union's interest. the rule in the basic treaty says that if there is no agreement on the budget, the 2013 budget ceiling, which is higher than the one currently proposed by the council, will apply in 2014 and in subsequent years. so it might be an advantage for the union if, at the same time, horizontal policies are also approved.
member of the commission. − mr president, colleagues, thank you for this debate, which was predominantly a true and realistic picture of the european budget. but i could also hear things that were not true, wrong and misleading. my job is to tell the difference. therefore, those who say that the european budget is small are right. this is 1% of the national wealth, less than 2% of public expenditure in the european union. but those who say – and i hear it constantly – that we are cutting our national budgets at home while the european budget is growing are wrong. more than 20 national budgets are growing, and we are now expected to finance a larger europe with the accession of croatia – and more duties – with less money. that is true. those who say that the european budget is about investment are right. you cannot find investment money for growth and jobs in the national and regional budgets; these are normally the first victim of savings. but the stability of the mff in the european union has nothing to do with the soviet planning i remember. this was about planning how many shoes or toys you were to produce annually; the european mff is about stability of investment over many years for multiannual projects, which is of great value in this time of crisis. those who say that one euro spent at european level could bring more added value than separate national expenditures are right. you can find the proof in international consortia in research for global competitiveness, in the trans-european networks in energy and transportation, and in humanitarian aid worldwide. those who say that we need to avoid an excessive gap between commitments and payments are right. some difference is normal, but in order to avoid excessive difference we need to go into the new mff without an excessive overhang legacy from this one. therefore, we need the european parliament to find missing money for the 2013 budget. as for what i see is a real witch-hunt in respect of the less than 6% of the european budget which is set aside for administration, i will leave that story to commissioner šefčovič.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, allow me to have the last word before the european council on heading 5 of the mff, on administration. despite the fact that it represents less than 6% of the budget, it is the subject of a huge discussion – i would even say a media campaign – in europe. therefore, i believe that it is absolutely necessary to underline the need for a top professional, independent and geographically balanced eu administration. the eu has to deliver on more and more demanding tasks, and in all 23 languages. this alone represents 15% of administrative costs. we have to deliver on a new task given to us under the eu semester. we will have to issue opinions on the national budgets. in the trade talks we discussed this morning we will have to face the best and finest negotiators from all over the world. this is without mentioning the european court of justice, where our lawyers have to face the best global law firms in the world, and in the overwhelming majority of cases – 90% – they win. fines imposed by the european court of justice have brought more than eur 30 billion into the eu budget over the last few years. member states, law firms and companies send their best people to brussels, strasbourg or luxembourg to cover eu matters. they also need to be of high quality. if you ask them how much they are paid you will not usually get an answer. the president of the european parliament tried to get one. he received no answer, and i do not think he will ever get one. but i can assure you that they are paid at a much different level than they are paid back home in their capitals. but i think this is right, because they are being paid for their quality, language skills and hard work. therefore, i would repeat here the plea i made to european ministers on monday: let us not get carried away; let us not break the eu machine. we have already offered to make almost eur 10 billion in cumulative savings since 2004. our civil servants working for the eu institutions will work longer hours and will retire later than most civil servants in the member states, and we are already proposing to cut 2500 jobs. this is the equivalent of the entire administrative staff of the european court of justice, so these are very significant savings. we know that more is expected, but i would also like to underline that if we overdo this we will create a situation where projects for regional development will be delayed or not be processed with the required quality. this would create a situation where translation will be scarce, thus leading to an even longer backlog of unsolved cases at the european court of justice, creating very serious legal uncertainty. so i would just like to say that, through marginal savings, we can do structural damage where it will be the citizens who will feel it first.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because it is about the eu's responsibility towards its trading partners. the accession of my country and bulgaria in 2007 led to the customs enlargement of the eu. as a member of the wto, the eu is bound by its rules. in this situation, an adjustment is needed to compensate for the increase in the consolidated customs duties and the related significant losses. the adjustment benefits all wto member countries, regardless of whether the newly acceding countries have lower or higher customs tariffs than the eu. it is the right of the united states to reinstate its previous trade rights following the expansion of the customs union. i therefore welcome the agreement with the us, which demonstrates the eu's commitment to a multilateral rules-based trading regime and the attempt to facilitate trade between the contracting parties.
in writing. − in 2007, the european union extended its customs union with two more countries, bulgaria and romania. in these circumstances, the eu was obliged to enter into negotiations with wto member states, with negotiating rights over the schedules of commitments of any future acceding member, with a view to agreeing on a mutually advantageous adjustment to compensate for the increased consolidated duties and the significant losses associated with them. if the adoption of the eu external tariff regime leads to an increase in customs duties above the level practiced by bulgaria and romania, then these compensations are necessary.
in writing. − the ideal of a customs union or free trade area is to facilitate trade between the territories that make up it, not to raise barriers. the accession of romania and bulgaria to the european union also meant the launch of tariff renegotiations with the countries that are part of the world trade organization. the biggest winners were wto members and free trade, because at the time of accession both romania and bulgaria had higher customs duties than the eu. in the opposite case, where romania and bulgaria had to increase their duties and tariffs to align with the eu's external tariff policy, thus breaching their wto commitments, it was the eu that had to make up the difference. this commitment has once again shown the european institutions' sympathy for multilateral trade.
in writing. - with the accession of bulgaria and romania, the eu has expanded its customs union. the eu was obliged, in accordance with wto rules, to enter into negotiations with wto member states with negotiating rights on the schedules of commitments of any acceding member with a view to agreeing on a mutually advantageous adjustment to compensate for the increase in the consolidated duties and the significant losses associated with it. eu enlargement is a positive factor for wto members. when the countries that joined the wto had higher tariffs than the eu, the wto members were the ones who gained. otherwise, when acceding countries had lower customs duties than the eu and were forced to increase their customs duties, the eu compensates for the difference. the eu-us compensation agreement covers products such as poultry and pork as well as food preparations. the agreement on the new tariff quota for these agricultural products will be implemented by means of an implementing regulation to be adopted by the commission. the us is entitled to re-establish its previous trade rights following their slight erosion due to the expansion of the eu customs union with the accession of romania and bulgaria.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report. the parliament should give its consent to the signing of this agreement. the compensatory adjustment for the us is a natural consequence of romania and bulgaria’s accession to the ue. the agreement adjusts our trade relations to this post-accession reality and follows the procedural rules of the wto.
in writing. − i support the decision to conclude the eu-us clearing agreement as it will have a positive influence and boost trade growth in the medium and long term. the enlargement of the european union, with the accession of romania and bulgaria, made the gatt 1994 agreement require a revision, so that there is a unified policy of all eu countries towards the united states. romania and bulgaria will have the same status as the other eu countries in relation to trade with the us. i believe that this step will lead to a rapid increase in trade between eu member countries, especially romania and bulgaria, and the united states. in practice, this is a matter of restoring market access, of reorganizing the trade partnership between the us and the eu, which is necessary by the enlargement of the customs union of the european community, an enlargement due to the accession of romania and bulgaria. a new agreement is a clear demonstration of the eu's commitment to the multilateral rules-based trading regime with all partner countries, with the wto at its core.
in writing. − the increase in unemployment in the member states of the european union is the most serious problem we are facing today. the high level of unemployment, especially among young people, threatens not only the solidarity that underpins the functioning of european societies, but also the future of the union. the aim of achieving a sustainable, sustainable and inclusive development model by 2020 is becoming illusory if the coordination of employment policies at european level is not to be stepped up. i support the adoption of the commission's report precisely because this coordination of economic policies is contrary to the provisions of the european treaties, which clearly emphasize that these, along with those relating to the promotion of employment, are not matters of national interest but matters which are at the heart of the european project. the adoption of this document is also a concrete step towards achieving the union's long-term objectives.

in writing. − according to the treaty on the functioning of the eu, the promotion of employment is a matter of common concern to the member states and must be coordinated within the council. to cope with the competition from the new emerging economies, i believe that europe must create the jobs needed by a dynamic, knowledge-based society. this requires investment in education and science, as well as in employment policies, so that the eu can keep pace with change and overcome the economic crisis.
in writing. − the treaty on the functioning of the eu provides that member states and the union are to develop a coordinated employment strategy and promote a trained, skilled and adaptable workforce and labour markets that are able to react rapidly to economic developments. the employment guidelines should form the basis of any country-specific recommendations that the council may address to member states. they should form the basis for the joint employment report sent annually by the council and the european commission to the european council. member states should make every effort to address the following priority areas in their national reform programmes: increasing labour market participation and reducing structural unemployment; developing a skilled workforce that meets labour market needs and promoting quality employment and lifelong learning; improving the performance of education and training systems at all levels and increasing participation in tertiary education; promoting social inclusion and combating poverty. the employment guidelines adopted in 2010 need to remain stable until 2014 so that efforts can focus on their implementation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's report approving the commission decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. under the new provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, member states are obliged to coordinate their employment policies, which is particularly necessary in the context of the economic and financial crisis and also taking into account that the europe 2020 strategy sets ambitious employment targets. member states must continue to harmonise their labour policies and ensure that the free movement of labour within the eu is guaranteed. it is also important that all member states continue to fully liberalise the labour market for workers in romania and bulgaria who face labour market restrictions in nine of the 27 eu member states.
in writing. − the interdependence between economic policies at community level and the labour policies of the treaty must be reflected in the national reform programmes of the member states. and so, by 2020, we can achieve high levels of global competitiveness and productivity with a trained, skilled and adaptable workforce. there is certainly more to be done in terms of employment policies. i could only mention a recent example, that of the united kingdom, where campaigns against the entry of romanian employees into the labour market have reached alarming levels, given that, according to the accession treaty, the restrictions imposed on romania and bulgaria expire at the end of this year. beyond the economic value of labour, let us not forget that we are talking about the fate of citizens, whom we can help to achieve financial independence and thus reduce the risk of poverty and social exclusion.
madam president, transparency opens the way to integrity and accountability, and we need greater transparency in the decision-making process for the pricing and reimbursement of pharmaceutical products. the pricing and reimbursement of pharmaceutical products fall within the member states’ exclusive competence. however, we need minimum procedural requirements in order to ensure the proper functioning of the single market, as well as legal certainty and transparency for national authorities. the names and declarations of interests of the experts involved in the decision-making process should be disclosed – they should be published and made available. moreover, the public should be aware of and have access to all the documents and information relating to a given decision. greater transparency is the key to assessing the level of integrity and independence of decisions taken and to reinforcing citizens’ trust and confidence in their national health authorities.
in writing. − the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that member states are responsible for organising their own health systems and for providing health and healthcare services. within this framework, each member state may adopt measures to manage the consumption of medicinal products, regulate their prices or lay down the conditions for their public financing. thus, a medicinal product authorised under eu law on the basis of its quality, safety and efficacy profile may be subject to additional regulatory requirements at member state level before it is placed on the market or released to patients under the public health insurance system. in view of the above, i consider that the existence of minimum procedural requirements should guarantee legal certainty and transparency for the competent national authorities and promote the production of medicinal products and the entry of generic medicinal products onto the market. research and development of new medicines should be encouraged to facilitate access to affordable treatments for all patients in europe.
in writing. − the primary beneficiary of the health care system must be and remains the patient. the european union must promote a transparent, predictable and coherent health system policy that guarantees all european patients real-time, effective and quality access to both original and generic medicines. the complexity and diversity of national measures relating to the pricing of medicinal products has increased considerably since 1989, when directive 89/105/eec on pharmaceutical transparency was adopted. the european commission has proposed fundamental provisions to update the current legislative framework in order to clarify the procedural obligations of member states and to ensure the proper functioning of the single market and the effectiveness of internal market legislation, both by avoiding delays in price-setting and reimbursement decisions and by removing obstacles to trade in pharmaceutical products. we need faster decisions on pricing and reimbursement to maintain the dynamism of the pharmaceutical market and to provide citizens with better access to medicines. facilitating faster market entry of generic medicines is also of particular importance for promoting a coherent and more transparent health system and will lead to substantial savings for both public health budgets and patients.
in writing. - i support this resolution because it is vital to support the increase of cost-effectiveness in pharmaceuticals. in order to ensure the proper functioning of the single market, to facilitate patients' access to reimbursements under public health insurance schemes and to encourage trade in these pharmaceuticals, we need a transparent legal framework and a transparent and harmonised system of price regulation.
in writing. − i believe that innovation and research in health bring significant benefits to patients and have positive consequences on the effectiveness and sustainability of health systems.
in writing. − i supported the initiative to improve eu citizens’ access to more affordable medicines. delays in pricing and reimbursements have in some cases reached more than 700 days, which is not to the benefit of eu citizens, especially vulnerable groups coping with chronic diseases. it is essential that member states provide for more transparency in their decisions regarding generic medicines.
i voted in favour of this report, which i consider to be much more realistic and balanced, a step forward in fisheries policies, but three things led me to do so: the introduction of the principle of consultation of regional interest groups, which i believe gives the professional communities the opportunity to express their views on fishing situations and to strike a balance between the need to protect the environment and their own survival interests; the decisions on the restoration of fish stocks, the blocking of 10 or 20% of fishing waters for three years, which i consider to be an opportunity for restoring stocks and for a sustainable economy, and last but not least the decision to look beyond the mediterranean and other seas, and the big bang regulation, by trying to find a solution to the cooperation that is taking place in non-member countries. as the black sea is still a problem, the professional community needs to be protected against poaching by third countries, and the possibility of regional or bilateral or multilateral agreements is useful.
i voted in favour of the report because the current common fisheries policy has not achieved its objectives. i have advocated setting targets to restore stocks above levels that can generate maximum sustainable production. i also voted for a ban on discarding catches, because i think it is a waste. in the black sea there is a specific problem, as only romania and bulgaria are subject to union rules on fishing quotas. therefore, there is a need for greater decentralisation of decision-making and involvement of the other riparian states. on the other hand, i opposed the creation of an advisory council for the markets, which would make the decision-making process difficult. i also voted against the establishment of structures for inland fishing, as decisions in this area must still be taken by the member states.
in writing. − fisheries are a natural, renewable, mobile and common property that is part of our common heritage. the common fisheries policy was introduced by the treaty of rome. initially, this policy was closely linked to agricultural policy, but over time it became increasingly independent of it. since its reform in 2002, the common fisheries policy has had as its main objective to ensure the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources and to guarantee stable incomes and jobs for fishermen. i welcome the commission's proposal to ensure that fisheries and aquaculture activities provide long-term sustainable environmental conditions and contribute to the availability of food supplies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it brings some new proposals in terms of the common fisheries policies. firstly, i am pleased that it has been agreed to include the professional groups in a dialogue on fishing situations, environmental protection and fish stocks. secondly, the ban on discarding is a positive thing because it reduces fish waste, which the commission estimates is 23% of all fish caught. another plus of this report is the policies that aim to restore fish stocks and to prioritise sustainable economics in this industry, a good example being the blocking of certain areas of fishing waters for a period of time to provide the necessary duration for the fish fauna of those waters to recover.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because a sustainable policy for the fisheries sector is needed. changes are needed to combat overfishing, to alleviate the plight of fishermen and to reduce the financial difficulties currently facing the fisheries sector. a common long-term policy is essential to preserve the marine environment, both for ourselves and for future generations.
in writing. − i believe that the common fisheries policy must contribute to supplying the union market with highly nutritious food, reducing dependence on the internal market in food, contributing directly or indirectly to job creation and, implicitly, to economic development in coastal areas.
in writing. - i voted against the report. i believe that parliament must support a fair reform, with the conservation of fish stocks as its priority. the correct way to ensure this priority would have been to adopt the solution proposed by amendment no 297, which respects the principle of the landing obligation but also establishes measures to enable the fisheries sector to adapt to this obligation. at the same time, i welcome the adoption of the amendments concerning the establishment of a black sea council, which i have called for on numerous occasions. i also welcome the inclusion in this text of important provisions on aquaculture, a disadvantaged sector in the eu that needs to be encouraged.
in writing. − i welcome this report from the fisheries committee and the efforts of colleagues to strengthen the commission’s proposal on the reform of the common fisheries policy. the amendments adopted in committee would bring the cfp into line with the 2020 objectives of the marine framework strategy directive because of the legal requirement for member states to adopt measures to rebuild fish stocks to healthy levels by the end of this decade. this would represent a significant step on the road to repairing our damaged seas, replenishing fish stocks, and protecting fishing industries in the long-term. this is just one of a series of amendments which would bring improvements, along with those banning discards and ensuring the establishment of marine protected areas. i would like to thank those colleagues who have worked hard to improve the commission’s proposal, and i wish them every success in the negotiations with council.
in writing. − i totally support a strong cfp reform, therefore a more sustainable fisheries policy. the preservation of biodiversity, and not least of endangered species, is of great importance. the current fisheries policy has led to a big number of wasted fish, and now parliament had a great opportunity to vote for a long-term supply of sustainable seafood in europe, as well as for a more secure future for our fishermen.
madam president, noise pollution is an annoyance with adverse health effects that has plagued people for a long time. a leading cause of this form of pollution is transportation. the noise from planes, motor vehicles and trains is a disturbance to citizens especially at night. just because noise pollution is unlike other types of pollution and cannot be seen, tasted or smelt does not mean that it deserves less of our attention. i voted for regulating certain types of motor vehicle because action must be taken to diminish this growing problem. i truly believe that the transportation industries – and i mean the big industries – must invest money here in responding to citizens’ wishes and to their need to live in a healthy environment.
in writing. − the european authorities have noted in recent years the increasingly significant impact of noise pollution on the health of european citizens. the fact that no less than 20% of european citizens, especially in urban areas, experience health problems as a result of exposure to high levels of noise pollution is a signal that both national and european authorities need to take into account. in this context, i support the proposal to amend the regulations in this area in the interests of protecting public health, both as regards the approval procedure for motor vehicles and as regards the reduction of noise levels. i believe that any european policy in this area must strike a balance between protecting the health and lifestyle of european citizens and supporting the automotive industry, which remains one of the pillars of european development and competitiveness. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − noise pollution is the bane of big cities, where it affects the environment not only during working hours but also during leisure time. in general we can talk about an extension of noise pollution to the global level of the environment. although car engines are quieter than in the past, noise on the streets and especially on the highways is continually increasing not only because of increased traffic but also because of increased vehicle speed. currently, on some modern highways the noise level has exceeded 80 db during peak traffic periods. in view of the above, i welcome the commission's proposal to introduce a new test method for measuring the sound level of motor vehicles and new noise limit values for the different categories of light, medium and heavy vehicles.
in writing. - noise pollution has a major impact on the health and, at the same time, on the well-being of european citizens; i believe it is our duty to do everything we can to reduce the effects of this type of pollution as much as possible. cars are responsible for a large proportion of noise pollution; therefore, measures must be taken to reduce the noise they emit. this must be done without putting too much pressure on the car industry, which is already in an economic impasse on the european market.
in writing. − sound pollution is one of the biggest problems facing europeans today, and it must be tackled with all responsibility, given the clear negative effects it has on public health and the environment. in this context, the regulation of traffic noise as the main source of noise pollution is a key element of a responsible policy to protect citizens and the environment. romania is one of the noisiest european countries. over 60% of the urban population is affected by noise due to heavy road traffic, and bucharest, the country's capital, has the highest percentage of residents exposed to noise, 85%, at noise levels above the sound pollution standards accepted by the world health organization. this is the situation in many other european cities. if we also take into account that road traffic is accompanied by air pollution, then the risk factors are even more important. it is therefore important that the european union has an ambitious and realistic strategy on vehicle noise, one which carefully strikes a sustainable balance between a high level of protection of health and the environment on the one hand and the competitiveness of the automotive industry on the other.
in writing. − i consider that for some heavy vehicles the suggested noise reduction levels are not feasible even if the latest technologies in the field were applied. i think new materials need to be developed to improve the sound insulation level.
in writing. − i welcome the commission's initiative to update the limit value for noise emissions from motor vehicles in view of the increase in traffic in europe, especially in large urban centres. but i think that in the future we should also consider proper maintenance of the streets which can lead to a reduction of more than 5 db (a). the use of special asphalt could also reduce road traffic noise by up to 10 db (a). significant reduction would also be achieved by decongesting traffic with by- roads, preferential lanes, and intelligent transportation. we must have an integrated approach to this sector, because this is how we can achieve results that are meaningful and visible to the citizens.
in writing. - i do not ignore the importance of this report and i think we should be concerned about the comfort of citizens, especially those in large cities or near high-traffic arteries. but i voted against all the amendments which set unrealistic targets for the car industry. i therefore voted against amendments nos 51, 61, 67 and 68. the european automotive industry already has, in all respects, particularly high standards. unrealistic standards will make automobile production more expensive, which means higher prices for car buyers.
in writing. − today i voted to improve the restrictions on sound levels from motor vehicles. we know that noise pollution is a serious public health issue which disproportionately affects those living in urban areas and near busy roads. we must therefore encourage the car industry to make quieter engines in order to help achieve lower levels of noise pollution, but without imposing unreasonable costs in what are already difficult economic circumstances, and bearing in mind that traffic noise depends on a number of factors, such as engine noise, tyres, and road surface. paradoxically, very quiet cars, namely electric cars travelling at very low speeds, can present a particular risk for children, cyclists and blind people. that is why i also voted in favour of mandatory electric-vehicle warning sounds, so that very quiet engines can still be heard.
in writing. − i welcome the awareness-raising and action on health issues related to environmental noise. however, i voted against amendment 51 and 68 because of the large-scale impact on the automobile industry in a time of crisis. i consider that amendment 51 would have set unrealistic objectives for the automobile industry. regarding amendment 68, not only do tyres already have to comply with the general safety regulation that already sets minimum requirements for noise, but also, testing conditions for tyres proposed in this am would have created a discrepancy throughout the regulation in discussion.

in writing. - i voted for a twenty percentage point increase in the co-financing rate for the migration and asylum funds. many member states are facing serious difficulties with their financial stability, but this should not affect the management of migration flows. i regret, however, that in some member states the use of funds is abusive and creates long-term problems. i therefore ask the commission to implement rigorous management and control systems, followed by permanent and appropriate checks and monitoring.
in writing. − as more and more european countries are facing the adverse effects of the international economic and financial crisis, the european union's border protection systems are being significantly affected by austerity policies or by increasing the efficiency of public spending. increasing the share of european union co-financing in specific projects to develop border surveillance is one of the measures that can ensure the functionality of this sector without necessarily entailing additional pressures on the european budget. while the imperatives of economic recovery must guide member states' policies at this time, the major importance of maintaining a flexible and effective border protection system should not be overlooked. many of the social or security problems facing member states can be exacerbated by inadequate management of migration flows in the context of a global, and not just a european, crisis. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i consider it necessary to amend the co-financing rates of the external borders fund for member states facing serious difficulties with regard to their financial stability. the economic crisis has had a severe impact on public finances in several member states. they have had to resort to eu financial support mechanisms. i would stress the particular importance of effective monitoring and evaluation systems for the use of resources. it is also important to mention the solidarity of member states facing major fiscal challenges. romania, as part of a macro-financial assistance agreement, will benefit from the increased co-financing.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has had a severe impact on public finances in several member states. i welcome and support the proposals to increase the co-financing rate for the member states receiving financial support.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that good management of borders and migration flows is essential for the european union. the additional union co-financing rate of the european border and coast guard fund up to 70% and 95% respectively is intended for those member states experiencing significant difficulties in terms of public finances and national budgets. this will allow member states to continue to comply with community standards and acquis in the management of borders and migration flows, while respecting the rights of migrants. this increase in the co-financing rate will however remain temporary and limited and will not apply in the next multiannual financial year 2014-2020.

madam president, nine out of ten victims of intimate partner violence are women and around 25% of all women have experienced physical violence at least once. the union’s efforts to reduce domestic violence through legislative measures have failed. poor implementation of criminal laws and poor imposition of sanctions are major reasons for impunity. this is why a solution could be for member states to recognise domestic violence as a form of gender-based violence in their criminal codes and implement protection orders and impose sanctions. non-criminal measures, such as shelters and real and long-term protection for victims, including putting distance between those aggressing and their victims, could be more efficient than any punishment. also we need to focus and think that the objective is protecting the victims and reducing domestic violence; i therefore insist on, and lobby for, these non-criminal measures.
in writing. − violence against women is a worldwide phenomenon. according to the world health organization, between 15 and 71 percent of women between the ages of 15 and 49 have been beaten, forced to have sex, or abused by their partners in their lifetime. despite the adoption of several strategies to protect women, the problem of violence against women remains acute every day one in five women in the 47 council of europe countries is subjected to violence. in addition, violence against women also has a negative impact on the european economy. the cost of violence against women in europe is estimated at eur 34 billion per year, or eur 555 for each european. as regards the above elements, i believe that an eu strategy to combat violence against women is needed, including a directive setting out a set of minimum standards for the member states of the european union.
in writing. − violence against women and girls has serious consequences for the physical and mental health of the victims and for social development in general. the main causes of this phenomenon are poverty, traditions, religious values, political instability, armed conflict, the media. the consequences of large-scale violence extend beyond immediate bodily injury or material loss. there are often serious and long-lasting health effects, as well as social and psychological consequences that affect victims of violence, their children and their families. despite the evolution of society, the increase in the level of education, we see not only the maintenance of traditional forms (beating, insulting, rape), but also the revival of special forms of violence: blocking women's access to income, genital mutilation, slavery, forced labour, prostitution. the eu must therefore give a comprehensive definition of violence against women, identify the factors that contribute to its proliferation and continue to prevent and control this social scourge at international level.

in writing. − violence against women and young girls is the most widespread form of human rights violation. studies indicate that the main causes are economic and power disparities between the sexes, customs, traditions, religious values, political instability, and armed conflict. although the european union has been and is a promoter of gender equality, the eu 2020 strategy contains few indicators that mention gender equality as a priority at european level. starting this year, the eradication and prevention of all forms of violence against women and girls will be one of the priority themes of the 57th session of the united nations commission on the status of women. i also consider it of major importance that development aid be linked to a continuous fight against all forms of violence against women in developing countries.

i would first like to welcome the commission's proposal for a rapid reaction mechanism to improve tax collection and taxation at european level. i also congratulate my fellow rapporteurs and shadow rapporteurs on their work on this report, which is so important in the fight against vat fraud. the current vat legislation clearly needs to be improved so that member states can have mechanisms to enable them to deal quickly with particularly serious fraud, in particular the carousel fraud, as my colleagues have said, or the fraud resulting from the use of shell companies. unfortunately, the lack of firm action in this direction causes annual losses to national budgets of several billion euros. moreover, not only member states suffer, but also european businesses, which face unfair competition in certain sectors contaminated by fraud. the fact that we do not currently have accurate data on the extent of tax fraud in the european union speaks for itself of the difficulties in identifying and combating this worrying phenomenon. immediate solutions to vat fraud are absolutely necessary, especially in the context of the fiscal difficulties we face and the dramatic impact of austerity measures on european citizens. i therefore support the european executive's proposal to set up a rapid reaction mechanism so that member states wishing to introduce special measures such as reverse taxation can do so without first requesting a derogation at european level. such a derogation now has to be considered by the european commission and voted on unanimously by the council, which puts national action on hold for several months. however, while the benefits of such a mechanism are undeniable, i would like to draw attention to the possible additional costs for businesses resulting from the decision to apply this measure. the internal reverse charge mechanism must remain exceptional in order to avoid any harm to taxpayers. i also share the rapporteur's view that the commission's proposal must be accompanied by a long-term strategy in this area, which encourages structural changes to vat systems. i therefore welcome the proposal for an own-initiative report and wholeheartedly support it.
fraud in the vat system, especially cross-border fraud, is very easy to detect, given that the european single market allows many products to circulate without being taxed. tax and vat fraud also cause significant distortions of the internal market. they constitute obstacles to fair competition and cause significant losses in public services at national level, generating billions of euros of losses annually at union level. companies that comply with the law are also affected. the member states must therefore cooperate as closely as possible to counter this phenomenon and it is beneficial to launch the rapid reaction mechanism. i support the rapporteur's proposal that the launch of this mechanism should be followed by a long-term strategy to combat fraud, which should also allow for the harmonisation of the vat systems in the member states, without which evasionists will always find opportunities for fraud.
in writing. both the eu budget and national budgets lose several billion euros annually due to vat fraud. in some serious cases, losses occur in a very short time, due to the speed with which fraud mechanisms are currently developing. at this point, member states may, within one month, implement a reverse charge mechanism that makes the recipient, not the supplier of goods and services, liable for vat. this measure became necessary because fraudsters became faster and more ingenious in developing ways to defraud the public purse. this rapid reaction mechanism thus ensures that the system is better equipped to combat vat fraud. in view of the above, i consider that the most effective solution to combat vat fraud is reverse taxation.

the eib is wholly owned by the european union. citizens, non-governmental organisations and the other european institutions must therefore be able to analyse the bank's activities in full. its transparency policy is an important step in this direction, but further efforts are needed, in particular with regard to the timely publication of the detailed description of the projects under way. when we talk about transparency, we also think about the bank's obligation to help combat fraud and tax evasion. the european commission has recently launched a set of criteria to identify third countries that do not meet minimum standards of good governance and taxation, and the eib must comply with them. at the same time, and i am addressing this to you, commissioner, i believe that the european executive can do more to enable this type of jurisdiction to be identified quickly, in this case, i suggest you complete a list of tax havens. finally, i would like to draw attention to another obligation which derives from the statute of the european investment bank: its duty to contribute to the strict observance of international law and the principle of the un charter. therefore, the projects the eib and the actors involved choose from and choose to participate in must also respect international law. finally, i would like to congratulate all the other rapporteurs on their work and their excellent cooperation.
member of the commission. − mr president, on 4 february the committee on economic and monetary affairs (econ) adopted a resolution rejecting two of the delegated acts adopted by the commission relating to technical standards supplementing regulation eu no 648/2012 (emir) on otc derivatives, central counterparties and trade depositories. having carefully examined the reasons for such rejection the commission, in the spirit of compromise, is prepared to make sure that when it adopts its decisions on mandatory clearing for specific classes of otc derivatives, the obligation for non-financial firms to clear will be phased in over an appropriate period of time. the commission also fully shares with parliament its attachment to the principle of legal certainty. therefore the commission would like to make the following statement:‘the commission decided that the regulatory technical standards in question should be strictly based on the draft technical standards prepared by esma. our responsibility is to take all measures to ensure that financial risks are appropriately supervised and mitigated and thus to protect our economy. ‘ the commission understands some of parliament’s concerns. the commission is prepared to make sure that, when it adopts its decisions on mandatory clearing for specific classes of otc derivatives, the obligation for non-financial firms to clear will be phased-in over an appropriate period of time. such a phased-in period could be similar to the one proposed in the technical standard for bank guarantees. this would allow non-financial firms sufficient time to fully adapt to the new landscape. at the same time it preserves a sound and solid financial regulatory approach. taking into account the provisions of emir, the commission is also willing to clarify the application of the confirmation deadline standards referred to in article 11(1)(a) of emir in the future. ‘the development of technical standards is terra nova for all institutions. the commission is sure that the process will be developed and refined over time. the commission stands ready to work together with parliament to ensure an open dialogue and transparency about our planning for forthcoming technical standards and ensure that parliament has enough time, in the framework of the relevant inter-institutional agreement, to assess them. in particular, as regards the procedures relating to the preparation of delegated acts and with a view to developing good practices in that matter, the commission will promote a clear understanding on working relations including for instance meetings and planning, and regular exchanges of views between the commission and econ on regulatory standards, taking full account of existing inter-institutional agreements on the timing of sending legislative acts to parliament.’
recent statistics show that by 2060, the number of elderly people will have increased by a whopping 79 percent. and yet, in the european union, at the moment, only the city of fredericia in denmark is showing social innovation and promoting the ability to live independently among older people. to implement such successful models in as many member states as possible, i believe that: european funds should be allocated to develop a european network on age-friendly environments; a european convention should be organised to give local, regional and national authorities interested in the concept of the third-age economy a better chance; and, last but not least, the objectives of the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations should be integrated into all relevant funding instruments of the european union, including the structural funds.
mr president, in 2010 the number of union citizens aged 65 and over was around 87 million. by 2060 it is expected to reach 148 million. public spending on health already accounts for 7.8 % of gdp in the eu and by 2060 this percentage is expected to reach over 10 % of gdp due to ageing. we adopted the european innovation partnership on active and healthy ageing, and this could be a good intervention at eu level with a view to improving the quality of life of elderly citizens and reducing pressure on the health system. the commission must now strictly and constantly monitor and assess the implementation of this partnership in each of the member states.
i voted in favour of the report because active ageing is of interest to all member states and the union has the resources to provide innovative responses to this. i welcome the initiative to put into practice the strategic plan for implementing the european partnership for the creation of better living conditions. it is important that the younger generations are also involved in promoting a whole-life perspective. romania, like other european countries, is going through a significant process of population ageing. by 2050, the age pyramid is expected to have a considerably reduced base due to the accelerated growth in the number of pensioners. a step forward to redress this situation was the launch in 2012 of the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations in romania.
in writing. − the report highlights the significant potential of the european innovation partnership on active and healthy ageing, both socially and economically. the partnership aims to promote and stimulate innovative solutions that give older people the opportunity to improve their health and quality of life, that meet their real needs and, at the same time, that provide them with the opportunity for social interaction. i believe that promoting a healthy lifestyle throughout life is a key component in developing the mechanisms and strategies needed to achieve the goal of increasing healthy life expectancy. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the european union's population is in the midst of an ageing process. this demographic change is the inevitable consequence of the considerable progress made by our society. demographic ageing poses a number of challenges for the labour market, for health systems, and for the quality of life after retirement. active ageing means growing old in good health, playing an active role in society and achieving professional fulfilment, but also being independent in daily life and engaging in civic activities. regardless of our age, we can play an important role in society and enjoy a good standard of living, even in old age. the challenge is to make the most of the enormous potential that older people have. i believe that any initiative to identify the solutions needed to build a better society for both the elderly and the young is welcome.
in writing. − the important role of local and regional actors in modernising, improving and rationalising the delivery of health and social care services to create models for better outcomes for people in the labour market should be emphasised. older people need an income, a home, access to all types of appropriate health, social and cultural services, and strong social networks to enhance their quality of life. older people also need opportunities to continue to contribute to the labour market without age-discriminatory restrictions. it is necessary to create the right conditions for people to work longer hours and be more productive, both by increasing flexibility in the labour market by introducing work opportunities through record keeping of working hours and part-time work, and by making available modern forms of employment contracts, including temporary contracts. the adequacy of pensions should be strengthened by tackling discrimination between women and men in the labour market, in particular by reducing career and pay gaps.
in writing. − europe needs a strategy to enable towns of all sizes and in all areas to adapt to the demographic and spatial changes the eu is facing due to an ageing population and to adapt them to the requirements of older people. on the other hand, thorough assessments of the actual needs of the ageing population and regular monitoring of the needs and requirements (current and future) of older people, as well as close collaboration with regional and local policy makers, are needed to meet these requirements.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it contains essential measures in the development of a strategic plan for the european partnership for active ageing. in a time of demographic transition, with the population of urban areas aging rapidly, there is an urgent need to re-adapt these areas to the new types of needs and capacities of their populations and to create a society for all ages by 2020. the report supports the european commission's initiative to increase the involvement of older people in policy-making and decision-making for better local and regional governance. this participatory approach allows the assessment and monitoring of the ageing population, which is necessary to assess progress towards the target of increasing average healthy life expectancy by two years by 2020.
in writing. − over-exploitation of wild fauna and flora, unsustainable trophy hunting, overfishing, significant increase in poaching, illegal wildlife trade, climate change and deforestation are the main causes of the disappearance of endangered species such as sea cats, polar bears, elephants, corn rhinos and some ornamental plants. cites is the main global agreement on the conservation of these species and aims to prevent the overexploitation of wild fauna and flora due to international trade in wild animal and plant species. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the eu strategic objectives for the 16th meeting of the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) as i believe that the extinction of known threatened species must be prevented and their conservation status must be improved and maintained.
in writing. − the conservation of biodiversity is one of the major international issues of our time. the european union, as one of the most important markets for wildlife trade, has a particular responsibility to ensure that this trade, as well as trade in derived products, is sustainable and does not lead to the endangerment of the species concerned. since 1984, the european union has been implementing the provisions of the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) through the european commission's regulations on trade in wild fauna and flora. in view of the 16th conference of the parties to the cites convention (cop 16) to be held in bangkok in march 2013, the envi committee asked the council and the european commission to set out the main strategic objectives of the european union and tabled a motion for a resolution urging the european union to take a leading role in protecting endangered species by actively participating in the cites convention negotiations. the resolution addresses the main issues to be discussed at cop 16 and suggests ways to increase transparency in cites decision-making.
in writing. − i believe that continuity of funding in the context of european development aid is necessary to achieve the main objectives of cites.
mr president, the organisation of plenary debates, cuts in travel-related budget lines, a reduction in the length and number of missions, increased use of videoconferencing, and optimised translation and interpretation services, all these structural reforms implemented in parliament have led to annual savings of approximately eur 29 million. however, i do believe that we can do more. translation and interpretation services could be used and paid for only on demand. this would permit savings in hours of non-needed translation, a lot of paperwork, and interpretation services as well as tonnes of paper, while continuing to ensure the multilingual principle. when we speak publicly and we want our constituents to hear us and to be accountable to our constituents, i can understand we want to use our languages. however, when we work internally between ourselves, among ourselves, on different dossiers i think we should limit the official languages to one or two and save a lot of taxpayers’ money.
the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy cannot be achieved without the private sector, without companies, without enterprises. it is obvious that they must be given facilities to develop and create jobs. but now i would like to turn to a specific issue, namely, the tendency of some businesses to mislead consumers. i therefore ask the commission to present clear measures to eliminate misleading and false information provided by companies on the environmental impact of products and services, their impact on consumers or on the social commitments and obligations of these companies. one way to stamp out this false information is to give the public clear and accurate information, so that they can judge what and how to use these products.
in writing. − the concept of social responsibility is essential both for the efficiency of the european social model and for achieving the sustainable and inclusive development objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the objective of achieving an employment rate of 75% depends essentially on the ability of national and european authorities, together with industrial entrepreneurs, to initiate social responsibility actions and campaigns. corporate social responsibility is not only an essential element of the 'european way of producing and building' but also a starting point for increasing the competitiveness of the european industrial sector. actions undertaken under the idea of social responsibility bring workers and consumers closer to producers, build relationships and social networks of extended solidarity and contribute directly to the development and cohesion of communities in the member states. i also support the amendment tabled by the commission which leaves open the possibility of adopting possible binding or regulatory measures on social responsibility.
in writing. − corporate social responsibility is more than a programme or a campaign. it is a philosophy, a way of behaving ethically and responsibly that touches on all aspects: from business, to the relationship with one's own employees, with customers, with shareholders, with suppliers, with the environment and, of course, with local communities. in recent times, more and more companies have realised that this approach can benefit them both by creating a competitive advantage and by promoting a positive image and ensuring a good relationship with all partners. at the same time, i believe that there should be coherence between social programmes, attitudes towards business, employees and the environment. if all these issues are dealt with discontinuously, there is no social responsibility at all.
in writing. − i support the rapporteur's view that there is a need for greater visibility and an appropriate level of awareness of the contribution of small enterprises to corporate social responsibility (csr), because the responsibility of smes is not reduced compared to that of large ones simply because they do not have a separate csr infrastructure.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as i welcome the european commission's initiative to develop a csr strategy to support businesses in integrating fundamental social, ethical and environmental rights into their business strategies to ensure better consumer protection. i believe that this report helps to raise the visibility of csr practices and to disseminate them. this will improve the transparency of companies with regard to social and environmental information, which will increase the trust of citizens in companies. 90% of european enterprises are smes, which, by their characteristics of operation, become strategic in disseminating csr practices. the involvement of smes in csr is a political priority of the european parliament supported, inter alia, by this report.
i believe that in a period marked by the economic and financial crisis, which has caused significant social impacts both globally and at the level of the european union, the strategic approach to corporate social responsibility is becoming increasingly important for the competitiveness of companies. in this respect, i recommend that the development of csr be fully supported by local public administrations and thus create all the necessary conditions for cooperation in csr. also, providing appropriate tools and facilities, such as incentive schemes or ways to promote existing successful csr initiatives, will lead to significant benefits for both businesses and european society as a whole.
i voted in favour of the report because i believe that corporate social responsibility is a catalyst for sustainable economic recovery in the union. we need to realise that, in addition to the benefits to society, csr actions also help companies to improve their image in the eyes of potential consumers. they can thus increase their competitiveness and be economically viable in the long term, providing more jobs. although smes play a very important role in the romanian economy, it is generally the large companies that conduct socially responsible business. there are a number of opinions that smes do not practice csr or are not familiar with the concept of responsible business. therefore, i believe that we need to raise their awareness of the importance and benefits of adopting responsible entrepreneurial behaviour.
in writing. − the most serious problems raised by the economic crisis are not confined to this sector of european societies. the most important issues raised by the prolongation of the recession are those relating to the impact of joblessness or prolonged unemployment on the living standards of european citizens. the situation is all the more dramatic for young people, the social group most affected by longterm unemployment. social responsibility measures can directly reflect on reducing unemployment at member state level. as the medium and long-term objective of the european union is to generate sustainable, sustainable and inclusive growth in european economies, a hard-hitting approach to social responsibility is inevitable. in these circumstances, i support the creation of a legal framework that allows both voluntary and mandatory actions to define the social responsibility of european entrepreneurs. i also believe that direct involvement of public authorities in the member states at this level is welcome. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − corporate social responsibility should respect fundamental principles and rights, such as those mentioned by the international labour organisation, in particular freedom of association, the right to collective bargaining, the prohibition of forced labour, the elimination of child labour and the elimination of discrimination at the workplace. businesses should also be involved in addressing social problems aggravated by the economic crisis, such as homelessness and poverty, and in developing the communities in which they operate. businesses are responsible for adopting proactive principles and policies to combat discrimination and social exclusion, promote gender equality and respect the fundamental rights of all. at the same time, member states should encourage undertakings to develop policies and measures on the need to respect the private and family life of all employees. such policies and measures should respect the principle of equality and should extend to negotiations on the duration and organisation of working time, the level of pay, the provision of practical facilities to workers and the establishment of flexible working conditions, including the nature of employment contracts and the possibility of interruption of professional activity.

in writing. − i voted for the report on corporate social responsibility because it is all the more important now, in the context of the current economic and social difficulties facing member states, to support and encourage small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), because they can bring about sustainable economic growth by creating new jobs and, by implication, solve social problems. in this context, it is useful to propose the creation and implementation of a framework of guidelines which is not a legislative norm but which is appropriate to the needs of smes, supports their development and at the same time harmonises, with optimal results, environmental protection needs and those relating to social issues. it would be useful for the commission, in cooperation with national authorities and multilateral platforms, to develop a sectoral cooperation mechanism between smes, leading to an integrated approach to existing problems, including those relating to social and environmental aspects. this framework of guidelines should in no way replace, but only complement, the applicable legislation, collective bargaining and dialogue with trade union members.

in writing. − as vat fraud is evolving rapidly, many member states are left with no legal basis in existing eu vat legislation for the countermeasures they wish to take. combating vat fraud often has an international dimension, which is another reason why member states are not able to tackle fraud rings linked to new forms of trade involving several countries at the same time. these reasons, together with the fact that vat is one of the main sources of revenue for member states' budgets, force us to increase the efficiency of vat in the context of fiscal consolidation. i believe that this is the only way to improve tax collection and tackle tax evasion and thus give member states the chance to increase public revenue.
