in writing. − the current crisis is a social and employment crisis and social governance must therefore be improved at eu level, alongside economic governance. the european semester is the most appropriate process to achieve this objective. member states must adopt measures to promote job creation, promote and support self-employment and start-ups, improve the business environment and facilitate access to finance for smes. at the same time, member states should take the necessary measures to transform informal and undeclared work into regulated employment, reform labour markets to make them more adaptable, dynamic and inclusive, and harness the high employment potential of the green sector to create jobs. all employment contracts should give workers access to a fundamental set of rights, including pension rights and social protection and access to lifelong learning programmes.

mr president, for too long the disappearance of human rights activists has plagued developing countries, and sombath somphone is no exception. we must take a more active role in investigating mr somphone’s abduction and make his case a priority in the 22nd session of the united nations human rights council. more pressure needs to be placed on the laotian authorities to aid his safe return. given the video footage, the government response has so far been unacceptable. we all know the horrible prison conditions and corruption of the authoritarian states, and it is our responsibility as stewards of democracy and human rights to ensure sombath somphone is immediately returned to his family.
human rights continue to be violated in laos, and the forced disappearance of sombath somphone is the latest evidence of this. through his work, he laid the foundations for a model of rural development capable of ensuring food security in a very poor country. in laos, more than three quarters of the population live in rural areas, and most make their living from farming. that is why his work in combating hunger among the rural population is all the more important. i think the authorities should quickly identify the circumstances in which this man disappeared and ensure his immediate release. it is also very important that laos ratifies the international convention for the protection of persons from enforced disappearance.
my speakers have reported extensively on the situation in zimbabwe; i therefore believe that the european union, as a promoter of human rights in europe and the world, must support the proposal to send a significant group of european and international observers to monitor the elections in zimbabwe. to remove any suspicion about the conduct of the electoral process, international observation teams must remain on the ground before and after the elections to ensure that electoral campaigns are conducted in accordance with internationally recognised standards. i also stress the need for the zimbabwean authorities to respect their commitments to guarantee respect for human rights principles and legislation. otherwise, the european union will maintain the suspension of development cooperation.
member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, thank you for bringing the issue of the imprisonment of human rights activists in zimbabwe to the fore. despite noticeable improvements in the general human rights situation in zimbabwe since the signature of the global political agreement and the creation of the government of national unity, 2011 and 2012 saw sporadic arrests of human rights defenders and activists. the recent arrest of the zimrights director, okay machisa, has triggered a new wave of concerns amongst civil society organisations that this could be the sign of a closing of democratic and electoral space. the eu has been following this case very closely and is in regular contact with the lawyer representing mr machisa. the eu is actively working to support a large spectrum of civil society organisations and human rights activists in zimbabwe through its various financial instruments. in 2011 the delegation committed eur 9.8 million in support of civil society organisations alone. last year eur 5.5 million were committed and the figure will probably exceed eur 10 million in 2013. we have also acted promptly through statements and declarations in response to prolonged and unjustified detentions of human rights activists and against unfair treatment of not only human rights activists, but also journalists and civil society. the eu is also coordinating closely with international and, as was mentioned, regional key partners to strengthen civil society and improve the political space in zimbabwe. zimbabwe’s civil society is competent and as far as groups of human rights defenders and democracy advocacy are concerned, it is remarkably cohesive. i believe that the eu has an important role to play in supporting a peaceful and democratic future for zimbabwe.
in writing. – unfortunately, the unlawful detention of numerous human rights activists in zimbabwe is nothing new. however, the presidential election supposed to take place this year has triggered an increasingly vicious crackdown by president mugabe, who might be removed from power. i support any action that has the ability to stop any further politically motivated prosecutions and call for the release of those activists already in custody. it is essential that the people of zimbabwe be allowed to have open elections free of harassment, unlawful detention and the threat of torture.
on behalf of the epp group. attacks on medical personnel in pakistan are jeopardising the efforts of international organisations to provide aid to people in need. in 1990, there were over 20,000 cases of polio in pakistan. however, thanks to the efforts of the world health organization, in recent years, there have been fewer than 100 cases reported on average. however, the vaccination of children in pakistan must continue, as the country risks becoming the only place in the world where the virus still exists. the authorities should ensure the safety of medical personnel, regardless of the area in which they operate. support will also be needed to improve the quality of the vaccination campaign, increase immunisation coverage, and address social and cultural constraints.
the european union supports the efforts of the authorities of third countries to respect women's rights and is concerned about the threats posed by extremist groups to women and young people in pakistan who work in various non-governmental organisations, and about the security of international medical staff in the country. we also hope that the pakistani authorities will take all necessary measures to ensure the safety of representatives of humanitarian organizations, especially those involved in the continuation of the national plan for the eradication of polio, launched in 2012, because only in this way will we avoid an increase in the number of infections, especially among children. i also think it is useful to organise awareness campaigns, especially in rural areas, to raise awareness of the essential, independent and humanitarian role of medical staff in providing assistance to the population, especially when it comes to developing access to basic preventive health services.
reporting for an opinion of the committee on development. - austerity measures, as you said, have put millions of women out of work in the european union, especially in the health and education sectors, which is seriously affecting society as a whole. more than a third of women are employed part-time, reducing their access to social services and pensions and pushing them into poverty and misery. the disparities in pay and representation in decision-making at public and company level also reflect the degree of discrimination that persists in the european union. equal opportunities is, as you said, a fundamental right and that is why i am also calling on the european commission to review the directive on reducing the gender gap and to impose sanctions on member states that do not implement it. the difficulties caused by the crisis have created new suffering and exacerbated tensions and domestic violence. i would like to reiterate in this context the need and the call to the member states and the commission to ratify the convention on the elimination of violence against women.
i welcome this debate, but i already consider it a stereotype in political and parliamentary practice. i would have liked this debate to take place in a completely different context, and not as an effect of the celebration of 8 march, when we are trying to analyse how a fundamental principle of the european construction, namely gender equality, is implemented and respected. gender equality, in fact, is the standard of civilization of some communities, and that's what we should be talking about, and what the three reports are trying to talk about. i welcome the report on the crisis, i consider it realistic. without a doubt, if someone pays the bill for this crisis, in terms of gender, women pay an extra vat, because they are the first beneficiaries, in the negative sense, of the crisis, they are the ones who are dismissed faster than men, they are the ones who receive lower salaries than men, they are the ones who do not always have the chance to reconcile their professional and private lives. but as far as stereotypes go, i think the issues here are much more nuanced. a report should have defined what a stereotype is in its legal value and in the possibility that, in terms of subsidiarity, many member states already have definitions and are trying to avoid these stereotypes. it is very difficult to draw the line between a fundamental right, that of free information, which is a matter of rights and freedoms, but also a matter of culture, and the criminalization of this as a sexist insult.
the reality of gender stereotypes is one that many women still face. the impact of these stereotypes is exemplified by the quasi-segregation of many sectors of activity, as well as the persistence of discriminatory situations such as double working hours or the unequal sharing of tasks and responsibilities. the maintenance of these divisions in fact contributes significantly to the permanence of social status differences, as well as to the persistence of a significant income gap between men and women at the level of the european union as well as at the level of the member states. at the same time, in the absence of stronger policy action, the maintenance of these stereotypes blocks the achievement of equality in the labour market. last but not least, it should be stressed that gender stereotypes are one of the factors responsible for the still high level of violence against women in the european union. in these circumstances, i believe that proposals for action in the education and training process are essential to combat gender stereotypes.
the right to work is an essential precondition for women to be able to be economically independent, enjoy equal rights and professional satisfaction. unfortunately, austerity imposed by the economic crisis is affecting women's employment and may lead to increased exploitation of women in both the legal and the illegal economy, with longer-term consequences for women in atypical careers, precarious, low-paid or part-time jobs. in all these cases, the pension contribution will be incomplete and the percentage of women exposed to poverty and social exclusion will increase. i believe that reliable common indicators are needed to have comparable european statistics, to allow correct assessments of different situations and needs, to formulate appropriate responses at european union level and to reduce differences in pay for the same work or work of equal value.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, as the rapporteur on the connecting europe facility (cef) i warmly welcome the forthcoming vote on the energy guidelines. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr correia de campos, on this occasion. as we know, the energy guidelines are a crucial element of the cef and need to be launched without delay in order to make the most of the seven-year budget. for a long time now we have acknowledged that the need for substantial investment in the european energy infrastructure is a precondition for the completion of the single european market. this will, in turn, improve the eu’s competitiveness and bring economic recovery in europe as well as more growth and jobs, while better connecting people and businesses. all these points have been acknowedged and agreed by parliament, by the commission and by the council. this is why parliament was surprised and disappointed at the severe budget cuts decided by the european council on the cef during the negotiations on the mff. while i agree that savings are necessary in the current context, i wonder how the council plans to relaunch the european economy by undermining its only growth instruments and, even worse, by reverting to the same old formula of grant-only allocation. the cef is an opportunity to be innovative and can maximise scarce resources thanks to the leverage effects of this financial instrument. i deeply deplore the member states’ conservative approach of capping the use of such instruments, thereby stripping the cef of all innovation and effectiveness. this will mean fewer projects that will be financed with less money; this is not what we really want. in any case, with a 60% cut in the energy part of the cef we will have to rethink our priorities accordingly when allocating these funds. we cannot pretend that all projects in all member states will be financeable. parliament intends to take its responsibilities as co-legislator seriously, and to stand united on its prerogative to negotiate with both the council and the commission on these priorities.
the new regulation is a notable initiative, as it aims to unify and simplify the framework for financing trans-european energy infrastructure. the connecting europe facility financial instruments are of particular importance in this context. romania will thus benefit from european funds for the promotion and implementation of national strategic projects. for the application of the new regulation, my country will be eligible for european financial aid for projects of common interest. nabucco and agri are two strategic projects in which romania is involved, and are also projects of common interest for the whole union. we are looking to ensure energy independence. in this regard, i hope that in june, the shah deniz consortium will choose nabucco to transport gas from the caspian sea basin to europe.
in writing. the ten-t regulation is important in achieving the objective of all member states having a level of interconnection equivalent to 10% of their installed generation capacity. the drawing up of the lists of projects of common interest according to the contribution of each project to the implementation of energy corridors should take into account the member states whose territory is affected by the project. it is important that if a proposal for a cross-border project meets the criteria but is supported by only one of the member states involved, the decision is delegated to the commission. the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer) has an important role to play in electricity and gas projects, but i believe that acer should take into account the results of the analyses carried out by entso for electricity and gas. the entso shall assist in market and network modelling, cost-benefit analysis of projects of common interest, taking into account the socio-economic benefits of energy infrastructure at regional level. when financial support is granted to a project of common interest, it must be verified that there are no harmful consequences for other commercially viable projects. all of these should contribute to security of supply, including through diversification of sources, partners and supply routes.
i would like to recall a few conditions which i consider to be a priority for the union's energy perspective. first, energy regulations in the member states must take account of the provisions on the liberalisation of energy markets and aim, as a matter of priority, at removing the obstacles to the integration of energy markets. we need to put more value on regional energy capacity. a concrete example: in the western region of romania there are important geothermal energy resources, unused due to bureaucratic obstacles. i call on the commission and the competent national authorities to jointly examine the possibility of overcoming the obstacles to investment in geothermal energy. the development of own generation capacity and regional and cross-border transmission networks can ensure low energy consumption costs. imported gas energy resources can be diversified both by continuing investment in the south european corridor and by creating the complementary lng tron in the black sea.
in writing. the draft resolution refers to the need to accelerate investments in biofuels from agricultural waste. the potential of this field is huge. agricultural crop residues, usually left in the field, could generate over €30 billion a year for the european economy. the benefits would not only be in the supply of energy but also in the revitalization of the agricultural sector, with this waste representing a real source of income for farmers. it could also create almost a million jobs over the next ten years. the union should draw inspiration from the system in place since 2009 in the united states of america, where under the assistance programme payments of up to usd 45 per tonne of harvested dry biomass are provided. the reform of the european agricultural policy, on which we will be voting for the first time on wednesday, also deals with the use of farm waste for energy production, which i consider to be particularly important.
in writing. i welcome the european union's firm stance that european energy policy must respond to the need to prevent the negative effects of climate change. to prevent european firms' competitiveness from being damaged by the increased costs of this european energy policy, the european union must act with the same energy so that the world's major economies - china, india, russia, brazil - adopt policies in the same direction.
in writing. given the context in which the stress tests were carried out, i consider the questions raised by amalia sartori to be welcome. we need clear commitments from the commission on the nuclear industry. the public needs more security and confidence that the authorities are doing all that is necessary to prevent nuclear disasters. in addition to the disastrous accident at fukushima in japan, stress tests last year found that, to date, some countries have not implemented the nuclear safeguards agreed after the three mile island and chernobyl accidents. it is clear that we need binding legislation in the union on nuclear insurance and liability and that this legislation needs to be implemented as a matter of urgency. even though the legal responsibility for the nuclear safety and security of nuclear installations lies with the member states, the commission must ensure that national authorities take all necessary measures to protect the public.
reducing greenhouse gas emissions is one of the main elements of the european initiative. the union shall regularly monitor emissions and removals for those gases through its monitoring mechanism. i welcome the commission's proposal to improve the union rules on this mechanism. the development of climate change instruments should also be facilitated. one such instrument is the greenhouse gas emission trading scheme. after six years of romania's participation in the eu ets, the scheme covers almost 12 000 carbon dioxide-emitting installations. it is an important step towards achieving the ambitious target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 20% by 2020.
in writing. the european union has committed itself, in the eu 2020 strategy and through the energy and climate change legislative package, to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 20% below 1990 levels by 2020. the establishment of common european rules on accounting, monitoring and reporting of land use, land use change and forestry will also be an important step towards achieving these objectives, and i support the rapporteur's position on the consideration of land use practices in the union's climate change policy. by implementing these provisions, europe seeks to take into account the positive contribution of greenhouse gas storage in wood and wood products to the wider use of forests as a resource in a sustainable forest management framework, and to increase the use of wood products.
in writing. land use change is a potential major source of carbon emissions, but effective monitoring of this process can provide ways to adapt to and mitigate the effects of climate change. a welcome development is that this agreement clarifies the absence of any obligations imposed on private operators and, in particular, farmers. the agricultural sector is already facing a complicated administrative burden related to the cap and it is important that no additional obligations are imposed on farmers. farmers should be paid fairly for their work and their essential role in food production, and not waste their energy and time filling out forms. this agreement follows the international negotiations on land use change. the european union is committed to supporting developing countries in their efforts to adapt to and mitigate the effects of climate change. a continuous evaluation mechanism is needed to verify the performance in reducing emissions. by developing a comprehensive monitoring mechanism, we can improve international cooperation and encourage an effective global climate change policy without subjecting those working in agriculture to unnecessary additional effort.
romania has received a roadmap for joining the schengen area. it has met those demands, investing both european money and its own budget of over 1.3 billion euros. by 2012, romania also made efforts to respond to political demands from some member states. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the amount of the aid granted to the beneficiaries. unfortunately, the government of that time, the same one that exists today, through political actions directed against the rule of law, showed that the reforms implemented can be reversed and cancelled that solution. the non-european attitude of some leaders of the socialist-liberal governing coalition has put romania in a situation without a clear perspective on joining the schengen area. the december 2012 european council requested the jha council to resume discussions; meeting last week, it postponed the resumption of discussions to december 2013. the reasons given are: the level of corruption, deviations from the rule of law, the situation in the judiciary, the existence in the government of ministers under criminal investigation. i believe that it is necessary to involve the european commission, through the means made available by the cvm, in order to normalize the situation in romania, so that in december 2013 a decision is taken for the benefit of the romanian citizens.
in the recent period, several romanian politicians have argued that romania has a well-developed system for the protection of minorities and that therefore the guarantee of the rights of national minorities in the country cannot be expected. allow me to contradict the government's propaganda of success in this regard. progress has been made over the last 20 years, but there is a wide gap between the normative situation in the legislation and the reality. thanks to the persistent work of the rmdsz, among other things, the right to use the mother tongue has been enshrined in law, but it is still lacking in its relations with public institutions. in recent times, several of our mayors have been punished by the state authorities for trying to enforce the law and for requiring knowledge of the hungarian language. in the western half of europe, the demands and rights of indigenous national minorities were addressed through a system of autonomy, and this would be the example to be followed in the new member states. then perhaps we, the people concerned, could report on the exemplary minority policy.
romania and bulgaria have fulfilled all the criteria laid down in the treaty for accession to the schengen area. the technical reports have proven this. unfortunately, unfavourable conditions in advance are standing in the way of the fundamental right to free movement. the double standard that some states use to stir up populist sentiments among voters is extremely dangerous. firstly, because it causes distrust in the union's ability to respect its own rules, and secondly because it makes romanian and bulgarian citizens the scapegoats of europe. we all remember the horrors of the last dark period of extremism in europe. the members of the council should act responsibly, not seek to divide the union between first-class and second-class citizens. romania and bulgaria want to cooperate for a european future, but to do so, they need real dialogue partners.
the romanian government is currently working on a draft law to reduce the support scheme for the renewable energy industry. in the context of today's debate in the european parliament on greenhouse gas emissions reductions, i strongly urge a prudent and balanced approach in the formulation of this proposal, given the impact that the formulation of the scheme to support investment in renewable energy may have on the energy system. predictability and legal certainty for investors are needed so that the change does not have the effect of stagnating the sector or stopping investments. at the same time, the loss of competitiveness of romanian industry and the energy poverty of consumers must be counteracted. the estimates show that in 2016-2017 final consumers could pay up to 30% more for energy. the objective must therefore be to make green energy self-sustainable and to help the final consumer to benefit from green energy. the revision of the legislation is a necessity. there is also a transparent public debate on this issue.
the union remains the largest donor of assistance to poor countries. however, unfortunately, the budget allocated to the european development fund for the period 2014-2020 has decreased by 11%, which will hamper the union's efforts in this area. eradicating poverty and achieving the millennium development goals must remain a priority in the union's external action. in the current context, more efficient use of the european development fund and the use of aid for the world's poorest countries will be needed, and the allocation of 20% of the total for health and education infrastructure is very important. the inclusion of the fund in the union budget as from 2021 may also lead to greater consistency in the use of aid and to a reduction in administrative expenditure.
although formally not part of the union's territory, the overseas countries and territories are of particular strategic importance. the renewal of the association framework is essential for both sides. this will help to strengthen competitiveness and reduce the vulnerability of the territories. in cooperation with the union, the focus will be on sectors that generate economic growth in those areas, such as tourism and agriculture. strong support will also be needed for the fisheries sector in the territories concerned, in particular in the fight against illegal fishing and coastal management. last but not least, the aid provided should ensure better integration into regional economies, but also promote cooperation with other partners. however, all measures will have to be adapted to the specificities and diversity of these areas.
rapporteur for the opinion, committee on legal affairs. - i would like to thank the two rapporteurs, ms róża thun and, in particular, mr louis grech, with whom i have cooperated very effectively. i would also like to thank the council for its efforts to adopt this extremely important directive as soon as possible. in order to guarantee consumer confidence in alternative dispute resolution procedures, we need minimum standards at european level. first, the persons responsible for adr need to have the necessary expertise and experience. secondly - and this is one of the most important aspects - the independence and impartiality of the dispute resolution personnel must be ensured. in my view, the compromise reached with the council is a pragmatic one, because it sets out clear criteria of impartiality and independence, strict obligations of transparency, and allows the maintenance of the existing alternative solution bodies. i hope it will have the unanimous support of parliament and that the member states will transpose it as soon as possible in the interests of european consumers.

blue-card answer. – it is actually rather easy, mr brons. if crimes are committed, they are not committed by race, they are committed by individuals, so whenever you want to penalise, you penalise the individual. at the same time, when another individual commits a crime because he or she does not agree with the fact that a person is different, this must be penalised and of course it must have an even bigger penalty.
in writing. since the beginning of the financial crisis, the attention of national and european authorities has been focused on economic and austerity policies, while the defence of the union's core values, such as fundamental rights, solidarity and social peace, has been neglected. today we can see the disastrous effects of this neglect. racist, xenophobic, anti-semitic and nationalist rhetoric and demonstrations have proliferated and have been promoted not only by extremist parties but also by leading political figures and movements. by far the ugliest and most discriminated community in europe is the roma. the european strategy of 2011 has not produced any results. therefore, i believe that it needs to be revised and improved, especially to address and recognise the phenomenon of racism against roma and to strengthen the role of local authorities in inclusion policies. i also want to point out that xenophobia and racism affect not just certain ethnic groups but entire nations. i am referring in particular to the romanians and bulgarians, who continue to be treated in many european countries as second-class citizens, who should not have access to basic rights such as freedom of movement and work, which is unacceptable.
in writing. − one of the major challenges facing europe today is the provision of sustainable, competitive and secure energy. despite recent progress, rising energy prices and dependence on imported energy, insufficient integration of the internal energy market, energy isolation of certain geographical areas and limited access to diversified energy sources still pose obstacles to a secure and competitive energy market. the new regulation on guidelines for trans-european energy infrastructures proposes to accelerate the completion of the internal energy market and the achievement of eu energy policy objectives, in order to reduce emissions and combat climate change by modernising and interconnecting energy networks. i believe this initiative is important in establishing a solid and ambitious framework for designing an energy policy adapted to our future needs.
in writing. − each eu member state has an energy mix that is determined by geographical, technological and energy policy conditions as well as national needs. it consists of a core load sector, which is continuously fed by fossil, nuclear and hydroelectric resources and a part of renewable energy. since the share of electricity from renewable sources could more than double between 2007 and 2020, i believe that it is no longer enough to think in national categories. the construction and expansion of transnational networks is imperative to meet the growing demand for electricity, to promote market integration, to maintain the security of the networks, to transport electricity produced from renewable sources and to compensate for fluctuations. it can also make an indispensable contribution to achieving energy efficiency objectives.
in writing. − trans-european energy infrastructure plays a key role in meeting the climate and energy policy objectives set by the commission. i believe that this proposal will lead to the modernisation and development of crossborder energy networks within the eu, which are necessary to ensure the future and energy security of the continent and to be able to deal with new challenges in this field. these challenges are associated with increasing demand for electricity, finding new ways to secure the transport of electricity produced by natural renewable processes and compensating for energy fluctuations. increasing energy efficiency depends on overcoming these challenges.
in writing. − europe needs faster, more decisive and concerted action to ensure a global perspective and a considerable level of interdependence between member states on energy infrastructure. better integration of the internal energy market, the removal of the energy isolation of certain geographical areas, better access to diversified energy sources are needed to ensure energy security and with tangible effects for consumers and businesses in terms of prices and sustainability.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is a key step in accelerating the completion of the internal market and in achieving the energy market and climate objectives. the european energy policy sets clear targets for 2020: a 20% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, a 20% share of energy from renewable sources in final energy consumption, a 20% increase in energy efficiency. for the european market to provide energy in a sustainable, safe and secure way, we need to move beyond the false national context of 'self-sufficient' and 'independent' and create synergies. i believe that this report fulfils this mission by defining nine geographical corridors and three priority thematic areas and by establishing rules for identifying projects of common interest, and by establishing the 'single national framework' for project acceleration and monitoring. on the basis of the proposal, projects of common interest will be allocated on the basis of a cost-benefit analysis. the same will apply to the allocation of investment costs according to the cross-border area where the benefits arise, thus providing incentives for high-risk projects and establishing eligibility conditions for financial assistance through the connecting europe facility.
in writing. − the european union must act as soon as possible to secure its energy future and protect its interests in this area. to this end, the role of trans-european energy infrastructures is critical in ensuring that the energy targets set are achieved to the highest standards. i therefore believe that the european union must make every effort to support the member states in complying with the guidelines set at community level and, most importantly, provide substantial financial support for the development of large-scale crossborder projects. that is why i want to express my dissatisfaction with the council's decision to reduce the budget allocated to the connecting europe facility from eur 50 billion to eur 29 billion. this mechanism, designed to replace the current ten funding regulation, was to be a very important resource for the member states, but with this budget, i doubt we will ever be able to achieve the objectives proposed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the current environmental impact assessment (eia) directive is flawed and needs to be improved. the case of vienna airport proved this. the approach to dealing with complaints from complainants about breaches of community law needs to be reviewed and the shortcomings identified by the ombudsman need to be addressed. therefore, an appropriate ex-post eim is necessary to allow a full evaluation of the implemented projects. the review of the directive should also include requirements relating to the objectivity and impartiality of the competent authorities in order to avoid any conflict of interest. the inquiry should serve as a model for similar cases or procedures that we may face in the future.
i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the land use sector needs to be gradually but effectively integrated into the union's climate policy. i support the rapporteur in her decision to bring the report into line with the conclusions of the durban convention. the sector absorbs the equivalent of 9% of greenhouse gases emitted in other parts of the economy. in line with the europe 2020 targets, my country has committed to reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by 20% by 2020. romania also agreed to increase the share of renewable energy in the national energy mix to 24%. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the romanian electricity market is in a situation of serious difficulties.
in writing. − land and forest management can mitigate or exacerbate climate change. forests and agricultural land make up over three quarters of europe's landscape. while the eu's greenhouse gas emissions come mainly from energy production and other anthropogenic sources, some emissions are offset by the uptake of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere through photosynthesis and storage in trees and other plants, soil, biomass and timber. in view of the above, i believe that there is a need for appropriate land use and management practices in forestry and agriculture that can lead to both the limitation of greenhouse gas emissions and the enhancement of removals from the atmosphere.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to include lulucf (land use, land use change and forestry) in the eu's climate policy. accounting for emissions from lulucf is a key step in supporting the european union's efforts to mitigate the effects of climate change and to meet the targets set out in the europe 2020 strategy, as well as to meet commitments made to the international community under the kyoto protocol and the united nations framework convention on climate change. the european union must 'lead by example' in tackling the effects of climate change, and this report can help to build such an example.
in writing. − the way we use land and forests is certainly contributing to climate change mitigation or exacerbation. the application of appropriate land use and management practices in forestry and agriculture can help to limit greenhouse gas emissions and enhance removals. therefore, the lulucf sector (land use, land use change and forestry) needs to be increasingly integrated into the european union's climate change policy. the proposed accounting rules for lulucf cover a significant gap in greenhouse gas inventories at the level of the european union, thus strengthening the environmental integrity of the eu's climate change policy. all economic sectors must contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. solid accounting standards for emissions and removals from lulucf activities are the first step towards achieving this objective. rigorous and harmonised accounting within lulucf will certainly contribute to biodiversity conservation, soil protection and adaptation to climate change.
in writing. − tackling climate change is crucial for development, avoiding natural disasters and eradicating poverty. that is why we need to increase monitoring of greenhouse gas emissions from land use, land use change and forestry. in this respect, i support the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on accounting rules and action plans for greenhouse gas emissions and removals, because it is necessary for member states to account for emissions and also report them.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on accounting rules for land use, land use change and forestry (lulucf) because it is a coherent and necessary measure in efforts to make sustainable use of natural resources. the achievement of the objectives set by the european union in the framework of the eu 2020 strategy and of energy and climate policy cannot be achieved without a robust system of accounting rules for emissions and removals from lulucf activities. as parties to the united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc) and the kyoto protocol, member states and the european union have obligations to comply with the convention. the report puts these obligations into practice and ensures that climate policy is consistent with existing eu legislation, namely the common agricultural policy (cap) and the renewable energy directive.
in writing. − i believe that there is a need for rigorous accounting rules applicable to the lulucf sector. however, as with any new administrative burden, we have an obligation to keep bureaucracy to a minimum. member states have a wide range of administrative obligations, which arise from regulations adopted at european level, and we need to balance the benefits of these obligations (in this case, accounting and reporting activities) with the costs they impose.
in writing. − tools to monitor the impact of climate change mitigation actions are a prerequisite for effective greenhouse gas emission reduction strategies. the unequivocal identification of the environmental status at a given time can provide the directions for action that can lead to the achievement of the emission reduction targets set at national, european and international level. i welcome the proposals to optimise and improve eu rules on reporting and monitoring of emissions, as they will strengthen the union's negotiating position in the international conferences concerned and reassert its role in the field of climate change. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report to improve the existing legislation on the mechanism for reporting and monitoring greenhouse gases. the proposed legislative changes will lead to more accurate data reporting, which means that a more accurate assessment of where member states are in achieving the barometers set and assumed by international climate change agreements will be possible. at the same time, i support the commission's proposal to keep the reporting requirements at national level and not to collect additional data from industry and smes. another positive aspect of this proposal is the increased transparency of the data reported.
in writing. − the challenges of climate change require ambitious targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. achieving these objectives requires new monitoring and reporting requirements that provide reliable and accurate data in a timely manner. the union and the member states should endeavour to provide the most up-to-date information on greenhouse gas emissions, in particular in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. the existing greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions monitoring and reporting system (gems) needs to be improved and updated to support the effective implementation of the european union's climate change policies. the monitoring and reporting system shall ensure the transparency, accuracy, consistency, comparability and completeness of greenhouse gas inventories. but in order to have an effective monitoring and reporting system it is important to avoid adding to the administrative and financial burden already borne by member states. the european environment agency has an important role to play in developing and implementing coherent methodologies and in supporting member states in the transparent and accurate monitoring of actual and expected progress.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report to reassure citizens that the european union is delivering on its commitments to combat pollution. to this end, it is necessary to improve the existing mechanisms for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions. rapid, reliable data and transparency in reporting greenhouse gas emissions are useful in the process of developing sound climate policies.
in writing. − member states need to improve the timeliness, transparency and comparability of their greenhouse gas emissions reporting. this is a key condition for seeing that the union and its member states are on track to meet the proposed targets and to develop new sound policies to address climate challenges.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is an improved version of the current legislation on reporting and monitoring of greenhouse gas emissions. the proposals aim to optimise and improve the legislative framework and ensure timely and reliable data on eu and member state developments in the timetable for achieving climate objectives. the provision of transparent and complex information will increase the union's credibility vis-à-vis its developing partners. i welcome the inclusion of the shipping sector in the eu's emissions reduction targets and, not least, the retention of the provisions in the old mechanism on the collection of data from smes and industry.
in writing. − i welcome the report by mr eickhout as it definitely brings us one step nearer towards achieving our targets and living up to the international commitments regarding climate change.
a european platform for out-of-court dispute resolution of disputes between consumers and traders arising from the cross-border sale of goods and services online can have beneficial effects for consumers and traders, who will be able to resolve conflicts with speed and minimum costs, for online transactions as a modern form of trade, and for the european union, which can thus provide safeguards at european level, which is likely to increase the confidence of european citizens in europe and in the efficiency of european mechanisms. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
i voted in favour of the report, given that european citizens often prefer not to report disputes because of the difficult settlement procedures. by buying goods and services cross-border and online, european citizens can get good prices, but there have been multiple reports of problems with the quality of products or their delivery. in 2010, one in five union consumers experienced problems when purchasing goods or services in the single market and this situation has not yet improved substantially. i support the rapporteur and believe that the online dispute resolution platform is an effective way to address the shortcomings. with its help, we will be able to avoid difficult and costly legal proceedings and consumer compensation will be facilitated.
in writing. − the establishment of a free european platform for online dispute resolution, available in all the official languages of the union, is a key instrument for the efficient resolution of disputes between consumers and traders arising from the purchase of goods and services online. this platform has the potential to ensure that all consumer complaints can be submitted to an adr entity and thus consumers will see their complaint resolved much faster than before a court of common law. i believe that the possibility of online dispute resolution will encourage european consumers to buy goods or services online and in other member states than their own, thus ensuring that they can take full advantage of the free movement of goods and services in the eu.
in writing. - i voted for this report because the european single market needs transparent alternative solutions to resolve consumer disputes and litigation. this system will make it possible to solve problems involving the sale of goods or the provision of services throughout the european union in a simpler, cheaper and faster way. i support this report because the eu must continue its efforts to ensure a high level of consumer protection throughout europe.
in writing. − the development of the single market at european level has allowed eu citizens to travel, shop and pay without restrictions, and the digital dimension of the internal market is now vital for consumers and traders alike. in order to have a complete digital internal market, existing barriers need to be removed and consumer confidence needs to be increased. i believe that the establishment of a reliable and efficient online dispute resolution system can contribute greatly to this increase in consumer confidence in the union.
in writing. − i salute this report as it represents an important step forward to encourage e-commerce and to make both consumers and traders more confident of developing transactions online. it is especially reassuring for small traders and consumers to know that they will find support in the event of a problem through an online dispute resolution system.
unfortunately, we find that many consumers and traders are not aware of, or do not have sufficient information about, the use of alternative dispute resolution mechanisms. i too argue that ensuring access to simple, efficient, fast and inexpensive ways of resolving disputes, at national and crossborder level, arising from the sale of goods or the provision of services would benefit consumers and therefore strengthen their confidence in the market. this access should exist for both online and offline transactions and is particularly important when consumers shop abroad. in this context, providing citizens with accurate and clear information on how to access adr entities is of crucial importance.
i voted in favour of the report because many consumers face problems when buying goods or services in the single market. the regulation on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes should increase their confidence. today, the use of the internet for shopping is increasing, but many consumers and merchants are hesitant to buy or sell online because of fears that disputes will not be resolved. although they exist in several member states, salw still present shortcomings. therefore, all member states must ensure that such entities exist in all business sectors and that they are accessible and effective. it is estimated that this could save consumers some eur 22.5 billion a year.
in writing. − alternative dispute resolution offers citizens the opportunity to have their complaints resolved more quickly, cheaper and in a simplified manner than if they had to go to the ordinary courts. when it comes to the purchase of goods or services, it is essential that all consumers benefit from those benefits and therefore have the possibility to bring complaints before alternative dispute resolution entities for consumer disputes (adr entities). that is why i support the proposal for a directive. it has the merit of ensuring that, throughout the european union, all citizens will benefit from a high degree of protection when they shop online or offline, nationally or across borders. i believe that the introduction of safeguards for the independence and impartiality of the persons responsible for these entities adds value to this directive, because it gives credibility and therefore encourages consumers to use their services. a significant improvement on the current situation is that traders are required to inform consumers about the adr entities to which they can turn, both on their websites and in the general terms and conditions of contracts or in other applicable areas.
in writing. − i support the creation of a european-wide online dispute resolution platform for consumers and traders, which will allow for the resolution of disputes in an effective and fast manner, thus avoiding the difficult and costly legal processes. this platform will also increase the confidence of our citizens in e-commerce and help reduce online fraud.
in writing. − i welcome the proposal on alternative consumer dispute resolution. more and more eu citizens buy their goods online and many of these transactions take place across borders. the increased numbers of consumers that experience problems when buying online justifies the development of an improved mediation mechanism; a mechanism that will help to fill the gaps in coverage for consumers and help to regain consumer confidence in cross-border e-commerce.

in writing. − ensuring high standards of drinking water quality has in recent years taken on an increasingly important role in eu policy-making, due to the close link between water, the environment and human health. consistency of legislation in this area is essential to meet the challenges of water pollution, which is why i believe radionuclides should be treated like any other carcinogenic contaminant and therefore monitored accordingly. in order to make this possible, i support the rapporteur's proposal to amend the legal basis of the commission's proposal. the adoption of the 'polluter pays' principle to determine who bears the cost of sampling and monitoring in the event of contamination from human activities is an appropriate choice in this context. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted for the report because i believe it is extremely important to ensure the quality of drinking water and to protect people's health. contamination of water with radioactive substances should be monitored. even if there is a council directive that imposes requirements in relation to the control of the titrate and the total indicative dose, this is not implemented by the member states. therefore, it is necessary to amend the legal basis and the proposal must contain all sources of natural and man-made radioactivity, as well as all types of exposed groups, in particular by age. the 'polluter pays' principle should also be introduced in the case of man-made pollution and the methods of controlling pollutants should also be strengthened. and information on water quality must be transparent and accessible to citizens.
in writing. − radioactive contamination of water is to be considered, mainly as a result of internal exposure due to absorption and fixation of radionuclides in the body. alongside natural sources of radioactive contamination, massive human-made sources of radioactive water pollution have emerged over the last 60 years, from atmospheric and underwater nuclear testing to the systematic dumping of radioactive waste into seas and oceans, radioactive waters, and nuclear reactors with an expired life. all of this poses a risk to european citizens and i believe that for legal certainty and the coherence of union legislation on drinking water quality, radionuclides must be treated in the same way as any other carcinogenic contaminant, in order to take into account the cumulative impact of the adverse effects of the different contaminants.
in writing. − ensuring safe drinking water for european citizens is a key concern of human health and environmental protection policies. it is important for the consistency of union legislation on drinking water quality that radionuclides are treated in the same way as any other carcinogenic contaminant in order to take into account the cumulative impact of the adverse effects of the different contaminants. in order to ensure a high level of protection of public health, it is necessary to establish common quality standards for water intended for human consumption with indicator function and to ensure monitoring of compliance with those standards. it is also necessary to distinguish between radioactivity from natural sources and radioactivity from the normal operation of nuclear installations (artificial radiation and/or radiation from human activities) in order to protect public health in europe. natural radiation levels and contamination from human activities need to be managed differently according to different criteria. member states should ensure that nuclear activities do not lead to contamination of drinking water resources. the polluter pays principle should also be respected in relation to the cost of sampling and monitoring in the event of artificial contamination and the monitoring of contaminants should be strengthened.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report to guarantee the citizens of the european union access to drinking water free of radioactive contamination. the authorities responsible for monitoring water must be as careful as possible in their controls, both to protect the environment and the health of the european consumer. in addition, the public should be informed as soon as possible in the event of contamination.
in writing. − the commission proposal defines clearly and explicitly the basic safety rules for the protection of the health of the general public against the dangers of ionising radiation, with reference to radioactive substances in drinking water. i support this proposal because it provides certainty as to the radiological quality of the water supplied by the distribution systems. i would make one comment: in my view, the long-lived radionuclides of polonium (po-210) and lead (pb-210) should be included in the definition of the total indicative dose (tid). this suggestion should be re-examined in the light of future technologies.
in writing. − i totally supported this report given the importance of monitoring radioactive substances in water intended for human consumption. in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety we agreed to make this legislation more consistent with the objective of protecting public health, and therefore we decided that it is necessary to change the legal base from the euratom treaty to the treaty on the functioning of the european union.

in a european union with a diversified agriculture, a common dimension applied to all member states was tried. but in order to be able to talk about competitiveness, about support for agriculture for all member states, to be able to respond to the current challenges of food security and food security or climate change, we must support a convergence mechanism that better reflects the principle of fairness in the level of payments per hectare, to impose a fair and objective redesign, accepted by all member states, that allows the reduction of the discrepancies in direct payments at european level. a fair, fair, greener common agricultural policy, attractive to those who want to invest in agriculture, favourable to young people and women, a common agricultural policy which supports the rural dimension, covered by an appropriate budget, which does not tolerate a reduction, is part of what millions of farmers are waiting for. the vote on the negotiating mandates tomorrow shows that the european parliament is capable of providing solutions, that we are prepared to support agriculture at european level.
there's an agricultural expression that says, "where there are four farmers, there are five opinions". and on the reform of european agriculture, there are, indeed, divided opinions. i prefer to see the positive side first. simplified schemes for small farmers will support many households. secondly, support for young farmers is essential: without young people not only agriculture will disappear, but the village world itself. in romania, for example, a third of farmers are over 70 years old and only 1% are under 30. last but not least, i would add as another positive aspect, the strengthening of farmers' organisations. however, the texts we are voting on tomorrow are disappointing in terms of the convergence between subsidies granted in the eastern european countries and those received by farmers in western europe. parliament started this reform with generous principles, such as the principle of fairness or objective criteria. unfortunately, those principles were lost along the way. budgetary constraints are one argument: new member states receive more money, but the gaps are still too wide. however, i am optimistic about the future of agriculture in romania and the development opportunities offered by the new common agricultural policy.
tomorrow we will vote on a reform with very ambitious goals, but unfortunately with a budget far below what we expected. i hope that these budget cuts will not lead to a renationalisation of the common agricultural policy which will maintain the so-called two-speed european agriculture, because the stronger states will have more opportunities to support their own farmers. remarkably, however, for the first time, more attention is being given to small farmers, who are being relieved of bureaucratic burdens by a special program. i also appreciate that the new cap promotes more sustainable farming and that organic farming enjoys more substantial support. i would like to thank commissioner ciolos for his support and attention to these matters. the common agricultural policy must ensure that the vitality of rural areas is maintained by facilitating the generational change so necessary at this time. that's why the young farmers program should be mandatory in all states.
in writing. the common agricultural policy has played and continues to play a key role in the european union's policies and budget. the cap reform will introduce new elements that will support and lead to the creation of a fairer, more sustainable and more open model of agriculture for the diversity of our rural areas. the cap reform examines, among other things, the distribution of the agricultural budget equally between new and old member states, reducing red tape, a fair distribution of direct payments, increasing transparency on aid to farmers, encouraging farmers to adopt green methods, ensuring a fair price for farmers and the eu's position in the global competitive market. a valuable aspect of this proposal is the encouragement of young people to take up farming and to open a farm, given that youth unemployment has reached as high as 50% in some member states. at the same time, this proposal will lead to a strengthening of the position of farmers in the supply chain. all these measures will lead to greater stability for farmers and food security for the general public. the vote by parliament is a first step towards an agreement on a reformed, ambitious and pragmatic common agricultural policy.
unfortunately, this solution penalizes only some of the member states, including romania. i would point out that my country is discriminated against by the larger states of the union. such a reform should have proposed a sustainable system of distribution of mandates to each state. the number of mandates would thus not change each time a country becomes a member of the union. in the future, a formula will have to be identified that no longer affects only certain countries. also, the verification of demographic data will be very important, especially since in romania, in the 2011 census, many people were not even censused. thus, there was a difference of over 1 million people between the statistical estimates and the preliminary census data.
member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members of the european parliament, good evening to everybody. i have the honour to address you in the name of the commission and in particular in the name of my colleague, algirdas semeta, who is responsible for this file. the objective of the proposed regulation on esa 2010 is to revise, update and improve the current european system of accounts, esa 95, in line with the recently updated international system of national accounts. it reflects the need for comparable high quality and up to date macroeconomic aggregates for the member states. this revision is a major project which will set up the national account standards for many years. at a european level, the esa is an essential tool for national accounts data used for major administrative purposes such as own resources, excessive deficit procedure and structural funds, and for the analysis of the coordination and convergence of member states’ economic policies. the revision of the esa has been based on a wide consultation of the national accounts experts and of users and producers of statistics in europe. we consider that the proposal is well-balanced in terms of user data needs and of the burden put on respondents and administrations. following fruitful discussions, a compromise text was agreed between the european parliament and the council with the aim of reaching agreement at first reading. we definitely support the compromise text, because it enables the commission to obtain the required data for its policies and to exercise its monitoring tasks, even if recital 16 includes elements that we consider as deviating from the common understanding of the european parliament, the council and the commission on delegated acts. the commission would therefore clearly state that it is of the view that article 290 of the treaty is to be interpreted as meaning that it is autonomous in the preparation and adoption of delegated acts. the standard recital on expert advice contained in the common understanding agreed between the three institutions is a reflection of that interpretation. the commission therefore regrets that recital 16 deviates from the common understanding. i would wholeheartedly like to thank the rapporteur, ms sharon bowles, for her deep involvement and a constructive approach to the proposal. thanks to an excellent cooperation between the three institutions, i believe that we have reached our common objective of setting up a very robust framework for harmonised and reliable national accounts data on which european union institutions, governments and economic and social operators can base their decisions. the commission will now concentrate its efforts on preparing the application of esa 2010, monitoring the full implementation by the member states of the agreed new framework so that the required statistical data are truly available and fulfilling its own reporting obligations to the european parliament and the council in this context. the commission is also very much looking forward to pursuing a fruitful dialogue with the committee on economic and monetary affairs and the european parliament, which is essential for the availability of high quality, transparent and trustworthy national accounts and other macroeconomic statistics for the benefit of sound policy making and of society at large.
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, first of all i would like to thank ms bowles for her excellent work on this report. we know very well what kind of problems we had with essential macroeconomic data reported by several countries: distorted budget deficits, hidden liabilities and lack of rules for reporting contingent liabilities. we need more transparent and accurate data and rules that are more harmonised with those of the major trading partners. the report which we discussed today is the result of long but successful trialogue work and it responds to our request. therefore, my political group will support this report.
first of all, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his work and welcome the report, especially at a time when we find chemicals all around us in most of the goods we buy. as this report also points out, and as the world health organization supports, chemical pollutants affect the endocrine system, being one of the potential causes of the various diseases of this century - cancer, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. there are hundreds of substances in our environment, but we have insufficient information about them. real measures are needed to protect the most vulnerable groups of the population, including children and pregnant women. we should not ignore the negative impact of these substances on biodiversity either. i hope that together, by supporting this report, we will call on the commission to develop an ambitious and adequate eu strategy on endocrine disruptors.
researchers point out that endocrine disruptors are found in most of the items we use, from plastic items, tin cans, water bottles, clothing, cosmetics, to baby bottles and medical equipment. exposure to such substances increases the risk of birth defects in pregnant women. i consider that protecting women against the possible risks presented by endocrine disruptors to their reproductive health is of the utmost importance. on the other hand, there is a need for long-term monitoring studies of women's health at european level to assess the long-term and multi-generational effects of exposure to endocrine disruptors. as such, i support the rapporteur's proposal to give priority to funding research into the effects of endocrine disruptors on women's health.
the number of endocrine diseases has increased considerably in recent years. they mainly affect the reproductive system. one of the major causes is endocrine disruptors, which can be found in the composition of many materials and products that we use every day. it is important to identify the disturbances that affect human and animal health. however, animal testing should be kept to a minimum. we also need to focus on protecting groups more sensitive to external factors, such as children, young people and women of childbearing age. therefore, i support activities to reduce exposure to disruptors and to manage chemicals that are harmful to health. i believe that horizon 2020 will be able to facilitate research in laboratories and promote innovation in this field.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs. − i drafted the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs on the integration of migrants. the opinion highlights the impact of the integration of migrants on the union's relations with its external partners. we have thus underlined the need to standardise migration and mobility dialogues, recommended the establishment of mobility partnerships with third countries and, where this is not possible, common agendas for migration and mobility. i also said that it was essential to introduce a standard social security clause. the opinion encourages the european union to set an example in the portability of social rights and to promote the coordination of social security with other regions of the world within the wto. moreover, the opinion highlights the benefits that circular migration can bring when it comes to relations with third countries and especially in post-conflict situations, when the diaspora can support the reconstruction of the home country. finally, we stressed the need for cooperation with third countries to help them implement the common european asylum system.
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, i would like to thank the rapporteur, ms hirsch, and all the other shadows who worked on this report. today we know two facts very well: the union needs stability, growth and jobs, but the union is also ageing and it needs migrants. we need the best talents from everywhere to boost our research capabilities, innovation and competitiveness. if we need migrants, we also need a coherent immigration policy consistent with other european policies. our first goal is integrating migrants. the main pillars of this integration are giving migrants access to education and health programmes, and fair competition for obtaining jobs. there are a few concerns that i need to raise regarding the report. firstly, there is the convergence between the legal requirement of the posted workers directive, immigration policy in asylum-seeking, and the present subject. as long as the revision of the posted workers directive is still under discussion at this point in time, it is risk-avoidance to insert requests for legal modifications with respect to equal pay for the same job. this house is still deliberating the approach to be taken for the revision of this directive. additionally, one needs to consider the cost and benefits of linking immigration and asylum-seeking with the requirements presented by the hirsch report. we support a fair and competitive environment. however, we cannot forget the existing community clause, as well as the existing requirements for transitional barriers imposed on european workers. secondly, the immigration of migrants needs to be gradual in order to be effective and to counteract negative spillovers. i do not agree that migrants arriving in a host country should be granted all of the same rights as a citizen from the very beginning.

the ageing process at european level will cause a significant increase in labour force shortages in the coming decades. this shortage of more or less qualified staff can also be covered by integrating migrants, a large segment of whom are women, into the labour market in their countries of residence. they can play a very important role, because migrant women not only offer great potential for the labour market, but they often play an important role in educating children and transmitting standards and values. i believe that the member states and the commission must develop education and communication programmes to inform migrant women of their rights and responsibilities and take measures to significantly strengthen their legal and social position, to prevent any discrimination and to use their potential contribution to economic and social development.
i want to express my total disagreement with the cheap populism by which some parties, especially in certain countries, seek to gain political capital by adopting a political discourse based on the denigration of immigrants. how can we talk about their integration into the labour market when even immigrants from within the european union are treated with such contempt in the member states where they work? at a time when we have serious demographic problems and external economic competitiveness is suffering more than ever, i recommend that european governments take all necessary measures to integrate migrants and improve the coherence of economic, social, educational and healthcare policies, do their utmost to attract skilled workers to correct the labour market deficit, show wisdom by putting aside these political discourses that promote hatred of migrants and, instead, make known the positive effects of them on the european market.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, i would like to thank you on behalf of president barroso, under whose remit the cooperation and verification mechanism falls, for this opportunity to set out the commission’s approach to this measure. when romania and bulgaria joined the european union in 2007, the council recognised that certain weaknesses remained in the areas of judicial reform and corruption and – in the case of bulgaria – organised crime. the concern was that these weaknesses could prevent an effective application of european union laws, policies and programmes, and that they would prevent romanians and bulgarians from enjoying their full rights as european union citizens. the council therefore decided to set up the cvm: four benchmarks for romania and six benchmarks for bulgaria were set out to help the commission to chart progress. the commission has regularly reported on progress, making recommendations setting out where further measures are needed in the two member states. last summer, in the fifth year of the cvm, the commission decided to produce a longer-term assessment. these reports concluded that some of the key building blocks were in place, particularly in terms of laws and institutions, so the focus has shifted to filling the gaps: implementation and the ownership needed to maintain the momentum of reform. around the time of the july report, important questions were raised about the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary in romania. the commission made a number of specific recommendations to romania and undertook to look again at these issues at the end of the year. the report adopted in january made clear that romania had implemented several – but not all – of these recommendations. it made other recommendations on points where further progress is needed. the commission believes that the cvm has proved to be an effective driver of reform. it has had a tangible impact in supporting reform and many of its recommendations have inspired the positive steps taken in the two member states over the past five years. however, it has to be recognised that this is a process which often needs deep societal change. it is not realistic to expect quick results. of course, there have been some misgivings expressed in bulgaria and romania about the cvm process. this has not been helped by the tendency of some member states to make a political link between schengen and the cvm. i would like to underline here, once again, that the commission does not support this link. the schengen process has its own tools to assess readiness. the cvm is not designed to duplicate or replace these. i am pleased to know that the council has once again this week welcomed the commission’s methodology, its analysis and its recommendations. the commission’s conclusions on the cvm are firmly in the mainstream of european opinion; for example, many of the issues raised in the commission’s report have been echoed in the venice commission of the council of europe. most importantly, this work is recognised by bulgarians and romanians themselves. last summer the eurobarometer poll showed that clear majorities in both member states thought that the european union had an important role in addressing these issues and had a positive effect. over seven out of the ten in both also believed that the european union action should continue until they reached a standard comparable to that of other member states. the commission remains in close contact with the bulgarian and romanian authorities. we will produce our next reports towards the end of this year. we will also continue our close monitoring and ongoing dialogue to reinforce the process and the reforms, and to help the two member states to meet the objectives of the mechanism.
