member of the commission. − mr president, first of all let me, on behalf of the commission, convey our best wishes to vice-president papastamkos for a speedy and complete recovery. the commission wishes to thank mr berlinguer for his excellent report, which offers us the opportunity to relaunch the discussion, not only on the entrepreneurial aspects of mutual societies, but also on the more general issue of promoting the social-economic sector, within which the mutualist movement is a major player. it is for this reason that the communication on the social business initiative contains an action covering mutual societies and cooperatives. the available data show that mutual societies are as much an integral part of the market and economy of the european union as other enterprises such as public limited companies. moreover, the success enjoyed by cooperatives and mutual societies, in both economic and social terms, proves that incorporated companies are not the only type of enterprise to perform well on the european market. accordingly, the commission obviously shares the viewpoint set out in the report, namely that the mutualist model deserves to be promoted in europe. the commission has always held that the european economy would benefit if the mutualist movement were represented in all the member states’ markets, given that the mutualist model contributes to diversity in the types of enterprise – a vital feature of economic growth. as your report very clearly notes, there are in certain countries a series of legal and administrative obstacles that mutual societies have to overcome when seeking to act as cross-border entrepreneurs or even to form groups. the commission is keen to improve the environment in which mutual societies develop and it is for this reason that it has funded a study on the current situation of mutual societies in europe. this study lists a number of legal and political problems relating to the recognition of mutual societies in certain member states, and proposes solutions. one of the aspects the study examined in depth was the need to have a study for a european mutual society as a solution to the difficulties mutual societies face when wishing to extend their activities beyond their national frontiers. on this point, the study concluded that the statute had not been shown to be the only solution to the problems faced by mutual societies. the question that now arises is what measures other than the statute might the commission propose to allow mutual societies to develop, particularly in the countries where they are not sufficiently known or in which there is no legislation covering this type of enterprise. the results of the commission’s research have been displayed since november 2012 on the website of the directorate-general for enterprise and industry. this month, the commission launched a public consultation on the study’s recommendations. the text of the questionnaire, which is addressed to mutual society organisations, national authorities and any other interested parties wishing to participate, was drawn up in close collaboration with two brussels mutual associations in the field of insurance, health and provident funds. the commission cannot decide whether it should present a proposal for a regulation on the statute for a european mutual society or what the thrust of a new policy initiative should be until the results of these consultations are known. this will be at the beginning of the second quarter of this year.
mr president, this initiative report, which was supported almost unanimously in the committee on legal affairs, asks the commission to submit one or more proposals for creating a statute for european mutual societies that would apply at european and cross-border level. as ms thein said earlier, swiss societies operate in all but six member states – despite existing disparities in the formal requirements on setting-up, operating and winding-up – and are providing financial services like insurance, property management, banking and so on. hence, a european mutual society statute would establish a level playing field for mutuals in the single market. our committee made four recommendations. the first concerns the objectives of the statute for a european mutual society, which should include the removal of all barriers to cross-border cooperation between mutual societies, while taking account of their specific features, in order to make it possible for a european mutual society to be established through the cross-border merger of two or more existing mutual societies, and to allow for the creation of a european mutual society through the conversion or transformation of a national mutual society into a new form, without complicated intermediate steps. the second recommendation is a reminder that a proposal for such a statute must take account of the particular operating rules of mutual societies, which differ from those of other economic agents. the third emphasises that such a proposal should not affect mandatory or statutory social security schemes managed in certain member states by mutual societies. the management arrangement adopted by the statute should be without prejudice to member state laws, and the regulation should not cover other areas of law. the last recommendation is on the governance of european mutual societies, and it emphasises that they should be managed democratically and financed collectively.
the scandals in the world of sport are running high, not only in third countries but also in europe. according to europol figures, around 90% of illegal sports betting is on football, but other sports should not be neglected either. we're talking about an illegal practice with a long history and huge sums of money, which, thanks to the development of mass media, has become increasingly known to the public. moreover, technological advances and the advent of online gambling have fostered an illegal and hard-to-trace transnational industry. current mechanisms have difficulty detecting match-fixing due to the global nature of these practices, which also involve factors from outside the eu. the fight against the manipulation of sports results must, however, continue to restore public confidence in the sporting phenomenon. early education is an important element in promoting values such as integrity, fair play and mutual respect. also, legalizing and regulating sports betting may solve some of the problem, since the greatest corruption in sports occurs in countries where betting is illegal.
sports provide, in addition to physical education, a social education that strengthens character. but what do we do when it affects the integrity of this discipline? what will be the character of sport when young people see corruption on television more and more often and the institutions of the european union, as well as national institutions, are powerless to deal with this phenomenon, practically unable to intervene to solve the problem? i would therefore recommend that the european commission make immediate efforts, together with the member states, to harmonise national legislation on corruption in sport, to conclude international agreements with third countries where criminal groups have been detected to eliminate them and, last but not least, to set up an international unit to monitor this phenomenon.
with the accession to the ccib, the european union will be able to exert greater influence on the cotton agenda. i therefore believe that the european union must take account not only of the demand for and supply of cotton on a world scale but also of the problems of human rights violations. sadly, forced child labor in the cotton fields remains a reality. according to estimates by the international labour organization, more than 215 million children worldwide are exploited in child labor, and 60 percent of them work in the agricultural sector. i shall dwell on the situation in uzbekistan because i have followed developments in that country as rapporteur for the european parliament on bilateral textile trade. according to several reports by various ngos, the iom, the international trade union confederation and unicef, children in uzbekistan are forced by the national authorities to meet daily quotas in cotton harvesting. they are exposed to a grueling schedule of extreme temperatures and are at risk of disease from the pesticides used to treat cotton. although uzbekistan has ratified the convention on the worst forms of forced child labour, as well as the convention on the abolition of forced labour, progress is slow to appear. i therefore call on the european commission to examine the latest report of the iom committee of experts and, if the information is confirmed, to launch an investigation to withdraw uzbekistan's right to participate in the gsp. finally, i would like to thank mrs muscardini for the way in which we have collaborated on this report. let us hope, as mr caspary has said, that the commission will take this report into account.

in writing. − the aspects of flag state control mentioned in the 2006 maritime labour convention should be more fully and specifically incorporated into eu legislation. a major advantage of introducing maritime labour into eu law is that it will benefit from a stricter enforcement regime within the eu, for example through infringement procedures, which will lead to an even higher level of compliance. eu provisions on flag state control should reflect what maritime work specifically and expressly aims to avoid - different interpretations by member states - which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping. the introduction of the maritime labour certificate and the maritime labour declaration of conformity are central elements for the implementation of maritime labour. clear rules on labour supply responsibilities are needed to ensure that member states fulfil their responsibilities for the recruitment, placement and social protection of seafarers.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. endocrine disorders and diseases have increased worldwide, and many studies consider endocrine disruptors to be a contributing factor. endocrine disruptors have been associated with a number of health problems over time, such as reproductive, congenital or neurodevelopmental disorders (autism). the worrying thing is that endocrine disruptors are found in a wide range of products, from the packaging of the food we buy to some electronic products without which many of us could not carry out our daily activities (the telephone or the laptop). the protection of human health is one of the pillars of community policy, and the precautionary principle must be fully applied.
in writing. − endocrine disruptors are increasingly recognised as a major challenge to human health and the environment. they have often been linked to a number of serious health problems, such as cancer, diabetes, immune dysfunction, obesity, reproductive dysfunction, cardiovascular disease, behavioral changes, and early puberty. the financial crisis is often cited as the main obstacle to the development of new legislation. a more precise and accurate description of the nature of the risks is needed to decide where to position this issue in terms of priority and resource allocation. the precautionary principle requires that, in this context of scientific uncertainty, we take appropriate measures to avoid or reduce potentially serious or irreversible consequences for human health and the environment by introducing and maintaining research programmes on the effects of these endocrine disruptors. the commission must pay particular attention to vulnerable groups such as children and women. the protection of women against the potential risks posed by endocrine disruptors to their reproductive health is a matter of the utmost importance and should be addressed by funding, as a matter of priority, those research and long-term studies aimed at monitoring women's health.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the protection of public health against endocrine disruptors and i will always support the application of the precautionary principle in the use of chemicals, regardless of the field. public bodies have a duty to compensate, through prudence and the fullest possible information, for the lack of knowledge of the consumer public about the potential adverse effects of certain chemicals. i consider that where these chemicals are components of foodstuffs, the precautionary principle must take precedence over any other consideration, whatever it may be.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because asbestos is very dangerous, causing diseases such as lung cancer and pleural mesothelioma. it is still found in many mines, unsafe landfills, water supply systems, near-shore wrecks, and public and private buildings. cases of people affected by asbestos inhalation are continuously increasing and by 2030 the number is estimated to reach around 500 000. it's a matter of concern, which is why we need to take action as soon as possible. we need to protect the most vulnerable workers, provide support to those affected and develop asbestos removal projects.
in writing. − the removal of asbestos-containing materials from buildings, particularly in less economically developed member states and rural areas, is a financial burden for building owners and should continue to receive active support at national and european level. for all persons involved (employer, supervisor, worker) in asbestos-related activities, training should cover: the properties of asbestos and its health effects, including synergy with smoking; the types of materials or products that may contain asbestos and the places where they may be encountered; how the condition of materials or products affects the ease of removal of fibres and the action to be taken if materials containing asbestos are identified. the commission should propose a specific directive containing the necessary requirements for the training of construction and maintenance workers, including construction specialists who work with asbestos by accident. such training must be provided at regular intervals and at no cost to the workers. safe working procedures, including the correct use of protective equipment, are required for workers who may be working in the vicinity of materials containing asbestos.
in writing. − according to the world health organisation, between 20 000 and 30 000 cases of asbestos-related diseases are reported each year in the eu alone, and it is estimated that more than 300 000 citizens will die of mesothelioma in the eu by 2030. this is why the commission must carry out a study listing the problems caused by the use of asbestos in each member state and identify the specific measures for the safe elimination of asbestos from public buildings, indicating the funds that will be needed to this end. the commission should also amend recommendation 2003/670/ec, as medical research has in the meantime shown a link between asbestos and ovarian and laryngeal cancer.
in writing. − the issue of mutual societies has been on the agenda of european decision-makers for some time, and i welcome the initiative of the european legislator to legislate in this area, which requires an effective and pragmatic framework to thrive. the importance of addressing this issue is all the greater as mutual societies provide essential services to citizens of the member states as well as to european citizens working outside their own country's borders, a growing socio-demographic category. the new rules must ensure that mutual societies remain a vital part of the european social system and of european economies, which are currently suffering from the consequences of the economic crisis. equally, the proposed rules must not depart from respect for fundamental rights and the principle of subsidiarity. i support the adoption of this report, which contains recommendations enabling european companies to use new legal instruments which are appropriate to their own activity and capable of preserving the mutual character of these associations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because a statute for european mutual societies would guarantee the creation of appropriate legal instruments in this field. at present, european mutual societies vary considerably in terms of the services they provide, their size or their mission. however, the statute will give them the capacity to develop crossborder activities and to operate within the union under normal conditions of competition. i also support the recommendation of parliament that any legislative initiative in this respect should not change existing national legislation. therefore, the harmonisation of the laws of the member states concerning mutual societies is not sought. i believe that the european charter should promote the innovative capacity of mutual societies so that citizens benefit from a greater diversity of services. moreover, it is important that european mutual societies are governed democratically.
in writing. − mutual societies play a major role in the union's economy, providing healthcare and social benefits to over 160 million european citizens, representing over €180 billion in insurance premiums and employing over 350 000 people in the union. increasing expenditure on healthcare and pensions could have significant consequences for the sustainability and coverage of current social protection schemes, which could lead member states to reduce the level of compulsory social protection contributions and to shift social security burdens to the private sector. mutual societies must play an important role in sustainable health through proactive prevention policies. the social economy, and in particular mutual societies, play a key role in the union economy, combining profitability with solidarity, creating quality jobs, strengthening social, economic and territorial cohesion, generating social capital, promoting active citizenship, social welfare based on solidarity and a type of economy based on democratic values, which puts people first and supports sustainable development and social, technological and environmental innovation.

author. - as the initiator of the inclusion of the situation in bangladesh in today's emergency debates, i would like to stress the importance of parliament's reaction to the events resulting from the death sentence of delwar hossain sayeedi, vice-chairman of the islamist jamaat party. indeed, we could not, i think, ignore the worst episode of political violence that bangladesh has known in the last 42 years. we are facing a paradoxical situation, because the international war crimes tribunal, which was supposed to help bangladesh overcome the horrors that accompanied the birth of this nation in 1971, is actually at the origin of the recent violence. we must of course reaffirm our categorical opposition to the death penalty and call on the bangladeshi authorities to commute the sentences handed down and to introduce a moratorium on these punishments. the respect of international fair trial standards is indispensable, especially in the case of a court that is supposed to promote national reconciliation. the violence that followed the sentencing is, for each of us, unacceptable and i am referring here, of course, to both the violence of jamaat party supporters and the violence of the security forces. peaceful demonstrations are, as we know, a fundamental right; violence is never a reasonable response. it is also very worrying that according to human rights watch, most of the victims were provoked by the police. we must therefore remind the government in dhaka that it is primarily responsible for the security of its citizens. finally, it should also be stressed that the recent violence in bangladesh shows a polarization of society, divided between a secular vision, embodied by the awami, and the religious vision, represented by the bangladesh nationalist party, allied with jamaat-e-islami. our resolution calls on all parties to overcome their divisions.

question submitted under the 'blue card' procedure i consider that arbitrary intervention on the carbon market at union level can have a negative impact on both the market and european industry. moreover, the main cause of the reduction in carbon emissions by more than 10% since the start of the second trading period in 2008 was not the price of carbon but the decrease in industrial activity due to the economic crisis. i do not support, as you do, the delay in the timing of the auctioning of emission allowances and i would like to ask you if you are aware that in the report on the state of the internal carbon market in 2012, the commission has already proposed the option of permanently withdrawing a number of allowances during the third period?
we agree that the ets market is currently facing serious problems, due, inter alia, to the imbalance between supply and demand that has emerged during this period of crisis in europe and that has had exceptional and unpredictable effects on the market. i believe that the change in the timing of the auctioning of emission allowances - the proposal by which the commission wants to revitalise the market - should not have as its aim the increase in the price of allowances, but should only be aimed at the proper functioning of a market which, for the parties concerned, has lost its credibility. i do not consider back-loading to be a measure capable of resolving market failures in itself, but a measure which may save time. the priority must therefore be to adopt a set of measures that have the potential to address the long-term structural problems of the carbon market.
since 2008, unfortunately, not enough investment has been made in making european industry more environmentally friendly. what guarantees are there that the investments needed to make european industry eco-efficient will be made, regardless of the price of carbon dioxide per tonne, which has fallen from eur 20 per tonne in 2008 to around eur 4 per tonne in 2012? now, the price per ton of carbon dioxide is low. the commission has also tried to set an arbitrary price of eur 30 per tonne of carbon dioxide in the energy taxation directive. european industry needs massive investment in re-technologising to become eco-efficient and to keep jobs in the union. the union needs both an ambitious environmental policy and the competitiveness of european industry and, above all, the preservation of jobs within the european union.
in writing. i must say at the outset that i disagree with the european commission's proposal to change this ets auction calendar for two main reasons. first, in the ets the price of allowances is set by the market. the current price of emissions, although low, reflects the reality of the market, so i see no need for artificial intervention by the authorities. secondly, delaying the placing of emission allowances on the market would inevitably lead to higher energy prices. in my view, this is not acceptable in the context of the current crisis and given that the liberalisation of the energy market has already led to higher energy costs for final consumers. i fully agree with the goal of reducing carbon emissions, but i don't think it should be achieved at any cost. the ets must function as originally planned and not jeopardise other important objectives such as re-industrialisation or the recovery from the economic and social crisis.
in writing. on the vote tomorrow, i will vote in favour of amendment no 20, which rejects the commission's proposal. the proposed 'end-of-period concentration' of greenhouse gas emission allowances to be traded in 2013-2020 is challenged by businesses and experts as both inefficient and likely to keep energy prices high. the european union could lose investment and jobs as a result of this measure, which we cannot afford in this period of high unemployment. the measure would also distort the european union's emissions trading system, which is a functioning system and has an interesting potential in achieving the proposed reductions in carbon dioxide emissions. the decline in the price of carbon is an effect of the economic crisis. i believe that we must want an industry which produces more and pollutes less, not one which does not pollute simply because it does not produce, while european citizens are worried about their jobs.
in writing. the european commission's proposal to withdraw a significant number of emission allowances has generated intense debate and extreme positions from both different industries and civil society. i think that a comparative analysis of the impact of the reduction of emissions in europe on the total volume of emissions in the world is needed and how much europe can advance in this area without jeopardising the future of its own industry.
between 1990 and 2006, carbon dioxide emissions from aviation almost doubled, accounting for about 3% of total greenhouse gas emissions. this number is continuing to rise and is projected to increase by 63% by 2020. but effective global warming management can only be achieved on an international basis. we need to make sure that the same climate targets are being considered globally and that carbon emissions do not ignore national borders. we must not forget that our commitment is to reduce our emissions by 20% compared with 1990 levels. that is why i think it is important that aviation, which is part of the eu ets, also plays its part in the fight against climate change. third countries must also accept that, if their flights also affect the eu, they cannot ignore the provisions of the ets. two thirds of emissions are caused by intercontinental flights, but only one third of these are caused by flights from the eu. i therefore support the position of the commission and the rapporteur in the interests of a successful negotiation as soon as possible. the legal basis for reducing the amounts to be auctioned should be established as soon as possible, as this is still lacking. it is also necessary to clarify that the scheme should not be applied for more than one year only within the union. this is our chance to prove that the european union is not standing in the way of international agreement.
the court of justice confirmed in 2011 that the inclusion in the european trading system of emission allowances from third-country vessels departing from or arriving at union airports is legally admissible. air carriers using the same routes must be treated equally. the union is ready to amend its legislation as soon as a global agreement is reached. the problems caused by aviation emissions can only be effectively managed by a global obligation to comply with the same measures or to achieve the same objectives through different measures. the union expects icao to agree on a global market measure and a realistic timetable for its implementation. the commission should submit to parliament a full progress report to the icao assembly in september 2013 and swiftly propose actions based on these results.

equality between women and men is one of the fundamental principles of community law. in this context, i would like to extend my greetings and congratulations to our reporter. the report welcomes the fact that it has been drawn up on its own initiative, which is intended to fill the gaps still existing in directive 113/2004 on the application of the principle of equality between women and men in the access to and supply of goods and services. i support the rapporteur's proposal, which calls on the european commission and the member states to take concrete steps to explain this directive and its impact, with concrete examples, to ensure that both women and men can make full and appropriate use of the directive as an effective tool to protect their rights. i also welcome the idea of creating a database covering legislation and case law in this area, as well as better protection for victims of gender discrimination. i also insist on the need to publish the european commission's report on the application of the directive, which was due to be published in 2010 but was postponed to 2014.
the derogation provided for in article 5 (2) of directive 113/2004 allowed for proportional differences in premiums and benefits for insured persons where the criterion of gender is a determining factor in the assessment of risks. according to the judgment of the european court of justice in the test-achats case of march 2011, article 5 (2) of the directive is contrary to the objective of equal treatment between women and men and is incompatible with the charter of fundamental rights of the union. we call on the commission to revise this directive and to include mandatory provisions to clarify the situation with regard to insurance companies and related financial services. we call on the commission and the member states to take concrete measures to ensure that all citizens of the european union can make full and appropriate use of the directive as an effective instrument for protecting their rights to equal treatment in access to all goods and services.

statistics published by eurostat showed that in february 2013 the unemployment rate in the european union reached 12% in the euro area and 10.9% at eu-27 level. in countries such as spain and portugal, the unemployment rate was above 50% in february 2013, and in portugal and italy, it was above 35%. also, according to eurostat statistics, in january 2013, compared to january 2012, the production of durable goods decreased by 5,5% in the euro area and by 4,3% in the eu27. four of the 27 member states - germany, italy, the united kingdom and france - accounted for more than 60% of the european union's industrial output in 2010. also, 10 member states together produced less than 4% of the european union's industrial output in 2010. the european union urgently needs measures to restore the union's industrial production, maintain its competitiveness and reduce unemployment in the eu 27. the commission, together with the member states, must develop an industrial policy in all the member states of the union and, in particular, in those whose industrial production it represents. i want to express my total disagreement with the cheap populism expressed by some politicians, especially in the uk, especially towards immigrants from the countries of the southeast of the european union. in a period characterized by economic and financial crisis i believe that our efforts should be focused on finding solutions to solve the economic and financial crisis, and not to provoke scandals with racist and nationalist tendencies. i would like to recommend to distinguished policymakers a number of empirical studies, by distinguished researchers and professors of economics in the uk, such as dustman, fratini, preston and others, which clearly show that immigrants do not negatively affect the labour market, they make a significant contribution to the gross domestic product of the host countries, and, most importantly, these eastern european immigrants have a lower unemployment rate than the locals, which indicates that they migrated only to work, and not to receive social benefits.
the european commission hosted a conference on replenishing the global fund to fight hiv/aids, tuberculosis and malaria for 2014-2016, which indicated the need for us$15 billion to fight these three infectious diseases globally. we need a full global fund. it is the most successful health instrument, having funded over 1,000 programmes to fight aids, tuberculosis and malaria in 151 countries, and invested $22 billion in the fight against them. we are at a critical moment, when the global fund's support in the fight against infectious diseases is essential. the progress made so far will be lost if we don't act now. we have a historic opportunity to stop the spread of these diseases, and if we miss this moment, the long-term costs will increase exponentially in terms of lives lost, decreased productivity and economic growth. i call on the european institutions to support the integration of health as a key element in the european union's external policy instruments and thus to help save at least 6 million lives and billions of dollars over a period of 3 years.

the increasing importance of communication and information networks in the efficient functioning of critical infrastructure, the increasing participation of european citizens in numerous virtual networks in multiple aspects: spending leisure time, purchasing goods and services, carrying out banking transactions, bring to the forefront extremely serious problems. protecting privacy, protecting identity, maintaining the security of public infrastructure, creating an area dominated by full freedom of expression are priorities that european policymakers must address. in these circumstances, i support the adoption of the report on the functioning of the european network and information security agency as a major step in identifying and combating potential threats to the security of european states and societies.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is vital that the mandate of the european network and information security agency (enisa) be extended until september 2013, thus allowing it to continue its work and allowing the european parliament to debate and analyse its future. since its establishment in 2004, enisa has proven to be a valuable agency for the european union through its successes in network and information security. however, in order to face the new challenges of the cyber environment, a reform is needed that will allow the agency to take on a more important role in combating cybercrime, but also to be able to cooperate more closely with member states on data protection and citizens' privacy issues.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report to support the need to modernise and optimise the european network and information security agency. since its launch in 2004, the agency has made a significant contribution to improving network and information security. the new challenges of a constantly evolving cyber world have necessitated a debate on updating the agency's role and developing an extended mandate to incorporate new tasks and possibilities for cooperation with the competent authorities in the field of data protection and privacy. moreover, in the context of the global dimension of network and information security, the agency must be allowed to assume a coordinating role when there are disruptions in the institutional architecture, in order to continue the fight against cybercrime to an appropriate extent.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the european network and information security agency (enisa). security incidents can undermine users' trust in technology, networks and services, thus affecting their ability to exploit the full potential of the internal market and the widespread use of information and communication technology (ict). internal market measures in the field of electronic communications security and, more generally, network and information security require the adoption of different types of technical and organisational applications by the member states and the institutions of the european union. the heterogeneous application of those requirements may harm efficiency and create obstacles to the internal market. for this reason, a european-level centre of expertise is needed to provide guidance, advice and assistance on network and information security issues on which member states and union institutions can rely. the adoption of this regulation will enable the agency to respond to these needs by developing and maintaining a high level of expertise and by providing assistance to member states, the union institutions and the business community.

in writing. - i voted against the change in the calendar because if the emission certificates had been withdrawn from the market, it could have led to an increase in the price of energy throughout europe for both household and industrial consumers. the commission considers that the change in the tendering calendar is a solution to achieve a structural reform of the system in the meantime. in romania, as a result of the liberalisation of electricity prices, prices could double by 2017 for household consumers. a further increase in the price due to intervention on the market for certificates could have very serious consequences for romanian citizens. also, in the context of studies showing that the 2020 emission reduction target will be achieved, i do not see why measures of the type proposed by the commission should be taken.
in writing. - i voted against this report because the commission's proposal to amend the auction calendar to postpone the release of 955 million emission allowances is as unnecessary as it is dangerous. the ets was designed as a market instrument to cap and progressively reduce co2 emissions by allowing participants in the scheme to trade in allowances. intervention in the market to stop the decline in the carbon price caused by the excess supply is contrary to the principles of the functioning of the market. delaying the trading of ets allowances will inevitably result in an increase in energy prices. these bills will be paid directly and indirectly by private consumers, because the industrialists will be forced to cover their costs through high prices. european industry will lose competitiveness to low-priced imports from outside the eu, which is contrary to the reindustrialisation target recently launched by the european commission. the carbon market is functioning, and the price is only reflecting the severe economic and financial crisis of the last few years. the economic recovery will drive up the price of carbon without the need for the european commission to intervene.

in writing. − the european commission considers that the proper functioning of the european carbon market, which is in transition to phase three, will be increasingly affected by the increase in net supply combined with the decline in demand. in this context, the commission proposed that the possibility of adapting the calendar for each period be introduced in the directive. the commission's objective is to raise the price of emission allowances by blocking the auctioning of 900 million allowances for a period of five years. the price of the certificates is the result of a wide range of factors, but the economic downturn in 2009 undoubtedly had a major impact on prices. i am against arbitrary and unpredictable interventions in the carbon market because i believe that they can negatively affect both the carbon market and the industry. also, artificially increasing the price of carbon will cause electricity prices to rise, carbon dioxide emissions to shift and unemployment to rise. i therefore voted for amendment no 20 by which the european parliament rejects the commission's proposal to amend directive 2003/87/ec by clarifying the provisions on the timing of greenhouse gas emission allowance auctions.
i strongly support the rapporteur's amendments which provide legal clarity to this decision and send a positive signal to international partners that the european union does not want the legislation in force to stand in the way of a global agreement, but at the same time stress that if the desired result is not achieved, the union will return to applying its own rules on greenhouse gas emission trading and for the aviation sector. the european union must reaffirm its leadership on climate change and, through the negotiations in the international civil aviation organisation, make every effort to make the signing of a global agreement a reality within the one year period available to it.
i voted in favour of the report because global warming can only be effectively tackled through an international effort, as carbon emissions do not remain within national borders. even though aviation currently generates around 3% of total greenhouse gas emissions, its level is increasing rapidly and the inclusion of the sector in the emissions trading system has only created a uniform framework for all transport sectors. however, in order not to affect the competitiveness of the aviation industry, the system must be extended to international flights. i believe that in the absence of such a decision, competition in the aviation sector would be distorted, with potentially serious consequences for airlines in the union, and that the best solution is to conclude an international agreement to regulate aviation emissions in a transparent and uniform manner.
in writing. − the aviation sector is strongly international in nature and therefore global aviation emissions problems can only be effectively managed through an international approach. the international civil aviation organisation (icao) plays a key role in this process by setting common objectives in an international agreement. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the implementation of this regulation. the commission's proposal to suspend the application of the eu ets for intercontinental flights for one year reinforces the positive attitude within icao and increases the chances of a successful conclusion of the icao general assembly in 2013. the proposal removes legal uncertainties on airline obligations and sends a clear message to international negotiating partners. the european union wants an international agreement and is open to negotiating the best forms of market measures to address aviation emissions in a similar way to addressing emissions from other sectors. the commission should provide the european parliament with a full progress report at the icao assembly in september 2013 and swiftly propose actions based on these results.
in writing. − i support this report because it is very important, in the context of the amplification of climate change, to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from airlines. although the aviation sector has been included in the union's greenhouse gas emission trading scheme (eu-ets) since 2008, it has benefited from preferential treatment over other industries and modes of transport when it comes to reducing emissions. unfortunately, we are currently seeing an alarming increase in emissions from air travel (especially intercontinental flights). the european union, together with the international civil aviation organisation (icao), must take the necessary measures to put an end to this uncontrolled increase in gas emissions, which is exacerbating climate problems and increasing the use of fossil fuels.
in writing. − welcomes the rapporteur's proposal to use the proceeds of the auctioning of allowances or any other equivalent amount to finance contributions to the global fund for energy efficiency and renewable energy and the green climate fund under the unfccc to finance measures to prevent deforestation and facilitate adaptation to the effects of climate change in developing countries. those measures can contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and adaptation to the effects of climate change in the european union and third countries, to the financing of research and development to mitigate and adapt to those effects, and to the costs of managing the eu ets.
in writing. − i voted in favour of temporarily and exceptionally suspending intercontinental flights from the eu ets emissions trading scheme applied to the aviation sector to stimulate progress in international negotiations on the development of a global market measure to combat aviation emissions. the global problems caused by aviation emissions can only be effectively addressed at international level, through a set of rules and obligations to be respected by each actor individually, in order to avoid distorting competition or slowing down efforts to combat climate change. the international civil aviation organization (icao) is tasked with regulating emissions, developing an effective global system to reduce the increasing levels of emissions generated by the aviation sector. the suspension of the application of the ets to intercontinental flights will not affect the level of ambition in terms of environmental protection, but will ensure that aviation industry participants are subject to the same set of rules until the ets is developed.
in writing. − i supported this proposal to allow more – although strictly limited – time for international discussions on co2 emissions from aircraft to be completed. it has proved a difficult issue to resolve, but the beginning of phase three of the ets has brought a new sense of urgency to the discussions. the eu is again driving the international debate on climate policy and bringing our international partners to the negotiating table so all parties can agree on a fair and effective solution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the greenhouse gas emission trading scheme. global warming can only be effectively addressed through an international approach. the union decided in 2008 to include aviation in its emissions trading scheme (ets) from 2012. the court of justice confirmed in 2011 that the inclusion in the ets of emissions from third country aircraft departing from or arriving at community airports is legally admissible. in november 2012, icao made significant progress on market measures to address emissions from international aviation. the european commission therefore decided to send a message to the negotiating partners and proposed to 'stop the clock'. a one-year derogation offers better prospects for reaching a satisfactory international agreement this year, rather than maintaining the current legislation. if no satisfactory international agreement is reached to address aviation emissions, all international flights will be included again from 2013. we stress that parliament should be able to assess the outcome of the icao negotiations before further measures are proposed by the european commission.
credit institutions and investment firms should be subject to similar scrutiny and to uniform criteria in all member states. administrative sanctions and measures, which must be applied strictly and uniformly, must be reported and published. i therefore call on the member states to establish and apply, without exception, dissuasive financial penalties, in other words very large fines, and to make them known to the public - all for natural and legal persons who have unlawfully obtained benefits or avoided losses. speaking of losses, i'd like to draw attention to the financial losses due to corruption. researchers at germany's hertie university in berlin estimated that if all member states collected taxes at the same level as denmark, over 300 billion euros would have been collected in 2012, twice the budget of the european union. this money has been lost.
overcoming the effects of the financial crisis depends crucially on the stability and sustainability of credit institutions and investment firms. reducing the external costs faced by these actors is one of the priorities that european decision-makers must take into account. at the same time, the union must ensure that the process of safeguarding systemic financial institutions must not become an additional burden for european taxpayers or bona fide depositors. the stabilisation of the financial system needs to be coordinated with the proper functioning of the internal market. harmonising european regulations can lead to increased transparency and accountability in the financial system, thus establishing the conditions for sustainable growth and development. the legislative process must, however, maintain the effectiveness of the fundamental principle for the union, the free movement of capital. last but not least, the european union must continue, including at this level, to combat tax evasion by strengthening and streamlining the process of collecting and distributing relevant information to the supervisory authorities in different member states.
i voted in favour of the report because the coordination of national provisions on the activity of credit institutions and investment firms, their governance arrangements and their supervisory framework is very important. i support the set of compromises negotiated during the trilogue with the council presidency. we are in a difficult situation because we have not yet overcome the crisis. in this context, we need to find the right balance, to create a functioning financial and banking space, capable of financing the growth we need at the moment in the european economy. at the same time, we need to facilitate access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises and encourage small-scale banking. i welcome the fact that the specificities of the member states' markets have been taken into account. it is also imperative that the supervisory power and the instruments of prudential supervision be held exclusively by the competent authorities.
in writing. − excessive reliance on external credit ratings should be reduced and all automatic effects of credit ratings should be phased out. the rules should therefore require credit institutions and investment firms to establish rigorous criteria and decision-making processes for the granting of credit. external credit ratings may be used as a factor among others in this process, but institutions should not rely solely and mechanically on external ratings and they should not prevail. i believe that, in addition to the supervision aimed at ensuring financial stability, there is a need to improve the mechanisms for supervision and the prevention of possible bubbles, in order to ensure the optimal allocation of capital taking into account the macroeconomic challenges and objectives, in particular with regard to long-term investment in the real economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. i believe that the role of credit institutions in the current economic crisis has been underestimated for a long time. the current proposal provides for detailed rules on liquidity supervision and will increase the level of transparency in banking, which is being called for by various non-governmental organisations and the majority of society. increased transparency will help credit and banking institutions regain some of the trust they lost from citizens with the onset of the economic crisis and will increase the efficiency of the eu's internal market. another positive aspect of the current report is the creation of a pan-european blacklist of troubled bankers, which the authorities will have to verify before a banker is hired.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this directive of the parliament and of the council, on the basis of the commission's proposal, for stricter regulation of the activity of credit institutions and for the prudential supervision of credit institutions and investment firms. the financial crisis has demonstrated the major interdependencies between the banking system and the speculative sphere, with potentially catastrophic consequences for the balance of the banking system and the lives of citizens. it is important that credit institutions have internal capital adequate to the risks they face, transparency, information exchange and market discipline are essential and, not least, banking supervision must always aim to protect the interests of depositors. i support the idea of encouraging small-scale banking through credit unions and mutual funds, as such structures allow for more effective supervision and prudent management and can lead to the formation of a sustainable and diversified banking culture.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the activity of credit institutions and the prudential supervision of credit institutions and investment firms and amending directive 2002/87/ec on the supplementary supervision of credit institutions, insurance undertakings and investment firms in a financial conglomerate. the commission has proposed a legal framework consisting of two legal instruments: a directive and a regulation. it regulates banking activities and lays down prudential rules applicable to credit institutions and investment firms. the directive contains provisions governing the authorisation of business, the acquisition of qualifying holdings, the exercise of freedom of establishment and freedom to provide services, the powers of the supervisory authorities of the home and host member states in this area, and provisions governing initial capital and the prudential analysis of credit institutions and investment firms. the main objective of the directive is to coordinate national provisions on access to the business of credit institutions and investment firms, their governance arrangements and their supervisory framework. it lays down uniform and directly applicable prudential requirements for credit institutions and investment firms.
thanks to intense negotiations by parliament, for the first time banks will report financial statements broken down by each country where they have branches, and not just at the general level. this will certainly lead to greater transparency in the declaration of profits and better collection of taxes paid in each country. but let's be realistic because all these documents that we adopt will be just letters on paper and will have no effect. the most important thing is to eliminate tax havens in the european union and also to legally pursue and confiscate money in tax havens anywhere in the world, in the union or outside it. i want to give you some figures: the investigative journalism network called the tax justice network published a study in april 2013 that found that there's up to 25 trillion euros in tax havens. also, offshore leagues has just this month published 130,000 offshore accounts. this is the money we need to get back.
the scale and effects of the global economic crisis make it imperative to strengthen the international financial system. policies that increase the transparency, accountability and predictability of financial institutions and dynamics are essential to successfully overcome the consequences of the crisis, which has significantly eroded the living standards of european citizens. at the same time, i support the adoption at european level of legislative measures capable of leading to the creation of a harmonised legal framework for european financial actors. only by harmonising the provisions in this area can we create the conditions for sustainable economic development. i also believe that we must bear in mind that the recovery of european economies cannot take place without a certain increase in competitiveness. while it is important to establish global guidelines on the sustainability of financial systems, it is important that the regulatory process does not place european economic actors at a disadvantage.
the commission has also taken into account the fact that the us is the largest market for the euro banknotes and coins in the world. i want to congratulate mr. karas on a very well-structured report. for reasons of legal certainty, a single set of rules for all market participants is a key element for the functioning of the internal market. in order to avoid market distortion and regulatory arbitrage, measures should ensure a maximum degree of harmonisation. the transitional periods provided for are therefore essential for the proper implementation of this regulation and to avoid uncertainty in the markets. member states and competent authorities should avoid adopting divergent or anticipatory rules which affect or weaken the principle of maximum harmonisation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation on prudential requirements for credit institutions and investment firms. the scale of the financial crisis has revealed a number of unacceptable risks inherent in the current regulation of financial institutions. according to imf estimates, the losses incurred by european credit institutions between 2007 and 2010 as a result of the crisis amount to approximately eur 1 trillion or 8% of the gdp of the european union. in order to restore stability to the banking sector and to ensure the continued availability of credit to the real economy, both the european union and its member states have adopted a wide range of unprecedented measures the costs of which have been borne, in the last resort, by taxpayers. in this context, by october 2010 the commission had approved eur 4 600 billion of state aid for financial institutions, of which more than eur 2 000 billion was actually used in 2008 and 2009. the proposal for a regulation contains the globally developed and agreed elements of the capital and liquidity standards applicable to credit institutions, known as basel iii, and harmonises other provisions in existing legislation.
the evolution of this report proves that the pursuit of objectives can also go beyond the rejection of a report. it was rejected in december, for example, and positive changes were made, and today it has been adopted. it's about changes that will help the passengers. many of us, many of the citizens of europe and the planet use airports and as such will benefit from measures to ensure that they spend less time at airports. for example, they will benefit from minimum quality standards for services at large airports, reducing check-in times and baggage delays. all this will lead to optimisation of air traffic and, again, the most important thing: it will take care of people's precious time when they have to travel and travel.
in writing. − ground handling services are essential for the smooth running of air operations. given that the turnover of ground handling services is eur 50 billion and the number of jobs in this sector is estimated to be at least 60 000 across europe, we need an effective european legal framework. member states should ensure that wage dumping is prevented not only for employees in the ground handling sector but also in the event of a transfer of staff, in order to ensure adequate social standards and to improve the quality of ground handling services. the competent authorities of the member states should take into account trade union rights and collective bargaining in the field of ground handling services in order to ensure adequate social protection for staff recruited for the provision of those services. in order to mitigate the negative effects of liberalisation in the ground handling services sector, airport managing authorities should define and apply mandatory minimum quality of service standards in the interests of safety, reliability and efficiency of operations.
in writing. − i support the rapporteur's proposal on an adequate level of social protection and appropriate working conditions for the staff of companies providing this type of ground handling services, including for companies that have subcontracted the work, as well as the development and continuous training of staff. it is appropriate to establish minimum standards to ensure optimal quality levels of education and training of ground handling staff, which need to be updated regularly, in order to contribute to the quality of operations in terms of reliability, resilience, safety and security and to create a level playing field for all operators.
in writing. − ground handling services ensure the smooth running of air operations. as a result, we have a turnover of 50 billion euros, which forces us to pay more attention to this area of activity. i support the commission's report both from the economic and social point of view, so as not to disproportionate the flow of wages and production costs. following the liberalisation in 1996 and 2012 respectively, competition created a high volume of activity and a decrease in prices on the handling market. in order to avoid wage dumping, which could affect the quality and safety of services, we should adopt the new changes and new guarantees offered by the commission in the new report.
in writing. − groundhandling services are essential for the 800 million passengers who use european union airports every year. following the adoption of this report, the large airports will have to work with at least three providers, which will enable improvements in the quality of the services but will also lower prices. with this new version of the report, only airports which have more than 15 million passengers or 200 000 tonnes of goods in transit will have to apply these liberalisation measures. the report on which parliament voted on 16 april 2013 will also allow significant progress in terms of social guarantees and will protect workers from dismissal or replacement by other less costly staff. for example, a provider who obtains a new contract will have to keep the employees hired by the previous administrator. the negotiations on the airport package can now start with the commission and the council.
in writing. − the rapid development of air traffic and the resulting constraints on the capacity of ground-based service providers raise the question of the efficiency, quality and safety of air transport activities. ground handling services are essential for the smooth operation of air transport in the eu, considering that in 2011 alone some 777 million passengers travelled in the union's airspace, with a slight decrease in the recent period, according to eurostat data. the liberalisation of ground handling activities is fraught with risks. following the opening up of the services market by directive 96/67/ec, the results were less satisfactory: temporary jobs, wage increases below inflation, but also a decline in quality. in the field of ground services, the opening of the market has led to lower safety standards, poor service, a lack of a uniform system, and numerous disruptions and delays in air passenger and cargo traffic. i support the rapporteur's position because i believe that the forced liberalisation of ground services cannot guarantee the efficient and safe operation of air transport activities or the respect of the rules and working conditions for employees.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on ground handling services at european union airports. in december 2012, the european parliament voted to reject and refer the proposal back to the european commission, with the main criticism referring to the social impact of the liberalisation of ground handling services for employees. ground handling services are vital to the smooth running of air operations. the continued liberalisation of the market in ground handling services should not be to the detriment of workers. member states should ensure, by means of legislation, that the staff of undertakings providing ground handling or own-handling services benefit from an adequate level of social security and working conditions, including in the case of subcontracting and service contracts. where the competent authorities of a member state find that the required standards are not being met at a particular airport, the accreditation of service providers or own-handling services shall be suspended, withdrawn or withheld until the appropriate standard is again reached. we stress the importance of introducing the representative collective agreement so that all ground handling suppliers and subcontractors must implement the representative collective agreement.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i support the ban on discarding skagerrak catches. i also welcome the fact that implementing rules are being put in place to ensure effective control of compliance by fishing vessels. the regulation lays down the rules applicable in the areas of the skagerrak under the jurisdiction of denmark and sweden. it would apply to all vessels fishing in those areas, including vessels from norway. conversely, eu vessels would be subject to norwegian rules if they fish in areas of the skagerrak under norwegian jurisdiction. unfortunately, there is no reliable information on the total amount of fish that is thrown back into the sea, so i advocate a precautionary approach. i also believe that the proposed amendments ensure the development of a sustainable fisheries sector at continental level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on certain technical and control measures in the skagerrak and amending regulation (ec) no 850/98 and regulation (ec) no 1342/2008. the european union shares many of its fishing waters with non-eu countries. the skagerrak and the north sea are the only seas where a non-eu member state (norway) has introduced a landing obligation. this regulation therefore lays down new technical and control measures in those areas of the skagerrak which fall under the jurisdiction of a member state. in order to ensure adequate monitoring of fishing activities, in particular as regards verification at sea of compliance with the obligation to land all catches from stocks subject to catch limits, it is necessary for member states to introduce an electronic remote monitoring system (rem). the rem system should be based on automatic control, data should be processed in accordance with data protection rules and should be available for research purposes.

young women are discriminated against anyway by their peers at the end of their careers, when they are expected to have extensive previous professional activity, which is impossible for the simple reason that being so young they have not had time to acquire this experience. so it's unacceptable to be discriminated against when you have to choose between having a child or a career. this is unacceptable in a modern society and that is why i join those who support making 2014 the 'european year of reconciling work and family life' and hope that the european commission will declare it so. studies show that a significant number of women face discrimination at work when they are pregnant or after they have given birth to a child.
in writing. − the european union and the member states must work together to avoid the discrimination that occurs in some eu countries against women entrepreneurs, especially single mothers, when they try to obtain loans or credit for their businesses and who still face obstacles based on gender stereotypes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i want to reiterate the request to the european commission to submit to parliament a report on the transposition of the directive implementing the principle of equal treatment in the access to and supply of goods and services. the directive is a very important step for gender equality and addresses the fight against gender discrimination outside employment for the first time at eu level. it also prohibits the less favourable treatment of women on the grounds of pregnancy and maternity, as well as harassment of any kind and the imposition of a discriminatory approach to the provision of goods or services. the transposition report is necessary to assess the consequences and the degree of implementation of the directive in the member states, to identify gaps and to draw up recommendations to overcome them.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. for the first time at eu level, a directive addresses gender equality outside the field of employment. we need to pay more attention to national bodies promoting gender equality. the european commission needs to monitor more closely how these bodies are fulfilling their tasks. the commission must also be transparent about the procedures for finding that these bodies have failed to fulfil their obligations and about the measures taken against them when irregularities are detected.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the transposition and application of council directive 2004/113/ec on the application of the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services. directive 2004/113/ec aims to establish a framework for combating discrimination on grounds of sex in the access to and supply of goods and services, with a view to implementing in the member states the principle of equal treatment between men and women. unfortunately, there are problems at european level, particularly in the area of access to and supply of goods and services. it is therefore necessary to prevent and eliminate discrimination on grounds of gender in this area. we call on the commission to review directive 2004/113 and to include mandatory provisions aimed at clarifying the situation with regard to insurance companies and related financial services. the commission and the member states should also take concrete measures to ensure that both women and men can make full and appropriate use of the directive as an effective tool for protecting their rights relating to equal treatment in access to all goods and services.
mr president, the european union and its member states are the largest providers of aid for trade in the world. in 2010 the european union committed eur 10.7 billion, thus accounting for around one third of total worldwide aid for trade. however, opening up to trade alone is not enough to achieve sustainable development. development needs well-functioning institutions, a healthy private sector, the pursuit of broad-based and inclusive economic development and, of course, an effective fight against tax evasion and corruption. therefore i support the proposal for country-by-country reporting as part of the revision of the accounting and transparency directive. i believe that a stronger focus should be directed towards bribery and corruption in the extractive sector in order to address and solve the resource-caused phenomenon.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that promoting development through trade must be a priority to support developing countries economically. in this respect, modernising the means of production, making them more efficient and increasing profitability must be constant objectives that can only be achieved by consolidating the efforts made so far. i believe that in order to achieve these objectives, the diversification of the economies of poor countries must also be promoted, while at the same time modern and profitable production is encouraged. we need to ensure that trade policies adopted at union level will bring about positive changes in the national economies of developing countries and that they, in turn, can contribute to the world economy. at the same time, the eu must consider supporting and developing small and medium-sized enterprises in poor countries at local level as a development policy objective.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because trade is one of the european union's core policies for promoting development in the least developed countries. development must be supported by other means than just humanitarian aid, and trade is an effective way to support sustainable growth for the very poorest countries. at the same time, the european union must promote the principle of good governance, closely linked to its trade policy, in order to ensure genuine economic and social development. therefore, before initiating any type of cooperation, the eu must ensure that a certain degree of transparency is achieved and that the third country follows the correct procedures.
in writing. − trade is a human activity that concerns us all and involves us all every day. as such, the rules that govern this activity concern and involve all of us, though not to the same extent. i believe that participation in world trade can generate wealth, enabling both eu member states to ensure a better quality of life for their citizens and development opportunities for developing countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on advancing development through trade as i think that both the eu's trade and aid policies should contribute to stimulating sustainable and inclusive growth in developing countries. more than just a political responsibility, it is also a moral duty to support developing countries in their efforts to reduce poverty. in order to ensure that trade is an efficient driver for growth, focus should be made on investing in developing country's trade capacity that will later empower local and national authorities to improve people’s living conditions. nevertheless, international trade agreements must not hold states back from legislating in favour of their citizens. because respect for, and the promotion of, human rights are part of the european union’s acquis, i very much welcome the inclusion of human rights provisions in the eu's future bilateral trade and cooperation agreements. furthermore, i believe that fair trade relations with developing countries require the eu to undertake a broader approach to trade negotiations, taking into consideration relevant aspects such as corporate social responsibility, labour rights, and food security.
in writing. - i voted against some paragraphs of the resolution which i do not consider correct, in particular paragraphs 6 and 35 and recital j. these paragraphs contain unjustified references directed against european agriculture, which is excessively associated with some negative effects on trade and development. i think parliament should be more cautious when it approaches the subject of agriculture in such terms. i regret that some of these references were approved by the plenary, which is why i voted against them in the final vote.
in writing. - i voted for the svensson report on promoting development through trade. the european union must, however, fight against the land grabbing of developing countries by big business and must also insist in the wto negotiations on the elimination of subsidies to farmers in food insecure countries who exploit land for purposes other than food production, such as the production of biofuels. also, eu-based companies that register their production in developing countries must respect human rights and freedoms, social and environmental standards, gender equality, basic labour standards and, in particular, the prohibition of child labour.
in writing. − i voted for the report on promoting development through trade as poverty reduction and the pursuit of the millennium development goals are central components of the european union's development policy and should also guide the eu's trade policy towards developing countries. fair trade between the european union and developing countries must be based on full compliance with and guaranteeing ilo labour standards and working conditions and must ensure the application of the highest possible social and environmental standards. we believe that for agreements to lead to development, a more flexible approach from the european union is needed, which encourages the diversification of the economies of the acp countries (african, caribbean, pacific countries) with more processing activities and regional trade. we underline the vital importance of promoting public-private partnerships on growth initiatives in european union development policies and of involving the experience, expertise and management systems of the private sector in partnership with public resources. we ask that experience be made available to local authorities in the member states of the european union, for example in setting up infrastructure to fraternize and cooperate with local authorities in developing countries.

in writing. − i voted for the report on trade and investment-driven growth for developing countries because i believe that the eu should have a coherent approach to trade and investment in order to achieve tangible results for sustainable growth in developing countries. we need to foster synergies between trade and development policies in area like agriculture, services, and industry, and to coordinate investment policies at the european level. i strongly support the calls for the establishment of full transparency in our trade relations with developing countries, as it is essential to ensure that trade and investment contribute to improving the living conditions of the populations. since capacity and institution-building are key components of development, i think that improving fiscal governance and fighting against corruption, as well as ensuring an open and participative dialogue with civil society in developing countries, is vital to guaranteeing that investment and trade benefit the citizens. to this end, the eu should include in its trade agreements relevant provisions to encourage responsible investor behaviour and supervise corporate payments.
