in writing. - i voted for the report on trade and investment, engines of growth for developing countries. trade and investment between the european union, developing countries and least developed countries are means of stimulating sustainable and inclusive growth for all, enabling technology and skills transfers and contributing to job creation, enabling increased competitiveness and productivity, as well as achieving greater social cohesion and tackling inequality. we urge the european union to design its trade agreements in such a way as to promote responsible investor behaviour and compliance with international best practices on corporate social responsibility and good corporate governance. we underline that social entrepreneurship and social innovation in developing countries are engines of growth for development and make it possible to reduce inequalities and foster growth, as the benefits are reinvested in the economy. we believe that when used as drivers of growth and sustainable economic development, trade and investment should pursue specific objectives in agriculture, industry, services and administration, while developing the production and infrastructure that they require.
the austerity measures dictated by the 'troika' have caused, for 3 years, an alarming increase in unemployment and the dismantling of the welfare state, with extremely serious consequences, especially for the young and the most vulnerable. in 2011, 27,3% of the population of greece was at risk of poverty and 11% were in a situation of severe material deprivation, without access to electricity and heat. i believe that we cannot allow the european central bank to limit its activity to controlling inflation and to ignore the consequences of its actions on the economic and social situation in europe. in the context of imbalances between the central and peripheral economies, the european central bank proposes a policy geared exclusively to the strongest economies, thus sacrificing, i believe, the future of the majority and the stability of the union as a whole. therefore, growth and job creation are much more important criteria for exiting recession than price stability, and these must become the main objectives of the european central bank. the bank cannot continue to refuse to provide direct financial support to euro area states, given that it offers this type of support to banking entities. finally, i would like to draw attention to the fact that the decisions of the 'troika', which have such important consequences for the lives of europeans, must be subject to democratic control. that is why i think the troika should be held accountable to the european parliament for the actions it is taking.
unemployment in the euro area rose from 10% at the end of 2010 to 10.7% at the end of 2011, with young people being the most affected. over the same period, loans to the private sector fell from 2.4% to 1.2%. i believe that maintaining a flow of credit to smes is particularly important as they employ 72% of the euro area workforce. what is the european central bank's strategy to support growth and reduce unemployment in the european union? finally, i call on the european central bank to follow the recommendations of the commission and the european parliament on improving the gender balance in high-level decision-making bodies in the economic sector. i would stress that the absence of women on the executive board of the european central bank is contrary to the principles enshrined in the treaty on equality between women and men.
parliament's discharge is always a sensitive subject, highly politicized and often highly publicized. i want to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs ortiz, because she has managed to overcome many of the pitfalls of the past years and we have an objective report, a serious report, which we can also put out to the press very well. when we talk about the discharge for 2011, we must bear in mind that this is the second year since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the second year in which the procedures have stabilised somewhat, but also a year in which many other procedures have entered a transitional phase, such as, for example, the internalisation of the european parliament's security. it is also very important to say that in a time of crisis, as representatives of the citizens, we must stand in solidarity with them and the european parliament's expenditure must be taken much more seriously, much more closely watched by us, not only by those outside the european parliament, and we must note that, although parliament has additional powers, it has managed to fit into the budget it had at its disposal, thanks to the efficient spending of the money it had at its disposal. we're talking about a new bid for a travel agency, and i think it's very important that when we're talking about a future agency, we also talk about auditing the agency's business, because it's very important to see how we're going to fit within the money that we have and how low the transportation costs are. last but not least, it is very important that we finance all the projects that promote the work of the european parliament - and i am talking about the communication centre, the house of european history and all the projects that bring groups of citizens from all over europe to visit the european parliament, to see the work of the european parliament and to gain confidence in this institution.
as regards the discharge to the european commission, i consider that the error rate on payments, identified at 3,9% by reference to the total budget, especially in the area of rural development policies ( 7% and regional policy, energy and transport ( 6%), as well as the shortcomings in the control system, remain major problems that need to be addressed quickly. the effectiveness of mechanisms for measuring progress and identifying errors in the implementation of various european policies and projects, and mainly at the level of payments, needs to be increased. the commission should reassess and increase the efficiency of the mechanism for the collection of traditional own resources. reliable data on differences in member states' contributions through vat and customs duties are required. it is expected that an assessment and, by implication, a neutralisation of the sometimes considerable differences between member states in the budgetary contribution in this segment would alleviate some problems that arise subsequently in budget implementation. the high level of error rate in shared management in cohesion policy is also problematic. an important step in improving this situation is to hold the member state responsible by strengthening the safeguards it provides. the structural funds could be used to simplify excessive or exclusive union contribution to certain policies. an example of this could be the policy of decommissioning nuclear power stations, where member states could use their structural funds to reduce the commission's contribution.
mr president, i support the decision of the committee on budgetary control to postpone their decision on discharge for the executive director of the european environment agency. further clarifications on the procurement of video-production contracts are needed before an informed decision can be reached. olaf is currently investigating these contracts. we must wait for the conclusions of the olaf investigation – which will come soon – before we take a final decision on whether or not to grant discharge. how does it look to our citizens if we rush to grant discharge to an executive director while olaf is investigating the procurement process? this investigation is still ongoing. i do not think it will look as if we are protecting taxpayers’ money. it is only fair to our citizens to take an informed decision after olaf’s findings are made available. this will mean taking our decision one way or the other in the autumn. next, i would like to say that i am satisfied that conflict of interest has become an important issue for both the court of auditors and for us in this parliament. it is important to european citizens and therefore it must be important to us. i trust that conflict of interest will stay high on the discharge agenda in all the years to come. and lastly, in the name of transparency, i call once again on all agencies to make available on their websites a list of their management board members, management staff and external and in-house experts, together with their respective declarations of interest and curriculum vitae. this is a way of preventing conflicts of interest, managing them and also of being open with the public. thank you.
i support the discharge to be given to the european agency for network and information security for the financial year 2011. the work of the agency is of particular importance for the security of information networks in europe. the construction of the agency's new headquarters in heraklion, equipped with state-of-the-art equipment and adapted to its operational needs, was completed in 2011 at a cost of eur 6 million according to the agency's technical specifications. i draw the attention of the commission and the agency's management to the need to dimension enisa's budget in line with its tasks and responsibilities, so that the bulk of the budget is allocated to operational activities. the court of auditors found that 33% of the appropriations for the agency's operational budget had been carried over, which may indicate delays in the implementation of its work and is contrary to the budgetary principle of annuality. although the situation has improved compared to the previous year, i believe that firm action is still needed to achieve better budget planning and execution.
the visa facilitation agreement will allow ukrainian citizens to travel more easily within the union. simplifying the requirements for documents justifying the purpose of travel will make it easier for young people to travel, which will encourage their mobility. but i would like to point out that in order to move forward in the dialogue with the union, ukraine must take concrete steps to strengthen democracy. more and more european citizens are being banned from entering ukraine. i take this opportunity to point out that recently, on 1 april, mr vlad burnea, a romanian citizen, that is, a european, a member of the romanian parliament, was informed at the border crossing that he was not allowed to enter ukraine, without being told the reason. he was going to cernăuţi to participate in an action of the romanian community.
first of all, i would like to thank mrs hübner for her excellent cooperation and for her willingness to include in the compromise amendments the additions i proposed to this report. in practice, the proposal for a regulation establishing a financial assistance mechanism for member states whose currency is not the euro responds to a vital need to ensure a level playing field for non-euro area countries, in a context where the economic crisis has affected the whole of the european union, causing a deterioration in the public deficit, the balance of payments and the overall debt. unlike the euro area countries, which benefit from the european stability mechanism with a lending capacity of eur 500 billion, non-euro area countries can access limited funds of up to eur 50 billion through the balance of payments facility. i welcome the increase from 12 billion to 50 billion in 2009, but this is still far below the amount available to the euro area countries. however, the commission proposal aims to align the conditions and procedures for obtaining a financial loan with those specific to the countries which have adopted the single currency. basically, equal obligations mean, and should mean, equal benefits. i therefore support the rapporteur's proposal to create a bank recapitalisation facility for non-euro countries. member states outside the euro area also need a fiscal backstop. however, a direct bank recapitalisation instrument would be preferable, with the aim of avoiding the fragmentation of the single market and lower competitiveness for member states that have not yet joined the single currency.
mr president, my country – romania – received financial assistance from the union in a very difficult moment of this current crisis, and i would like to express my gratitude to all member states and european institutions for this help. however, when in difficulties, the countries outside the eurozone feel that they do not have access to the same range of financial instruments as the eurozone countries have. i therefore fully support the proposal of mrs hübner, our rapporteur, to raise this issue in the report. in particular i support the proposal to create a special financial instrument for the recapitalisation of banks and to attach to this instrument a conditionality requiring sound monetary, fiscal and economic policies.
the revision of the existing regulation would allow member states whose currency is not the euro to have instruments similar to those of euro area countries. my country was among the first to benefit from financial assistance from the union, thanks to the balance of payments assistance mechanism. through the assistance, romania was able to stabilise its public finances and embark on a number of important reforms. so, despite the very high political costs, my country has managed to reduce the budget deficit and keep the public debt under control. but there is now a risk that some commitments in the current agreement with the imf and the european commission will not be met by the current socialist government. such a scenario would jeopardise all the reform and stabilisation efforts made by previous right-wing governments.
the unprecedented financial situation of recent years has seriously damaged economic growth and financial stability, leading to an increase in public deficits and debt in many member states, both within and outside the euro area. since the negative effects in the member states whose currency is not the euro can spread very easily throughout the european union, i believe it is prudent and necessary that these countries participating in the single supervisory mechanism also benefit from the bank recapitalisation facility provided for by the european stability mechanism. moreover, given that many of these countries face major difficulties in accessing community financial instruments, the provision of increased financial assistance under the balance of payments mechanism will lead to an improvement in administrative capacity and, by implication, to an increase in the absorption of european funds.
the financial crisis has had a considerable impact on the development of member states' budgets, which has required an increase in the balance of payments assistance facility to eur 50 billion. significant sums have been made available to countries facing difficulties, including my own country, romania. however, there are some shortcomings in the implementation of the provisions of this mechanism, as non-euro area countries do not benefit from the same financial instruments as euro area countries. there is a need to identify similar conditions between euro area and non-euro area countries, although the newly created euro area mechanisms make this more difficult. balance of payments financial assistance can make a significant contribution to the achievement of several objectives by strengthening administrative capacity and, as a result, by increasing the absorption rate of cohesion policy funds. i fully support mrs hübner's proposals and congratulate her on her excellent report.
in writing. we have seen the eu quickly intervene in favour of some euro area countries, which is a positive fact, but at the same time we cannot ignore the fact that there are many countries, including romania, that are outside the euro area and that, in complicated situations, need europe's support. not being part of the euro area has a number of disadvantages which we accept, but in the cohesion process, measures are needed, mechanisms to support these countries, as has happened with the other countries. such a measure would have positive effects not only on the states in the area but also on europeanism as a public perception. i welcome the presence of a wide range of financial assistance instruments available to non-euro area member states, as provided for in the balance of payments proposal, but attention should be drawn to the lack of a bank recapitalisation instrument in the package of financial assistance measures available to non-euro area member states. in order to ensure a level playing field between euro area and non-euro area member states, it is important to move towards bank recapitalisation in non-euro area member states as well.
i appreciate that the new guidelines on regional state aid are a step towards simplifying the rules and making them more flexible. however, i would like to stress that the new guidelines refer to a completely different economic situation than that of the previous regulatory period. in those circumstances, i consider that the new restrictions imposed in the areas covered by article 107 (3) (c) and relating to aid to large undertakings in the community sense are not justified. there are many businesses with local relevance that exceed the threshold proposed by the employees. there is no contradiction between supporting these businesses and supporting small and mediumsized businesses, as the green member has suggested. however, i agree with the proposal of my colleague and other colleagues that a state-supported enterprise should be obliged to remain in that state. in addition, when establishing the criteria for delimiting the areas covered by regional state aid, the commission should take into account the specificities of certain regions, such as rural areas, regions with natural handicaps, mountain regions, regions with an ageing population or those with chronic unemployment.
although the role of regional state aid is indisputable in increasing the competitiveness of enterprises and attracting investors in underdeveloped regions, measures taken to protect competition have led to an excessive limitation of the eligibility conditions for the granting of these incentives. it should be borne in mind that competition for investors is often between european regions and non-eu countries, and the strictness of state aid rules means that our regions start at a disadvantage. in this context, i believe that, in times of economic crisis, we need a new european strategy: 1) adapted to international competition, 2) limiting the restrictions imposed on aid to large enterprises and 3) linked to the other european policies, namely cohesion policy and industrial policy.
regional state aid should exploit the growth potential of the single market in a context of limited public resources. romania is directly interested in the new guidelines proposed by the commission, especially as most of the regions will fall under category a. thus, undertakings in difficulty are subject to state aid schemes to the extent that they fulfil the legal conditions. in the last period, several romanian plants in the steel or petrochemical industry have faced economic difficulties, and some of them have ended up making massive layoffs. i believe that in the next financial programming period, member states should make the most efficient use of budgetary resources. state aid should also be targeted at enterprises that can generate economic growth and contribute to reducing unemployment.
in romania, the government wants to change the country's administrative structure by the end of this year. the reason: the current statistical development regions are not efficient enough in using cohesion resources. that's right. but i doubt that the administration of regions designated 15 years ago, in a careless and unprofessional manner, will help romania's capacity to use resources. the european union regulations will be used as a reason to cement the wrong regional classification. the reform of a country's public administration is a national responsibility, but if eu regulations are invoked to make better use of cohesion resources, perhaps the european commission could also give its opinion on the matter. i don't think that the most appropriate principle in the process of regional development is for the governing parties to have as little interest in their own local politicians as possible. it is much more appropriate to base economic indicators on individual regions, to create regions which have been created organically in the course of history. in the case of romania, these regions can be identified.
in the context of the current crisis, the revision of the 2014-2020 regional state aid guidelines can play a crucial role in boosting growth, but the new guidelines must create the conditions for modernising the methods of allocating such aid, simplifying procedures and minimising the risk of possible future economic slippages. there is a need for a balanced delimitation of areas in the allocation of aid so that economically backward regions are effectively supported by reducing existing disparities. i would like to draw attention to the risk of the relocation of economic activities both within and outside the union, as a result of the limitation of the possibilities for public intervention in favour of large enterprises. more coherence between the regional aid guidelines and cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020 must also be ensured, with attention also paid to innovation and research. i say this with pain at a time when the government of my country, a socialist-liberal government, is cutting funding for research and innovation.
in writing. the constitutional situation in hungary raises obvious questions. in 2010, fidesz, led by viktor orban, won the elections to the hungarian parliament with a majority of 53% of the popular vote, which according to the hungarian electoral system turned into a supermajority of 68% of the total number of mps. what followed the installation of the orban government was an avalanche of amendments to the constitution of hungary, many of which seemed to favour the executive and the ruling party. whether we are talking about the electoral law, which was also declared unconstitutional by the constitutional court of hungary, or we are talking about absurd initiatives to criminalize homeless people or laws restricting the freedom of the press it is quite clear that the current constitutional situation in hungary is not reassuring. hungary's new constitution has been criticized by the european parliament, the united states, the council of europe, the european commission, various member states, and various human rights organizations for giving too much power to the ruling party. i therefore believe that the european institutions must take action to investigate possible democratic abuses and oversteps by the hungarian executive.

mr president, i voted to grant discharge to the secretary-general of the european economic and social committee for the financial year 2011 in order to acknowledge the efforts made in terms of budgetary and financial management. i welcome in particular the committee’s efforts to limit its budget for 2013 by keeping it at the level of 2012 as well as the cooperation agreement reached between the committee and the committee of the regions, which should enable it to make savings and synergies of around eur 40 million. i also welcome the fact that the declarations of financial interests of the committee’s members are now publicly available.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it is important to strengthen cooperation between the members of the european economic and social committee and the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament. i welcome the fact that, on the basis of its audit work, the european court of auditors considers that, overall, the payments for administrative and other expenditure of the institutions and bodies for the year ended 31 december 2011 were not affected by a significant level of error. i would point out that in the 2011 annual report the court of auditors included observations on the conclusion of contracts with temporary and contract staff, identifying a number of inconsistencies in the guidelines applicable to promotion and recruitment of staff.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the discharge for the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2011, section vi european economic and social committee. on the basis of its audit work, the european court of auditors considers that, overall, the payments made by the european economic and social committee (eesc) for administrative and other expenditure of the institutions and bodies for the year ended 31 december 2011 were not affected by a significant level of error. we support the eesc's efforts to limit its 2013 budget to the 2012 level and thus ensure a flat-rate increase. we draw attention to the obligation to publish data on energy consumption and the share of renewable energy. parliament also asked the eesc to present in its annual report information on specific budgetary savings resulting from the implementation of a joint agreement on administrative activities. we would point out that in the 2011 annual report the court of auditors included observations on the conclusion of contracts with temporary and contract staff, identifying a number of inconsistencies in the guidelines applicable to promotion and recruitment of staff. we ask the european economic and social committee to guarantee that these inconsistencies will not occur again.
mr president, i voted in favour of granting the discharge to the secretary-general of the committee of the regions for the financial year 2011, following the positive opinion of the court of auditors and in particular the fact that no significant weaknesses had been identified in respect of human resources and moreover in respect of procurement. however, action should be taken in order to improve the budget execution rate, which fell from 99.4% in 2010 to 97.5% in 2011. i welcome the reforms implemented to make savings, such as the progressive phasing-in of video-conferencing, which should allow for lower travel expenses, or the cooperation agreements signed with the european economic and social committee aiming at creating synergies and enabling savings, for instance in terms of translation services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because, overall, the payments for administrative and other expenditure of the institutions and bodies for the year ended 31 december 2011 were not affected by a significant level of error. i welcome the committee of the regions' internal organisation projects, which aim to promote cooperation between services and to create synergies through joint activities and actions. i am pleased to note that the recommendations and requirements made by parliament's committee on budgetary control are recorded by the committee's budget service in a central database and that the progress of their implementation is regularly monitored.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the discharge for the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2011, section vii committee of the regions. the new role of the committee, as described in the treaty on the functioning of the european union, requires organisational adjustments. we welcome the committee's internal organisation projects, which aim at cooperation between services and the creation of synergies in joint activities and actions, and we ask for updated and more precise information to be provided to the european parliament on the budgetary consequences of the measures adopted. we also stress that, for reasons of transparency, the declarations of financial interests of the members of all institutions, updated regularly, should be accessible on the internet. in this regard, we welcome the decision taken in 2011 by the committee bureau to publish the declarations of financial interests of members on the internet and hope that they will become accessible as soon as possible. i voted against amendment no 1, which calls for the committee of the regions, as a body designed to give a relatively small number of bodies privileged access to the legislative and policy-making process within the union, to finance its activities through contributions from local and regional bodies which it considers serve a valuable purpose.
mr president, with regard to the european ombudsman, i also voted for discharge to be granted for the financial year 2011, following the positive opinion of the court of auditors and in particular the fact that no significant weaknesses had been identified in respect of procurement and human resources. i welcome the fact that the european ombudsman service managed to improve its budget commitment rate by nearly three points from almost 89% to 92.54% and its budget execution rate by one point from 84% to 85.62% since 2010. this is not a large difference but it is nevertheless a difference and shows progress. i expect further improvements in this area in the future. nevertheless, the average length of inquiries continued to increase in 2011. only 66% of cases were closed within 12 months, while 80% of cases were closed within 18 months. adequate and immediate measures should be implemented to reduce the length of procedures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because in its 2011 annual report, the european court of auditors found no significant deficiencies in the european ombudsman's audited aspects of human resources and procurement procedures. i note that of the total appropriations, 92,54% were committed (89,65% in 2010) and 85,62% were paid (84,03% in 2010). i welcome the improvement in utilization. i believe that further efforts should be made to improve the rate of use and to monitor changes made. further progress is needed in ensuring timely feedback on actual payments.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's decision of 17 april 2013 on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2011, section viii european ombudsman, granting the european ombudsman discharge. the ombudsman's budget is purely administrative, amounting in 2011 to eur 9 427 395, of which eur 7 318 795 was allocated to title 1 (expenditure relating to the institution's staff), eur 1 469 200 was allocated to title 2 (buildings, equipment and miscellaneous operating expenditure) and eur 639 400 was allocated to title 3 (expenditure relating to the institution's performance of its specific tasks). of the total appropriations, 92,54% were committed (89,65% in 2010) and 85,62% were paid (84,03% in 2010). the european parliament calls for further efforts to improve the rate of use and to monitor changes made. the european parliament notes with concern that the average duration of investigations continued to increase in 2011, with only 66% of cases closed within 12 months and 80% of cases closed within 18 months. we are calling for a substantial increase in the proportion of cases that are completed in a shorter time frame.
mr president, i voted for granting the discharge to the european data protection supervisor for the financial year 2011, bearing in mind the opinion of the court of auditors and also the fact that public procurement rules were respected. i welcome the fact that the data protection supervisor has managed to improve significantly its budget commitment rate from 82.73% to 89.31% since 2010. nevertheless, further efforts are needed in order to reach an implementing and execution rate above 90%.
i voted in favour of the report because the protection of personal data and respect for privacy are fundamental rights. i welcome the fact that the balance of payments executed in 2011 by the european data protection supervisor is free from material error. however, the authority needs to continue to improve its monitoring and control system. particular attention shall be paid to the economic management and efficient use of appropriations in the exercise of the authority's responsibilities. i believe that a twofold interest must be pursued: effective data protection and the provision of low-cost services. a differentiated approach is also needed for the online and offline domain. we need to increase citizens' trust and impose security guarantees. i also call on the national supervisory authority for the processing of personal data in romania to monitor data more effectively.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2011, section ix - european data protection supervisor. this decision gives the european data protection supervisor discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2011. in 2011, the authority had commitment appropriations totalling eur 7 564 137 (eur 7 104 351 in 2010) and the level of implementation of these appropriations was 89,31% (82,73% in 2010). the european parliament calls for further efforts to improve the level of implementation and for changes to be monitored. parliament also requests the authority to draw up the draft annual budget so that it better corresponds to the authority's needs. we welcome the authority's inspection reports on 13 eu institutions and bodies based in brussels, which aimed to verify whether the public is informed about video surveillance in a comprehensive and effective way by the eu institutions and bodies. the european parliament suggests that information and good practice be exchanged with national data protection authorities.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2011, section x european external action service (eeas). although 2011 was its first financial year, the eeas bears full responsibility for the financial year 2011 and must ensure strict compliance with the legislation. in this respect, we call for greater transparency in the competences of the eeas's administrative structure and for the reduction of dual competences. we regret that the proportion of staff from the newer member states is very small compared to the eu-15 staff. we stress the need to achieve a gender balance and, as far as possible, a more pronounced geographical balance in the selection and appointment of staff. we urge the eeas to develop appropriate mechanisms and take the necessary measures to achieve a more adequate and balanced representation in a timely manner and we urge the eeas to use the vacant posts to achieve geographical balance at all staff levels. we ask the eeas to forward its staff evaluation report to parliament. finally, we remind the eeas of its responsibility to deliver concrete results and stress the importance of respecting the reciprocity between the results achieved and the overall budget.
mr president, i support the provisions related to transparency and conflict of interest that are included in this report. i welcome in particular the fact that it calls for follow-up to the special report on the management and prevention of conflict of interest, a work which was produced last year during the discharge of the european agencies. i insist also on the fact that high-level transparency is key to mitigating the risk of conflict of interest. therefore i urge all agencies that have not yet done so to publish on their websites a list of their management board members, management staff, external and in-house experts together with their respective declarations of interest and curriculum vitae. however, i would like to say that i voted against amendment 15 because it considers that the potential merger of agencies would have a hasty effect and should be disregarded by the commission. on the contrary, i believe that mergers offer the possibility to avoid duplication, with agencies having overlapping fields of activities; to solve some structural issues; to make those agencies more efficient and to save taxpayers’ money.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because annuality is one of the three basic accounting principles (unity, annuality and balance) and is indispensable to ensure the efficient execution of the european union budget. i am pleased to note that the newly established agencies attend the network meetings three times a year and that these meetings include exchanges of good practice. however, in some cases, improvements in internal planning are needed, as agencies need to improve their procedures. the lack of flexibility in the budget was flagged as a shortcoming by some agencies, indicating that savings could be made if there was sufficient flexibility from one title to another in the budget.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european union agencies for the financial year 2011: performance, financial management and control. the european parliament underlines the importance of the tasks carried out by the agencies and their direct impact on the daily lives of citizens, in particular as regards the quality of medicines, food safety, aviation security and the control of infectious disease outbreaks. in this context, we underline the essential importance of the autonomy of agencies, in particular regulatory agencies and those performing the function of independent information gathering, and recall that the main purpose of the creation of decentralised agencies was to carry out independent technical and scientific assessments. the european parliament considers that the financial rules applicable to the agencies should be simplified, which would allow for the reduction of costs associated with the administrative staff of the agencies. the european commission is invited to develop proposals in this regard and to encourage agencies to use the option of simplification in recruitment procedures where the standard procedure is designed for a larger organisation and creates an excessive burden for the agents.

mr president, we granted discharge to the executive director of the european police college for 2011 in order to acknowledge the efforts it has made in the last few years – and in the last two years in particular –in terms of budgetary and financial management. however, some weaknesses remained in 2011 such as the use of payments on incorrect budget lines within chapters or titles. i expect the college to take action to prevent the occurrence of such weaknesses in the future and to keep the discharge authority informed. moreover, the college will have to leave its current premises in 2014. therefore i believe we should make full use of this opportunity and relocate the college to the hague, where europol and eurojust are located. in my view such relocation has the potential to foster further synergies between the different agencies, solves the current remoteness issue of the college and leads to economies of taxpayer’s money.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european banking authority for the financial year 2011. this decision gives the executive director of the european banking authority discharge in respect of the implementation of the authority's budget for the financial year 2011. the authority is a newly established agency based in london, which was established by regulation (eu) no 1093/2010 and officially started its operations on 1 january 2011 as an independent authority. the authority has taken over all existing and current tasks and responsibilities from its predecessor, the committee of european banking supervisors (cebs). the authority shall also be an integral part of the european system of financial supervisors and shall work in close cooperation with the other european supervisory authorities, the european insurance and occupational pensions authority and the european securities and markets authority, within a joint committee, as well as with the european systemic risk board. in accordance with the founding regulation, 60% of the 2011 budget was financed by contributions from the member states and the european free trade association (efta) member states, and 40% was financed from the union budget. parliament called on the commission to assess the possibility of developing a proposal for the financing of the european supervisory authorities (esas) budget entirely from the union budget.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european centre for disease prevention and control for the financial year 2011, giving the director of the european centre for disease prevention and control discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget. the european parliament notes that 2011 was the first year in which the court of auditors delivered a qualified opinion on the centre's annual accounts. in 2009, the centre concluded a framework contract with a maximum value of eur 9 million, which allowed it to sign specific contracts, up to this amount, with selected suppliers. following subsequent amendments, the value of these contracts increased to eur 14,9 million. by the end of 2011, payments made totalled eur 12,2 million, of which eur 3,2 million were payments made in 2011. commitments and payments exceeding the threshold of eur 9 million set in the framework contract are not in compliance. the european parliament notes that in 2011, the public procurement office was involved in the organisation of 60 open procedures, 59 tenders and a call for tenders, and in the reopening of 46 procedures (framework contracts for it services).
mr president, i voted to grant discharge to the executive director of the european chemicals agency for the year 2011. i regret, however, that until september 2011, the agency’s policies for managing conflicts of interest were incomplete. for instance, the declarations of interest were neither screened nor published but were sealed. training on conflicts of interest was absent. so if we do have a policy on conflicts of interest, we have to demonstrate this and make public all these declarations of interest and not keep them closed in a room. i welcome the fact that, in the meantime, the agency adopted a new policy for the management of potential conflicts of interest, a more detailed template for declarations of interest and a code of conduct for management board members. however, in my view, adopting policies is not enough. we need the rules to be implemented transparently. i call, therefore, for the introduction in the agency’s annual activity report of a special section describing the action taken to prevent and manage conflicts of interest.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european chemicals agency for the financial year 2011. in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1907/2006, the agency is financed by fees paid by industry for the registration of chemicals and, where appropriate, by grants from the european union, in accordance with article 185 of the financial regulation. in 2011, the agency was entirely self-financed by fees and did not receive any subsidy from the union budget. the agency was supported from the union budget by the commission (dg environment) with a sum of only eur 500 000, contractual compensation for carrying out preparatory work for the new regulation (eu) no 528/2012 on biocidal products (7). according to the court of auditors' report, the agency's general budget for the financial year 2011 was eur 93 200 000, compared to eur 75 500 000 in 2010, representing an increase of 23,44%. the total carry-over of appropriations for commitments and payments was eur 14 421 314,76, representing 16,2% of the commitments provided for. we ask the agency to inform on the measures taken to remedy the deficiencies caused by the excessive level of carry-overs, as this situation is contrary to the budgetary principle of annuality.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european institute of innovation and technology for the financial year 2011. in 2010 and 2011, the institute and its partner directorate-general, the directorate-general for education and culture (dg eac), worked together to create the appropriate internal structures and procedures to enable the institute to manage union funds in accordance with the principle of sound financial management and to meet the minimum conditions for financial autonomy. those conditions shall establish the following: effective separation of the tasks of the authorising officer and the accounting officer; a functioning accounting system enabling the use of funds to be verified and reflected in the union accounts; an appropriate payment procedure ensuring sound financial management of union funds. on 23 march 2010, the institute signed a hosting agreement with the government of hungary. under this agreement, the host member state undertakes to contribute to the institute's staff costs, which must cover the salaries of 20 staff members, for a period of five years. the 2011 contribution shall consist of five annual instalments of eur 1 560 000.

mr president, i supported the proposal to grant discharge to the executive director of the european network and information security agency and voted in favour of amendments 1 and 3, which delete paragraph 9 of the present report. although i strongly condemn the duplication of resources or agencies having two different seats, i believe that the present case is somehow different. from a practical point of view, the agency in its current location in heraklion experienced difficulties related to access to the island and the lack of services such as schooling. as a consequence, it was difficult to attract and keep duly-qualified staff members, and travel costs relating to missions were very high. though imperfect, i believe that the compromise found by opening a branch of the agency in athens will help solve some of the problems associated with running the agency. this proves once again that whenever an agency is created, we should refrain from setting it up in a remote location, because in the end this will always lead to severe infrastructure issues and we will always find that we spend much more money on such agencies, in terms of both administration and staffing.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the estimate of the revenue and expenditure budget of the european parliament for the financial year 2014. in the absence of an agreement on the regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework (mff) by the end of the year, article 312 (4) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides for the application of the ceilings corresponding to the last year of the current mff, and article 30 of the current interinstitutional agreement on budgetary discipline and sound financial management provides for the extension of the 2013 ceilings, adjusted on the basis of a fixed deflator of 2% per year, until the adoption of a new mff. it is noted that in 2014 all costs related to the accession of croatia will have to be covered for a full year. the estimated direct costs, which could amount to eur 13,6 million, including support for croatia's integration into the union, are noted. we believe that in the current austerity context, long-term investments such as parliament's real estate projects should be managed with prudence and transparency. we stress that the financial implications of the european elections are exceptional and acknowledge the efforts already made to budget these one-off costs. the secretary-general is requested to find a way to spread these costs over the entire parliamentary term in the future.
in writing. − one of the main reasons for the success of the european project is the importance that both the european institutions and the member states have attached to political and institutional solidarity. as the relationship between european states is not only one of close political, cultural and social ties but also of deep economic interdependence, the creation of a financial assistance mechanism for non-euro area states is important for the strengthening of the european union. i support the development of this mechanism, because it is also necessary for the coordination of institutional dynamics outside the euro area. as a number of legislative measures have significantly changed the institutional relationships within the euro area in recent years, it is necessary to adapt the links with the member states of the european union that have not adopted the single european currency to the new financial architecture. the development of the european union depends on the creation of a mechanism capable of ensuring a level playing field between actors in the euro area member states and those operating in non-euro area countries.
in writing. − at the european summit in june 2012, the heads of state or government announced that, once the single supervisory mechanism was operational, the european stability mechanism could be used directly to recapitalise euro area banks. however, the same possibility would not exist for non-euro area member states opting for single supervision. member states outside the euro area have access to the balance of payments (bop) instrument, whose means are, however, limited compared to the european stability mechanism. however, the instrument has limited funds at its disposal. the bp instrument is considered not to exceed eur 60 billion. this funding limit is due to the fact that the funds are guaranteed by the eu budget.
in writing. − this interim report is a welcome proposal, introducing procedures for the granting of financial assistance between the euro area and the non-euro area. in order to ensure a level playing field between euro area and non-euro area member states, there is a need to promote a position to ensure that banks are recapitalised also in non-euro area member states. romania was one of the first countries to benefit from the balance of payments facility to stabilise its public finances. this balance of payments (bop) instrument will benefit all non-euro area countries in difficulty without access to the european stability mechanism.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this interim report, which is a step forward in the process of creating the banking union with its three components: the single supervisory mechanism, the single regulatory authority and the single deposit guarantee scheme. the main unresolved issue in this project remains the relationship with the non-euro area member states. they can join the single supervisory mechanism on a voluntary basis, but it is essential that the future single resolution fund be accessible to them in order to make it possible to recapitalise banks in non-euro area member states as well. most banks in countries that have not yet adopted the single currency come from the euro area, so the interdependencies are very strong and the mutual impact can be major in financial and economic terms. a fair, solidary and effective solution is therefore needed.
in writing. − i welcome the rapporteur's proposal on the possibility of establishing an indirect bank recapitalisation facility for the union countries not yet part of the euro area, for the possible involvement of these eu countries in the future single supervisory mechanism and in view of the need to provide them with a fiscal protection mechanism.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation establishing a financial assistance mechanism for member states whose currency is not the euro, as the economic crisis has had a severe impact on them, causing a rapid deterioration in both their public deficit and balance of payments and their overall debt. member states outside the euro area have access to the balance of payments facility, but its resources are limited compared with the european stability mechanism. the initiative to streamline the procedures for granting financial assistance between the euro area and the non-euro area is therefore welcome. in this context, clear objectives and precise guidelines are needed in the elaboration and evaluation of the macroeconomic adjustment programme, in particular with regard to the procedural and policy requirements aimed at restoring a sustainable balance of payments and restoring the capacity of the state to fully fund itself on the financial markets. thus, to ensure a genuine level playing field between euro-area and non-euro-area member states, it is necessary to move in a direction that allows for bank recapitalisation in non-euro-area member states as well.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing a financial assistance mechanism for member states whose currency is not the euro. in 2002, council regulation (ec) no 332/2002 established the balance of payments (bop) mechanism, which provides financial assistance to member states whose currency is not the euro. the total amount available under that facility was increased from the initial amount of eur 12 billion to eur 25 billion in december 2008 and to eur 50 billion in may 2009 in response to the financial crisis. of the eur 50 billion, eur 13,4 billion was paid for romania, latvia and hungary, in addition to the precautionary reserve of eur 1,4 billion for romania. bp's financial assistance can play an important role in supporting member states to improve their administrative capacity to absorb union funds more efficiently. i voted for both the council and the commission to take account of a number of requests before the proposal for a regulation is sent to the european parliament. among these requests, i consider it important that no link or material conditionality be established between the bp mechanism and the use of the structural funds in the bp proposal.
with economic growth of only 1.5%, 2011 was a particularly important year for the european central bank. it represents a period in which the risks to the stabilisation of the euro area have increased considerably. no one disputes the outstanding achievements of the european central bank, but despite the improvements made during 2011, there were problems that persist today due to the bank's inability to send positive signals to the markets. the expansionary policies of this institution did not have the expected effects in terms of credit growth, but on the contrary, loans to the private sector halved, from 2,4% in 2010 to 1,2% in 2011. as a lack of credit is one of the main reasons for the slowdown in the european economy, i call on both the european central bank and the commission to focus their efforts in the future on promoting reforms to improve access to finance, strengthen global competitiveness and, by implication, generate sustainable economic growth.
mr president, mr luhan asked me to ask you if you also have explanations of vote on the lópez-istúriz white report.
in writing. − the actions taken by the european central bank in 2011-12 have played an important role in ensuring the stability of the euro area and financial markets. maintaining this proactive stance of the institution is essential for european economies to successfully overcome the consequences of the economic and financial crisis. the institutional continuity of these interventions by the european central bank is important for the credibility of the single european currency in particular and of the european union as a whole. however, many questions still need to be answered. the level of corporate and household borrowing is still lower than before the crisis. equally worrying is the fact that the level of loans to this destination decreased in real terms during 2011. in addition, together with the european central bank, european decision-makers must take measures to stimulate sme financing, as this segment of european economies is significant for the overall competitiveness of the european union and its innovative capacity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because 2011 was a year of many challenges caused by economic and financial conditions. this explains the need for changes in the guidelines and procedures of the european central bank (ecb) during the year. in this context, the ecb has consistently sought to create an anchor of stability and confidence. in the second half of 2011, the inflation rate in romania decreased considerably from 7.5% to 3.4% due to both internal and external factors. domestic demand also contributed to the gdp growth. on another note, i would like to point out that since 2011 the governing council of the european central bank has been represented by men only, and i believe that a change must be made in this regard.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european central bank's 2011 activity report. the measures taken by the troika have not produced the expected results. moreover, they have caused a worsening of the economic situation. the european union is now in recession, and many countries are experiencing very high unemployment. in this context, the troika must be subject to democratic control
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the 2011 annual report of the european central bank as, under article 282 tfeu, the primary objective of the ecb is to maintain price stability and the ecb should support the general economic policies of the union without affecting price stability. i voted for paragraph 18 which stresses that institutions that have received very significant liquidity support from the central bank should be subject to conditionality, including through the commitment by the institutions receiving such support to increase the level of lending by setting lending targets for the real economy, in particular for small and medium-sized enterprises and households, without which these efforts could prove ineffective. i voted against amendment 8 which removes these conditions and replaces them with monitoring. in the absence of appropriate conditionality, non-standardised measures may not produce the desired effects but may increase volatility and encourage asset bubbles in financial markets or facilitate the process of reducing leverage without significant credit allocation counterparts. we therefore ask the ecb to carefully analyse the effects, both positive and negative, of these and other measures.
mr president, i voted for the discharge of the executive director of the european railway agency for 2011. in particular, i strongly support paragraph 11, which calls on the agency to scrutinise and prohibit possible conflicts of interest when hiring experts and staff from the sector it supervises. i regret that the agency is based in two different locations. this brings inefficiency and additional costs. the situation should therefore be solved as a matter of urgency. the two locations should merge into one in order to save money, time and human resources.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the european railway agency for the financial year 2011, as the court of auditors has informed the european parliament of the assurances it has obtained as regards the reliability of the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2011. for the coming period, the agency will face a major challenge, namely the replacement of half of its operational staff. however, i would like to point out that the use of two headquarters by the agency leads to reduced efficiency and higher costs. the possible conflicts of interest will also have to be investigated more closely.
in writing. − i voted to close the accounts of the european railway agency for the financial year 2011 because the agency contributes to the creation of a european railway area without borders and to ensuring a high level of safety, in a context where the european railway market remains fragmented and the interoperability of systems has not been achieved. we note that the rate of payments related to budget appropriations improved for all titles, but remained low for title iii 'operational expenditure', at 47% (39% in 2010). we call on the agency to take further action to address this situation as it is contrary to the principle of annuality. it is also recalled that the agency will have to replace half of its operational staff in the period 2013-2015. in this context, we ask the agency to carefully manage the duration of the contracts of the temporary staff members in order to ensure that the fulfilment of the agency's main tasks is not affected. we call on the agency to improve its staff selection procedures to ensure full transparency and equal treatment for all candidates.
mr president, the european securities and markets authority was granted discharge today. i believe the current financing scheme of the authority should be addressed as soon as possible, given that 60% of the budget is financed by the contributions of member states and efta countries. in my view this puts the independence of the authority at risk. therefore, i support paragraph 4 of the present report, which calls on the commission to evaluate the possibility of having the european securities and market authority, the european banking authority and the european insurance and occupational pensions authority funded entirely from the union budget. moreover, i commend the management board’s decision of january 2011 establishing the terms and conditions for internal investigations with regard to the prevention of fraud, corruption and illegal activity detrimental to the union’s interest.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because there were reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the annual accounts of the european securities and markets authority for the financial year 2011 and as to the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. however, some of the provisions of the financial regulation are not fully adapted to the authority's funding scheme. 60% of the budget of the authority is financed by contributions from the member states and efta countries. the budget execution rate was also not very high. it is welcome, however, that the authority's recruitment procedures have become consistent with the recommendations of the court of auditors.
in writing. − i voted to grant discharge to the authority in respect of the implementation of its budget for the financial year 2011. the authority, a newly created agency based in paris, was established by regulation (eu) no 1095/2010 and officially started its operations on 1 january 2011 as an independent authority. the general budget allocated to the authority for the financial year 2011 was eur 16 964 913,92. in accordance with the founding regulation, 60% of the 2011 budget was financed by contributions from the member states and the european free trade association (efta) member states, and 40% was financed from the union budget. the applicable provisions of the financial regulation are thus not fully adapted to the authority's financing scheme, as 60% of its budget is financed by contributions from the member states and efta states. we consider that this issue should be addressed at the latest at the next revision of the financial regulation as regards the agencies and ask the commission to assess this situation and report accordingly to the discharge authority.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the discharge report on the implementation of the budget of the european training foundation for the financial year 2011, as the european court of auditors stated that it had obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the foundation's annual accounts for the financial year 2011 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. at the end of the financial year 2011, the foundation had a positive budget result of eur 117 686,58. the annual activity report of the foundation (aar) also indicates that it achieved a loan commitment rate of 99,69%, similar to the execution rate in 2010, but higher in nominal terms. we would like to underline that the foundation has successfully continued, for the second year running, the torino process, which aims to provide a concise, well-founded and comprehensive analysis of vocational education and training reform in each country, including the identification of key policy trends, challenges, constraints, good practices and opportunities. the findings of the analyses undertaken since 2010 are to be further consolidated at the conference and the agreement on the torino declaration, as well as the torinet initiative on capacity building in evidence-based policy making.

i voted for this report because the procedures for granting financial assistance between the euro area and the non-euro area need to be harmonised. romania received €5 billion in financial assistance from the european union between 2009 and 2011 through the balance of payments facility. this contributed significantly to the reduction of the budget deficit to below 3% of gdp, as assessed by the commission in its last assessment in january 2013. this is why non-euro area member states must continue to benefit from financial instruments in the event of a deterioration in the economic situation, and the increase in available funds to eur 60 billion must be harnessed, used to its full potential. these states must be subject to a strict oversight process to ensure that the funds are used by the authorities of the member states exclusively for the purpose of financial recovery.
- i voted for this report. the market for security coupons amounts to 52 billion euros annually. in cross-border trading activities in securities, the different legal frameworks in the member states lead to ambiguous and dysfunctional situations that allow intermediaries to avoid taxation. the harmonization and clarification of vat rules applied to vouchers in all member states will simplify cross-border business relations between companies and consumers, especially as regards the payment of tax obligations. this will lead to a reduction in tax evasion, fraud and money laundering. i urge the commission to ensure and monitor the proper implementation of these regulations.
in writing. − several eu countries are currently facing the very critical problem of falling government revenue. overcoming the effects of the financial and economic crisis requires a high degree of stability of public finances. the adoption of measures which have the potential to increase both the efficiency and the transparency of the vat collection system on vouchers may be an appropriate solution in the current economic and financial circumstances. at the same time, these measures must strike a balance between the need for stability of public finances and the proper functioning of the internal market. the creation of an effective and uniform european statute, respecting the conditions of fair competition and the principle of avoiding double taxation, can lead to a more effective fight against tax evasion and to an improvement in the rate of collection of value added tax. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because it is necessary to clarify and harmonise the european union rules on the application of vat to vouchers. this will have a positive effect on business by eliminating double taxation situations and uncertainty about tax compliance. it will also close loopholes that facilitate tax evasion by some companies that take advantage of differences in regulation between member states. by clarifying and harmonising eu rules on the vat treatment of vouchers, this proposal will significantly improve the functioning of loyalty schemes and gift vouchers. from a commercial point of view, this proposal will avoid market dysfunctions and situations of double taxation or non-taxation.
in writing. - a market of coupons worth over eur 50 billion a year is not negligible and, given that no directive has so far provided for rules on transactions with these instruments, i believe that we urgently need a common solution at union level. there are many cases where member states have tried to regulate this issue at national level and the result has not been the expected one. while some of these have accused the tax authorities of double taxation, there have been countless cases in which they have been accused of tax evasion. in this respect, i believe that a better classification of value coupons, the adaptation of the vat regime for this type of product and the transposition of the new community regulations at national level will clarify all tax uncertainties and remove one of the last barriers to traders who want to take advantage of the opportunities of the single market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the common system of value added tax as regards the treatment of value coupons. council directive 2006/112/ec of 28 november 2006 on the common system of value added tax lays down rules on the time and place of supply of goods and services, the taxable amount, the chargeability of value added tax (vat) and the right to deduct. however, those rules are not sufficiently clear or exhaustive to ensure the consistency of the tax treatment of transactions involving security coupons, which has undesirable consequences for the proper functioning of the internal market. in order to eliminate the possibilities of tax evasion and fraud and to improve the collection of vat on vouchers and thus increase public revenues, it is necessary to strengthen the scope, neutrality and transparency of the tax treatment of voucher transactions. the european parliament has requested the commission to review the application of directive 2006/112/ec and to report to the parliament and to the council on its economic and fiscal impact by 1 january 2017. the report shall contain an analysis of the impact of this directive on the economies of the member states.
