in writing. − i welcome the amendments to the decision approving the hague convention on the acquisition of maintenance abroad for children and other family members and consider that the establishment of a common mechanism for the recovery of maintenance and other forms of family maintenance is a necessity. parents who migrate outside the eu are increasingly common and can even lead to the non-payment of a maintenance allowance, sometimes vital for a decent living, thus undermining the healthy development of minors. i voted in favour of the swift adoption of the amendments, which will allow the convention to enter into force at eu level and will facilitate both compliance with obligations and the international recovery of maintenance claims between family members.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because it is necessary to approve the amendments quickly, thus allowing the hague convention on the acquisition of maintenance abroad for children and other family members to enter into force as soon as possible in the european union. the hague convention of 23 november 2007 on the obtaining of maintenance abroad for children and other family members is an important instrument for citizens, as it provides a mechanism through which child support obligations can be claimed and enforced against a debtor domiciled in a third country. the amendments relate in particular to the situation of cyprus, latvia, luxembourg and portugal.
in writing. − it is estimated that there are 16 million international couples in the european union and that around 30 million eu citizens live outside the eu. in 2007, 1.2 million divorces were recorded in the 27 countries of the european union (the latest figures). these figures illustrate the significant problems that may arise in the settlement and enforcement of maintenance decisions arising from situations where one parent lives in a third country. the 2007 hague convention on maintenance obligations complements the european union's domestic legislation on maintenance obligations, adopted on 18 december 2008: regulation (ec) no 4/2009 on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of judgments and cooperation in matters relating to maintenance obligations. the regulation and the protocol on the applicable law will apply between the member states of the european union as from 18 june 2011.
in writing. − it is estimated that there are 16 million international couples in the european union and 30 million union citizens living in third countries. the problem of obtaining foreign child support will certainly become more acute in the years ahead. when families break up, it is often the children who suffer the most. this is why this legislation, which is primarily a child protection measure, is welcome. the european union already has solid rules guaranteeing that children receive financial support when one parent lives apart from the family in another eu member state. the european union's signature of this international convention ensures that children are afforded the same protection when one of the parents moves outside the european union. the best interests of the children must come first, and parents should not be able to avoid the responsibilities they have by leaving the european union.
in writing. − the report concerns the application of the hague convention on the award of child maintenance abroad. i consider that the mechanism provided for in that convention, by which maintenance obligations may be enforced against a debtor domiciled in another country, is of particular importance in the context of the increasing mobility in the european union and the increasing number of mixed families. i note, however, that the provisions of the convention are not yet sufficiently known; a large number of european citizens and even civil and family law practitioners do not have the necessary information on the applicable rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a council decision amending annexes ii and iii to the council decision of 9 june 2011 on the approval, on behalf of the european union, of the hague convention of 23 november 2007 on the acquisition abroad of a maintenance pension for children and other family members. the objective of the hague convention on the foreign acquisition of maintenance for children and other family members is to ensure the effective acquisition of maintenance abroad by entitled persons. the hague convention is an important instrument for citizens as it provides a mechanism by which child support obligations can be claimed and enforced against a debtor domiciled in a third country. annex ii to decision 2011/432/eu indicates the reservation to be made by the european union upon approval of the hague convention on the acquisition abroad of a maintenance allowance for children and other family members. annex iii sets out the declarations to be made by the european union upon approval of the convention. member states have notified the commission of further changes to the reserve and declarations set out in annexes ii and iii. it is therefore necessary to amend those annexes before the deposit of the instrument of approval of the hague convention.
accession negotiations with croatia were concluded in june 2011. croatia will become a member of the european union on 1 july 2013, provided that the treaty of accession is ratified by all member states. we welcome the progress made by croatia in areas such as the judiciary, the fight against corruption, human rights and the protection of minorities and in relation to war crimes. as regards transport policy, further efforts are needed to increase the administrative capacity of the agency for railway safety and to establish a joint accident investigation body. in the energy field, further efforts are needed, in particular to complete legislative alignment in the field of the internal energy market and to ensure the development of a competitive gas and electricity market. croatia also has to meet the 2020 requirements for the promotion of energy efficiency and renewable energy. we welcome and expect a lot from croatia also in terms of implementing the european union strategy for the danube region.
croatia's accession to the european union will certainly bring added value to the european union, in particular in terms of contribution and participation to the danube strategy and, not least, to the south east europe region. i would like to make a few remarks on future developments in croatia and i would like to suggest: 1) that it continue to use ipa funds, cohesion funds and structural funds, 2) that it continue to cooperate with the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia and, not least, that croatia continue to cooperate with slovenia in order to dialogue and find solutions for territorial cooperation in their border conflicts.
it is undeniable that, compared with the previous report on turkey, it has made some progress towards modernisation and the building of democracy. turkey has made a number of important reforms in the judiciary as well as in other areas such as human rights, family protection and so on. but these reforms are a first step forward and the european union must encourage turkey to continue along this path, as many of these areas need sustained reforms to reach eu standards. the initiation of constitutional reform is a positive development and i hope that we will soon see concrete progress towards a constitution that meets the copenhagen criteria. it will be very important that the new constitution ensures the separation of powers in the state, clarifying the relationship between the state and religion, and guaranteeing the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. i welcome the positive developments at eu level, the lifting of objections to the opening of a new negotiating chapter. i think we should also open the chapter on the system.
mr president, firstly i would like to welcome the report and congratulate the rapporteur on his excellent work and his cooperation with all the other meps. secondly, i would remind you that we knew from the very beginning that the dialogue between pristina and belgrade would not be easy. and indeed it has not been easy. last week there was a failure in the dialogue, and today there was a new meeting. today it was the kosovan prime minister who left the meeting, but we still hope there will be an agreement. it is fundamental to the european union to continue to work towards reaching such an agreement. the balkans are a strategically-fundamental area for the eu, and solving the issue of serbia and kosovo is fundamental to bringing the two countries closer to the eu. we need to have a strategic vision there and to do everything in our power to reach goals which are common to both serbia and kosovo but also to the european union. the eu has to avoid any political ambiguity, which serves no viable long-term purpose. an eu failure in the serbia-kosovo negotiations will not be an isolated failure but a strategic one – a mistake of incredible proportions – that would allow external interference in an area that is essential for the union. i would remind you that last week there were rumours about the possible presence of a foreign military base in serbia. so what we need now is for the council to set a date for starting the negotiations. serbia deserves a date. the western balkans deserve a genuine commitment to see that the enlargement process is still realistic and tangible. i congratulate the commission again on the efforts it has made.
as you are well aware, the protection of ethnic minorities in serbia raises particular problems. in the timoc valley, the romanian minority is facing difficulties in respecting its fundamental rights. i also draw attention to the tendency to create an artificial linguistic identity, the so-called vlach language. at the same time, the serbian authorities are putting up all kinds of obstacles to prevent those who have enrolled their children in romanian language classes at school. at the same time, romanians in serbia need access to public radio and television stations, just as the serb minority in romania has access and funding at the same time! the romanian orthodox church in serbia does not enjoy the status of a traditional church, and its jurisdiction is limited to the serbian banat, and the romanian minority does not have access to services in their native language.
i am pleased to see that the motion welcomes the legal framework for minorities but also mentions its shortcomings. it emphasises the fair representation of minorities and access to quality education in minority languages. the integration of the western balkan countries is unthinkable without a lasting and reassuring solution to the minority issue. at the same time, it is sobering that the union is not paying the slightest attention to the countries that have already joined and is not demanding the same things from serbia that it is now demanding very rightly. citizens belonging to national minorities are also european citizens, and it is time that we are not treated as a security policy problem and a threat to stability, but that the enforcement of our purely civil rights makes discrimination against us an eu issue. i hope that no one is under any illusion that any member state will be able to solve its minority problems once and for all before accession and then not have to deal with them afterwards. national minorities are state-building factors, not some problem to be solved quickly and then not to be dealt with after accession.
in writing. the eu's paradoxical combination of dogmatism and double standards in the western balkans is responsible for its failure to mediate the serb-kosovo negotiations. undermining the chance for internal reforms, such failure pushes serbia towards russia, on a different agenda from the european one and thus towards a move away from the eu. the 'more for more' policy does not work in the western balkans, as eu integration is less pressing for the countries of this region than solving state security problems. national security issues can only be resolved in the context of a coherent vision for the entire region. integration policies cannot be mixed with policies to resolve constitutional and territorial crises. at the same time, until states address their identity and cohesion issues, they will not be able to make significant progress with integration policies. in the case of the serbo-kosovo crisis, the eu has demonstrated that it has no solutions to solve the problems of identity and national security. so we need new actors and new ideas. in this context, the training of a facilitator group, complementary to the eu, composed of candidate countries and member states with expertise and influence in the area, such as turkey and albania, romania and italy respectively, could be envisaged.
enlargement is a process that must be supported by absolutely all member states and, as is well known, five states have not yet recognised kosovo. the report by mrs lunacek encourages recognition, although this is the exclusive prerogative of each member state. and despite international recognition, kosovo has made absolutely no progress. i call for dialogue between serbia and the european union not to be conditioned by dialogue between serbia and kosovo. finally, i would like to say that the time allotted to this debate is impressive. i would have liked the republic of moldova to be equally privileged, a country with real european prospects.
several people have mentioned that five eu member states refuse to recognize kosovo. interestingly, in these countries, governments and politicians often ask the minorities there: when are you going to recognize the borders of the country? when are you gonna be loyal? it is clear that these five countries are not able to deal with their minorities in a proper european way. despite all the prejudices, we, the traditional national minorities of europe, were not happy that kosovo became an independent state. we wanted it to have a territorial and cultural autonomy within serbia. but history has taught us to take account of european realities. and now we're just cheering for kosovo to set an example for the five and other eu member states that can't respect their minorities. the ahtisaari plan, with its potential for cultural and territorial autonomy, should set an example for those eu member states - old and new - that are unable to guarantee human and community rights in a way that is reassuring to minorities.
first of all, i would like to congratulate the excellent results of the meeting of the representatives of the member states in clonakility on tuesday. the talks at this meeting are a good sign that an agreement on fisheries reform can be reached before the end of june. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used effectively. at this rate, we will be getting a new treaty sooner than a coherent solution for fishermen. the multiannual plans provide the fisheries sector with the stability and continuity it needs, and parliament must therefore be able to express its views on all the elements of these plans. in that case, parliament is not appealing to the goodwill of the council but invoking a right which is granted by the treaty of lisbon. the parliament and the members of the fisheries committee also do not want to impose their own views on the plans, but rather those measures requested by the local communities. moreover, the legal services have already spoken, too. i find it difficult to imagine what the consequences would be of such an institutional deadlock in any other area in which parliament has, by virtue of the treaty of lisbon or the previous treaties, the right of co-decision. the irish presidency has had and has responsibilities for reforming the common fisheries policy and has shown openness, transparency and a concern for efficiency and results in this process. i hope that, following this debate, he will do the same in seeking a solution to the current institutional deadlock. i am also convinced that the commission, as guardian of the treaties, will also play an active role in identifying this solution.
as rapporteur for iceland of the european parliament, i have a legitimate interest in the union's strategy in the arctic region. iceland, although a small country, plays an important role in the region this is also evidenced by the fact that the first director of the newly created arctic council secretariat is an icelander, and that the first meeting of the arctic circle will take place in october in reykjavík. i am pleased to note, on the one hand, that since the last debate in parliament on the subject we are discussing today, the commission has drawn up a policy for the arctic and, on the other hand, the arctic council has strengthened its political and administrative capacity. it is, i think, time for this institution to open up to those who are already extremely involved in the region. the european union is a major contributor to research in the arctic, allocating around €20 million per year for this purpose between 2007 and 2013. it is therefore clear that for us, participation as a permanent observer in the arctic council is first and foremost a matter of responsible partnership. i don't know if we can say the same for other candidates for that status. i feel that in china, it's more about ambition. the european union has proven that when based on common rules and values, cooperation is the most successful instrument for the development of a region. the arctic states are, of course, the ones who have the most say in the region in which they are located. but recent history can provide us with useful lessons.
the arctic is an area of increasing strategic importance. amid global warming and the melting of the ice cap, large reserves of hydrocarbons have been discovered, which arouse the interest of several countries. the european union has a major role to play in supporting cooperation in the area, but also in addressing the challenges currently facing the region. the main objective for a coherent strategy should be to promote the rational and sustainable use of arctic resources. particular attention will thus have to be paid to environmental protection. the energy resources found in the arctic ocean must be exploited in a responsible way that does not affect the ecosystems of the region. i'm particularly concerned that the area could start a real competition for resources.
april 2013 marked the first anniversary of the european citizens' initiative. happy birthday to you! this instrument of participatory democracy is in its infancy, of course, but it has already achieved important successes. we were informed by the commission that one of the initiatives - right to water for all - has passed one million signatures and continues to collect signatures. the european parliament has made a substantial contribution to the drafting of the text: more than two thirds of its content was indeed produced by us, the meps, demonstrating once again our commitment to strengthening the involvement of european citizens in defining or changing european policies. and we should be congratulated on that! i am equally very proud to have personally contributed with my distinguished colleagues in the committee on petitions to this substantial advance of european participatory democracy. i would now like to call on the commission to pay greater attention to the risk of this instrument being used for nationalist and extremist purposes in some member states, and to call on the commission to put pressure on the member states to create all the conditions provided for in the directive for the exercise of citizens' rights.
the balance sheet after the first year of the european citizens' initiative shows that out of 14 initiatives, only one reached the one million mark. i very much appreciate the commission's flexibility in this respect. the past year has shown that the procedure is very complex and unfortunately not harmonised at member state level. in order not to create obstacles to citizens' political participation in this procedure at the level of the european union, i believe that in the future it is necessary: 2) a platform for maintaining websites that is certainly easier to use in this respect, i think we should also consider the possibility of centralising this system and having the commission be the main responsible for this, and 3) the creation of contact points and information for citizens, respectively advice at the level of the member states.

in writing. the european citizens' initiative has emerged as a tool to democratically strengthen european decision-making. however, more than a year after its launch, one initiative alone has managed to gather over 1 million signatures, although the geographical criterion is not yet met. in the next period, i think we'll see the best of how the instrument works. the verification of signatures, the examination by the commission and the hearing in parliament will prove the viability of the initiatives tabled so far. i think the main shortcomings are related to the way signatures are collected, and the need for a single platform, which only the commission can implement. that's why i'd like to express my support for one of the initiatives that aims to create just such a unique platform.
i would like to join my colleagues in criticising the lack of information to parliament on the updating of the scoreboard for monitoring macroeconomic imbalances. as regards the outcome of the recent analysis on correcting these imbalances, published on 10 april, i regret to note that the european executive is omitting certain important aspects. first, it does not take surplus as an indicator of macroeconomic instability. thus, germany, which has a surplus of around 6% of gross domestic product, is not explicitly included in the analysis. moreover, the decline in the share of national income devoted to wages, a source of negative competition at european level, is becoming a model to follow. however, i believe that to close the gap between the core and peripheral economies, we need to raise wages in the group of countries with the strongest economies, while boosting competitiveness and demand in the peripheral countries.

in writing. − the relationship between the european union and a pro-european state such as the republic of moldova deserves special attention. i suggest that the following social problem, which is frequently encountered, should be taken into account in future: a very large number of children do not live with their parents, as they are away working in different member states of the european union. the reason for this situation is the requirement for the issuing of visas for minor children. by denying children the right to parental education, we risk causing a breakdown in society. a possible solution, which we should consider in the future, is to exclude the visa requirement for minor children with one or both parents, moldovan citizens, residing in the territory of the european union.

in writing. − the adopted resolution assesses the impact of the economic and financial crisis in third countries, with a special focus on developing and least developed countries. as fewer resources are available, more people are affected by poverty. thus, we are faced with a lack of respect for fundamental human rights, such as the right to food, water, education, adequate housing, land, decent work, health or social security, which leads to an increase in inequalities between citizens in developing and less developed countries. i believe that the eu must continue its engagement with third countries, promoting the economic, social and cultural rights of citizens and stepping up efforts to ensure universal and non-discriminatory access to basic services. i also stress that the governments of third countries must develop youth employment policies that focus not only on job creation but also on ensuring a level of income and working conditions appropriate to a decent standard of living.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the impact of the economic and financial crisis on human rights. the financial crisis has spread worldwide through various transmission channels, interacting with other crises (such as the food crisis and the fuel crisis). as a result of the crisis, the world bank and the un estimate that between 55 and 103 million people are living in poverty, thus jeopardising progress on human rights. global unemployment reached 200 million in 2012 an increase of 27 million since the start of the crisis in 2008. globally, 74.8 million young people aged 15-24 were unemployed in 2011, an increase of more than 4 million since 2007, with an exceptionally high level of unemployment in the middle east and north africa. parliament encouraged developing countries to use the trade preferences offered by the eu under the generalised system of preferences (gsp) to boost their economies, diversify their exports and improve their competitiveness. it is important that the eu supports and adopts the international goal of universal access to energy by 2030 as this will contribute to increasing economic power and social benefits for the poorest and most vulnerable people in developing countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because annual statistical data on demography are fundamental for the study and definition of a wide range of policies, particularly those relating to social and economic issues, at national and regional level. demographic issues are multiplying and playing an increasingly important role in the development of the european union. however, it seems to me that distortions can be created at the level of the calculation, especially in the case of countries with significant numbers of nationals leaving their borders, which can have a significant impact on the level of representation in the european union. i also believe that the data obtained should be used to create indicators of various kinds.
in writing. these demographic statistics are used by the european commission for the calculation of the allocation of the structural funds and by the council for weighting qualified majority voting. some delegations wished to change the definitions of what is meant by 'habitual residence of the european citizen' so that their national population data would be artificially inflated by taking into account the many emigrants who left their country of origin for economic reasons. the emigration of workers is a phenomenon that has been amplified by the crisis and affects many countries, not just eastern europe. denying this and trying to divert it for political strategies within the council is unacceptable. the european parliament will be able to play its full role as co-legislator and to enter into negotiations with the council in order to find a balanced and reliable method of calculation for the european population census and to weight national political influences within the decision-making body in the way most suited to the reality of cyclical migration.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european demographic statistics has important consequences for the democratic process within the european union. i supported amendment no 24 with 40 other members of the european parliament, which amends article 4 by proposing that the european commission should provide data on the population of the member states where they are legally or lawfully resident at the reference time for the purpose of qualified majority voting in the council. the european commission's proposal aims to introduce a method of determining the number of inhabitants of a member state on the basis of the 'usual residence' term, which will influence the member states' share in the council. in this context of economic and financial crisis, member states whose nationals are integrated into the labour markets of other member states by residing in their territory will be at a disadvantage in the decision-making process in the council. moreover, population data provided by member states, collected on the basis of obscure procedures (it is sufficient to declare, after 3 months of residence, the intention to stay in the territory of another member state in order to be considered 'normally resident') will influence the importance of the vote in the council, also contradicting the principle of free movement of persons.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amendment no 26, which sought to remove article 4, an unacceptable article because the procedure proposed for determining the number of inhabitants of the member states is at least unusual and leaves room for many interpretations. as this amendment was rejected by the full house, i voted against the report in the final vote.
in writing. - i voted for amendments nos 24 and 26, which seek to delete article 4, which provides for a change in the existing method of calculating majorities in the council, in accordance with article 2 (c). i also voted for amendment no 25, which deletes the first recital, which refers to the change in the qualified majority in the council as from 1 november 2014. i believe that majorities in the council are clearly defined by the treaties of the european union and the regulation on european demographic statistics should not change these provisions. the provisions proposed by article 4 and recital 1 of this regulation will have a negative impact on member states affected by the crisis and on their nationals residing in another member state. i think that is not fair, because these citizens are often only entitled to vote in local elections in the member states of residence, and not in general, presidential or european elections in those states. thus, as long as these citizens cannot express themselves by voting on the policy of the member state of residence, the only state that can represent their interests at european level, within the council, is the member state of origin.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the dismantling of ships outside the oecd has a significant impact on the environment and health. any ship taken out of the european union for dismantling is a hazardous waste and therefore cannot be legally dismantled at present except within the oecd. most final owners try to maximise their profits by selling their vessel to facilities that do not meet the standards of protection of workers and the environment, and thus can offer the highest price. a european list of recycling facilities located anywhere in the world should be drawn up, provided that they comply with certain standards. an appropriate inventory for the proper recycling of ships must also be carried out.
in writing. − every year, around 1 000 end-of-life ships are broken and recycled using the ‘beaching’ dismantling methodology, most of them in south asia under dangerous conditions and with little or no standards for the protection of workers, human health or the environment. i reiterate parliament’s opinion, as explicitly stated in its resolution of 26 march 2009, to prohibit the ‘beaching’ method for end-of-life ships and adopt it as the basic for this regulation. i urge a clear stance on this concern by fully implementing the export ban of hazardous waste also for waste ships, an inventory of hazardous materials for all ships calling at eu ports and the creation of a financial mechanism to support environmentally sound ship recycling.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on ship recycling. the purpose of this regulation is to prevent, minimise and, as far as possible, eliminate accidents, injuries and other adverse effects on human health and the environment caused by the recycling and treatment of eu ships. this regulation also aims to reduce disparities between operators in the union, oecd countries and third countries concerned as regards occupational health and safety and environmental standards. i voted for the creation of a financial mechanism (recycling fund) applicable to all ships entering eu ports, regardless of their flag, to ensure that the environmentally friendly treatment of ships containing hazardous waste is competitive with substandard operations. i also voted for amendment no 114, which calls for member states to encourage shipbuilders, together with shipbuilders and manufacturers of materials and equipment, to limit the use of hazardous materials on ships and to reduce them as far as possible from the design stage. this can prevent the release of hazardous substances into the environment, facilitate ship recycling and avoid the disposal of hazardous waste.

in writing. − montenegro is one of the western balkan states which, through its reforms, has shown its desire to be part of the european family of states that respect the rule of law, which led to the council's decision to open accession negotiations on 29 june 2012. i welcome this decision and encourage both decision-makers and civil society to make a concerted effort to make progress in all areas where gaps remain. one of the essential factors in the transition to a truly democratic society is the eradication of corruption, and i encourage the government, which has so far shown a willingness to cooperate with international organisations and take action on this subject, to make every effort to combat this phenomenon which still persists at all levels of society. i also believe that the authorities must urgently address the lack of alternatives to detention for children who break the law, because of the consequences that this punitive measure has on the child's development. we must not forget that detention has a stigmatizing effect on children, alienating them from their families and communities and restricting their opportunities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the progress of montenegro, as this country has made significant progress on the road to eu accession. we welcome the council's decision to open accession negotiations with montenegro on 29 june 2012. this decision is a major step in the country's accession process and a clear reaffirmation of the eu's commitment to the european future of the western balkan countries. montenegro is the first country for which the eu is applying a new approach to the negotiations, with a stronger focus on issues of democratic governance, fundamental freedoms, the rule of law, the judiciary, and the fight against corruption and organised crime. we draw attention to the fact that in the accession process there are still some shortcomings that need to be addressed, in particular the fight against organised crime and high-level corruption. we welcome the progress made in protecting and integrating all minorities and persons with disabilities. we call on the authorities to take further measures to combat discrimination and raise public awareness about improving the living conditions of minorities, their access to social security, health, education, housing and employment services and guaranteeing their adequate participation in public services.

in writing. the european union has set itself the objective of increasing the share of energy from renewable sources in total european energy production, but this requires better implementation of cooperation mechanisms between member states to promote the use of energy from renewable sources and to address shortcomings in cross-border electricity trade. on the other hand, the persistence of regulated retail prices will allow consumers to decide on the choice of supplier, because in the end the biggest beneficiaries of the completion of the internal energy market are consumers. in addition, competition should also be extended to renewable energy sources, as this is the best incentive for innovation and cost reduction, thus preventing the spread of energy poverty, which is why member states should make greater use of cooperation mechanisms and also increase communication between them to build additional infrastructure where appropriate.
in writing. developing renewable energy infrastructure and attracting investment for sustainable energy production are major challenges that we need to address with smart solutions. the achievement of sustainable energy objectives requires the uniform application of internal energy market legislation to remove energy bottlenecks and extend interconnections. the eu has significant untapped renewable energy resources. they can contribute to increasing energy independence at local and regional level. local and isolated communities are the main beneficiaries of sustainable energy potential. i consider the development of mixed energy infrastructures to meet electricity and heat demands to be a priority. for example, in the western region of romania, where i come from, the exploitation of geothermal energy could supplement the energy needs of local communities. the attraction of smes in the field of renewable energy would help to create investment partnerships and would constitute a potential for job creation. the commission should take into account that global markets offer opportunities for the efficient exploitation of renewable energy resources. i would remind you that the possible restrictions imposed on technology producers in third countries will only endanger more than 240 000 jobs in the photovoltaic sector.
in writing. i would like to stress the need to strike a balance between european policies to promote renewable energy and the need to maintain the competitiveness of european union industries in particular the metal, chemical, heavy equipment and machinery industries. these energy-intensive industries are competing with industries in countries that do not place equal emphasis on climate action. the european union must maintain its leadership in promoting renewable energy, but also take account of the progress made by large energy-consuming countries such as russia, china and others and adjust its own policies accordingly.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, i welcome ms cornelissen’s report on women’s rights in the balkan accession countries. i am glad to note that the report takes into account the views of a wide range of stakeholders, including civil society organisations, parliamentarians and government representatives across the region, and it identifies issues which the commission also considers important in assessing the progress made on gender equality in the western balkans. as the report mentions, the implementation and enforcement of legislation in this area is key, and therefore the commission not only helps with transposition of the acquis in the field of gender equality in the candidate countries and potential candidate countries but also provides financial support and monitors the implementation and effective enforcement of national legislation through the various instruments of the pre-accession strategies. as you well know, full transposition and enforcement of all european union directives in the field of gender equality is a strict condition for membership of the union. it is also vital to develop institutional and administrative structures that facilitate the implementation and enforcement of equality rights. in this context, the commission has encouraged a stronger focus on gender equality and women’s rights in the western balkans. for example, we provide assistance for the training of judges in this area and we cooperate with non-governmental organisations dealing with gender equality. european instruments for democracy and human rights can grant direct funding to women’s rights organisations, which have benefitted immensely from this mechanism. women’s rights initiatives have also been strengthened through the european union’s technical assistance for civil society organisations project. back in our 2011 enlargement strategy, we proposed an innovative approach to trigger domestic change in the field of justice and fundamental rights. the strategy presented stronger mechanisms while transforming chapter 24, on justice, freedom and security, and chapter 23, on judiciary and fundamental rights, into powerful incentives for reform. chapter 23 is among the first chapters to be opened and the last to be closed once a solid track record of reform implementation has been achieved. let me conclude by noting with satisfaction that croatia, as a future member state, has completed legal alignment in the field of gender equality, and i warmly welcome your suggestion that the gender equality ombudsperson in croatia could serve as an example for the whole region. this is another example of the transformative power of the enlargement process.
in writing. to join the eu, the western balkan countries need to adopt the eu acquis on gender equality. i would like to express my concern that 30% of the victims of crossborder trafficking in human beings in the european union are citizens of the balkan countries, with the majority of the victims being women and girls. in this regard, these countries should support awareness-raising campaigns, as well as concrete measures to combat corruption and organised crime to prevent trafficking. but i also believe that some progress has been made on gender equality and i would like to take this opportunity to congratulate the crossborder initiatives in this area in recent years. i believe that this kind of action should be supported more consistently by national governments and the european commission.
rapporteur. − mr president, we keep saying that media freedom is a fundamental right at the very foundations of the european union, and that is true. but are we pleased at how the media and media freedom look these days across the eu? there are some reasons to feel pleased, but there are also other strong reasons why we should worry a great deal. in this house we have had several debates on the status and role of the media in various member states. i would like to thank commissioner kroes for her constant support for media freedom and pluralism. i wish i could say the same for the commission in general, but the truth is that the reason this report exists is precisely because this parliament would have liked to see a stronger reaction from the commission, and especially from the commissioner for fundamental rights, each and every time media freedom has been under threat in any of the member states. article 2 of the treaty and article 11 of the eu charter on fundamental rights need to be fiercely protected by the commission as the guardian of the treaty. this has not happened so far. i therefore hope that the guidelines and recommendations of this report will, from now on, be taken into consideration by the commission and by the member states, since they represent not only our view as elected representatives of eu citizens but also the result of hundreds of hours of consultations with media organisations, union representatives and regulatory bodies. basic standards such as journalistic and editorial independence should not be missing from any newsroom. member states in the eu should support and promote investigative journalism and ethical journalism. it is of great concern that journalists are more and more frequently the victims of pressure, harassment and even violence. we call on each member state to ensure that journalists can report freely and safely. an attack against a journalist should be considered an attack against media freedom and against citizens’ rights to be informed. it should therefore be investigated and penalised immediately. it is of great importance that in each member state there is transparent and stable legislation which protects journalists in their mission as the watchdog of society. we should avoid a situation such as the one in my own country, romania, where, after seven years during which defamation and slander were no longer penalised by the penal code, following a very recent decision of the constitutional court there is now widespread confusion about their recriminalisation. in fact the report we will be voting on tomorrow calls on those member states in which defamation is still a criminal offence to decriminalise it as soon as possible. we need transparency of media ownership, we need to prevent excessive media concentration and we need rules to address the conflicts of interest resulting from the amalgamation of political office and control over media outlets. we need the independence of media supervisory bodies. we need journalists, not so that they will write nice things about us but to keep all of us informed and to keep us – the politicians – in check. we have to make sure that they can do their job. that is the very bottom line of this report.
i very much appreciate mrs weber's report and congratulate her on her work. in recent years, the problems faced by the media have been almost identical in all member states. the adoption of this report on standard rules for media freedoms in the european union will therefore be an incentive for the european commission to become more courageous in regulating this area in the future. i have two comments on the subject in general: the first concerns the commercial media, where i believe we need transparent information on the identity of the recipients of these media, which would be to the benefit of the citizens, who could find out much more information and analyse in more detail what is being offered to them, and the second concerns the establishment of a verification mechanism by which the european commission can ensure that the member states guarantee the effective application in their territory of the charter of fundamental rights, which implies media pluralism, equal access to information and respect for the independence of the press.
all european countries that have joined or wish to join the european union must comply with the copenhagen criteria, which include the charter of fundamental rights. article 11 provides for respect for the freedom and pluralism of the media. as such, public media services, financed from the state budget, are essential. they have an institutional duty to provide the public with high-quality, accurate and reliable information, and they must be independent of external pressures and private or political interests. on the other hand, private media have similar information duties. i therefore support the need for a genuinely balanced european dual system, in which the public and private media respect their respective roles, the professional independence of national news agencies is guaranteed and the creation of news monopolies is avoided. last but not least, i want to congratulate mrs weber on this report.
in writing. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union recognises, in article 11, freedom of information and expression as a fundamental right and, at the same time, guarantees that media freedom and pluralism must be respected. it is thus recognised that the media play a key role in promoting and maintaining democracy, ensuring that citizens have access to a variety of information to form informed opinions on events in the public sphere. however, journalists and the media in general face difficulties in carrying out their work in many eu countries, often under pressures that affect their independence. at the same time, the media sector is also affected by structural problems such as concentration trends that lead to abuses of dominant positions and affect the principle of pluralism. it is therefore very important that national and european institutions protect media freedom through measures that guarantee the independence of journalists from pressures from owners of media companies and from political courts. i also believe it is essential that member states adopt legislation to prevent infiltration of newsrooms by intelligence agents, as such activities undermine the credibility of the press.
the audiovisual media services directive is the main piece of regulation in this area in the european union. i would have liked, however, that the current public consultation on a possible revision of the directive had been wider. we cannot simply guarantee the independence of national regulators. account should also be taken of the extension of the provisions of article 9 (2) by encouraging media organisations to develop codes of conduct in areas other than commercial communication. the recommendations of the high level group on media freedom and pluralism should also be taken into account. one of them would be the establishment of an independent monitoring centre at european level to monitor developments in the media in the member states and make any recommendations.
in the context of technological developments, regulating the media has become a priority, both from the perspective of freedom of expression and access to information, and from a commercial point of view. the development of the internet means that an increasing number of citizens have access to traditional or on-demand audiovisual services. at the same time, markets and consumer behaviour are changing rapidly. the commission's analysis of the application of the audiovisual media services directive thus becomes a useful tool in planning the adjustment of the regulatory framework in this field. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of minors against commercial communications which encourage unhealthy behaviour, particularly in the food sector. i also welcome the fact that all member states have complied with the provision to provide at least 10% of independent european works, but draw attention to the limited objective of this process. i also point out the importance of providing media services to people with visual or hearing impairments. thank you, congratulations to the reporter.
in writing. i am pleased that this report addresses the issue of accessibility of media services for people with disabilities. it is imperative that we take steps to increase equality of opportunity for people with disabilities and to really give them their right, namely access to adequate means of communication, access to information, thus ensuring a step forward for their integration into society. there is a need for cooperation between broadcasting companies in developing technologies that take into account the needs of visually and/or hearing impaired persons, persons with disabilities and the elderly. junk food and alcohol continue to have a negative impact on children and in this respect i welcome the emphasis in this report on the protection of minors. i acknowledge that significant progress has been made in the control of inappropriate audiovisual commercial communications to children, but it is not sufficient, especially due to changes in communication technology. the perception of what is normal and good in society is very important for young people and in this respect i support the report's request to the commission to submit proposals on the issue of media education.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, thanks to the honourable member, mr geier. this report does indeed contain many interesting aspects and is very timely indeed. it is particularly important at this time of economic crisis to draw attention to the continuing economic transformation struggle of declining industrial regions. also at this time of crisis, cohesion policy funding is a major instrument to implement effective industrial policies and to support, in particular, small and medium sized enterprises. investment into businesses by the erdf in the current funding period 2007-2013 is eur 54.2 billion overall across the eu-27. the large majority of those investments support innovation and we believe that much of what is pointed out in this report is already being addressed by the better alignment of cohesion policy with the europe 2020 goals and the synergies which we hope to achieve through smart specialisation. this involves effort and increased cooperation at all levels: at european level, at member state level, and at regional level. it is about true multi-level governance and an alignment of strategic visions and road maps and better synergies between policy areas. the concept of smart specialisation, which mr geier mentions positively in his report, calls for tailor-made innovation strategies at regional level which are based on careful analyses of regional assets and development potential, and on comprehensive stakeholder involvement. indeed we believe that smart specialisation can do at least three things to help old industrial regions in supporting economic transformation,number one, help them to develop an excellence-driven vision of regional development and structural change, and to re-focus their industrial and knowledge assets in the direction of emerging industries and services and international markets. in that sense smart specialisation can be seen as a specific-based approach to industrial policy. number two, strengthen cooperation and knowledge transfer between the key players in the regional innovation system – governments, industry and science – with the benefit of offering much more integrated approaches to knowledge-based regional development. public-private partnerships need to implement those approaches. number three, increase multi-level and horizontal policy coordination, bringing together a range of complementary policies such as research and technology policies, industrial policy, regional and rural development policies, labour market policy, etc., and mobilising actors and resources in the in writing. industrial area strategies in the european union are an important topic for many regions and for many eu citizens. i would stress the importance of the references in this motion for a resolution to the need for a region-wide perspective when addressing problems relating to industry in general or to a particular branch of industry. in this context, it is worth noting, first of all, the need for synchronised development of the industrial sector with the education sector, in order to ensure complementarity. secondly, industrial zone strategies must be complementary to rural development strategies in the region, which is important for food and housing reasons and for coordination with measures to diversify economic activities in rural areas. small rural enterprises can function not only as suppliers of food and services to industrial areas, but also as suppliers of raw materials or sub-components to developed industries. it is therefore essential that industrial area strategies take into account the region as a whole, including nearby rural localities.
in this parliament, over the last two or three years, i have said on several occasions that the existence of tax havens which do not want to conclude transparency agreements, automatic exchange of information with the european union, is a disgrace to the citizens who pay their taxes in these member states of the european union. that is why i welcome the proposals made by the european commission, i welcome the progress made by commissioner šemeta in this area, and the proposals in the reports on preventing tax evasion through tax havens. but i do feel it is my duty to propose two new measures which will be more effective in achieving success in this fight against tax evasion through tax havens. firstly, to ban all transactions in the european union by companies registered in tax havens which do not want to conclude transparency and automatic exchange of information agreements with the european union - not only in public procurement, but also to ban all transactions in the european union. secondly, take the good proposal that has emerged in the uk that multinational companies should be obliged to declare publicly the profits they make in all the countries outside the european union where they have registered units.
the various methods of stimulating economic growth in the european union are useless unless there is close coordination at european and international level on tax havens. the attitude of many companies operating in europe is a total disrespect for national governments and taxpaying citizens and it is our duty to take immediate action. given that the losses generated by the transfer of profits outside the european union for tax avoidance amount to several billion euros per year, i believe that we must make every effort to identify these companies, find ways to stop these unethical practices and restrict their access to european funds and even to participate in public procurement procedures within the territory of the european union.
we are facing a tragicomic situation. on the one hand, parliament and the commission are fighting with the council for millions, tens of millions, hundreds of millions of euros for projects that are essential to european policies, and at the same time we accept that for years we have been seeing huge sums, a trillion a year, of tax evasion and fraud on a european union scale. at the same time, we tell the young people of the union that we have no money for the youth guarantee and then we give them like beads of glass, six billion, maybe three, for now, holy promises. i think it is time for the council to put an end to this game of, i would say, complicity in crime, fraud and evasion, and to take a firm decision, because it is not ethical standards that scare those who (the president withdraws the speaker).
in writing. in the eu, €1 trillion of public money is lost every year as a result of tax fraud and tax evasion. it generates an annual cost for the european citizen of about eur 2 000. this puts at risk the maintenance of the european social model, which is based on the provision of quality public services accessible to all citizens, and affects the efficiency and fairness of tax regimes within the union. tax evasion and avoidance are reducing the funds available to stimulate public investment, growth and employment. i believe that we need concrete measures at european level to prevent, identify and reduce tax fraud, just to avoid the loss of billions of euros of public money every year. member states should allocate the necessary resources to their national tax administrations and to the staff responsible for tax control. at european level, we need a mandatory common consolidated corporate tax base and the development of new strategies to combat vat fraud, as well as a more rigorous fight against tax fraud through the judicial system under criminal law.
in writing. as the economic crisis has deepened social inequality in the european union, tackling tax fraud is becoming a moral and political obligation, not just a way to increase public resources. when citizens are suffering the effects of austerity, tackling tax havens and improving tax collection systems are essential measures, including for regaining the credibility of the european institutions. all the european union's deficits could be covered in nine years if tax evasion could be stopped. public losses from fraud have reached the staggering 1 000 billion euro per year, an additional cost of 2 000 euro for every european citizen. these tax-free funds have now exceeded the eu's health budget and are four times the size of the education budget of all 27 member states. to achieve the european commission's objective of halving tax losses by 2020, the action plan should aim at harmonising the disparities between member states' tax systems, regulating tax crimes in a uniform manner, combating customs fraud, narrowing down the definition of tax havens, improving vat collection, strengthening tax discipline and increasing transparency, including in the financial reporting of multinational companies.
in writing. tax fraud and evasion cost the member states' budgets an estimated €1 trillion a year, the equivalent of €2 000 a year for every european citizen. they are a heavy burden, especially in times of crisis, and lead to the erosion of the single market and taxpayers' confidence. in the context of the interdependence of european economies and common policies, these phenomena must be countered by concerted action. without these, tax competition is encouraged and national and community bodies lack the appropriate tools to combat tax fraud and evasion. i welcome the communication from the european executive in this field, which was released last december. but i think that more drastic measures are needed. these include introducing state-level tax reporting requirements for all companies and a blacklist of tax havens by the end of next year. the taxation of savings income directive must also be implemented as soon as possible to put an end to banking secrecy.
in writing. – i want to thank the council for touching on these issues, and parliament for proposing concrete actions against these huge problems which are causing significant losses. this is added to other major problems that we have in the european union. the sum that europe is losing every year is outrageous. we can see tax evasion on a significant scale. we need to have convincing answers to tackle this issue, and i think that the mojka kekus report takes an important first step. tax fraud is not only national; this is why we need a common platform to exchange information. in addition, according to the report, the commission has to study the possibility of introducing eu taxation on cross-border business models and electronic commerce. the report points out that the eu should take the leading role in discussions on the fight against tax fraud, tax avoidance and tax havens. i have to mention again on this occasion the importance of the financial transaction tax. we need to take the burden of the crisis off the shoulders of citizens. the introduction of a financial transaction tax at eu level would ensure this and could bring eur 54 billion to the eu budget.

the european commission must do all it can to reverse the decline in industry in the european union and bring it down from the current level of 16% of gdp to 20% by 2020. of course, sustainable growth can only be achieved by paying due attention to environmental factors, which is why i believe that regional strategies in this area should include measures to protect soil, water, air and biodiversity as a central element. i encourage the member states and european regions to make effective use of the structural and investment funds at their disposal to help the industrial sector, which has been hit hard by the crisis, break out of the deadlock. i believe that young entrepreneurs can play a key role in the revitalization of europe's old industrial areas. it is therefore necessary to encourage them to do so by providing business advice from the competent authorities and by facilitating access to european funds.
european industry has been in decline for some time. whether it's declining competitiveness or higher labor costs, many firms have relocated their operations to other parts of the globe. this is also the case in romania, which unfortunately does not have a clear vision of the development of the industrial sector at this time. there is no coherent strategy and no political will on the part of the socialist government to strengthen the industrial sector. in addition, several steel and petrochemical plants have made or are about to make massive redundancies. although there is a solution to access the european globalisation adjustment fund, the government has not taken such measures so far. in the context of the regionalisation proposed by the usl, i believe that there should be a clear strategy for industrial development at national level and at the level of future administrative regions.

mr president, major accidents related to offshore oil and gas operations can have devastating and irreversible consequences. we must minimise the risk of these accidents and, in the event of an accident occurring in union waters, deploy an effective response in a timely manner. for the time being, there is no database at union level to collect and share data on accidents; there are different databases in the member states. as such, i welcome articles 22 and 23 regarding the sharing of information and transparency, and the data contained in annex 6 that foresees a common format for reporting this information.
given that most of europe's oil and gas production takes place offshore and the risk of accidents is quite high, standardisation of existing national laws and regulatory practices is strictly necessary. in addition, operators throughout the union are obliged to ensure the use of best methodologies for controlling major risks and to contribute to strengthening the capacity to prevent and respond to potential accidents. the european union now has the opportunity to take a leading role in the safety of oil and gas operations worldwide and thus must step up the international promotion of high safety standards, which will lead to environmental protection and to the reduction of economic losses and damage resulting from accidents.
both offshore and onshore extraction activities must comply with environmental standards. the natural gas reserves of the black sea and shale gas could provide energy independence for my country, but also lower costs for the population. recently, romania has been granted a permit to explore for shale gas on the black sea coast. it is worth noting that, after coming to power, both the left-wing coalition and the meps representing it have changed their minds by 180 degrees. they too have realized that shale gas is the best solution to reduce dependence on imports and create jobs, even though they were bitterly opposed during the opposition period. if exploitable resources are found, production could begin within a few years, subject to strict environmental conditions.
in writing. − the 2010 deepwater horizon oil spill in the gulf of mexico and, more recently, the elgin oil and gas leak in the north sea, have brought into focus the need to review policies related to the safety of offshore oil and gas installations and to ensure the protection of the eu's marine environment in the event of major accidents. the report contains concrete measures to eliminate the fragmentation and general disparities between member states' practices and legislation in this area and to guarantee the necessary safety and environmental standards throughout the union. i believe that the basic principle of eu environmental law, namely that the polluter pays, must be respected by all operators when they establish the financial guarantees necessary to cover the costs of clean-up and compensation in the event of major accidents. the high standards of action to limit environmental and human health damage set out in this report should be promoted internationally and in relevant global and regional forums, and mechanisms to ensure the effective application of these standards should be further examined.

in writing. − offshore oil and gas operations have recently been operating in increasingly difficult environments and conditions, with a high risk of accidents with devastating and irreversible consequences for the marine and coastal environment, as well as significant negative effects on coastal economies. the european union therefore has a vital interest in preventing and reducing the incidence of major accidents related to offshore oil and gas activities, limiting their consequences and improving the response mechanisms in case of an accident. the new proposal for a regulation is therefore a key instrument for ensuring the highest safety and environmental standards throughout the european union. in accordance with the international and european union legislation in force in this field, particular emphasis should be placed on strengthening the participation of citizens in informing the general public about major accidents and the measures taken to prevent and limit damage to the environment and human health. particular attention should also be paid to ensuring the protection of the arctic environment, a marine environment of unique and exceptional importance for the european union and a key player in climate change mitigation.

in writing. − the report on the proposal for a directive on the safety of offshore oil and gas exploration, exploitation and production activities is a step forward for the eu in reducing the risk of major accidents related to these activities and is the first european legislation to be adopted in this area. i voted for the implementation of best practice in the regulation of offshore oil and gas activities in all eu member states and for strengthening the capacity to respond to emergencies that may affect eu citizens, the economy or the environment. the european parliament's report advocated the independence of the competent authority for the safety of oil activities, making a clear separation between the body responsible for the safety of operations and the one dealing with the economic development of these projects, thus avoiding any conflict of interest. the european parliament has strengthened the rules on obtaining operating licences and imposed strict requirements on companies applying for licences, requiring them to prove, before commencing operations, their financial capacity to cover potential environmental and economic damage.

i voted for this report. approximately 30% of the victims of crossborder trafficking in human beings in the european union are citizens of the balkan candidate countries, mostly women and girls. a 2010 united nations report shows that human trafficking generates more than 2.5 billion euros a year in europe alone. despite the inclusion of strict penalties for traffickers from the balkan states, the networks are growing and reproducing through new recruitment. therefore, strict penalties imposed by law do not ensure that organized crime involving the trafficking of women and girls is stopped. that is why we need to create a very strict framework that discourages traffickers, and the governments of these countries need to allow free access to justice, strengthen the system that provides assistance to victims of traffickers. it also has to ensure the protection of these women who are trafficked and who must only have the capacity of witnesses.
