in writing. − women's rights and gender equality should not be mere bureaucratic notions, promoted in high-level discussions in order to impress the audience. as in any other eu member state, the balkan candidate countries must take account of all the principles underlying the european construction. these countries must ensure that gender equality is respected on their territory, that women in the balkans enjoy the same rights, autonomy and protection as men. the rapporteur and i welcome the progress made by the balkan countries in gender equality legislation and support the continued promotion of the gender dimension in the enlargement process of the european project. with gender equality as one of the basic pillars of the enlargement of the european union, we will ensure that in the future women in the new member states will not be discriminated against, will have equal opportunities in decision-making at political and governmental level, will be represented in all the structures of leadership, political, social and economic life in their respective societies.
in writing. − i welcome the preparation of this own-initiative report, which has proved to be very necessary as seven countries in the western balkans - albania, bosnia and herzegovina, croatia, kosovo, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and serbia - are at different stages of the accession process. given that these countries need to adopt and implement the eu acquis and other eu obligations in the area of gender equality, i stress the need and importance of public awareness campaigns in combating stereotypes, discrimination (on grounds of gender, culture, religion) and domestic violence, in order to promote gender equality. they also support the call on the governments of these countries to introduce measures to reduce the gender pay gap, to address the high unemployment rate, especially among women and especially those in rural areas, to ensure a legal framework for equal pay for equal work, to encourage their active participation in political life and to build functioning democratic institutions, by adopting measures that can ensure the reconciliation of private and professional life.
in writing. − i believe that at european level the governments of the balkan candidate countries must be supported and encouraged to develop strategies to combat violence against women and trafficking of all kinds.
in writing. − when we talk about equal rights, we also mean equal opportunities for women, who make up more than half of the population of europe. compared with previous years, i appreciate the efforts made by the balkan states to align their legislation with the acquis communautaire in this area, but draw attention to the importance of implementing these provisions. a step forward would be to better educate women, to make them aware of their rights and to make them aware of the importance of reporting any abuse they are subjected to. equally important to me is the issue of women's participation in decision-making at all levels of government, which is regulated by some states in the region by introducing minimum quotas of representation. in this context, i also stress the need to ensure the real economic independence of women, both through employment and through entrepreneurial initiatives. although many of the issues discussed in this report are general in the countries analysed, i believe that it is necessary to be more specific. the concrete examples for each country would be relevant, whether we are talking about violence, unemployment or trafficking in live meat, etc., so that we can really contribute to improving the situation of women in the countries that want to join the eu.
in writing. i voted for this report by mrs cornelissen because it gives women in the balkans real hope that their situation will improve. i believe that it is really necessary to redistribute some of the aid given to the candidate countries so that measures promoting equality between men and women are finally implemented and that women in the balkans can enjoy the same opportunities as their male counterparts. i therefore gave my support to this report without any hesitation!
in writing. - i voted in favour of all the provisions on the right to contraception, this being a vote of conscience. the member state i represent - romania - went through a long period under the communist dictatorship in which access to contraception was restricted and abortion outlawed. this period left a special trauma among romanian citizens. given this experience, i support free access to contraception and sex education. with regard to the same resolution, i consider that the high number of victims of cross-border trafficking in human beings from the balkan countries at eu level is a cause for concern and that european police cooperation needs to be stepped up to combat this phenomenon.
i voted for this report. one reason is that member states are being asked to remove insult and slander from their criminal law and i am totally in favour of that. in romania, the offences of insult and slander were abolished in 2007, on my own initiative. now, in 2013, libel and slander were reinstated in the penal code. the road we took was the other way around, we went in reverse. another serious issue affecting press freedom is the conflict of interest resulting from the simultaneous exercise of a political mandate and control of press institutions. this affects the independence of journalists and the way information is presented to the public. the osce report on the december 2012 parliamentary elections in romania shows that only one tv station presented the events equidistantly. this confirms the need for a legal framework to regulate such abuses, as a result of the concentration of media ownership in the hands of politicians.
i support the report by mrs renate weber because, like her, i believe that defamation should not be criminalised in the member states. an independent media must be impartial and objective, respect people's privacy, and distinguish between facts and opinions when reporting. the report also calls for the development of a european standard for the quality of work and the development of a european code of ethics. the latest mcv report notes the pressures that some media are putting on the judiciary in romania. i would therefore like to ask the romanian authorities to draw up a code of conduct, as recommended in the latest cvm report. the independence of national supervisory bodies must also be guaranteed. this will improve the quality of journalism and the citizens will be better informed.
in writing. − the independence of the media is one of the conditions for the correct and objective information of citizens. unfortunately, in recent years, due to the economic crisis, a number of problems have been reported that the media are facing in all member states. in this context, i welcome the preparation of this report and support the need for a study by the european commission on the effects of the crisis and the poor working conditions in the journalistic community, in order to analyse and try to remedy their consequences on media freedom and pluralism. i also stress 'the fundamental role of a balanced dual system in which the public and private media respect each other's roles', as the rapporteur also argues, and the need for proportionate and stable public funding for the public media in order to guarantee their political and economic independence. at the same time, i believe that transparency in the selection and appointment of media managers, in the election of boards of directors, based on professionalism and undeniable experience, is absolutely necessary.
in writing. − i support this report, given that freedom of expression in the public sphere is proving to be a key factor in stimulating citizens' participation in public debate, and that an active, competitive and pluralistic audiovisual and written media landscape is essential for the proper functioning of a democratic system. on the other hand, an autonomous and strong public sphere, underpinned by an independent and pluralistic media, is the best context in which the collective freedoms of civil society, such as the right to assembly and association, but also individual freedoms, such as freedom of expression and the right to access information, can flourish.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the eu charter: standard settings for media freedom across the eu, as i sincerely believe that free and independent media are an essential component of every democracy. more than ‘public watchdogs’ that enforce accountability, media are also the link between the decision-makers and the citizens. i very much welcome the call to member states to guarantee that funding of public service media should be sustainable, proportionate and stable, and to prevent dominant positions which impede pluralism. european authorities need to act to ensure that freedom of expression and information, as fundamental values of democracy, are fully protected.
in writing. - i voted for this report because the media play an important role in democracy, being a tool for informing citizens. journalists should be free, not be subject to pressures that might come from media owners, their managers, governments and should not be influenced by financial constraints. we have underlined in amendments to this report the importance of promoting responsible and ethical journalism, based on the 'code of conduct for journalists', in order to develop journalism based on professional objectivity and impartiality. it is essential that european citizens can form their own opinions without being manipulated by the media and benefit from a media that offers citizens freedom of interpretation and their own critical competences. national regulators have an important role to play and should cooperate and coordinate at eu level in promoting quality media. it must also be borne in mind that media freedom also includes the freedom of access to the media, to access the internet at a reasonable price, for all european citizens.
on the subject of pensions, i would like to draw attention to an issue which concerns me very much personally and which the commission should address as soon as possible. it is the lack of a social security system that takes into account the mobility of artists within the european union. last year, a task force was set up at the european commission level, together with relevant associations in the field, to identify and analyse the needs and obstacles faced by this highly mobile social group, such as artists. the results of this report will be published at the end of this year. to support these reforms, i will be organising a big debate in the european parliament in june with the european commission, the council of the european union and artists from across the european union to provide ideas to the european commission to consider in implementing the reform.
i voted in favour of the report because the economic crisis and demographic developments in the union are putting pressure on national pension systems. in romania, the huge pension fund deficit prompted the right-wing government to take a series of measures to consolidate the budget. despite the enormous political costs, the economy was stabilized and growth resumed. however, structural reforms are needed to avoid a collapse of pension systems in the union. despite the differences between member states, one thing is certain: young people will bear the brunt of the current situation, as they will be required to work for a longer period of time during their lives. i want to encourage the development of pillar two and pillar three pensions, which could provide adequate income after retirement.
in writing. − in a europe facing an ageing population, i believe that ensuring an adequate and viable pension for european citizens must be a priority for the european union. the current financial and economic situation has aggravated and amplified the impact of the strong trend towards an ageing population. the crisis has shown that more needs to be done to improve the efficiency and safety of pension schemes, which not only provide older people with the means to live a decent life, but also reward their hard work. the european pension agenda set out in the white paper is an excellent starting point for debate, after which reforms can be implemented through 'soft law' and possibly legislation. while retaining the responsibilities of the member states and the social partners, i believe that we need to create appropriate, safe and sustainable systems. moreover, they must also contribute to increased labour market mobility and free movement, systems that can provide solutions for the present and the future.
in writing. − given that the eu 2020 strategy aims to achieve a 75% employment rate for people aged 20-64, member states need to increase the employment rate and in particular the employment rate of older women and men. member states should therefore provide appropriate counselling and support to jobseekers and rehabilitation measures for long-term reintegration into the labour market. member states must strengthen public pension systems by improving the quality of jobs, wages and social services and by maintaining the means to finance social protection systems. given that young people enter the labour market late and the final contribution to the full pension is affected, i consider it necessary that the duration of the training periods be integrated into the calculation of the final pension. member states should also apply socially acceptable incentives for a later retirement and, where appropriate, develop attractive models for a flexible transition from working life to retirement.
in writing. − the pension problem at european level is becoming acute. i believe that we need to reform the eu pension system in order to save the european socio-economic balance, which is seriously damaged by the recession and threatened by an ageing population. to drastically reduce excessive deficits, many eu governments have decided to adopt austerity measures that directly affect pensions and the pensioners who receive them. i voted for this report because i believe that it is essential that measures and systems be adopted as a matter of urgency to ensure that pensioners in the eu countries have a decent standard of living. i hope that member states will act to reduce the vulnerability of pension systems by stimulating multiple pillars, increasing employment, achieving a work-life balance, reassessing early retirement and protecting workers' pensions in the event of insolvency.
in writing. − the challenges facing the european union in recent years - such as the financial and economic crisis, slow economic growth in the long term and an ageing population - have once again highlighted the vulnerability of pension systems at european level. this is why most eu countries will have to strengthen their budgets and reform their economies under austerity conditions, with a focus on rigorous public financial management. as such, member states need to assess the need to implement reforms of the first pillar pension systems, taking into account changes in life expectancy and changes in the ratio of pensioners, unemployed and economically active persons, in order to guarantee a decent standard of living and economic independence for older people, in particular those belonging to vulnerable groups.
in writing. − while pension systems are a matter for member states, the european union has committed itself, through the eu 2020 strategy, to making adequate, sustainable and secure pensions available to citizens. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that a harmonised european framework for adequate and secure pensions is essential, given the pressure on national budgets caused by austerity policies and ageing populations. although pension systems vary widely across member states, they are based on three pillars: the taxpayer solidarity pillar, financed from the state budget, the occupational pension pillar, based on negotiations between employee and employer and subject to private investment, and the private pillar based on individual savings. among the most important provisions, i welcome the adoption of a governance package and solvency rules for pillar two pensions, to mitigate the risks of pension funds' vulnerability to financial markets and bring them into line with private pensions. i believe that stricter rules are essential in safeguarding investments and protecting employees from economic recession and volatility in financial markets.
in writing. − the demographic challenge is no longer a future scenario but today’s challenge, posing major difficulties for the pension systems in all member states. the over-65 age group accounts for about 17 % of the total population in 2010, is rising by more than two million per year, and will reach almost 30 % of the total population in 2060. life expectancy at birth will increase by 7.9 years for females and 6.5 years for males by 2060. the pension system, especially the first pillar public scheme, is under severe pressure due to the economic and financial crisis and the demographic challenge. member states must implement the reforms needed in first pillar systems, taking into account changing life expectancies and the ratio between employed people and pensioners, which will be 2 to 1 in 2060, as opposed to 4 to 1 in 2008, in order to guarantee a decent living standard and economic independence for people in old age. the three-pronged strategy proposed by the stockholm european council in 2001 and reinforced in the context of the europe 2020 strategy – public debt reduction, increasing employment, especially for older people, and reforming social and security systems – has to be at the very roots of the member states’ strategies regarding this reality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because of the following considerations: i believe it is extremely important, especially in the current context of the economic crisis, to recognise the role of smes as the main source of new sustainable jobs and, consequently, as factors that can drive economic growth in the eu. smes can contribute effectively and significantly to the viability of national pension systems and their long-term adequacy. i welcome the fact that many member states have already started to implement or implement major programmes in the framework of pension reform, programmes that take into account the sustainability and adequacy of those systems. it is very important that any such reforms be preceded by consultation with representatives of all age groups, including young and old, to ensure fair outcomes and maintain a consensus between generations. the commission and the council are invited to publish an integrated summary, drafted in a concise and simple manner, to enable citizens to assess the features and options of their national pension systems in comparison with other eu systems.
in writing. − the population of the member states is ageing, the birth rate is falling, life expectancy is increasing and the number of people over 60 still working is quite low. in the wake of the economic crisis, governments are forced to cut spending to balance revenues and reduce budget deficits. the european agenda for adequate, safe and sustainable pensions is an excellent starting point for debates leading to a fair solution and a decent standard of living for europe's pensioners. it is important that we find ways to increase mobility and free movement in the labour market, which can solve some of the problems we face today. improving the employment rate by including marginalised people and increasing the retirement age in direct correlation with increasing life expectancy is also a viable option. complementing pay-as-you-go contributions (the current model) with private capitalised systems is an alternative to the crisis in the current pension system. equally important in the future will be the savings of each of us to supplement the amounts received through the traditional pension systems.
in writing. the european commission has published a green paper entitled 'towards adequate, sustainable and secure pension systems'. the content of the publication, its holistic approach, is confirmed by this report. stresses the need for transparency in the information provided to citizens and, in the current multiple crises, aims to help make accessible, reliable and responsible decisions on pensions, thus strengthening citizens' confidence in pension systems that are based on solid foundations and sustainable in the long term. it suggests that, taking into account the subsidiarity of the member states, the european community should focus not only on pension reforms but also on the sustainability of the financing system. member states are interdependent through their economies and the same applies to their pension systems. they should therefore harmonise their pension policies and improve the transparency of their pension systems, in particular by promoting the development of three-pillar pension systems. the individual design of pension entitlement, the life-course approach and the guidelines for the operation of supplementary pension schemes should be respected at the level of the guidelines by encouraging the exchange of good practices. the portability of the second pillar should be made possible, and equality between men and women should be better enforced in terms of pension entitlement, by taking into account periods of maternity, child-rearing and care for elderly family members.
the banking union is a vital project to break the link between heavily indebted governments and banks facing their own difficulties, and to avoid using taxpayers' money to bail out financial institutions. i welcome the important role that the european central bank will play in the supervision of banks in the member states participating in the single resolution mechanism, including through the possibility of giving instructions to the competent national authorities. i also believe that improving access to information and eliminating the possibility of judicial arbitration will lead to improved oversight. given that in romania, euro area banks hold three quarters of the banking system's assets and two thirds of its capital, and given my country's intention to adopt the single currency in the future, membership of the banking union becomes a necessity. in this context, i support the amendment to the european commission's original proposal to give non-euro area countries voting rights on the ecb's supervisory board. the risk of the banking union being divided into deciding and executing states has also been considerably reduced by the balanced voting system within the european banking authority. we are very close to completing the first pillar of the banking union, the single banking supervisory system, and i think it is worth congratulating all those who have made this happen, first of all commissioner barnier, the rapporteurs and the shadow rapporteurs. i would like to thank in particular the two rapporteurs, mrs thyssen and mr giegold, for the special attention they have paid to the participation of non-euro area member states in these reports. for my country, romania, it is important to participate in this single banking supervision system, not only because over 80% of banking assets are held by banks with foreign capital owned by euro area banks, but also because we trust in the professionalism of those who will carry out this supervision from the european central bank. i would stress, however, the need for the subsequent negotiations between the council, the european parliament and the european commission to establish clearly the responsibility of the european central bank towards the european parliament for the fulfilment of this new banking supervision function.
in writing. the new regulation provides the european central bank with certain specific powers necessary to carry out its task of supervising the european banking system, while also ensuring the opportunity to design a future european banking union that provides the public and economic actors with safe and sustainable financial services without major risks to the real economy of the european union. i also welcome the creation of a 'single supervisory mechanism' for the prudential supervision of credit institutions, thus fulfilling one of the necessary preconditions for recapitalising banks through the european stability mechanism and regaining confidence in the european banking sector. at the same time, i welcome the fact that this proposal includes appropriate safeguards to guarantee the participation in the decision-making process of member states outside the euro area as well, as they will also be affected by the new changes proposed due to the high degree of interdependence of the european banking system.
in writing. the adoption by the commission of the legislative proposals on the ssm for credit institutions led by the ecb is just one step in the ambitious project of building a european banking union. we need a single european supervisor to combat the vicious synergies between the troubled banks and the indebted states of the euro area. the key elements for a successful banking union should not exclude enhanced supervision, fiscal protection mechanisms and deposit insurance rules. attractive conditions must be created for non-euro area member states to participate in this banking project. a stable framework must be created to enable banks to fulfil their role as financiers of the economy, especially in situations where member states have limited capacity to fully address the problems. the single supervisor will prevent excessive risk taking by banks and increase pressure, acting over national authority, on banks to repair their balance sheets. we need predictability and rules to act in cases of 'mortgages' or bank liquidation. this legislative package has initiated the mechanism that will create in the long term a supranational european banking union, effectively covering the whole of the european single market.
the issue we are debating today, the access of dyslexic and blind people to books, is an important one and all the more serious because it has been perpetuated for years. both the member states of the union and the european parliament promote and respect fundamental rights under the charter of fundamental rights and through the ratification of a significant number of international treaties, including the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. so we have an obligation, beyond declarations and solemn commitments, not just to recognize, but to put these rights into practice, so that these people who are our fellow human beings, our fellow citizens, can have equal access to information and to community life, equal access to the labor market, if possible, and this can only be achieved by access to books specific to their disabilities. i would like to remind the european commission of the european parliament's clear position in this area and the resolution we adopted. as a member of the committee on petitions, i am convinced, commissioner, and honourable members, that these rights cannot and should not be treated exclusively from a commercial perspective. it would be shameful and unacceptable that at the beginning of the 21st century these people, who have already suffered in terms of their quality of life, should once again be discriminated against because of an absurd commercial concern on the part of some member states.
our debate today started from a figure from the world blind union, which shows that only 5% of books published are available in a format accessible to the blind, which is worrying, because these people are discriminated against in terms of access to books. i support the objective of the current negotiations in the world intellectual property organization for a treaty guaranteeing equal access for blind people with those who are visually impaired. we must find a balanced solution that meets this objective and at the same time does not cause disproportionate damage to copyright holders. blind associations have raised a number of issues related to the obligations of this treaty which make it difficult to distribute books in accessible formats across borders. we need to take these concerns into account and find negotiated solutions that facilitate the international distribution of these books so that this treaty really adds value for the visually impaired.
in writing. the exceptions introduced in favour of blind people should facilitate their access to special books. however, the provisions may make procedures more difficult and obtaining materials for the blind more difficult. in romania, as in other eu countries, people with visual impairments face important problems. because of the many certificates of disability issued to those who did not qualify, those who are truly in trouble do not receive sufficient help. the social exclusion of blind people in romania is a real fact, especially if we consider that access to books and special manuals is very difficult. also, their printing cannot be done without adequate funding. another problem is the limited number of schools where blind children can learn.
although major progress has been made in implementing the provisions of the stockholm programme action plan, delays remain. i am referring to one of the political priorities of the programme, namely the continuing enlargement of the schengen area. the document calls on the council, subject to the fulfilment of the requirements for the application of the schengen acquis, to adopt measures to allow for the abolition of border controls, and as is known, both romania and bulgaria have fulfilled the criteria for some time, a fact confirmed by both the commission and the european parliament. so if we want the stockholm programme to be a success, i think the political priority of the schengen enlargement must be met. i hope by the end of this year that will happen.
mr president, in recent years the mobility of people within the european union has created major problems, such as the settlement of cross-border inheritances, that may accelerate in the coming years. citizens own estates in different member states. that ownership triggers the application of multiple inheritance laws and creates conflicts of law. i consider that having a framework for european cooperation on succession is an accomplishment that brings legal security to all european citizens. the successions regulation retains the principle of one law applicable to succession by determining the deceased’s habitual residence. although the regulation does not deal with taxation, i believe that having only one law applying to your estate will provide an opportunity with regard to previously unavailable tax planning. the commission recommendation of 15 december 2011 regarding the elimination of double taxation of inheritances is a good step in this direction, and i will wait for the report in 2014 to see what the commission decision on this matter will be. a solution would probably be to have the certificate of avoiding double taxation apply in this matter of inheritance as well.
the issue of certificates of succession has been partially resolved by the adoption of regulation 650/2012, but difficulties continue to be reported with regard to the different level of taxation for heirs and double taxation. these issues are not new, but have been addressed in the committee on petitions, where i am vice-chairman. i believe that from 2015, when the european certificate of succession regulation will come into force, taxation aspects will have to be harmonised. legislation, not just a recommendation, would therefore be needed to avoid double taxation of inheritances. this would remove legal uncertainty and create a single european framework in this area. at the same time, the adoption of a legislative act would be a step towards creating an area of freedom, security and justice.
access to documents of the european institutions is an important way for citizens to monitor the work of the union, and greater transparency would also increase citizens' confidence, contributing to a better understanding of the european decision-making process. that is why i believe that the present impasse must be overcome and that a regulation adapted to reality must be adopted. although parliament has adopted its position on the amendment of the legislative act, this procedure is currently blocked. it is important to give european citizens greater access to documents of the institutions, whether agencies or offices. the time limit of 15 working days within which the documents are to be provided shall be respected. i also consider that a similar time limit should be imposed for the settlement of requests for confirmation.
to help the eu emerge from the prolonged recession, the roadmap for completing economic and monetary union should focus on social and growth measures. unfortunately, this is a new attempt to make the labour market and wages more flexible and a danger for social europe. coordination of structural reforms at european level is needed to reduce these disparities. the commission document, however, seems to be aimed at implementing a specific type of reform: those centred around austerity. these include further privatisation and wage cuts, further deregulation of labour law and further weakening of trade unions. europe will not emerge from the political and economic abyss it is in by budgetary austerity alone, and the economic recovery in the united states confirms this idea. but it is not too late to start on the right path. the measures the commission should promote include the introduction of a national minimum wage in all member states and the placing of the social pillar at the centre of economic policies. at the same time, solidarity at european level, expressed through the joint guaranteeing of public debts, is becoming of fundamental importance for the future.
the impact of the economic crisis makes the impact of tax fraud, tax evasion and aggressive tax planning on european public finances an increasingly pressing political issue. with the damage caused by these phenomena estimated at €1 trillion, european and national authorities alike are forced to take decisive action to limit and combat these situations, which threaten both the sustainability of the internal market and the efficiency of the various tax systems. i therefore support the action plan proposed by the european commission to combat tax fraud, tax evasion and tax evasion. these measures must be countered by more decisive action by the european institutions at international level and by increased cooperation between the member states of the union.

in writing. − every year, the european citizen pays a cost of eur 2 000 as a result of tax fraud and tax evasion. i voted for this resolution against fraud, tax evasion and tax havens to support the european social model, which is under pressure from the fiscal gap during the most serious economic, financial and social crisis in recent years. i support the ambitious target of halving the fiscal gap by 2020 through national reform programmes for stability and growth. the public revenues thus available can finance fiscal consolidation measures while mitigating the effects of austerity. if, in order to combat tax fraud and tax evasion by natural and legal persons, the report provides for measures at national level in the form of the allocation of substantial resources to tax administrations and control staff, as regards tax havens, i support the proposed direction, namely a common european approach to them by all member states.
in writing. − every year, eur 1 trillion is lost to tax evasion and avoidance in the eu. in 2011, the size of the shadow economy was estimated at around eur 2.4 billion. this represents 19.2 % of eu-27 gdp. last april, ‘offshore leaks’ disclosed details of 130 000 offshore accounts following a years-long investigation by the international consortium of investigative journalists together with 36 international newspapers. moreover, the ‘tax justice network’ estimated that eur 16 trillion to eur 25 trillion are hidden in offshore places. i am highly concerned about the magnitude of offshore financial activities and the lack of encouragement to disclose offshore accounts. this is why i voted in favour of this report. i welcome that the present report recognises the vital importance of independent investigative journalism in exposing fraud schemes, corruption and organised crime. i urge the commission to fund investigative journalism and to reinforce the eu’s legal framework in accordance with the ‘follow the money’ principle. exposing cases where huge amounts of money are diverted from the normal financial circuits and hidden in tax havens should be revealed to the public.
i voted in favour of this report because crossborder tax evasion requires member states to work together to tackle the problem. the new framework for legislative cooperation, adopted over the past two years, facilitates the development of new instruments by the commission and the member states. but even in this context, there is a need for increased information sharing and compliance with minimum standards of good fiscal governance. one of the instruments we should take seriously is the removal of tax obstacles to crossborder transactions. the increasingly high level of tax evasion in romania, well above the european average, has led to the issue being prioritised at national level. this situation led to the creation of an interministerial committee to combat tax evasion by the former right-wing government.
in writing. − the main challenge facing european union societies, states and institutions today is the imperative to overcome the economic and financial crisis. although strong signals of stability have been sent by european political leaders and institutions in recent times, more needs to be done to revive growth and create jobs. the effects of the recession have led to falling incomes, job losses, a decline in the real living standards of european citizens and increased social exclusion. in this context, although fiscal policies remain a sovereign prerogative of the member states and although there is a high degree of coordination at this level between member states, overcoming the economic crisis requires intensifying the process of cooperation between member states. at the same time, it is important that member states avoid, in the process of taxing consumption, exacerbating social inequalities and worsening the conditions of competitiveness of european entrepreneurs.
in writing. − the debt crisis has raised several new issues in the eu that require the appropriate adjustment of fiscal policies in the short, medium and long term. it is well known that tax policy is a matter for the member state and that the different tax systems of the member states must be respected and that barriers to the internal market and uncertainties and misunderstandings arising from legal differences should be eliminated as soon as possible. there is thus a need to create at union level a well-integrated system coordinating national tax systems in order to take account of the reductions and increases made in the national systems. to restore the credibility of fiscal policy and reduce sovereign debt, fiscal discipline and structural reforms must be introduced. increasing taxes in certain areas, such as excise duties, could have some positive effects, channelling additional resources and thus bringing benefits to citizens and the real economy. tax incentives for research and development can help to create growth and jobs in knowledge-based economies. member states should also complete the procedures for all ongoing legislative proposals on tax fraud, tax evasion, tax evasion, aggressive tax planning and tax havens.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i believe that it is to the benefit of citizens to have a clear and transparent tax environment within the single market. the report suggests creating a system to coordinate the tax systems of all member states. i believe such action would contribute to reducing levels of fraud and evasion and i think it would be a huge step forward in order to strengthen growth and improve public finances. providing tax incentives for research and development and suppressing the barriers of the internal market will foster long-term benefits. the eu needs a tax policy that will lessen the dramatic effects of the economic and financial crisis which our citizens are facing.
in writing. - mr president, the annual losses in the european union due to tax evasion and tax avoidance represent a cost of approximately eur 2 000 for each eu citizen. there's money that's being lost from the budget that could be used for education, research or other vital areas to stimulate long-term economic growth and employment. i voted in favour of this report because i support the creation at eu level of a mechanism to coordinate national tax systems, taking into account the particularities of each. for crossborder, internal and external investments in the eu, ensuring a transparent, predictable and stable tax environment is in the interest of all businesses, citizens, state institutions. member states must ensure that tax discipline is respected and that dissuasive measures are put in place to reduce tax fraud and evasion. thank you, thank you!
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation because the charter of fundamental rights introduces a set of principles which underpin the democratic functioning of the union. i should point out that extending the provisions of the protocol to the czech republic would have limited effects and would probably increase legal uncertainty. there is also a risk that the standards of protection of fundamental rights will be lowered if the protocol is applied in the czech republic. at the same time, the unknown position of the czech parliament can create even more political confusion. therefore, i believe that the recommendation not to convene a convention to consider the proposed extension of the protocol is the best solution at this time. the czech authorities should take a clear position on the protocol in order to settle the debate on the subject.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the current situation regarding the application of protocol 30 should be clarified as soon as possible. the czech republic wished to accede to the protocol due to concerns about the effects of the charter on the beneš decrees. however, since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, no relevant case law has been recorded in czech case law concerning the application of the charter. and i believe that the act cannot create exceptions to the application of the charter of fundamental rights. the fact that the czech senate voted against the application of the protocol in 2009 also shows that there is no clear position of the czech authorities. i think the problem should be solved internally first, and then we could go ahead with the proposed changes. this would avoid legal uncertainty.
in writing. − the principle of mutual recognition and judicial cooperation in civil protection matters offers the prospect of uniting the diversity of civil and administrative courts throughout the union. people for whom a civil protection measure has been adopted will in future feel that they are part of a single system of protection designed to provide them with the security they need in any of the countries of the european union. i too believe that the protection enjoyed by a citizen in one eu member state should not disappear when that person chooses to move to another state, but that every effort should be made to ensure that that protection is recognised and respected by the authorities of the state of destination. in this respect, i welcome the use of the standardised and multilingual certificate proposed by the rapporteurs and the increased attention paid to the assistance and information provided to the protected person. the provision of these two activities in an accessible language, through translation or interpretation of protection measures, is a guarantee that citizens will receive the protection they deserve in another member state to which they decide to move.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it will strengthen the rights of victims of crime in the union. the proposal is another step towards the objective of creating a common area of freedom, security and justice. simplifying the recognition of protection orders entails increasing trust in the judicial systems of the member states. the measures are aimed at protecting victims of violence, especially in cases of domestic violence, harassment and violence against children. as vulnerable groups to such crimes, women and children should enjoy protection throughout the union. i also welcome the administrative provisions which will no longer require the legalization of the certificate to be recognised in another member state. this will reduce costs and formalities and harmonise the protection of victims of crime across the union.
in writing. − this proposal responds to the need for a comprehensive european legal framework capable of ensuring that victims of crime are recognised for the harm they have suffered and are afforded the highest possible level of protection within the union. this will complement the european protection order directive, which ensures the mutual recognition of protection measures in criminal matters. the combined application of the two instruments (criminal and civil) will allow persons enjoying a protection order to move freely and safely within the eu as provided for in article 3 of the treaty on european union and will ultimately lead to the strengthening and development of the area of freedom, security and justice in the union. i think it would be useful to set up a mechanism which would eliminate intermediary formalities by using a standardised and multilingual certificate. this would ensure not only the promptness and speed of the reconnaissance but also the execution of the protective measures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report and congratulate the rapporteur on her work in preparing the report on this regulation, which complements the directive on the protection order covering criminal matters, the two instruments together including as many measures as possible to be taken by the member states. the regulation on the mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters will enter into force on 11 january 2015. it will apply in all member states and provide that protection granted in one member state will be maintained when the victim moves or travels to another member state. the procedure for applying for protection will also be simplified by removing all intermediate formalities. in order to ensure recognition and enforcement of protection throughout the union, the regulation includes a standard certificate in several languages containing the essential information. by using it, translation costs will be minimized, so that the protected person will have no additional expense.
in writing. - mr. president, i voted in favour of the report. it is important that there are laws to deter and punish violations of individual freedoms and rights, but it is equally important that victims are supported by the authorities and have legislation to protect them. in 2012, statistics showed that in romania between 75 and 80% of women are abused in the domestic space (verbal, psychological, physical or sexual). these amendments particularly support the vulnerable group of persons subject to violence within the family by simplifying formalities and by european recognition of their special status. the restrictions on the mobility of victims of convicted violence that have existed until now are thus removed. it is important that this regulation is transposed and applied as soon as possible, including the administrative component of the new standardised forms, so that concrete effects can be seen among beneficiaries. thank you!
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because one of the most important improvements this agreement will bring is the recognition of the status of authorised economic operator (aeo) of european companies by the canadian authorities, following the example of the agreements already established between the eu and norway, switzerland, japan or the usa. furthermore, this agreement highlights the need to increase security throughout the supply chain, while facilitating legitimate trade between the eu and canada, and creates a framework for exploring future means of cooperation to improve practices in this area. i would like to draw attention to the fact that the problems relating to agricultural products are still unresolved, in particular the export of beef to europe and european dairy products to canada.
in writing. − customs relations between the european union and canada are based on the customs cooperation and mutual assistance agreement on customs matters of 1998. the objective of the new agreement is to strengthen customs aspects of the security of the international trade logistics chain, including container security, while facilitating legitimate trade. the agreement provides a legal basis for enhanced customs cooperation between the eu and canada on issues such as risk standards, security controls, minimum standards for risk management techniques, information and data exchange, strategic partnership in the field of goods inspection, and cooperation in multilateral fora such as the world customs organization. as a member of the delegation for relations with canada, i consider this risk-based approach to be appropriate for the global security of the supply chain, which allows for the smooth conduct of legal international trade without constituting an unnecessary economic burden for authorities and commercial operators.
in writing. − i encourage better cooperation between the eu and canada, as i consider risk management to be one of the union's priorities for developing better trade relations. by this agreement, the european union is successfully aligning itself with global security standards, as it is clear that in a highly globalised society no country can ensure supply chain security alone, and international cooperation and standards are essential. it is a turning point in mutual recognition, including the recognition of trade partnership programmes, with trade facilitation measures through the aeo (authorised economic operator) programme and the canadian pip (protection partners) programme. in addition, the estimated annual benefits of approximately eur 11.6 billion for the union and eur 8.2 billion for canada, together with the fact that the agreement has no implications for the union budget, represent another major advantage generated by its approval and implementation.
in writing. − in a globalised world, where no country can ensure supply chain security alone, international cooperation and the promotion of global security standards are essential. the eu-canada agreement on customs cooperation is part of a broader process and sustained actions undertaken by the eu over the last decade in the field of supply chain security and risk management. in this context, i welcome and approve the conclusion of the agreement on mutual recognition of customs security between the european union and canada. this new agreement establishes the necessary legal basis for enhanced customs cooperation between the european union and canada and will facilitate legitimate trade without creating an unnecessary economic burden for authorities and traders. moreover, it will complement the comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta) currently being negotiated.
in writing. − i voted for this recommendation, as i truly believe that every opportunity to bring the eu and canada closer should be seized. by enhancing customs cooperation and mutual assistance, this agreement will help to secure the supply chain and permit legitimate international trade to flow easily. nevertheless, in the context of the comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta) under negotiation, canada should be committed to strengthening its partnership with all member states and their citizens. however, while i welcome measures that improve our trade flows, goods and services cannot be more important then our own citizens. i believe that every citizen of the eu should be treated equally, but because of the lack of reciprocity in the case of visa requirements, romanian, bulgarian and czech citizens are being subjected to unfair discrimination. as i mentioned before, this point is a priority and will need to be resolved.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, because i consider the agreement to be a natural step forward in the eu’s customs relations with canada in the matter of end-to-end supply chain security and risk management. taking into account the 1998 agreement on customs cooperation and mutual assistance in customs matters (cmaa), the agreement will establish a legal function for increased eu-canada customs cooperation that aims to secure the logistics chain of international trade in order to facilitate legitimate trade. furthermore, it will be a milestone for mutual recognition of agreements on customs security and on supply chain security policy. within the framework of the eu’s authorised economic operator (aeo), negotiated both with the us and china, we have registered over 10 000 european companies as certified safe traders since 2008. the agreement with canada is an opportunity to increase this number in our efforts to secure supply chains and to extend the legal framework for scarce resources concentration on high-risk consignments.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the purpose of the financial supervisory mechanism is to provide a coherent response to the crisis at european level. the mechanism is an important step towards the creation of a european banking union. cooperation between the european banking authority and the european central bank is therefore essential to achieve the objectives proposed. as it is aimed in particular at euro area banks, the supervisory mechanism should take into account the risk of spillovers of euro area banking crises to non-euro area members. to deepen integration and move towards genuine political union, harmonisation of financial sector rules is mandatory. romania, although not yet part of the euro area, will be able to participate in the mechanism together with the euro area countries and the other participating non-euro countries.
in writing. − in 2008, when the financial crisis spread across europe, there were 27 different systems of bank regulation in operation in the eu, all based on national rules and national rescue mechanisms. although some form of coordination exists at eu level, it is concerned with relatively informal exchanges of information and cooperation procedures. the european banking authority was established in 2011 to help coordinate the activities of national regulators and ensure the consistent application of eu-wide rules. the banking union proposal will result in a change in the way euro area banks are supervised, creating a single supervisory mechanism to be set up within the european central bank.
in writing. − the european banking authority was established in 2011 with the main objective of ensuring the supervision and stability of the financial system at european level. i believe that this new proposal will give the european banking authority the tools it still needs to be able to achieve the most comprehensive supervision of the european banking system. in view of the high degree of contagion, i believe that supervision must be as broad as possible to cover banks in member states without the single european currency, thus ensuring the stability of the whole european financial system and not just that of the euro area. the implementation of a single regulatory framework for supervision is a natural consequence of the common desire to simplify, harmonise and review supervisory and regulatory mechanisms.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because there are high expectations of union citizens for the banking union and the deadline for the single supervisory mechanism is fast approaching. the romanian banking system is dominated by the branches of euro area banks. so my country is subject to similar risks as any eurozone country, with romanian citizens being directly vulnerable. i also believe that euro area countries need to reach an agreement with non-euro area countries to apply the mechanism. even if the final vote is to be postponed, i believe that the inclusion of the subject on the agenda of the plenary session shows the determination and urgency of the achievement of banking union.
in writing. − i welcome the rapporteur's recommendations and draw attention to the safety measures that member states must take, especially with regard to european citizens using pyrotechnic articles in a non-professional context. i consider that the market surveillance of these products is an activity that requires close coordination at the level of all member states, especially in the context of the expansion of distance transactions in these products via the internet. one of the major dimensions that must and is considered in this report is public health. from the perspective of better regulation of pyrotechnic articles, public health means offering increased protection to consumers of such products, whether children or the elderly. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because in my view the directive is part of our efforts to establish a common framework for the marketing of pyrotechnic products. it also deepens and strengthens the rules for consumer protection, which are so important for pyrotechnic articles. i am confident that the new legislative framework will address a number of gaps in european union law and is a natural step towards completing the single market. as regards the romanian case, i consider it worth mentioning that since the restriction of the marketing of pyrotechnic articles in 2006, the number of cases of persons injured by them has decreased from over 350 to 25 per year.
in writing. − the inconsistent implementation and enforcement of current union harmonisation legislation in the member states, together with the complexity of the regulations, has led to increasing difficulties for both economic operators and authorities in interpreting and correctly applying the legislation, leading to unequal market conditions and also to the introduction of unsafe products on the market. in order to ensure that all economic sectors covered by union harmonisation legislation benefit from the improvements brought about by the new legislative framework, the provisions of the decision should be integrated into existing product legislation.
in writing. − the audiovisual media services directive 2010/13/eu is the cornerstone of media regulation in the european union. this directive has been implemented to a different extent by the member states. i believe that special attention should be paid to minors who are most exposed to the dangers of commercial communications. i am referring in particular to advertising for alcoholic beverages, unhealthy products or advertising that encourages certain consumption patterns. i believe that the measures taken by the member states to protect minors, including the tightening of national provisions, are encouraging. member states should be encouraged to develop codes of conduct addressing the issue of inappropriate audiovisual commercial communications during children's programmes.
in writing. − connected tv brings with it both important opportunities and significant challenges. in the context of new technological solutions, we need to ask ourselves how we can successfully promote european works and the creations of independent producers, how we can protect consumers, including children, from the excessive influence of advertising, how we can create a level playing field for broadcasting companies, how we can protect freedom of expression and media pluralism and how we can promote media education, especially among young people. the protection of minors, which is the subject of the report, is of major importance. minors are most exposed to potential dangers, especially those presented by commercial communications. this includes advertising for alcoholic beverages, unhealthy products or advertising that encourages certain consumption patterns, for which advertising spots have been sanctioned by various measures taken by the member states (including by tightening national provisions to protect the category of minors). media education is another key objective of the directive. given that access to channels and choice of audiovisual services have increased significantly, we consider it appropriate to integrate media education and digital skills, especially in digital media, into national school curricula.
in writing. − i welcome the complex nature of the directive, which combines the right to the provision of audiovisual services with the right to freedom of expression, information and the protection of the public interest. i stress the importance of making these services accessible to all, especially those with disabilities, protecting european works and independent productions (the share is 10%), protecting minors, avoiding excessive advertising (the share is 12 minutes out of 60), and guaranteeing media freedom and pluralism. however, it is critical that the directive does not deal with ensuring equal opportunities for women and men, nor with protecting the image of women in the provision of these services, given that audiovisual media services very often contain messages discriminatory against women. the media education that the directive is talking about must also include the principle of gender equality.
in writing. − i support this report because i believe that we need to have a concrete assessment of the implementation at european level of the audiovisual media services directive 2010/13/eu. the european commission is facing difficulties in drawing up the report on the application of the directive because this directive, which regulates the media at eu level, has not been implemented in a timely or adequate manner by all member states. it is also vital that member states encourage the media (broadcasting companies) to provide services to increase accessibility to information for disadvantaged or disabled segments of society (blind or hearing-impaired people).
in writing. − in an increasingly active and dynamic society in terms of information and dissemination of information to the public, regardless of where they are located, it is essential that all european citizens can have access to media services. as such, i consider that member states must encourage and facilitate the provision of media services by broadcasting companies to persons with visual or hearing impairments, who have the same rights to information as all other persons. however, it is essential that all broadcasters first have a clearer vision of the needs of these people and take more action to develop technologies that ensure wider access to programmes for all citizens by developing, inter alia, audio descriptions, audio/voice subtitles, sign language and navigation menus, with specific reference to electronic programme guides.
in writing. − media broadcasting in europe has suffered significant changes in past years. we are concerned about the importance of promoting cultural diversity through the distribution of european works. the audiovisual market is part of the single market. this own-initiative report comes in response to the first report from the commission to parliament on the application of directive 2010/13/eu (avmsd). the report, among other points, aims to analyse the effectiveness of the directive and the progress it has made. the report encourages the commission, trying to solve some misunderstandings, to examine what ‘uncertainties or inaccuracies in the definitions have led to difficulties in implementation in the member states’. in the report, it also said that member states should ‘take effective measures to promote better synergies among regulatory authorities [...] so that eu films can reach a wider audience both within and beyond the eu on linear and non-linear services’. the commission has to analyse in depth the evaluation of the markets and also of consumer behaviour in this time of changes. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which welcomes the first report on the application and the related effectiveness of directive 2010/13/eu. the purpose of european multimedia content is to promote european programmes and works and to bring the voter closer to his or her representatives in the institutions. but not only: the directive sets out to assess the effective implementation of the rights to information, the protection of minors, freedom of expression and the protection of minorities in all eu countries. this is an ambitious task, with important objectives, which must be developed and reviewed in the light of a future that is different, also for the new media channels, which are increasingly diversified and hybrid.
in writing. − regulating relations between media operators is necessary, as concentration of media ownership can undermine press freedom or have effects in terms of encouraging corruption. romania is a negative example in this respect, with the largest press trusts owned by politicians or people directly involved in the political sphere. manipulating public opinion has unfortunately become a rule that more and more tv stations are guided by, the most relevant example being that of the intact trust (with 6 tv stations) owned by dan voiculescu, accused in corruption cases and former collaborator of the communist security. the pressure exerted by such media institutions has a direct effect in diminishing the plurality of opinion and through aggressive campaigns created against prosecutors, magistrates or judges of the constitutional court, by which they try to discredit them and implicitly attack their independence, trying to influence the act of justice. this is also criticized in the latest mcv report, which speaks of the questionable effectiveness of the surveillance activity carried out by the national audiovisual council, where a review of existing rules is needed to guarantee that freedom of the press is accompanied by adequate protection of institutions and fundamental rights.
in writing. − the consequences of this legislation are far-reaching, and i therefore welcome the ongoing scrutiny of its implementation. this report recognises some of the limitations of the avms directive, for example those relating to the self-regulation of advertising of junk food to children. i believe we need much stronger restrictions than those currently in place. voluntary measures, such as those contained in the eu pledge, do not go far enough and really just serve as a way for manufacturers to avoid proper regulation. we are facing an obesity epidemic with huge consequences, and part of the solution lies in restricting the promotion of high fat and high sugar foods to children.
madam president, syria marks a break between grand politics, the interaction between the great powers and its materialisation on the ground, leading to the suspension of the responsibility to protect principles. both intervention and non-intervention have high costs, but the factor which ultimately counts is the syrian people. the civil war has generated millions of both internal and external refugees who have fled insecurity only to find it in their new locations, complicating the region’s already complex political, security and economic situation, as lebanon and jordan indicate. the solution to the refugee problem lies in syria and it is exclusively political – it is just that things went too far to make a dialogue with the bashar regime possible. moreover, the opposition continues to be fragmented, and foreign involvement on both sides continues unabated, complicating the situation with every passing day. one wonders how many lives could have been saved and how much destruction avoided if the un security council had been allowed to act earlier in the conflict. the eu and the member states which are already vigorously involved in managing the social consequences of the civil war should continue their involvement, taking the lead in the international efforts to alleviate this exponentially-increasing humanitarian problem.
if syria today has not reached the situation of rwanda or afghanistan, it is because of its neighbors: turkey, jordan and lebanon. the ability of these countries to receive and host refugees depends on the support of the western world, depends on the support of the european union. the crisis will spiral out of control completely when neighboring countries are unable to take in syrian refugees, whose numbers are likely to double by the end of the year. we must bear in mind two things: first, that this support is not sustainable in the long term - that is why efforts are needed to find a political solution; second, that the millions of refugees, over 60% of whom are children or young people, will need constant support after returning home to rebuild their lives. finally, a final remark is related to those refugees who were displaced from syria without being syrians, and i am referring primarily to the palestinians - they should not be ignored either.
member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − madam president, during the arab spring, the european union froze the assets of senior figures from the former tunisian, egyptian and libyan regimes. today, as everyone who travels to the region can attest, the return of misappropriated and frozen assets is of great political importance. for the people of tunisia, egypt and libya, this is a matter of justice and dignity. they want an end to the impunity and corruption of the past; they want the misappropriated assets to be returned and invested in their countries. although the competence of the european union is limited in this matter, it is a priority for the high representative and for myself. let me highlight some of the actions taken over the past few months. we have renewed our sanctions for a further 12 months to give egypt, tunisia and libya time to achieve the return of assets. we have modified our sanctions legislation to ensure that information-sharing on assets can be facilitated. we have simplified the process for transferring assets to tunisian, egyptian and libyan authorities once a judgment is obtained. we co-organised an expert seminar which brought together members of the tunisian judiciary, international organisations and the member states and which allowed our tunisian colleagues to improve their expertise and rethink their asset recovery strategy. as part of the follow-up to the european union-egypt task force, we are developing a roadmap for asset recovery. we are also using the european union’s influence to raise the profile of this issue. internally, we have addressed asset recovery in the council and in several meetings and events organised with parliament. externally, we have raised asset recovery at the g8’s deauville partnership. unfortunately, despite our efforts, progress on asset recovery has not been what we hoped for. the political will is there, but the ownership of these assets has been deliberately obscured, and judicial procedures must be followed. therefore, the frozen assets cannot just be released overnight. ownership must rightfully be transferred to the new state structures. this is a complex legal process which must be resolved bilaterally between tunisia, egypt and libya and the individual european union member states concerned. the european union is ready to facilitate this process as much as our competences allow. we must not use complexity as an excuse for delay. however, due process must be respected while we all work together. the european union will continue to work with our partners, member states and international organisations to accelerate the process so that the money returns to where it belongs.
on behalf of the epp group. we are discussing today the recovery of assets for the countries engaged in the arab spring, more than two years after the beginning of the transformations that the southern neighbourhood has experienced. as commissioner füle suggested earlier, i think there are two perspectives involved. i'm talking about the prospects of the citizens of tunisia, egypt and libya. it's first of all the perspective, if you will allow me to use this expression, economic; it emphasizes the economic, financial importance, first of all, for the governments of the arab spring countries, who are facing the challenge of economic reconstruction, and from this perspective, certainly, the recovery is seen as a means of putting something at the foundation of reconstruction. on the other hand, we have the other perspective, i would say even more important, the perspective of justice and dignity. citizens of tunisia, egypt and libya want their assets back because they see it as a measure of justice, given that those assets have been tied to decades of corruption. on the other hand, it's a long process, it's a complex process, as also said earlier, we remember that in the philippines the assets that ferdinand marcos had stolen were not recovered until a quarter of a century later. in some of the countries mentioned, specifically in tunisia, so far only $28 million has been recovered from an account in lebanon, very little. what we can do is to cooperate at member state level by providing technical and legal assistance to speed up the process as much as possible.
i am a supporter of enlargement of the union, whether it is eastward enlargement of europe or whether it is enlargement to the western balkans. however, bosnia and herzegovina is the only country in the region that has not made progress in european integration. a major reason could be a lack of vision when it comes to where the country should go. the administrative structure of the country also makes decision-making difficult. there is doubt among both politicians and the public about bosnia's ability to function as a genuine state. but the differences between politicians, their own interests put before the national interest, stop the eu from getting closer, just as it is in the republic of moldova, so whether we are talking about expansion to the east or to the western balkans, politicians find it difficult to reach a consensus. the situation of minorities is another area of concern. the constitution only allows ethnic bosniaks, serbs and croats to run for the presidency of the country or for the upper house. i would point out that there is a risk of creating a climate of scepticism among the population.
on behalf of the alde group. beyond the balanced report by our colleague mr howitt, a few questions are worth asking in this debate today, because macedonia, along with turkey, represents the countries that are waiting for a positive signal from the european union. it seems that turkey will be a failure, and probably macedonia, if there is no will. the political will must be demonstrated here in brussels, because you are always asking us for more europe, but unfortunately you are not doing much to achieve more europe, and we are being guided by the somewhat unilateral policies of some member states, which is not, in my view, acceptable. this is a political decision which is vital for the union. because, in view of the failure of the eastern partnership, which is probably foreseeable, i believe that a failure of enlargement policies would also create an image that would not put us in a favourable position in front of the european citizens in terms of trust and cohesion. commissioner, we were talking about reforms - you testified that reforms are taking place! we all criticize certain political behaviour, but i would not like to use a double standard: there are countries, member states, where political behaviour is far from being somehow necessary and consistent with a democratic standard of the european union. it is important, however, to think positively, to avoid using terms that are somewhat obstructive. i believe that in macedonia, as in the whole area, ethnic relations have normalized, there are citizens who have dual citizenship, because this country allows dual citizenship, which others do not tolerate. we should no longer be talking about what's called antiquation, a phenomenon of retrieving history. history is a good of cultural identity of every people and we must respect this for macedonia - that we do it more or better or worse, from an aesthetic point of view it is not for us to judge, but it is certain that from our point of view, the european liberals, it is vital to start negotiations and we support this.
