member of the commission. − mr president, when listening to these speeches, i must say that i have to come to the conclusion that i am starting on a very dangerous enterprise, because around every corner there are dangers, difficulties, things that might go wrong, things that we have to protect. many speakers also mentioned the possibilities and opportunities of this agreement, but i do not fully understand why, as the biggest economy in the world and convinced (i think) of our values – mr schulz, for example, said that we should preserve them – we are so afraid in the end to negotiate with a country which is different from us. of course, if it were not, we would not have to negotiate with them, but in any case it is closer to us than a lot of the countries we are negotiating with. that is also very difficult to deny. so i do not see why we cannot have a somewhat more open approach on this. secondly, continuing on the subject of openness, i have no problem saying what we are doing and what we want to achieve and, when not speaking in public, how i want to achieve this. but you are all politicians. so you should know – and i think you do know – that you cannot negotiate openly. you do not do that in your parties either; you do not do that in your constituencies. you need to focus – and yes, of course we have to report on what we are doing, explaining why we are doing things and why we are making some concessions; we will have to make concessions in the course of these negotiations. but you need a certain degree of confidentiality in negotiations. you also need it because your counterpart is asking for it; if not, you cannot negotiate. it is interesting that it seems that there is a copy of one of the drafts of the negotiating mandate. so what? it is a draft. the presidency has, of course, to make sure that they come to an agreement within the council, so they put forward possible ways to get out of any difficulties that we have to deal with. immediately, very vocal members of this parliament say that this is a scandal and that we are traitors and cannot be trusted. of course you can trust me, because in the end you can say ‘no’. you have done so in the past. you said ‘no’ to acta: i am still not convinced that it was the right choice, but you decided to do so and that was how it was. you have the final word. but a parliament is not created to negotiate. it is not its job. i think i have been in a parliament for a longer time than most of you –25 years. maybe there are some who have been in a parliament as long – mr brok has already left, but he has certainly been in a parliament for more than 25 years – but not very many. i have never sought to negotiate an agreement from within a parliament because it simply does not work. what you have to do – and you do it in an eloquent way – is indicate the important points that you want to mention, that you want me to look at and which you will question me about. you will scrutinise me and in the end will vote against me if i do not do that. but a parliament cannot negotiate, because a parliament only exists as a body when it votes. outside of voting you take up individual positions. you cannot negotiate with 20, 30 or 50 different positions. that is not possible. you need to negotiate on the basis of a mandate, and then, of course, you have to demonstrate that you have been following your mandate. many of you have expressed concern about agriculture. mr de castro has disappeared, but i was very pleased when he mentioned that we also have a lot of offensive interests in agriculture. we have: on agrifood and on geographical indications. geographical indications are also protected in the united states, by the way, but in a different way, with trademarks, and there we have certainly very important offensive interests to defend. there will be discussions on gmos, but the results of the negotiation will not be that any gmo can be imported. of course there will be discussions on hormone beef, but the result of the negotiation will not be that it will be possible to import hormone beef into the european market, because we have to negotiate within the framework of the existing legislation. this is exactly the same for the audiovisual sector, which i understand is a very sensitive sector – one of the reasons being, by the way, that as politicians you have a lot to do with this sector. you want to be on tv, just as i have to be on tv and the ministers have to be on tv, so that people know what we are arguing for. this is very sensitive in any parliament, you can be sure of that. but on the other hand, this is a sector where you see things changing in an ever more rapid way. numerical is not just arriving – it is here. it is going to blur all the existing schemes of production, it is going to blur the business models that we deploy here and in other parts of the world. is this really the right moment to say simply that we are not ready to discuss this with (by the way) the biggest producer of audiovisual products in the world? is this wise? i think it is wise to say, look, there are a number of red lines. i explained them very clearly in my introduction. we will look at that. we will look at the result of all this. what does it bring us? i think we need to have a number of discussions with the united states, because what is happening with the delivery systems of content will force us, whether or not we have negotiations with the us, to look at our business models. we will have to. it has become much less anchored anywhere, and traditional politics start from topics and subjects and rules being anchored somewhere. that anchor is disappearing, and i think that is why it is a very good reason to have at least a discussion, one that does not have any risk for you because, based on the treaty of lisbon, in the end a unanimous decision by the council of ministers is required. you need a majority in parliament and you need a unanimous decision in the council. where is the risk in having a discussion on that? i do not understand it. maybe somebody can explain it to me, but i do not grasp it. except of course that, yes, i know there are symbols in this and if ever there was something to be afraid of in politics it is symbols, because when you start talking about symbols you forget about the content.

in writing. the transatlantic trade relationship is the backbone of the world economy. together, the european union and the united states account for about half of the world's gdp (47%) and one third of the world's trade flows. every day, almost eur 2 billion worth of goods and services are traded bilaterally, helping to create jobs and grow our economies. the economic links between our economies are deep and diverse, with total investment of over eur 2 trillion. the latest estimates show that an ambitious and comprehensive eu-us agreement could generate, by 2027, total annual gains representing an increase of 0.5% of eu gdp and 0.4% of us gdp. they would equate to an additional annual revenue of eur 86 billion for the eu economy and eur 65 billion for the us economy.
the restoration of tariff preferences for myanmar was a natural step as a series of comprehensive reforms were initiated. the release of the activist aung san suu kyi from house arrest in 2010, which i campaigned for many times, and the holding of free and fair elections in 2012, are small but important steps towards real democratization. the meeting between president barosso and the myanmar leader also led to an agreement to explore the possibility of concluding a bilateral investment agreement. however, i would like to draw attention to some problems that still persist in myanmar: the practice of unpaid forced labour, used mainly by the military, is still widespread in many regions.
the european union should not be held legally responsible for the actions of individual member states. in the case of bilateral investment agreements, each member state shall be responsible for non-compliance with the provisions of the respective acts. this is all the more important since bilateral investment has become a community competence since the adoption of the treaty of lisbon. however, the 190 bilateral investment treaties between the member states have a discriminatory effect, as the standards of protection vary from one treaty to another. in addition, there are cases where investors from outside the union enjoy more rights and privileges than those from inside. this is unacceptable as it creates barriers to the single market and discourages intra-community investment.
european territorial cooperation effectively contributes to strengthening links between regions, ensuring a high quality of life for eu citizens. innovative projects and joint problem-solving create opportunities between european citizens in regions with similar development potential. macro-regions are innovative forms of cooperation that put the principles of multilevel governance into practice. they have the capacity to bring together local, regional and community authorities to exploit effectively the common development potential. a successful macroregion must be a first step towards a european model capable of combining smart, inclusive and sustainable growth of european regions. the baltic and danube strategies confirm the appropriateness of the macro-regional initiative for the alps. i believe that territorial cooperation groups play a key role in the implementation of macro-regional strategies. egtcs can become the platforms for implementing territorial development strategies and can help to strengthen cooperation between authorities at different levels. the common development objectives, initiated by the municipalities of the alpine regions, cover areas such as competitiveness, innovation, water, energy, environment, climate, increased accessibility and transport. their implementation will, as with the danube strategy, turn obstacles into advantages and contribute to the prosperity of mountain regions. in the alps today, in the carpathians tomorrow. the commission has made it clear that macro-regions cannot benefit from separate funding, administrative structures or new legislation. but the macro-regional strategy must be encouraged by firm, concrete measures. that is why i propose that projects included in these strategies receive special attention in the framework of the partnership contracts and future operational programmes, with additional advantageous scores. in addition, for macro-regional strategies to bear concrete fruit, effective communication and a continuous exchange of good practices between actors in the regions involved are needed so that the actions undertaken produce measurable results.
i would like to stress the importance of a macro-regional strategy for the alps in the field of agriculture and especially in the field of animal husbandry, the only human activity possible in some mountain areas. a strategy for mountain areas must prioritise agriculture as a key factor in maintaining a vibrant rural environment and in preserving jobs and human dignity in these areas. it must also include the creation of the necessary living conditions for the people living in these areas. secondly, i would like to stress, as many of my colleagues have done, that the carpathian mountains, which extend over the territories of several central and eastern european states, should also be included in a future similar strategy. the carpathian chain shares with the alps the entire list of natural, economic and social challenges. the alps and the carpathians also share the immediate vicinity of the danube, a river which is the subject of a european regional strategy. i therefore believe that the carpathian mountains, which are located in eight countries, six of which are members of the european union, should be the subject of a future strategy closely linked to the alpine strategy.
the importance of the strategies already developed, such as the baltic sea and the danube, was that they provided both an integrated framework for addressing the challenges and opportunities in this region and pilot projects for future macro-regional strategies. i strongly support the idea of joint programmes in the alpine, carpathian and, in particular, black sea regions, an area of recognised strategic importance, given its wealth of natural resources and a potential market of over 350 million consumers. unfortunately, cooperation in the black sea has a rather modest place in the current plans of the european union. but i think we need to be more courageous and play a significant role in this region by creating a european black sea strategy. a possible strategy will bring significant benefits not only to the black sea basin states but also to the union as a whole, thus creating a real bridge between europe and asia.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because, in order to apply the provisions of regulation no 450/2008 as effectively as possible, it is necessary to postpone the entry into force of certain articles until 1 november 2013. the modernised customs code creates a new electronic customs environment. the new code thus creates a common basis for the application of customs provisions existing in all 27 member states. the legislative act also ensures increased convergence between the information systems of the competent authorities of the member states. the modernised customs code will facilitate trade, but it will also play an important role in preventing certain external threats that the european union may face.
in writing. − the objective of this new code is to facilitate trade while guaranteeing a high level of border security. this new code integrates the customs procedures common to the member states, while also strengthening the convergence between the 27 customs administrations' computer systems. the rules on customs declarations and the placing of goods under a customs procedure will be modernised and streamlined and, in particular, customs declarations will be required to be made electronically as a rule and to contain only one type of simplified declaration. in order to reduce the risk to the community, its citizens and trading partners, the harmonised application of customs control by the member states will be based on a common risk management framework and an electronic system for its implementation.

in writing. − the economic and monetary union represents a major step in the integration of eu economies. it involves the coordination of economic and fiscal policies, a common monetary policy, and a common currency, the euro. the creation of an incentive-based enforcement mechanism aiming at increasing solidarity, cohesion and competitiveness must go hand in hand with additional layers on economic policy coordination. in this regard, it is necessary to introduce a new instrument such as the convergence and competitiveness instrument, which should be based on conditionality, solidarity and convergence. this should apply to all euro area member states and be open to all member states of the union while taking into account the stronger interdependence of euro area member states. this new instrument should be a vehicle for an increased budgetary capacity and be geared towards conditional support of structural reforms, thus increasing competitiveness, growth and social cohesion, ensuring closer coordination of economic policies and sustained convergence of the economic performance of the member states, and addressing imbalances and structural divergences. the measures taken should not have negative effects on social inclusion, worker’s rights, health care and other social issues, even in the short term.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the future of economic and monetary union because i believe that there is a need for better coordination of economic policies at european union level. however, they believe that to emerge from the current recession, the commission's new proposals on macroeconomic governance will need to focus on growth and solidarity and promote social inclusion, protecting workers' rights and health systems. the future convergence and competitiveness instrument will therefore not be able to rely on reducing wage costs, but on increasing purchasing power.
in writing. − in view of the close trade and cooperation relations in other areas of the economy between the countries of the union and their interdependence, i welcome the proposal that the new convergence and competitiveness instrument (cci) to be created at union level should be applicable not only to the euro area countries but also accessible to the other non-euro area countries. this would benefit all countries if the icc would conditionably support structural reforms to increase competitiveness, economic growth and social cohesion in eu countries.

mr president, the agreement which the european union and the united states are about to negotiate is undoubtedly a great opportunity for two great challenges which we have especially in the european union, which are growth and employment. together - it was just said here - we account for almost 50% of gdp and a third of world trade. it is an ambitious agreement, but it will have to overcome important differences, both in terms of legislative frameworks and values. sensitive issues include data protection, intellectual property rights and the cultural and audiovisual sector. on this last point, i must say that it is not only the regulatory frameworks that differ, but also the dimensions of the european and american markets. and in this context of clear dominance by the united states, the european union must ensure that its cultural diversity is protected by supporting and promoting this sector. that is why, 'since i clearly supported the negotiations', i voted for the cultural exception in parliament's recommendations and in the agreement.
i voted for the resolution because a trade agreement with the united states would benefit both sides. however, i believe that those industries which are vital to the european union will have to be protected. but such cases should be the exception rather than the rule in negotiations. the two markets are well integrated and the effects of the agreement will be felt immediately. attracting investment that creates jobs must be the main objective for the european union in these negotiations. at the same time, the freer access to the us market would bring additional gains for european companies. at a time when european industry is in decline, we must expand the markets for european products. under a comprehensive agreement, the presence of american firms in the union will be strengthened, and unemployment, especially among young people, could be reduced.
in writing. − i strongly support the recommendation to launch negotiations between the european union and the united states of america for a comprehensive trade and investment agreement, as this would allow the untapped potential of a genuine transatlantic market to be exploited. such a partnership would bring economic benefits to both parties, while contributing to the global economic recovery. the agreement provides an opportunity for the two actors to explore new ways of removing unnecessary regulatory barriers that hinder trade and investment, thereby boosting the potential for smart, robust, sustainable and balanced economic growth. i believe that the future negotiation process must be as transparent as possible, and that the parties involved should therefore participate actively and present initiatives and relevant information which the european commission can then use to conclude an agreement that is as beneficial as possible for the union and its citizens.
in writing. − the eu and the usa share common values, comparable legal systems, and high – albeit different – standards of labour, consumer and environmental protection. the eu and the usa must exploit the full potential of closer economic cooperation in order to leverage the benefits of international trade in terms of overcoming the economic crisis and achieving a sustained global economic recovery. the agreement with the usa would support the creation of high-quality jobs for european workers, directly benefit european consumers, open up new opportunities for eu companies, in particular smes, to sell goods and provide services in the us, ensure full access to public procurement markets in the us, and improve opportunities for eu investments in the us. also, it is important to strengthen the development and enforcement of labour and environmental laws and policies and promote the core standards and benchmarks laid down by the ilo, as well as decent jobs and sustainable development. furthermore, in the political context, it is necessary for the usa to analyse and make further steps in order to support romania's efforts for inclusion in the visa waiver programme and in order to contribute more to the good economic and trade relations between the two countries.
in writing. − the signing of a transatlantic trade partnership would benefit both the european union and the united states of america. an agreement between these major players in the field of trade would, in a period dominated by the global economic crisis, allow the revival of industrial activity and increase the flow of exports. these factors would lead to sustainable economic growth, increased competitiveness and, above all, new job creation.

in writing. − macro-regional strategies aiming at a better use of existing resources in a given territory have proved to be effective tools for the danube and baltic sea regions. i therefore believe that the experience gained should be used to develop such strategies for other regions of the union, such as the alps. the potential of this region must be exploited, as the alps are of interest both at european and international level. to do this, several issues facing the macro-region need to be addressed: the need to improve mobility, energy security, environmental protection and economic and social development. i believe that a future macro-regional strategy for the alps should coordinate existing eu funds, particularly in the context of cohesion policy, with the aim of implementing projects that aim to address common challenges. i voted in favor of this resolution.

in writing. − there are more than 5 000 textile factories in bangladesh, employing approximately 3.5 million people, bangladesh being the world’s second-largest exporter of ready-made clothes. 1 127 people died on 24 april 2013 in the garment factory collapse at the rana plaza building in dhaka in bangladesh, making it the worst tragedy in the history of the global garment industry. the conditions in such textile factories are often poor, with little regard for labour rights such as those recognised under the main ilo conventions and often with little or no regard for safety. the commission should investigate bangladesh’s compliance with these conventions and the tariff preferences should not be granted if the labour conditions are not improved. the commission should actively promote mandatory responsible business conduct among eu companies operating abroad, with a special focus on ensuring strict compliance with all their legal obligations, in particular international standards and rules in the areas of human rights, labour and the environment. also, an important role can be played by workers and trade unions, for example through the continued development of worker-led safety committees in all factories and by educating workers on how they can protect their rights and safety, including their right to refuse unsafe work.

two things i'd like to point out. first of all, this is the second resolution on the death penalty in india that we are adopting in this mandate. the first spoke of the conviction of devinder pal singh, whose plea for clemency was rejected in march this year. once again, as we did when we first discussed it, we want to send a signal to the indian authorities, telling them, reaffirming the common position in the union on the death penalty, which we consider deeply inhumane, a violation of human dignity. the second thing i want to say is about the protests that followed the secret execution of afzal guru and the way they were responded to. all of this has highlighted the fragility of the kashmir peace process and, at a time when india is seeking to strengthen relations with its neighbours, destabilising the situation in kashmir is not a good thing, which is why we encourage the parties involved to work together towards a diplomatic solution to the situation in the region.

in writing. the economic and financial context of recent years has affected the most vulnerable social groups, with many families becoming homeless due to the inability to pay their mortgages. people paid for the greed of the banks and that's not fair. moreover, austerity measures have deepened this economic and social disaster, as social benefits, including housing heating benefits, have been reduced or eliminated. it is our duty, especially in these difficult times, to seek to create minimum living conditions for our own citizens, including by facilitating access to social housing that is accessible not only to the most disadvantaged social categories, but also to the middle class. i think it is fundamental that the european union should define a framework for action to support social housing by providing financial support that is directed mainly at the local level. it is also very important that future structural funds provide for eligibility for funding for measures such as social housing or investments in the thermal renovation of housing. last but not least, i believe that member states should also consider introducing a reduced vat rate for the construction of social housing.
in writing. in the context of the debate on housing, an area where member states are lacking, the positive impact of social housing investment on the local economy in terms of growth and job creation was mentioned. this impact is undeniable and needs to be taken into account in european and national strategies, alongside measures to improve the energy efficiency of homes, which also play an important role. this approach goes beyond the traditional framework of the housing debate, which is often limited to its social role of supporting families in need. this type of approach allows the debate to be extended to housing for professionals working in rural areas: doctors, pharmacists, teachers, agricultural specialists. i believe that investing in housing for housing would attract more and better trained specialists to the countryside, which would also contribute to economic growth and the maintenance of a vibrant rural environment. many member states, such as romania, want to be able to invest in such specialist work accommodation with the help of european funds, which should be taken into account in future european policies.
educational and professional mobility is an important objective of european policies. recent studies show that there are significant gender differences in labour mobility in the european union, which favour stereotypes and encourage gender discrimination in the labour market. in the context of the current economic and financial crisis, the ability of women to move freely within the eu and to choose a job has been severely affected, with unemployment rates of 10.7% and 22.7% for women under 25. given that women are more exposed than men to social risks throughout their lives, i believe that education and occupational mobility policy should be designed and implemented in the context of integrated social employment policies at european level, with the main objective of combating discrimination based on sex, race, origin, religion, age or health.
the difficult economic situation in the union is affecting women's professional mobility. this has a strong negative effect: it creates the conditions for gender discrimination. women are offered low-paid jobs that lack prestige and do not help develop their skills. in addition, women face another obstacle: reconciling family and professional life, which we all know is difficult. women in romania have an additional problem, because they still face restrictions on the labour market in nine member states. a uniform approach to the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications at member state level is necessary. we also need a strategy for the vocational counselling of women, but also for the harmonization of national laws on the social protection of women with children.
as long as state aid is used responsibly, it can help to maintain and even increase the competitiveness of the union's economy. they believe that it should be directed towards less developed regions and sectors that can contribute to economic growth. at the same time, their modernisation must take into account that we are in a period of crisis and that the number one priority is to reduce the unemployment rate, especially among young people. since budgetary resources are limited in most member states, they should be used as efficiently as possible. i therefore support simplifying the rules in this area, but also better informing the national authorities about reporting obligations. procedures would be more transparent and aid would be granted more quickly.
member of the commission. − mr president, i welcome mr vlasák’s report on regional policy as part of wider state support schemes. i am glad to note that the report initiated by the committee on regional development also takes into account the views of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and the committee on employment and social affairs. the report identifies issues which the commission also considers to be important when defining the rules of the regional aid guidelines for 2014-2020. the aim of the guidelines is to promote the development of disadvantaged regions in europe, while ensuring that the aid does not lead to distortions of trade and competition in the internal market. these guidelines should allow the commission to focus on cases involving large amounts of aid that could have a significant impact on the internal market. member states could spend small amounts on aid without ex ante commission scrutiny within the limits set by the general block exemption regulation, which will be extended both in terms of the categories of measures and the amounts of aid. as the report mentions, ensuring consistency between eu cohesion policy and state aid policy is of key importance. therefore, the revision of all state aid rules in line with the principles of state aid modernisation will help to ensure that cohesion policy is implemented efficiently. however, it has to be noted that eu cohesion policy and eu state aid control policy are two different policies. they need to be coherent, but not identical. another element of the reform raised in the report is the more restrictive approach on aid to large enterprises, such as investment projects in ‘c’ areas. these investments are more likely to lead to distortions of competition and are a worse use of public money than investment in smes. the precise conditions are still being discussed. having considered the conclusions of the european council of february 2013 and listened to the many stakeholders, the decision was taken to slightly increase the overall population coverage level from that contained in the initial proposal to at least 45% of the eu 27 population. the decision was also taken to include a special safety net for countries under the macroeconomic adjustment programme, bringing the overall population coverage to around 47%. i believe that this increase in overall population coverage in assisted areas would allow us to focus on the regions that are most in need, from an eu perspective, while giving member states sufficient room to tackle internal disparities, including in border regions, islands or other areas. the adoption of the new rules is planned for the second half of june. as the report also suggested, the commission plans to keep the rules and maps of the current regional aid guidelines (rags) in place until 30 june 2014, in order to allow member states to prepare for the entry into force of the new rules on 1 july 2014. the final rags are still under discussion in the commission, and this situation may still change.
in writing. regional state aid is support for the implementation of cohesion policy by providing concrete support for economic development, reducing interregional disparities, creating jobs and promoting sustainability. unfortunately, the european parliament has only an advisory role in regulating regional state aid procedures. i believe that a better representation of citizens' interests requires amending article 109 of the treaty to eliminate the current democratic deficit through the codecision procedure. i support the commission's initiative to introduce new sectors into the regulation, such as energy infrastructure and the environment. the new airport-specific guidelines should also take into account the key role of regional airports in the development of regions. the drawing up of national state aid maps is strictly a matter for the member states, in accordance with the general guidelines proposed by the commission. i also consider it necessary to review de minimis aid and adapt it to the requirements of the member states. the new regional state aid guidelines should provide support to european companies wishing to relocate their production to third countries. for example, according to the boston consulting group, reshoring initiatives in the united states will create about five million jobs in the next few years.
studies are showing us more and more clearly that diet has a direct link to a number of serious health problems: cardiovascular disease, type ii diabetes, various forms of cancer. when combined with a sedentary lifestyle, poor nutrition is a serious health threat. the world health organization is talking about a veritable epidemic of obesity, and this is worryingly affecting children, who are the most vulnerable group. the way in which the european institutions deal with this issue will have a major influence not only on the health of european citizens in the decades to come, but also on the economic and social situation of the european union in the future. legislation to protect consumers and promote healthy eating must be a top priority in the european union, and what we have achieved in this case is a real development. there are consumers who need special foods for their special circumstances, but all consumers need clear and accurate food information so that they can make informed choices and protect their health. the european union has made progress in this area, with a number of important laws being passed in recent years, but this progress is undermined by outdated legislation that is no longer relevant to today's food market. the revision of the legislation on food for people with special nutritional needs was therefore an absolutely necessary process. i would like to thank the rapporteur for the way she has coordinated this process, for her willingness to take account of the proposals of others and for successfully defending parliament's position in the negotiations with the council. the agreement reached reflects many of parliament's priorities. redefining the scope of this legislation will block fraudulent attempts to promote products such as sports foods, slimming sticks or so-called growth milk as healthy foods. i particularly appreciate the fact that we have managed to establish very strict provisions in this regard.
alongside the reform of the common agricultural policy and the structural and cohesion funds, the continuation of european support for the most deprived is perhaps the most important success of the european institutions in the current legislature. parliament must insist on maintaining resources at the 2007-2013 level because the budget proposed by the commission represents a substantial reduction, i.e. less money for more beneficiaries. a billion euro cut in food aid is not a wise move in the current climate. i also draw particular attention to the concerns about reducing food waste, which has reached alarming proportions. it is unacceptable to live in a society of abundance, which prefers to throw away food rather than feed people in need. we have 40 million poor people in europe and we waste 90 million tonnes of food a year.
the economic and financial crisis facing europe has led to an increase in the number of people at risk of social exclusion. a significant proportion of these people depend almost daily on food packages or meals distributed under the programme financed by the european fund for aid to the most deprived. as such, to ensure a healthy and balanced diet for the beneficiaries, it is necessary for local and regional authorities, in partnership with non-governmental organisations, to organise local, regional and cross-border management networks to promote the consumption of local products and the use of perishable and non-perishable regional food products that are not traded by food chains. i also believe that the criteria for selecting foodstuffs need to be improved and, where appropriate, in particular to reduce waste at each stage of the supply chain and improve the efficiency of the supply chain, such as (...)
in writing. poverty and social exclusion are also on the rise in europe today. it is primarily the responsibility of the member states to stop this process, but the european union cannot stand idly by. the establishment and operation of a european aid fund to support the most deprived persons would be an important contribution to poverty reduction, but it is our responsibility to ensure that the fund can start functioning as soon as possible. we need to act even more quickly, as the food-sharing programme will end at the end of 2013, so the new fund should be operational by the beginning of next year to avoid a breakdown in eu aid. i think parliament will have the flexibility it needs. it is important that the council also takes a swift decision and that the commission finally has time to prepare for the aid from 1 january 2014. it should be stressed that the problem of poverty is far from being solved by the relief fund. if we are to take the europe 2020 strategy seriously, member states must take decisive action to reduce poverty as soon as possible. of course, in an age of deficit-cutting and debt reduction, it's hard to expect any serious sacrifices from governments. but europe must decide and say: is maintaining budgetary discipline at all costs more important than meeting the europe 2020 strategic objectives? i'm afraid i can't do both.
in writing. the financial and economic crisis in the member states of the european union has increased the number of people at risk of poverty and social exclusion. the number of member states participating in the programme of the fund for aid to the most deprived has increased from 9 to 20. the proposal for a programme for the next multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 is therefore more than welcome. it is the programme that directly benefits more than 20 million people in the european union. it is an expression of solidarity as a fundamental european value.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it represents a step forward in the process of further aligning european legislation with the treaty on the functioning of the eu. i also believe that the adoption of the report will facilitate the achievement of the objective of the proposal, namely to ensure the sustainable exploitation of the cod stocks in the relevant areas. i would like to welcome the fact that it will be based on scientific, sound data and not on political decisions. this ensures that the code stock plan will be updated in the future in an optimal manner, based on the realities of the territory. i would also like to support the need for clarification of the decision-making procedure at commission level in order to provide legal certainty.
consumer spending represents 56% of the eu's gross domestic product and is essential to achieving growth targets and emerging from the crisis. although the single market offers extraordinary opportunities to meet consumer demand, 60% of europeans are still not using the opportunities, due to lack of confidence. the main reason is uncertainty about consumer rights related to cross-border or online purchases. i therefore believe that a new consumer protection policy agenda must immediately aim at increasing consumer confidence by ensuring an increased quality of services, guaranteeing the authenticity of products, avoiding illegal or unfair practices and protecting personal data used in electronic transactions.
i voted in favour of the report because one of the objectives of the european consumer agenda is to increase consumer awareness. if clear information is provided, then the risks to consumers will be reduced. whether we are talking about food or other types of products, the health of the consumer must always come first. i'm particularly concerned about the level of information when we talk about genetically modified organisms. often, the labelling of products containing such organisms is inadequate and citizens are not aware of the possible risks they face. another problem is that some gm crops are very close to normal ones, thus increasing the risk of contamination of conventional crops. there are studies that show that in mammals, genetically modified products can cause changes in weight or in the functioning of vital organs.
in writing. − consumer protection, both in terms of public health and accurate information on available products and services, must remain one of the guiding principles of european policy. at the same time, however, it is necessary to increase the information dimension of european and national public policies, especially as a significant proportion of consumers are not aware of their rights or the means of redress. these issues are all the more pressing for vulnerable consumer groups such as children, whose protection from the consumption of unhealthy food is essential. consumer protection policy must respond to the multiple concerns felt at the european union level: the significant decline in the incomes of european citizens and the increase in the level of poverty, the increased difficulty of access to basic products and services for vulnerable groups, the ensuring of more effective food quality standards.
in writing. − the globalisation of markets brings a multitude of economic benefits, but at the same time it raises a number of problems in guaranteeing the protection of the european consumer. it is essential to ensure a high level of consumer awareness of their rights and that this information is effective, transparent and accessible. consumer education and empowerment is the basic foundation for sustainable economic growth. special attention should be paid to vulnerable groups of people, such as children or people in social or financial difficulties, by providing both appropriate information and special protection. food security must take precedence over financial interests. the european consumer has already shown his concern and concern about the correctness of product labelling in the community, so sustained efforts are needed in funding those programmes which ensure verification of the production chain, compliance with labelling, guaranteeing compliance with quality standards, and the continuous updating of these standards by carrying out laboratory studies.
in writing. − european consumers are increasingly concerned about the possible differences in the quality of products of the same brand and packaging distributed within the single market. an important contribution to strengthening consumer rights is their training to detect dangerous or counterfeit products and misleading advertising, which is why consumer education and empowerment must be ongoing, lifelong and start in school. in addition, there is a need for better protection of vulnerable consumer groups, especially children and the elderly, especially in transport, financial services, energy and it services. i believe that in this process, the closest and most effective cooperation is needed between the public sector, consumer organisations and the private sector, including traders and intermediaries in the supply chain.
in writing. − in may 2012 the european commission published the draft european consumer agenda in line with the eu consumer policy strategy 2007-2013, including new measures for the period 2014-2020 to help the consumers. consumer protection is vital for a healthy economy. hence, in these difficult times, it is necessary to boost the confidence of consumers and awareness of their own rights. the inequalities related to consumers should be reduced, consumer organisations should be encouraged and those who do not respect them should be held accountable. i believe in transparency of information and protection for consumers. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because access to justice is a right enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the union, and i therefore consider the document to be an essential step in respecting this principle. however, i believe that not enough has been done to inform citizens, with only 12% of the population aware of this right. moreover, to make legal aid more accessible, improved collaboration between public institutions and non-governmental organisations is needed. in romania, a pilot project on assistance for the establishment of an effective system of free legal aid was launched in 2006-2008. the project involved institutional and non-governmental actors and was funded through the phare programme. i regret that last year, using the pretext of the crisis and the need to cut spending, the government decided to reduce free legal aid services.
in writing. − the main problem that this report seeks to address is the knowledge gap concerning the existence of public procurement in crossborder disputes. only 12% of european citizens are aware of this possibility and it is obvious that, in view of this, there is little use of this instrument and no exercise of the right in situations where it would be lawful and possible to make use of it. in addition, as provided for in the text which i voted for, the member states could consider the possibility of designating a single legislative body, capable of receiving and transmitting in each eu jurisdiction and ensuring sufficient know-how of the officials involved in these tasks.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which gives greater substance to access to legal aid for persons involved in crossborder litigation. natural and legal persons involved in cross-border disputes have the possibility of seeking legal aid in the state in which they live, in the state in which the court seised is situated or in the state in which the court's decision is enforced. i support the recognition in all member states of the decision of the authorities of a state to grant legal aid to a person involved in cross-border litigation. as only 12% of european citizens are aware of the existence of cross-border legal aid, the commission and the member states need to step up their efforts to inform citizens.
in writing. − it is of least concern that, according to the commission, only 12% of citizens are aware of the existence of crossborder legal aid. in view of the increasing number of european citizens living, working or establishing their families outside their home country, and in view of the increasing number of interactions between companies from different countries within the common market, access to cross-border legal aid is of particular importance, and therefore, in addition to implementing measures, the authorities of the member states must also make efforts to make citizens aware of the possibility of having recourse to this type of support.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation because the latest report on customs actions to respect intellectual property rights shows an increase in the number of counterfeit cases. this means that the union's customs services have become more efficient or that fraud attempts have increased. the protection of intellectual property rights is essential to promote research, innovation and job creation in europe. customs services need to be constantly upgraded, as those who sell counterfeit goods diversify their fraudulent methods. in addition to infringing copyright and causing financial damage to governments, such products can endanger consumer safety. this is all the more evident since, in most cases, the quality of pirated products is inferior to that of the originals.
in writing. − clear and transparent eu legislation is needed to regulate the market in foodstuffs for special nutritional purposes, which are essential for certain vulnerable groups of the population (such as infants, young children, patients under medical supervision). experience has shown that certain european rules on the composition and preparation of such foods, specifically designed to meet the specific nutritional requirements of the persons for whom they are intended, no longer ensure an adequate level of protection of the general public and no longer effectively ensure the functioning of the internal market. i therefore welcome the new proposal for a regulation which improves and simplifies the legislative framework through a series of clear provisions designed to guarantee the free movement of safe and healthy foodstuffs, especially when they are intended for vulnerable groups of the population. new procedures to regulate the composition and labelling of foodstuffs for particular nutritional uses will ensure greater transparency and allow the public to have access to accurate and relevant information about the food they consume. i also welcome the commission's commitment to pay particular attention to limiting and, if necessary, banning the use of certain pesticides which, according to the latest studies, are likely to have harmful effects on health.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation on the enforcement of intellectual property rights by customs authorities, because the rules put in place better guarantee the protection of the interests and, above all, the health of citizens. counterfeiting is affecting a growing range of everyday goods such as cigarettes (34% of counterfeit goods seized), household goods (14.5%), soaps, household appliances, clothing and toys (7%). the sale of counterfeit products is not only a form of deception but also a potential risk to the health and even the lives of consumers.
in writing. − food for people with special nutritional needs, known as 'parnuts' food, is an area of interest at european level, due to a growing market demand for the supply of safe and healthy products to the food chain for certain vulnerable groups of people. infant formula, formula for premature infants and low birth weight infants and special medical feeding require special attention and a harmonised approach in the eu. therefore, once these products are placed on the market, they must meet strict requirements regarding labelling, presentation, advertising, promotional and commercial practices. the new rules adopted today on the labelling and content of infant milk and feedingstuffs for people with special medical needs will be better defined to protect consumers. i believe that we need specific rules for the category of 'dietary foods', especially for athletes, and for foods for weight loss or for low-calorie diets, which take account of innovation in this sector and consumer safety.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because individual measures taken at member state level generate different levels of food safety and protection of human health. they are a burden on consumers and the free movement of food within the union. infants and children have specific nutritional needs, vital in ensuring normal development. the current efforts will be a step forward in educating parents about infant and child nutrition. an important aspect of the report is that relating to food advertising. the prohibition of practices such as exaggerating benefits or discouraging breastfeeding are key elements of the proposal. in romania, there is a code of ethics on advertising food intended for children, as well as numerous legislative provisions. however, there is a need for a single, harmonised regulation.
in writing. − the proposed regulation is intended to replace directive 2009/39/ec on foodstuffs intended for particular nutritional uses and a number of commission acts implementing that directive, while also eliminating the concept of dietetic food. the regulation aims to clarify the legal framework by avoiding overlap between the specific legislation applicable to these foods and the legislation applicable to normal foods, and by closing legal loopholes in the existing system. furthermore, i believe that its purpose is to ensure that eu rules on these types of food are applied in a similar way in all member states, thus contributing to legal certainty, in the interests of consumers and producers, while preventing distortion of the internal market.
in writing. − i supported this report because i believe that the elements of the compromise concern topics of the greatest interest to european citizens. the aim of this regulation was to ensure a high level of consumer protection, in particular for foods intended for infants and children, foods intended for medical use and also to clarify the rules on the establishment of composition and information requirements for certain foods (including foods for medical use), foods for people intolerant to gluten, foods used in low calorie diets, formula for premature babies and low birth weight infants, and market access for smes. the labelling and presentation of products must be accurate, clear and easy to understand, and not misleading to the consumer. i believe that a particularly important element of the compromise discussed in the report is market access for smes. the commission may adopt technical guidelines to facilitate compliance by food business operators with the provisions on compositional and information requirements and the union list of substances.
in writing. − i believe that the eu rules on these types of food should be applied in a similar way in all member states, thus helping to ensure legal certainty in the interests of both consumers and producers.
in writing. − i welcome the amendment to directive 2004/40/ec on the minimum health and safety requirements regarding the exposure of workers to the risks arising from physical agents (electromagnetic fields). protecting the interests, safety and health of workers at work is one of the guiding principles of european legislation, which is why we need new time limit values for their exposure to electric, magnetic and electromagnetic fields. despite the awareness of the short and long-term effects of exposure to electromagnetic fields, the competent authorities at european level and in the member states must continue their efforts in this regard. at the same time, legislation designed to protect the health and safety of workers must be revised accordingly as soon as scientific or medical discoveries point to the possible occurrence of serious risks.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the protection of workers at work is of particular importance, especially for those exposed to the greatest health risks. i am referring in particular to pregnant women, who should not be exposed to harmful radiation. the employer should allow the worker to avoid entering areas where radiation exceeds the limit values. otherwise, the baby's development may be affected, resulting in birth complications and health problems that may affect the child for life. also, in the long term, various forms of cancer can occur with prolonged exposure to electric or magnetic fields. last but not least, i believe that protection systems should be accompanied by further studies on the effects of exposure to electromagnetic fields.
in writing. − improving occupational safety and health is important not only from a human point of view to reduce the suffering of workers, but also as a way of ensuring the success and sustainability of enterprises through better economic development in the long term. despite considerable efforts, the number of accidents at work and occupational diseases remains high and i therefore believe that the introduction of minimum safety and health requirements is also necessary for workers exposed to risks from physical agents.
in writing. − directive 2004/40/ec should be repealed and more appropriate and proportionate measures to protect workers from the risks associated with electromagnetic fields should be introduced. the directive does not address long-term effects, including possible carcinogenic effects of exposure to time-varying electric, magnetic and electromagnetic fields, for which there is currently no conclusive scientific evidence establishing a causal relationship. those measures should aim to address all known direct and indirect biophysical effects of electromagnetic fields, so as not only to ensure the health and safety of each individual worker, but also to create a minimum basis of protection for all workers in the union. the commission and the member states should intensify research and data collection on the long-term effects of exposure to electromagnetic fields. employers should be required to ensure that risks from electromagnetic fields at the workplace are eliminated or minimised. it is possible that in certain cases the exposure limit values laid down in this directive may be exceeded only temporarily. in this case, employers are required to take the necessary measures to return to compliance with the exposure limit values as soon as possible.
in writing. − to protect the health of workers in areas where work includes exposure to electromagnetic fields and to limit their effects, member states need to require the employers concerned to ensure that workers' exposure to electromagnetic fields is limited. as such, it is necessary for the employer to identify and assess, for the purpose of assessment, the magnetic fields at the workplace, taking into account the relevant guidance specified by legislation and other relevant standards and guidance provided by member states, including exposure databases. the assessment shall be made on the basis of emission levels and other relevant safety data provided with the equipment by the manufacturer or distributor in accordance with european legislation, including the risk assessment, if applicable to the exposure conditions at the workplace or installation site.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. in the context of the fact that the current regulation has not achieved its objectives and according to the assessments it will not achieve them by 2015, i welcome the new provisions. we must not lose sight of the fact that some 60% of european fish stocks are exploited beyond the maximum sustainable limit. maintaining fishing mortality rates at a sustainable level, based on scientific advice, should facilitate the recovery of fish stocks. member states will have to give priority to the development and promotion of measures and incentives aimed at avoiding unwanted catches. i think it is important that member states take the necessary measures to minimise discards.
in writing. − an initial plan to restore cod stocks came into effect in early 2004, followed by the current long-term cod plan in early 2009. the review of the long-term plan for the cod is a matter of fundamental importance, not only for the welfare of those stocks, but also because it is a source of effort control for several fleets. this plan shall include automatic annual reductions, under certain biological conditions, both in effort and in total allowable catch. these reductions take place regardless of whether the reserve improves, and only if the improvement does not strictly meet the conditions set out in the plan.
i voted in favour of the report because the latest eurobarometer on corruption shows that 74% of eu citizens consider it a major problem in their country. in romania, the percentage is 96%, up three points from the previous eurobarometer. we therefore need stronger tools at national and european level to combat corruption, one of which is the widespread confiscation of assets derived from corruption as well as other crimes. the former right-wing government promoted a bill on extensive confiscation, but currently the law is not effectively implemented and those who have obtained wealth illegally continue to keep it, even after they have been convicted. unfortunately, the most affected are ordinary citizens, who lose their faith in the justice system.
in writing. − organised crime is a threat to the european economy and society. traditional mafia-like organisations in certain regions of southern europe have gradually expanded their reach, taking advantage of the opportunities offered by economic globalisation and new technologies, forming alliances with other criminal groups in other countries, even on other continents, and sharing markets and spheres of influence, all in the context of countless criminal activities and profit opportunities. the fight against organised crime is a global one, affecting many areas of eu action and policy. the impact on local economies, societies and institutions is therefore increasingly evident at various levels. organized crime has now become a global economic actor, enjoying enormous competitive advantages and fraudulently harming the legal economy.
in writing. − unfortunately, organised crime and corruption in europe have developed to a worrying level. i voted in favour of the measures that the european union wants to take against these phenomena, being aware that in order to bring romania into line with european standards, we must strictly comply with the legislation imposed. it is also true that these criminal groups have developed new methods of obtaining illicit proceeds in recent times and have also expanded both within europe and far beyond the continent, one of the elements that has enabled this development being precisely globalisation. in addition to the enormous financial damage caused by corruption, money laundering and criminal organisations, these activities have reached a new level, using violence and intimidation at the level of citizens to achieve their goals. i also support the rapporteur's proposal for a special committee on these situations, which seeks to provide a guide to better european and national legislation and at the same time to form a coherent and uniform legal framework to act directly against these organisations.
in writing. − poverty is a major factor in organised crime, exploited by criminal organisations, and is essential to eradicate and improve access to employment and social protection. the total number of victims of forced labour in eu member states is estimated at 880 000, of which approximately 30% are victims of sexual exploitation and 70% are victims of forced labour, with women representing the majority of victims in the eu. forced labour brings considerable profits to mafia organisations, leads to social dumping and causes numerous losses to society in tax terms. the commission should present a proposal to develop article 18 of the trafficking in persons directive to encourage member states to criminalise the use of services provided by victims of all forms of exploitation related to trafficking in human beings, including sexual and labour exploitation. measures to combat trafficking in human beings and forced labour must focus on the root causes, such as global inequalities. member states should therefore respect their commitments in development aid and the millennium development goals.
i voted in favour of the report because in romania the economic crisis has affected the real estate sector most and the ability to obtain a decent price for housing. the construction of social housing for young people under 35 was one of the priorities of the former government which, through the ministry of regional development, managed to open several thousand apartments between 2010 and 2011. the prime house programme, launched by the same right-wing government, has also made it easier for young people to get access to mortgages. the programme aimed both to purchase a home for young romanians so that they could start a new life and to stimulate the construction sector and job creation. unfortunately, the current socialist government does not attach as much importance to the continuation of the youth housing program.
in writing. − with the economic and financial crisis intensifying, access to housing is becoming an increasingly pressing issue for a growing number of european citizens. the number of citizens currently in social housing is high, reaching 25 million. there are also major disparities between member states in the number of social housing available. in these circumstances, it is important that investment in social housing becomes a priority at member state level, and the european union should give greater support to this process. investment in this area is all the more necessary as high unemployment, growing economic inequalities and the amplified decline in incomes of european citizens threaten the objective of building an inclusive european society.
in writing. − inadequate living conditions have a considerable impact on health and improving the quality of housing can prevent the negative effects of crowded, excessively wet, cold living spaces on the health of those living in them. homelessness is a source of stress and suffering, with negative effects on the quality of life and on the health and well-being of individuals and families. social innovation needs to be supported by both the european platform to combat poverty and social exclusion and the research framework programme to analyse new policies aimed at improving access to housing and reducing homelessness. the rules on the eligibility of energy rehabilitation of dwellings in the context of social cohesion for funding from the european union structural funds should continue to be applied by the member states. they should be encouraged to cooperate with local and regional authorities in setting priorities and ways of using structural funds resources. member states should include in their national reforms a special component dedicated to developing affordable solutions to enable older people to live in their own homes for as long as possible, facilitating their reintegration into social life by increasing their personal independence.
in writing. − the european union's move to support disadvantaged classes through housing plays a key role in the context of the current social imbalances in europe. the european union is currently facing a shortage of social housing, with over 100,000 people dying every year due to inadequate housing conditions. a good housing policy can generate economic growth, avoid macroeconomic imbalances and thus contribute to poverty reduction, planned land use, urban development and the fight against climate change. therefore, promoting social inclusion through access to quality housing and social services, and active policies in this regard, should be a priority at member state level. in addition, particular attention should be paid to improving the quality of social housing. i consider the report by my colleague karima delli to be timely in the context of the economic and social crisis which has made access to social housing more difficult, but i abstained from voting on the report because of some of the points mentioned in the document which contradict the position of the group of the european people's party.

in writing. − gender segregation in the labour market, the lack of adequate working conditions, the pay gap, inadequate measures to balance family and working life, the persistence of stereotypes and the risk of gender discrimination are factors which in many cases discourage women from exercising their right to move, reside and work freely within the union. i therefore believe that every effort must be made to remove these obstacles so that equality between women and men does not remain a matter of principle. a case that deserves increased attention is that of women who travel abroad to obtain domestic service jobs involving the care of children, disabled or elderly people, and who are often employed without a contract or work illegally and therefore have no right to social security, healthcare and other benefits related to pension contributions. member states should take all necessary measures and make such persons aware of their rights, including their rights to access declared work, social services and health services.
in writing. − vocational mobility highlights the need to adapt education and training systems to new labour market requirements, to stimulate lifelong learning and the acquisition of skills, and to improve systems for the recognition of professional qualifications. states need to work together to find solutions to prevent or compensate for effects of occupational mobility in certain member states and in certain fields (e.g. the mobility of healthcare workers, who are mostly women) that may affect human rights in the countries of origin. member states should also work together to combat any form of trafficking in human beings that may arise in the context of women's educational and occupational mobility, in particular prostitution and forced labour. the commission must find ways of ensuring that the level of education acquired as a result of youth mobility is consistent with the job offers corresponding to that level, so as to guarantee the effectiveness of mobility in both its educational and vocational phases. special attention should also be paid to supporting the mobility of women over 45, who are more likely than others to accept poor working conditions, and to finding specific solutions to the problems faced by roma women.

the reporter. - and i will say, as cecilia wikström, that today is a historic moment for the european union's asylum policy and i am glad that we have managed to reach this result together, whereby we are voting on the whole asylum package this week. so it is a success for parliament, for the european commission, for the council and i want to start by thanking the european commission, commissioner cecilia malmström in particular and her team, i want to thank the council and in particular the irish presidency, which has been extremely helpful and helpful in finalising this dossier and, of course, my shadow rapporteurs from all the other political groups. i think it is important, in reference to eurodac, where i am rapporteur, to state exactly what eurodac is. it's a system for collecting fingerprints from three categories of people: 1. persons from countries other than the european union who are seeking asylum or international protection in the european union; 2. persons caught crossing the border of a member state illegally and 3. fingerprints of persons also outside the european union caught illegally on the territory of a member state. all these categories of persons and fingerprints are used for the implementation of asylum policy. i'll give you an example of why we need such a database: because there have been cases where a person has sought political asylum in france and then sought political asylum in other countries, in germany or in the uk. those courts can check exactly how many other places, if any, the person has applied for political asylum in the eurodac database. there have also been a few cases where asylum seekers claimed that, for example, two months ago they were being tortured in a particular country; or, checking in the eurodac system, it was discovered that, on that date, they had already entered the european union and, as such, the argument was not real. what i mean is: i mean that we want to protect and support all those who are truly in need of international protection and are welcome in the european union. and obviously, they have to be honest with us. but we don't want to protect those who come here lying to us and trying to cheat the system. just as we don't want anyone, any european citizen, to take social benefits from more than one eu country, we don't want that to happen to those seeking political asylum. so we apply the same rules to eu citizens and international protection seekers. the main novelty of this report is the access of investigating authorities in serious crime and terrorism cases to responses from the eurodac fingerprint database. i will give an example again: if a serious crime or terrorist act is committed in a member state and fingerprints are collected at the crime scene and they are not identified in the national database or in other databases, then that state can ask eurodac whether or not it has such fingerprints in its system. eurodac just does a comparison, doesn't give you a name back, tells you yes or no and sends you to the country where those fingerprints were collected. therefore, there are safeguards for the protection of personal data, the person is informed when his fingerprints are lifted that they might be used for this purpose. we have balanced and matched the two interests of protecting personal data and protecting the public interest.
mr president, colleagues, i have always been a great supporter of the establishment of an eu asylum system and an eu migration system, because i truly believe that the european union should be a major international actor, and the truth is that one cannot hope to play such a huge role without coherence and consistency in one’s domestic policy on migration and asylum. with the vote tomorrow we will conclude the difficult and hard work which has lasted for several years. am i personally happy with the outcome? not entirely; nevertheless, i consider that we have made the first step in the right direction and i hope that from now on we will improve. of course, for this to happen, we will have to change the prejudices shared by some governments and some citizens that those coming to the european union are in one way or another related to organised crime or terrorism. they are not; criminals do not need our regulation and directives to harm. those coming to us as asylum-seekers are those who do so to save their own lives, often leaving war zones or conflict zones or unbearable circumstances. they are not the enemies, just people who want to survive. we should not forget our own history – including our recent history – when citizens of countries which today are members of the european union were obliged to escape their homeland and europe and find shelter in other parts of the world. they were well received by their countries of adoption, which explain the large european communities existing today in the world. i welcome the decision taken by the european court of justice a few days ago on unaccompanied minors, as it is right that vulnerable children should never be more in danger than they already are, and no effort is too much to act in their best interest. i expect the member states to fully respect this, and i believe the same reasoning should apply in the case of victims of torture and other vulnerable people. blue-card answer. – well, i would say that the beauty of the european union is that we do not only have legislation on asylum seekers and asylum policy, but we also have a number of other programmes that are trying to foster cooperation with countries which are in very difficult situations. unfortunately, wars occur for a variety of reasons, and not only those that you can easily see. i am afraid that it is not up to the european union to stop all the wars in the world, but what we can do is show solidarity and treat people in the same way as others have treated us in the past.
