in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is a natural and necessary step towards aligning the regulation with the new rules of the tfeu. in the same vein, i would like to draw attention to the important role the union has to play in combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. consistency in union policies is needed to achieve development objectives. some 60% of european fish stocks are exploited beyond the maximum sustainable limit. improvements are also needed in the governance of fisheries at international level, and coordination between external and cooperation policies is essential to achieve this. the eu is still the world's largest importer of fish and therefore must constantly step up its efforts to ensure the sustainable use of the marine environment and its resources.
in writing. − illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is a global scourge, accounting for about one third of catches in certain important fishing areas, such as tuna, swordfish, cod and dissostichus eleginoides. by its nature, illegal fishing disregards conservation measures, endangering fish stocks and representing one of the main obstacles to the implementation of sustainable fishing worldwide. in addition, its tendency to play by the rules is contributing to the degradation of the marine environment, the weakening of fish farming and worrying social dumping. illegal fishing is mainly carried out in the open sea, due to the discretion afforded by the vastness of the oceans, and in exclusive economic zones of developing countries that lack effective water monitoring facilities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, given the need to align it with the provisions of the lisbon treaty and the importance of the subject of illegal fishing. i call on the commission to apply effectively and efficiently the powers conferred on it by this report in order to combat poaching in the black sea, which has reached a worrying level. given that the majority of the poaching vessels in this area come from turkey and ukraine, non-eu countries, the commission needs to step up dialogue with these countries in the framework of bilateral fisheries management bodies.
in writing. − the existence of a common set of rules at union level for the granting of asylum is part of the efforts to create a single area of freedom, security and justice. i want to stress the importance of respecting the deadlines for informing applicants, but also for resolving their requests. the information must also be provided in a language that asylum seekers understand. i also think it's important to provide unconditional legal and medical assistance. where the detention of the asylum seeker is applied, unaccompanied minors should not be subject to such a measure. last but not least, if protection is granted by the member state, then the integration of the asylum seeker in that state must be guaranteed. access to the labour market, education or vocational training services must be a priority.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it represents a great improvement on the existing rules. the new package agreed by parliament and the council brings some important improvements both in terms of the procedures and conditions for receiving and examining asylum applications. the new directive agreed by the european parliament and the council establishes a protection regime for asylum seekers that will better protect their rights, including with regard to detention, which will be applied only as a last resort and under more humane conditions. i would point out, however, that the existing legislation has never been the main problem with the european asylum system, but rather its incorrect application by the member states. the commission must therefore ensure close monitoring of the implementation of the future asylum legislation.
in writing. − in 2012, the eu received some 300 000 applications for asylum (international protection), 7.8% more than in the previous year. however, there are wide differences in the level of assistance provided by member states, differences which this directive seeks to reduce. an important provision is the one on reducing the period during which asylum seekers do not have access to the labour market. the directive reduces it from 12 to 9 months. member states continue to decide on the conditions under which applicants for international protection are granted the right to work, but must ensure that they have effective access to the labour market. i also support this directive because it allows asylum seekers access to the education system within a maximum of 3 months of filing their application and guarantees access to the health system. this ensures that applicants for international protection are treated with dignity and respect in the member state where the application was lodged.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because it is well known that some member states, particularly because of their geographical position, are exposed to migratory flows. it is important to ensure a higher degree of solidarity between member states as well as higher standards of protection. the exchange of best practices and staff should become a normal thing at union level. in addition, if applicants cannot have adequate protection in one member state, their resettlement in other member states should be guaranteed. of course, such a measure must also be approved by the persons while ensuring respect for their fundamental rights. common rules in this field can contribute to a more efficient resolution of asylum applications and to the identification of a solution that is most appropriate for the applicants.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it represents a great improvement on the existing rules. the new package agreed by parliament and the council brings some important improvements both in terms of the procedures and conditions for receiving and examining asylum applications. i particularly welcome the improvement of solidarity mechanisms between member states, but i believe there is still room for progress in this area. the new regulation also brings important improvements to the right of asylum seekers to information and appeal, while at the same time providing better protection for vulnerable categories of people. i would point out, however, that the existing legislation has never been the main problem with the european asylum system, but rather its incorrect application by the member states. the commission must therefore ensure close monitoring of the implementation of the future asylum legislation.
in writing. − the regulation brings significant improvements to the common asylum system. the changes to the dublin system introduced by this regulation and the eurodac report allow for the management of multiple applications for international protection, while introducing new measures protecting asylum seekers. until now, asylum applications were processed in the member state where they were lodged and asylum seekers were transferred to the first member state to which they entered the union. the regulation voted today introduces exceptions to these transfers in cases where the applicant has family living in another member state or if they are in a difficult situation, for example because of illness. another innovation concerns surveillance and monitoring, which will make it possible to detect more quickly the elements that can generate crises, especially in the member states bordering the union, in order to avoid the degeneration of situations in which these states cannot cope with a wave of migrants in cases of armed conflict or other situations that cause large groups of people to leave their countries suddenly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because i believe that only improvement and harmonisation of procedures and guarantees will make it possible to achieve a common asylum system at european level. so we need all member states to apply similar rules to asylum applications. special safeguards will have to be created for vulnerable applicants such as minors, pregnant women or people who have been subjected to acts of violence. the introduction of references to the best interests of the child is welcome in the context of many mothers or fathers who decide to leave for other countries with their children without asking the other parent for consent. the advisory and expertise services will also play an important role in identifying unjustified or abusive applications more quickly. last but not least, the application of common rules will increase trust between member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it represents a great improvement on the existing rules. the new package agreed by parliament and the council brings some important improvements both in terms of the procedures and conditions for receiving and examining asylum applications. i believe it is essential that people in need of international protection have easy access to asylum procedures and also have constant access to information and legal and medical assistance. i would point out, however, that the existing legislation has never been the main problem with the european asylum system, but rather its incorrect application by the member states. the commission must therefore ensure close monitoring of the implementation of the future asylum legislation.
in writing. − the concept of a common european asylum system was first introduced by the tampere european council in 1999 and since then much progress has been made. in fact, in 2012, 330,000 people applied for asylum in europe. i voted in favour of this report so that the european asylum system can be further improved, not only by new rules improving the handling of asylum applications, but also by giving the police of the member states and europol free access to the database of asylum seekers, in order to combat organised crime and combat terrorism.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this directive because it improves the reception conditions for asylum seekers. the new feature is that member states can receive financial support to implement the standards drawn up by the second phase of the common european asylum system. if a member state receives too many asylum seekers compared to its resources and population, it can receive immediate financial, administrative and technical assistance through the european refugee fund and the european asylum support office. for example, such technical assistance may allow the asylum interview to be conducted in a language known to the asylum seeker. member states can thus provide asylum seekers with access to an adequate and rapid procedure for receiving asylum.
it seems that in order to stimulate europe's development potential, we have a serious effect on economic and financial growth and we need for the future a better targeting of financial resources and public spending, to create the right conditions to rebuild the european economy. cohesion policy of course plays an important role in this, but it must be accompanied by effective rules at european level and we must take into account the impact of regional state aid, which leads to sustainable development in regions defined at european union level. although there are many voices who disagree with this idea, in view of the economic and social situation in the member states and the danger posed by third countries which enjoy certain advantages in attracting foreign investment, i believe that in the future the governments of the member states must maintain regional state aid in any form at a level at least similar to the present one. only then will we be able to redirect investment to the most deprived regions and eliminate disparities across the european union.
in writing. − poverty and social exclusion are realities that the european union has to face in each of its member states. to meet these challenges, concrete mechanisms have been created to help reduce and ultimately eliminate poverty. the european social fund is one of them, and, in line with this logic, we must also include the new fund for aid to the most deprived people in the european union. the disadvantaged european citizens must be supported to overcome their current precarious financial situation, to live and develop as far as possible from the risk of material deprivation and food shortages. we must ensure that, from the perspective of social exclusion, today's poor children are not tomorrow's disadvantaged european citizens. this is the aim and the potential of the new aid fund: the prospect of helping to improve the lives of people on the margins of european society in the medium term, and to remove them as far as possible from the social disadvantaged and, therefore, from all the risks of poverty.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because, as several eurobarometers show, the fight against poverty is one of the most important challenges facing the union. that is why i welcome the proposal to set up a european fund for the most deprived. in the context of the crisis and economic difficulties in several member states, the number of people living in poverty has increased. this is why there is a risk that the europe 2020 target of reducing those living below the poverty line will not be met. the non-replacement of the former aid programme risks increasing the number of people in difficulty at european level. however, i would like to point out that the proposed instrument is not enough to combat poverty, but provides solutions for emergencies at member state level. we need measures to increase employment, especially among young people.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has aggravated poverty and social exclusion across the union. in 2011, 120 million europeans, six million more than two years ago, were at risk of poverty or social exclusion. over 40 million are facing severe material deprivation. one of the main characteristics of material deprivation is the inability to have access to adequate food in terms of quantity and quality. children are particularly vulnerable to malnutrition, and poor dietary habits can adversely affect brain development and learning ability, as well as lifelong health.
in writing. − it is particularly well known that in times of economic stagnation or recession, the number of people affected by poverty increases, while the resources of governments to combat this phenomenon often decrease or remain the same. in fact, according to a eurobarometer survey, european citizens consider the fight against poverty to be the european union's second biggest challenge. the european union's europe 2020 target of reducing the number of people affected by poverty and social exclusion by at least 20 million is threatened by the current state of member states' economies. it is worrying that between 2009 and 2011 the number of europeans at risk of poverty increased by around 6 million, which is why i welcome the creation of this new and extremely comprehensive instrument to provide a safety net for the most deprived. even more alarming is the fact that in 2011, there were approximately 25 million children at risk of poverty and exclusion, and if we take into account the negative effects of malnutrition on brain development and health, europe may lose a considerable part of its future generation.
in writing. − through the programme to help the most deprived, which will be discontinued at the end of this year, almost 19 million people benefited in 2011 alone. in order to achieve one of the europe 2020 targets of reducing by at least 20 million the number of people affected or threatened by poverty and social exclusion, we need a new fund for the period 2014-2020. the eur 3.5 billion will be directed to the most deprived people in the member states whose assistance needs are identified by national, regional authorities or partner organisations, or indirectly through the provision of food and goods to the homeless or children. member states will have to plan and provide assistance in line with national systems. the focus should be on persons at risk of material deprivation and food shortages, in particular elderly women in rural areas or with dependent families and women over 45 years of age, homeless persons, children and households with children. the fund is therefore for citizens and must remain an important component of the eu's policy to contribute to the eradication of poverty, material deprivation and social exclusion.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because the fund for european aid to the most deprived (fead) is a sign of european solidarity and an instrument to alleviate the most severe forms of poverty in the 27 member states. the budget allocated to this fund is not to be used as a cohesion fund and the decision to use it is left to each member state. at the same time, combating and eradicating poverty remains the responsibility and obligation of each member state, the efsd being complementary to national policies.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis facing europe has led to a steady increase in the number of people at risk of social exclusion. worse still, more and more children are in this situation. a significant proportion of these people depend almost daily on food parcels or meals distributed under the programme financed by the european fund for aid to the most deprived. as such, it is beneficial for the provision of a healthy and balanced diet to the beneficiaries that local and regional authorities, in partnership with non-governmental organisations, organise local, regional and cross-border management networks that favour the consumption of local products and the use of perishable and non-perishable regional food products that are not traded by food chains. i also believe that food selection criteria need to be improved and, where appropriate, in particular to reduce waste at every stage of the supply chain and improve the efficiency of the supply chain, as well as to raise public awareness of this important issue.
in writing. the vote by which this house approved this report is a sign and a testimony that the only community body directly elected by the citizens is attentive to issues related to the values of social solidarity. we have strongly called for the allocation of 3.5 billion euro for seven years to be maintained for the food funds and social aid for the poor. it is an important signal that we cannot ignore: the commission's proposal is to set up a european solidarity corps to support the european solidarity corps in the event of a disaster. in a time of great crisis, when there are more and more new poor, supporting the basic needs of the poor in the eu is a gesture of fundamental importance, and for this reason we fought for an amendment to the original proposal, requiring that the unspent funds remain tied to the purposes of social aid, and not directed to other purposes.
in writing. − the european union has set itself ambitious targets to reduce the number of people affected by poverty and social exclusion. i am convinced that the european poverty fund plays a key role in achieving the target of reducing the number of people living in poverty by 20 million by 2020. i regret to say that the current economic and financial crisis is hitting the most vulnerable people hardest. at the same time, young people are the most vulnerable victims, and the statistics are a living testimony to this. we have a duty to make sustained efforts to prevent them from becoming a "lost generation". another cause for concern is the growing number of homeless people. i believe that a synergy of the european poverty fund with the financial levers that finance social housing is necessary to reduce this phenomenon. i support this report because i am convinced that the fight against poverty and exclusion can yield tangible results if the tools for integration into working life are promoted and effectively implemented at member state level. we need to create optimal frameworks whereby 'occupational activation' leads to overcoming the social barriers of people at risk of being removed from the labour market.
in writing. as a strong supporter of european solidarity, i have followed this fead dossier closely in line with my ongoing commitment to the pead. the opponents of this fund forget that the citizens have accepted the austerity measures in order to achieve banking, financial and budgetary solidarity. these same european citizens would not understand that the european union, which has the duty to protect them, cannot guarantee them social solidarity through this european fund for aid to the most deprived (fead). as the european parliament's permanent rapporteur on the esf, i will vote without hesitation for the establishment of this fund and in particular its mandatory nature for all member states. i encourage the rapporteur to stand up to the european council of ministers in the trilogue negotiations which will be opened shortly.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and i consider that the maintenance of european food aid is one of the most important achievements of the european institutions in the current legislature. i supported in particular the amendment to increase the financial allocation to eur 3.5 billion, which is still far less than the financial effort made in the united states, for example, to support disadvantaged people. i also show that the eu urgently needs a strategy to reduce food waste, which amounts to over 90 million tonnes a year.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the change to the eurodac system will lead to greater transparency of asylum procedures in the member states. the introduction of europol and member states' law enforcement access was necessary because of the abuses being committed by criminal networks in third countries. members of these networks often apply for asylum in the union using false identities. and then they carry out criminal or even terrorist activities in the member states. in the context of the threats facing the union, we need a secure and reliable database. i believe that the regulation is a further step towards creating a common space of freedom, security and justice.
in writing. − the eurodac system enables eu countries to help identify asylum seekers and persons caught crossing fraudulently an external border of the union. by comparing fingerprints, eu countries can determine whether an asylum seeker or a foreign national found illegally in one eu country has previously applied for asylum in another eu country, or whether an asylum seeker has entered the union fraudulently. eurodac consists of a central unit set up within the commission, equipped with a central computerised database for comparing fingerprints and a system for the electronic transmission of data between eu countries and the database.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the reintroduction of border controls in the schengen area must remain a measure used only in emergency cases. until now, the exceptional nature of the situation was not very well defined. that is why i am glad that the definition of 'exceptional' cases has been made very clear. eliminating migration from this category reinforces the idea that free movement is one of the fundamental rights of european citizens. the amendments also limit the possibility for a member state to re-establish controls for too long and unilaterally, thereby preventing possible abuses. the increased role of the european commission in the procedure will also lead to greater transparency and increase trust between the schengen states.
in writing. − the right to free movement is one of the most obvious rights and advantages of the european union. any attempt to restrict this right should be made only as a last resort. careful assessment of exceptions to this right is necessary and only cases considered to represent a serious and imminent threat to public policy and internal security of one or more member states may lead to the temporary reintroduction of border controls. any decision to temporarily introduce such border controls should be taken in agreement with the commission and the member states directly concerned, in order to ensure that weaknesses in the area of free movement are correctly identified and that the best possible solution is found to remedy them, without seriously affecting this fundamental right. in order to prevent cases that may constitute such serious threats, it is of the utmost importance that member states cooperate, consult each other and continuously improve their alternative methods of ensuring public policy and internal security.
in writing. − as the shadow rapporteur for the schengen governance package, i voted in favour of this report, as i believe that it clarifies and limits the conditions under which a member state may introduce internal border controls. from now on, if a member state intends to introduce temporary controls, it will have to consult the commission and the other member states in advance and give detailed reasons for the need for such a measure. at the same time, it is provided that these border controls may be maintained for 10 days in the event of unforeseen events and for 30 days in the event of foreseeable events. these deadlines can be extended up to a maximum of 2 months and 6 months respectively, which is a novelty because there are no maximum deadlines in the current rules. under the new rules, migration cannot be considered a threat to security or public order, meaning that internal borders will not be able to be entered due to migration flows.
i welcome the introduction of the new mechanism because it solves one of the grievances that my country has publicly expressed: the application of a double standard in the implementation of the schengen acquis. i would stress that at the time of the technical assessment, romania was better prepared to join the schengen area than some of the countries that are already members, which we can very easily interpret from the report presented by the commission last week. however, the signal received by prime minister ponta in berlin from chancellor merkel makes it very clear that in the eyes of external partners, there are still important steps to be taken, such as respect for the rule of law, the fight against corruption, transparency of decision-making and legal stability. we all want the socialist government to live up to these expectations and romania to be part of the great schengen family by the end of the year.
in writing. − unlike the current system, which is not legally binding and only provides for peer review, the new system has more effective and dissuasive mechanisms. it will allow for a more accurate assessment of the level of compliance with the schengen rules and for immediate remedial action, which will remove any impression of impunity. member states will be obliged to solve all the problems they encounter. the new system also provides for the possibility of unannounced on-the-spot visits at internal borders, which will help to preserve one of the main achievements of european integration, namely the free movement of citizens within an area without internal borders.
in writing. − with the proposed regulation, we envisage the elimination of a long series of misunderstandings and discriminatory measures by some states, which led to the delay in romania's accession to the schengen area. furthermore, they managed to tie the accession to the judicial cooperation and verification mechanism, which is totally unjustified. that is why we reject a system based on double standards. it is important that the rules are the same for all, because it is unfair to have different criteria and assessment systems for the member states and the candidate countries. i hope that the amendments proposed by parliament will not leave any door open to restricting the freedom of movement of certain citizens of the member states by arbitrary criteria. it is quite obvious that this mechanism cannot work without full mutual trust between the member states. this is achieved through clear, objective criteria for evaluation and, where necessary, joint management of problems. i hope that the adoption of this resolution will speed up the process of accession to schengen for the candidate countries.
in writing. − as the shadow rapporteur for the schengen governance package, i voted in favour of this report, as the schengen area is moving from an intergovernmental to a european approach to schengen evaluation with the commission coordinating the entire evaluation mechanism and not being a mere observer as before. the commission will adopt the annual and multiannual evaluation programmes, lead the evaluation teams together with a representative of a member state, coordinate the follow-up process where potential shortcomings are identified. freedom of movement within schengen will also be strengthened, as the commission will now be able to make unannounced visits to internal borders to ensure that there are no abuses. the european parliament will also have a supervisory role in the evaluation process and will have the right to be informed and receive the relevant documents at each step of the evaluation. this is a major change from the current situation where parliament is not informed at all and does not even have access to the evaluation reports.
in writing. − as eurobarometers also highlight, freedom of movement within the eu is one of the most important benefits for citizens of eu membership. unfortunately, it is still a distant dream for some of the population, even though the countries in question fulfil all the criteria for accession to the schengen area. the governance package, with its two regulations - one establishing a new evaluation mechanism for emergency situations and another amending the schengen borders code - will add a greater community dimension to free movement. more specifically, it will avoid the possibility of abuse when reintroducing border controls, a decision that will be subject to rigorous evaluation criteria. in practical terms, it will guarantee the freedom of movement of citizens and remove the double standards that affect certain eastern european countries. despite the loss of the co-decision power, it will ensure that the european parliament is better informed in the event of critical situations. on the basis of the new mechanism, i am confident that it will be possible to recognise that romania and bulgaria are ready to join the free movement area, as the schengen evaluation is already being carried out in the case of both countries, with positive results.
in writing. − we supported this report because, at the moment, smes represent 99% of all european societies, so we have a clear obligation to take account of their specific needs. repeated amendments to the directives, as well as cumbersome and non-harmonised national legislation, have increased the administrative burden on these companies. statistics show that in romania, as in the rest of the member states, the preparation of financial statements is one of the most burdensome legal obligations of companies. i believe that this directive will reduce the administrative burden on the companies concerned. it will also ensure clarity and compatibility of financial statements across the union, with the main benefits being improved functioning of the single market and increased cross-border trade. i am pleased that we are taking important steps in the europe 2020 strategy, facilitating the transformation of the eu into a smarter, more sustainable and, above all, more inclusive economy.
in writing. − both accounting directives have been in force for 30 years and provide a complete set of rules on the preparation and content of statutory financial statements. when listed companies became subject to the provisions of the ias regulation in 2005, smes became the de facto main users of the accounting guidelines. the commission proposes to replace these two directives with a single directive, better adapted to the present situation and future needs of both those responsible for drawing up financial statements and their users. this proposal complements the 2009 proposal on the financial statements of micro-entities, which was adopted by the european parliament on 13 december 2011. following the impact study carried out between 2009 and 2011, the commission aims to reduce administrative burdens by 25% by 2012 and foresees potential savings of eur 1.5 billion per year for all businesses falling within the scope of the directive.
in writing. − i voted for this report because many member states now impose stricter information requirements than the minimum required by the current directive. in order to ensure equal treatment of companies and to effectively reduce the administrative burden, such excessive regulation should be avoided, as it leads to market fragmentation. one of the most important changes introduced by this directive is the removal of the obligation to submit quarterly financial reports for all companies. access to information also needs to be improved. a european-wide database will facilitate access to companies' financial information and encourage the level of interconnection between member states and cross-border investment. another way to encourage these long-term investments could be to strengthen the legal frameworks in the member states on the penalties applicable to breaches of transparency requirements.
in writing. − given the increasing volatility in global financial markets, investors are increasingly demanding information on the practices of firms. clearly, investors want more transparency to get a complete economic picture of investments and risks. in addition, transparency, as disclosure, is an important indicator of sound corporate governance. companies are increasingly adopting corporate governance standards, including transparency, by joining global reporting regimes such as the extractive industries transparency initiative, in addition to voluntary guidelines for multinational enterprises such as the oecd guidelines for multinational enterprises and the global reporting initiative, which set the transparency agenda. the introduction of a harmonised system of information on majority holding of voting rights is intended to improve legal certainty and increase transparency.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the common agricultural policy is one of the most important policies of the union, absorbing a significant part of the european budget. since the basic rule governing the union's finances requires the annual budget to comply with the multiannual financial framework and since the sub-ceilings set for the agricultural policy for 2013 have already been exceeded, the commission proposes an adjustment rate for direct payments to farmers. even if the modulation will only be applied to amounts above eur 5000 and that this reduction will not be applied to my country, nor to bulgaria and croatia, i believe that the measure will have negative effects on the union's agriculture, especially in the current period of crisis. that is why i support the report and i also believe that we must reject the commission's proposal and the reduction in direct payments, in order to avoid negative consequences and farmers' protests, such as the protest by milk producers at the end of last year.
in writing. − in order to ensure equal treatment of farmers, i consider that the adjustment rate should only be applied to the amount of direct payments to be granted to farmers for aid applications submitted in calendar year 2013, irrespective of when the payments to farmers are actually made. the unequal distribution of direct payments between small and large beneficiaries continues to pose problems for the cap. this regulation proposes to apply the adjustment rate, under financial discipline, to amounts exceeding eur 5 000, in order to contribute to achieving a more balanced distribution of payments. this is in line with what was proposed on financial discipline in the context of cap reform in article 8 of the commission proposal for a regulation (eu) laying down rules on direct payments to farmers under support schemes within the framework of the common agricultural policy.
in writing. − i believe that maintaining the eur 5 000 threshold in the application of the financial discipline mechanism is essential for romania. our country will not have financial corrections for 2013 in direct payments, they are applied only to payments over 5 000 euros.
in writing. - i voted against amendments nos 8, 10 and 11, as i believe that financial discipline for small beneficiaries of agricultural subsidies is not justified. the correct principle to apply in this situation would be that the reductions should only affect those who receive large sums of money or, alternatively, a proportionate reduction depending on the amount of subsidy received.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal because i consider that the efforts to implement and continuously improve the area of freedom, security and justice are among the greatest achievements of the european construction. the free movement of persons, guaranteed by the schengen agreement, contributes to the development of a sense of belonging to the union. i also support the need to simplify the rules of the road in the schengen area and to strengthen controls at the external borders, as long as they do not affect the benefits derived from the protection of human rights. i have personally supported on countless occasions the importance of free movement and the imperative that my country should also enjoy the principles of the schengen acquis as soon as possible. in conclusion, i share the logic of the report that, despite the current circumstances in which the concept of urgency dominates political decisions, the union is continuing the integration process by applying policies with a long-term vision.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because the new schengen verification mechanism will be based on technical, clear and transparent criteria, valid both for member states and for those wishing to join this area. the right of citizens to free movement within the schengen area has also been strengthened, and illegal checks at internal borders will be strictly monitored to prevent abuse. i want the new schengen verification mechanism to put an end to the double standards faced by romania and bulgaria in trying to join the free movement area, and for romanian and bulgarian citizens to finally enjoy a fundamental right enshrined in the lisbon treaty.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the abolition of illegal checks at the internal borders of the european union. customs controls carried out within the schengen area are a flagrant violation of the right of free movement of union citizens. according to the statistics presented, from june 2009 to may 2013, the most frequent checks on buses transiting the schengen area took place at the borders between italy and france, belgium and the netherlands, germany and the czech republic, germany and denmark. approximately 55.3% of buses passing through germany are inspected by customs or other authorities carrying out customs checks. i ask the european commission to ensure that the application of the amended schengen borders code will be in accordance with the principles of free movement as set out in article 77 (1) (a) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union.
social investment can be seen as an important tool for growth and cohesion, with both short-term and medium- and long-term impacts, especially on employment, which offer important prospects for the european economy. i therefore believe that we need to focus in particular on the possibilities for improvement in the coordination of social policies at european level and not to forget benchmarking, which is extremely important for the less developed and advanced countries in this respect to take knowledge from the more developed countries. i believe that to succeed in this area, we need to pay more attention to developing a concrete european strategy for social innovation, to closing the gaps between member states, to making efficient use of the european social fund and the european regional development fund and, last but not least, to promoting sustainable partnerships between states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution because the current economic crisis has exposed the inability of social assistance systems to cope with current challenges. whether we're talking about demographic change and the increasing number of older people, or whether there are too many citizens living off welfare, it's clear that we need a change. i think every state needs to evaluate its welfare system as carefully as possible so that the funds it has available are directed to those who really need it. people who receive assistance, even if they do not meet all the legal conditions, as is often the case in romania, should no longer receive any support. only then can we build a society in which the values of work and responsibility prevail.
in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth sets targets to lift at least 20 million people out of poverty and social exclusion and to increase the employment rate to 75% for the 20-64 age group. social protection systems have three functions: social investment, social protection and economic stabilisation. i believe that investing in youth employment should be a priority and a key component of national social investment strategies. member states should therefore take strong measures to combat youth unemployment, in particular through preventive actions targeting early school leaving or early leaving from training systems, and develop comprehensive strategies for young people who are not in employment and are not in education or training.
in writing. − the well-targeted and efficient social investments help stabilise the economy, promote employment and enhance the skills of the labour force. the member states should modernise, and, where needed, structurally reform their social investment policies without delay, in order to offer the best possible services to citizens. thus, the member states should consider signing a ‘social investment pact’ which would set investment targets and create a reinforced control mechanism for improving efforts to meet the targets of the europe 2020 strategy. the member states should adopt measures favourable to job creation as part of their social investment programmes, such as introducing labour-related tax reforms incentivising employment, promoting and supporting self-employment and business start-ups, improving the framework for doing business and facilitating access to financing for smes, transforming informal and undeclared work into regular employment, creating incentives to improve the employment level of the most vulnerable social groups and integrating flexicurity and modernising wage-setting systems in order to align wages with productivity developments. also, i strongly support the allocation at least 25% of cohesion policy funding to the esf and earmarking 20% of esf allocations in each member state for promoting social inclusion and combating poverty.
in writing. − i believe that social investment must contribute to reducing early school leaving, improving the quality and efficiency of tertiary and equivalent education, increasing participation and performance levels of graduates, promoting new skills and competences of the workforce to adapt to labour market requirements. on the other hand, measures are needed to help the unemployed, especially the long-term unemployed, to re-enter the labour market, investments in education and information to improve labour market outcomes and better match the skills of graduates and workers with labour market demands, and to create working conditions for as long as possible.
in writing. − in the current economic context, many firms from smes to large enterprises relate to various forms of state aid, whether we are talking about subsidies, tax deductions, preferential credits or other exemptions. the granting of such state aid schemes may be one of the ways in which a member state or a region of that state intends to fight for economic growth, the preservation or even the creation of new jobs. these two dimensions must, in my view, be taken into account when analysing the usefulness of such aid, because it is in fact another means available in the community to achieve the same objective: to help european citizens to escape the effects of the economic crisis and to hope for a more prosperous life. in this state aid award process, it is absolutely necessary to pay close attention to the application-approval process itself, on the one hand to ensure that this aid is granted prudently, in line with the economic reality of the company or region, but also that the entire administrative award process does not differentiate between regions and does not prove to be too bureaucratic. i welcome the rapporteur's options and i vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − the attractiveness of regions for foreign direct investment can be improved by allowing them to provide a range of incentives such as grants, tax credits, incentives, loans or guarantees, but these are limited for large enterprises in c regions and limiting their productive investment in a regions. the european parliament and the council opposed this proposal, agreeing that certain investment priorities should be open to these companies and their productive investments. i support the rapporteur's proposal that the granting of aid should not depend on the size of an undertaking but on its contribution to regional development, employment, the quality of investment or the sustainability of the project.
in writing. − maintaining a high level of competition at european union level is a guarantee of its sustainable development and the social character of the market economy. in the current economic crisis, boosting the competitiveness of european players helps to position them effectively on international markets, helping to meet the needs of european consumers. competition measures must also be without prejudice to the principle of full freedom of movement for goods, goods and persons and to the sectoral regulations of the european union, in order to achieve the optimal functioning of the internal market for goods and services. last but not least, state aid policy, legitimised by the impact of the economic crisis, needs to be aligned with the union's competition policy.
in writing. − i voted for this report because competition policy has proved to be a very useful tool in combating abusive practices by certain economic operators. in the current economic context, enforcement of competition rules is also one of the most important tools available for european economic recovery. an active competition policy focused on removing existing barriers will improve the access and participation of smes and the tertiary sector in the internal market. i would like to mention that i encourage the dispute settlement procedure, in the context of which discouraging fines cause great difficulties for operators and above all endanger jobs. finally, i believe it is very important to encourage and above all to promote a culture of competition both in the eu and globally.
in writing. - i voted for this report. fair competition is a key condition for the recovery of the european economy and for reducing costs for consumers, who pay less for products and services offered under fair competition. in 2011, the commission imposed fines of over eur 614 million on 14 companies in cartel and merger decisions to protect competition. the method of setting fines, as the only instrument to discourage unfair practices, is however laid down in a non-legislative document: the 'guidelines on fines' of 2006. the commission should develop, by means of a legislative document, a detailed basis for the calculation of fines and clear principles for setting them. consumers are only better off when they have access to open and competitive markets, and the commission must discourage non-compliance and unfair competition practices on the basis of the principle of legality.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution because, in the context of the crisis we are still facing, the union cannot afford to postpone any further measures to coordinate the economic policy reforms needed to strengthen emu and create a banking union. the principles underpinning the future emu must be stability, sustainable growth and democracy. i would like to remind you that the role of emu is to create deeper integration and stronger governance, to which all countries can join, without discrimination against countries outside the euro area. moreover, for a monetary union to work, it requires more than a number of countries using the same currency: discipline and solidarity are essential. special attention should be paid to the principle of transparency and urgency of the monetary union process, all this in the context of the latest eurobarometer showing that romanians have one of the lowest confidence in the positive development of the european economic situation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i support the need to strengthen economic and monetary union. economic and monetary union (emu) is a major step in the process of integrating the eu economies. we need a real emu, based on sustainable growth and solidarity. emu must generate stronger integration and governance, and participation in its construction must be open to all member states on a voluntary basis. we need to step up the process of coordinating european economic and political reforms and align them with the instruments of the european semester, as well as with all the instruments generating economic stimulus and solidarity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because youth unemployment is the main problem facing the union today. although a number of policies have been adopted at european level, not all countries are implementing them. one example is romania, which, despite having a youth unemployment rate of 22.7%, is delaying the adoption of the national youth employment plan. moreover, the european commission, in its country-specific recommendations, called on romania to implement the plan without delay. but it seems that the plight of the youth is of no interest to the present government. i believe that it is a priority to focus on technical and vocational education, based on curricula that take into account the demands of the labour market. access to cheap credit for young people is also essential to stimulate entrepreneurship and job creation.
in writing. − i support the rapporteur's proposal on the importance of increasing voluntary mobility opportunities for young people by removing existing barriers to apprenticeships and training and to cross-border practice, in order to better match the supply to demand of vocational training activities for young people in the workplace. for these measures to deliver long-term results, and at the same time avoid the risks associated with brain drain, there is also a need to improve the transferability of pensions and labour and social protection rights across the eu. in addition, measures are needed to ensure that sufficient numbers of highly qualified persons remain in the labour market of their communities or return to their member states of origin, with a view to enabling those member states to recover economically and stimulating sustainable growth.
in writing. i have always supported turkey's eu accession process and have opposed the freezing of the negotiating chapters on human rights. it is precisely because i am among the friends of this country that, in the last year, i have been concerned about the state of democracy and human rights in this country. i think that recent events prove to us that turkey has active citizens and involved civically and politically. this is a chance for the country's democratic consolidation. citizens who peacefully protested in taksim square must be involved in the decision-making process . pluralism of opinion and dialogue of ideas is the best guarantee of both democracy and a prosperous european future for turkey and its citizens.
in writing. – the present protests in turkey, almost as violent as those seen during the last years in the uk, greece or spain, and the police reactions as firm as those witnessed in italy or france, are particularly worrying since they occur in the vicinity of a troubled region and in a country needed for regional stability. the causes of this turmoil are neither the economic situation nor the lack of democracy, neither social disparities nor absence of political freedoms. any comparison with the ‘arab spring’ is, therefore, senseless. the deep roots of these clashes could be found in the global crisis of democracy and, maybe, in the continued delay of the eu integration of turkey with its geo-political and psycho-political consequences. therefore the eu must avoid behaving as the moralist wolf. the eu accession process of turkey must not be derailed by these events but accelerated. dialogue is the best way for overcoming the tensions. for its success all sides must show moderation, self-control, proportionality, consistency and good faith. turkey is a major player in the mediterranean, central asia, the balkans, the middle east, the caucasus and black sea. one hopes that no other competitor will fuel or use turkey’s present difficulties.
i am glad that the text of the brok-gualtieri recommendation underlines one fact, namely that the external action service is a new body and that we could not therefore expect full functionality in the first two and a half years of its existence. i think, therefore, that some voices in our parliament have been too hard on lady ashton, given the constraints to which the new institutional construction has been subjected. but there is certainly room for improvement, and i think the key word here is flexibility: flexibility in terms of reallocating resources and staff when political priorities change rapidly, as was the case with the arab spring; flexibility when we talk about the responsiveness of external assistance; but even more flexibility when operational decisions are needed within the common security and defence policy, as was the case in mali. the introduction of qualified majority voting in the council would be useful in such situations, which is, as we know, permitted by the treaties. i would also like to stress that, while not intended to replace national diplomacy, the external action service is a resource in a context where, at national level, budgets for diplomatic and consular representation are being reduced.
in writing. – 2013 is the year of the first review of the newly-established eeas, set up by the lisbon treaty at a time when the current world crisis was not yet a permanent feature of our lives. looking back, one sees the true dimensions of the task confronting the eeas: to construct itself - in a field still subject to national decision - at a time when the eu has been forced to become increasingly inwards-looking and, inevitably, centrifugal, given the propensity of the ms to care more for themselves individually than for the common entity the eu represents. those were huge challenges, given that the eaas was a first-time experience, in the sense that it combined foreign policy, development and defence - which were fields pursued individually and in parallel; that it did not have enough personnel, which had to be recruited and, most important, that it had to react to a number of important issues, many conflictual in nature, while structuring itself. although i personally have my doubts about any bureaucracy, i have to recognise that, in this case, the eaas has succeeded in playing the positive role of doubling national foreign action with eu action.
i would like to refer to the andrikienė report on the promotion and protection of freedom of religion, belief and belief. i congratulate the rapporteur, laima andrikienė, on this very convincing report. the european instrument for democracy and human rights, for which i am the epp group rapporteur, is the main instrument for promoting and supporting freedom of religion or belief within the european union's human rights programmes. i would like to say that i am deeply concerned about the situation of christians, among others, in iraq, egypt, kazakhstan, uzbekistan, pakistan. for example, in pakistan, two little girls have been sentenced to death in the last two years after being accused of blasphemy. one of these girls, aged 14, is still in prison, accused of burning a koran. last week, the tortured body of an 11-year-old christian boy was found abandoned in the punjab region. the pakistani authorities can't let this go, and we can't let them let this go. he must release masih bhatti and take steps to protect the christian minority in pakistan.
the development of guidelines on freedom of religion and conscience is important, as religious minorities are facing serious threats and persecution in many parts of the world. the spirit of fundamental human rights as enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights should also be reflected in the european union's external action. the most effective means of enforcing these fundamental rights externally is to ensure that they are guaranteed in all european states. there are no exceptions and no reinterpretations, no double standards, no mechanisms for assessing the application of fundamental rights that are subject to partisan political battles. religious freedom is a value that europe, with its christian roots, has learned to respect at the cost of bloody wars. religious freedom in europe, more specifically in the principality of transylvania, is a european invention, but it is also a christian value. that is why it is our duty as europeans and as christians to proclaim, to disseminate and to defend, if necessary.
in writing. respect for the principles of democracy and pluralism cannot be achieved without the existence of a free, independent and pluralistic traditional or online media. maintaining and strengthening media freedom and independence not only in europe but also worldwide is a common interest of all countries. this is also why independent regulators are needed, precisely to ensure an open and supportive media base. the commission should also be able to provide the necessary information to the member states and the commission on the implementation of the union's policy on the protection of the environment and the promotion of the environment, in particular by providing the necessary information to the member states and the commission on the implementation of the union's policy on the protection of the environment and the promotion of the environment. on the other hand, the european union needs to demonstrate that it is a top political authority to ensure the protection of journalists globally, given that many journalists do not have access to legal aid, although their profession is increasingly at the forefront of the struggle for human rights, whether in the online environment or in the traditional press.
in writing. i welcome the schaake report on freedom of the press and media in the world. the role of online platforms in the fight against dictatorial regimes in recent years has demonstrated the importance of the media in facilitating democracy in the world. it is essential for the eu to recognise the major role that free media, both traditional and online, play in accurately and fully informing the public and in maintaining democracy. not only is the right to freedom of expression a fundamental right, but it is in our collective interest to strengthen the freedom and independence of the media around the world. however, the role of certain platforms in inciting people to terrorist activities should not be ignored and the eu should take strong action in this regard. the commission must strictly monitor the independence of the press in the member states and must pay due attention to the respect of freedom of expression in all bilateral agreements it signs.
madam president, the main challenge regarding transatlantic relations is how to preserve their importance in a rapidly shifting power distribution within the international system, accelerated by the current financial and economic crisis. however, even if the centre of gravity of that system is moving from the atlantic to the pacific, the very substance of transatlantic relations – the values and interests they are based on – do not evaporate. they remain as strong as ever. consequently, the current us strategic rebalancing towards the asia-pacific region – understandable given this region’s role in the world’s balance of power – does not obscure the strong bond created over time between the us and europe. the us will continue to interact substantially with us, and we will honour the pledge to defend europe in case of threat. moreover, the atlantic itself is witnessing turbulence in west africa, the increasing engagement of china and india, and the rise of the latin american emerging powers, bringing new dimensions that require the attention of both the us and europe. under the changing circumstances described above, europe will have to assume a larger role in its own defence through both nato and the eu. it will have to stay engaged in the turbulent area between the atlantic and the pacific, west and north africa, the middle east, the gulf and south asia and support the us in its efforts to avoid conflict in east asia, the area which is becoming the driving force of the world economy.
the partnership between the european union and the united states is based on common principles, values and interests. these desires could not be achieved without ensuring common security, and the best example is the sacrifice of romanian soldiers, along with american soldiers, in iraq and afghanistan. i would therefore also like to stress the importance of the deployment of the missile shield on romanian territory, at deveselu, in view of ensuring the security of the union. the timetable for the implementation of the project is thus maintained and the base will become operational by 2015, which means that the third phase of the programme, namely the installation of a similar system in poland, will also follow the original timetable. the timely completion of the project is good news for both romania and the european union, given the worrying developments in iran and north korea. finally, i would like to appeal to the american authorities to include romania in the visa waver programme in the spirit of strategic partnership and military cooperation.
madam president, relations between the european union and the united states have an impact that goes beyond their bilateral implications, particularly as regards security and defence policies and the strategic stability that we both need. nato’s active layered ballistic missile defence shield provides a significant benefit to the eu and nato countries. the first three phases of the missile deployment are expected to be achieved as planned by 2018, and sites in romania and poland will be included. however, i regret that the final phase of the deployment was postponed until 2022. i strongly believe that this decision should be reconsidered, especially in the light of the present threats. i welcome the continuation of the consultations of the poland/romania/turkey trilateral dialogue on strategic and security issues, which was initiated by romania last year. it is important that the strategic partners in eastern europe hold frequent meetings to discuss the security of the euro-atlantic area.
member of the commission. − madam president, i am glad of this opportunity to talk with you about mali. the moment is particularly timely, as the planned presidential elections are only one month ahead. also, the un is in the process of taking over the african-led international mission to mali. in response to the questions that have been formulated, first, europe has risen to the challenge of this crisis, which has seriously threatened mali as well as the entire sahel region. we acted in line with our strategy for security and development in the sahel of 2011. this policy has been sensitive to respecting the ownership of the legitimate authorities. europeans have been present in a coordinated manner, both through the participation of the eu in the ‘international support and follow-up group’, and of its member states bilaterally. all have acted cohesively since even before the coup d’état of 22 march 2012. they have also delivered considerable emergency humanitarian help of eur 112 million through dg echo and bilateral relief. europe has done much of the international effort to support mali. alongside the french operation serval, the eu’s african peace facility financed the deployment of african troops via ecowas and we have spent eur 50 million on this. the cfsp military mission eutm mali began to train the malian army in april. europeans regularly asked the malians to prepare a roadmap, that was finally adopted on 29 january, and offered support for its implementation. the european union, the major development partner for mali for decades, is also the main international stakeholder in the reconstruction of the country. the important role of the european union was shown at the 15 may high-level international donor conference in brussels that was co-chaired by mali, the european union and france. considerable means for the reconstruction of mali have been pledged, amounting to a total of more than eur 3.25 billion. europe is providing nearly eur 1.4 billion, of which eur 848 million comes from member states and eur 523 million comes from the commission. i am emphasising this not just a typical pledge, it is actually in response to the action plan prepared by the malian side. on the development side the european commission follows a comprehensive approach, whereby we use all instruments at our disposal to address challenges in the short, medium and long term, including inter alia humanitarian aid, an instrument for stability, thematic and regional programmes, as well as a state building contract. the commission aims at the stabilisation of the country, the restoration of democracy and rule of law, as well as mitigation of the crisis that is affecting mali and its population since 2012. the commission has started implementing projects in line with this approach and intends to continue with additional interventions this year in line with the recovery plan for mali that i already mentioned for the years 2013-2014. the vice-president/high representative appointed an eu special representative, who is one of the key players in facilitating the inter-malian talks which aim to ensure the most peaceful possible resumption of state control over the whole of its territory, notably kidal in the north. in brief, europe is present in every priority area stated in the malian roadmap: support to the reform of the army under democratic control, support to the national commission for reconciliation; and support to elections with a european observation mission that will be led by louis michel. our diplomatic visibility and overall credibility are very good. and i may add that, despite some critics, the european union was actually very quick to adapt to a rapidly evolving situation. our instrument for stability package of eur 20 million, put in place in february, has made it possible to address urgent needs for security, state planning, presence and mediation. europe is also active at regional level. aid to mauritania and niger has been topped-up by eur 25 million each in may. concerning security, the csfp civilian mission eucap has started capacity building in niger, and the eu also supports the ‘collège sahélien de securité’ launched by niger, mauritania and mali. nevertheless, the most difficult part remains to come in mali but also in the whole region. it will require our continued attention. in mali, reconstruction is a multifaceted challenge: it will depend to a large extent on the political will of local stakeholders to make real progress on governance reforms. another challenge will be delivering international support effectively. we must avoid the mistakes of the past two decades when donor money did not have the planned impact on governance and development. the reform of the security sector, including justice, and consolidation of the rule of law are also key. the precise international burden-sharing arrangements are not yet fixed, but europe with its member states will be a major player with its capacity-building effort through the european development fund and the instrument for stability as well as through csdp action. similarly, reconciliation in mali will be a complex and long-term process. the eu has mobilised the means to support the national dialogue commission. a conflict resolution and peace promotion project is currently being implemented. but successful reconciliation will require strong commitment by all parties to a negotiated solution. this is at the heart of the ongoing inter-malian talks, which our eu special representative and delegations are facilitating. i also emphasise the question of human rights. the fact that the malian authorities are now sensitising their troops on human rights issues has to be welcomed. but vigilance remains essential to avoid abuses by any party. the eu finances african observers as well, for this reason, but breaches happen and they endanger reconciliation. we are following closely the human rights situation and continue to give support where needed and possible. on a regional level, cross-border security cooperation remains a major challenge, as recently shown with the attacks in niger and in algeria. a lot has still to be done, and the fight against terrorism, drug trafficking, and corruption requires considerably more effort. given the situation in libya, we see an urgent need for a regional framework, able to address the saharan dimension of the sahel, which is currently missing. a forum allowing for exchanges between north african and sahel countries, together with international partners, is not only important for immediate security issues but also for long-term socio-economic challenges. in short, i believe we can provide more comprehensive support to the malian people, but we cannot replace one thing: the will of malian stakeholders really to rise to the challenge. i expect very much that the developments of last month gave an assurance that they will do everything to rebuild, to strengthen the country, towards addressing the issues that have been hidden and not addressed for quite a substantial time, but it is on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, i will begin with the news item we are all following: in ouagadougou, under the authority of president compaore, an agreement is being signed on the situation in kidal and each of us knows how important this signature is for the normalisation of the situation, since otherwise the elections will be in danger and the holding of elections cannot be imagined with such a fragile situation in kidal. but let us remain optimistic and return to the central question of our debate today, namely the question of reconstruction. we have seen a successful military intervention - french forces have already been congratulated on several occasions - and there have been promises of aid, including the 'together for a new mali' conference. these are extremely important promises because the country's needs are indeed immense. i would just like to remind you that the resources of the malian government fell by 30% after the coup d'état in march 2012 and that almost half a million people were forced to abandon their homes. tens of thousands of them are still in refugee camps. medical services and access to education have not yet been restored in the north and, according to credible estimates, nearly one million malians are at risk of starvation. this is the challenge of reconstruction and, of course, as the commissioner has stressed, europe has a role to play in this context.
in writing. afghanistan is located in a critical region from the perspective of international security. that is why i also want to welcome the progress in the negotiations on a partnership and cooperation agreement between the union and afghanistan. the completion of the negotiations and the signing of the agreement will provide a strengthened framework for political and economic cooperation for the next decade. the main areas that the agreement will have to focus on are development, trade and good governance. romania is participating with combat troops in afghanistan, having one of the largest contingents. that is why it is also in the interest of my country that afghanistan stabilizes and that after the transition period, afghan institutions are fully functional. in this context, the decision to extend the eu-pol mission until the end of 2014 is welcomed.
cameroon is the only country in central africa to have negotiated an interim economic partnership agreement with the european union following the expiry of the world trade organisation's waiver of unilateral preferential trade arrangements for african, caribbean and pacific states. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the exporting producers concerned have been able to obtain a sufficient level of protection from the union market. i believe that the european parliament should give its consent to the economic partnership with cameroon, because it would be a model for the rest of the central african countries, which do not yet feel ready to start negotiations with the european union in this direction. at the same time, cameroon must ratify the agreement as soon as possible in order to benefit from its full benefits.
the millennium development goals were drawn up in a spirit of solidarity to meet the needs of the least developed countries, which face extreme poverty, alarming infant mortality rates and scarce natural resources. so far, three key goals have been achieved: halving the percentage of the population living in extreme poverty, improving access to safe drinking water, and reducing the rate of urban poor from 39 percent to 33 percent. however, the commitments of developed countries to help narrow the gaps need to be matched by real political will at global level. poverty eradication as well as sustainable development must be at the top of the post-2015 development agenda, while avoiding setting a new set of targets without identifying concrete ways to achieve them and the sources of funding.
the second revision of the cotonou agreement was one of the first files i followed on behalf of the epp group at the beginning of this parliamentary term. three years later, we are finally called upon to approve the conclusion of this agreement, while the next revision of the text is already scheduled for 2015. we all know the difficulties in negotiating this second revision, in particular - as has already been stressed here - the compatibility of the human rights provisions with the values of the union. but i think it is time to take the pragmatic option of approving this text. we must ensure that the cotonou agreement remains the basis of a strong partnership with the acp countries and at the same time a relevant instrument in the context of the new challenges facing the acp countries. after the acp-eu association council adopted last week the financial protocol with a generous financial allocation of eur 31.5 billion for the financing of the 11th european development fund, our agreement is all the more important. in this context, it must be recognised that the review contains the necessary ingredients for more effective development cooperation, capable of contributing to the achievement of the millennium development goals in the acp countries:
