in writing. − despite delays in ratification, the agreement represents an important intermediate step towards greater regional integration of the central african states. cameroon is the most dynamic economy in the region, and the removal of trade barriers with the union can contribute to the country's further development. and so the transition to an emerging economy by 2035 could be favored. the union is cameroon's largest trading partner and the economic partnership agreement will further promote the development of bilateral trade. the support measures will also lead to the strengthening of good governance in the region. i also want to welcome the inclusion of a human rights clause in the agreement, which creates additional obligations for the signatory parties. in this way, democratic reforms in central africa will be encouraged.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because the amendment to the cotonou agreement confirms the importance that both sides attach to the partnership. at the same time, the union's commitment to supporting states in difficulty is reaffirmed. correlation with the millennium development goals can help to achieve them. however, i think more could have been done in terms of human rights. i consider that, in this respect, the proposed amendment is not sufficient. there are still many signatory states to the agreement which systematically violate human rights, and parliament has drawn attention to these abuses. nor is the issue of tax havens or the readmission of illegal immigrants addressed. however, in the context of the approaching deadline for the third revision of the agreement, i believe that the current text provides a good basis for discussion.
in writing. - i voted for these recommendations. the eu's 'more for more' principle, reaffirmed in 2011, calls for strengthening political and economic relations with partners who are making progress towards democratisation. i believe that this principle should be the basis for the new amendment to the cotonou agreement. the way in which the aid is distributed must be in accordance with the performance standards of the signatory states as set out in annex iv, article 3 (b). the evaluation criteria shall take into account, inter alia, the progress of the implementation of institutional reforms and the concrete results of the programmes in the implementation phase. the second amendment to the cotonou agreement does not take these standards into account. taking as an example the non-compliance with the cotonou standards of ethiopia and congo, union aid to ethiopia was eur 644 million in the period 2008-2013. in the case of congo, the aid granted between 2008 and 2013 was eur 584 million. in the period 2014-2020, funds under cooperation with acp states amount to usd 31,5 billion. i call on the commission to reassess the democratic development of the acp states and to reallocate funds in direct proportion to the progress of the acp countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because romania, as a country that has long been under a communist dictatorship, understands very well the importance of media freedom. one of the major problems with media impartiality is the political control exercised over some media institutions. especially since these media can, in turn, exert pressure on state institutions as was recently seen in the european commission report on romania's progress in the cvm context. the union will not be able to be a real driver of media independence in the world until it has solved its own internal problems. this is why, if not uniform and harmonised legislation, at least a single code of professional conduct in the eu would be desirable.
in writing. − according to the freedom house report, press freedom in the world is at its lowest level in a decade, and only one in six citizens today lives in a country with a free and independent press. in my view, governments have the primary responsibility for guaranteeing and protecting freedom of the press and media. at the same time, a balance needs to be struck between national security concerns and freedom of information, in order to prevent abuse and guarantee the independence of the press and media. last but not least, a warning sign should be sounded regarding the media empires owned by politicians, who sometimes carry out disinformation campaigns. it is essential that the press and media can operate independently and without political and financial pressures.
in writing. − the economic crisis has had clear consequences on freedom of expression, even where the political power has not intervened in the media. economic censorship is no less dangerous than political censorship. if we can act consistently against political censorship, economic censorship is much harder to crack and fight. it is not the press, not the internet, not social media that are "to blame" for the discontent of citizens in their countries, but bad governance. under these circumstances, restricting freedom of speech is tantamount to adding fuel to the fire of discontent. democracy and pluralism are the best environment for asserting the needs and expectations of citizens, for decent solving of their problems. censorship doesn't solve problems, just as restricting freedom of speech for whatever reason, even in established democracies, can't lead to better governance, progress and prosperity.
in writing. − the right to freedom of expression is a universal human right, which is at the heart of democracy and is essential to the realisation of other rights to which people all over the world aspire. i believe that at european level, a strategy on press and media freedom should be adopted within the framework of the european union's external policy and the recommendations of this report should be integrated into future guidelines on freedom of expression (online and offline).
in writing. − although many reports suggest that the press in the european union is working in increasingly better conditions, there is still room for improvement to strengthen the position of journalists and the independent status of the media. i think paragraphs 29 and 30 raise a pressing problem for the press and media in the european union. i insist on paragraph 29, which talks about monitoring some of the mass media for unethical and allegedly illegal behavior. paragraph 30 underlines, as in other recent parliament reports, the need for monitoring by the commission of the independence of the press and media. i call on the member states to ensure that the freedom of the press and media is guaranteed and protected. i ask the european commission to monitor closely the freedom and independence of the press and media, as well as the abuses committed by journalists in breach of ethical provisions.
in writing. − freedom of the press and media in the world has become an increasingly worrisome topic and i have therefore strongly supported the adoption of this report. i am mostly concerned about the interference of governments in press and media issues. journalists all over the world are too often subject to pressure by powerful political media groups which try to impose a political line on them. as the report points out, governments have the responsibility of guaranteeing and protecting the freedom of the press and of ensuring the right of journalists to report freely and to have access to information. governments often fail to do this, not only in third countries, but also within the eu. i find this to be particularly worrying; therefore i am pleased to see that the final report acknowledges the fact that the eu can only be credible if its own member states respect the freedom of the press and media.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the data and information produced by the public sector of member state governments and by the union institutions or bodies constitute a vast pool of resources. these resources are diverse and valuable, they can be a source of knowledge, but also an accessible tool in ensuring the transparency that is so important to our citizens. i am among those who encourage the wide availability and reuse of information for private or commercial purposes and its distribution, not only to economic actors, but above all to all interested persons. finally, i would like to mention that, where possible, all this data should be provided in electronic form.
in writing. − i believe that, in order to facilitate re-use, public sector information should be made available in automatically processable and technologically neutral formats, so as to avoid, as far as possible, situations where specific technology is required for document processing.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because the recovery of the economy is an absolute priority for the union at the moment. the union's institutions must work together effectively, they are not in competition with each other but interdependent, and delays in decision-making make it impossible to complete the financial work. certain urgent matters should be concluded before the end of this mandate, but their implementation requires the cooperation of the commission and the council. i would remind you that econ has asked for an impact assessment of european legislation and i believe that it should be carried out as soon as possible. the lack of coordination and reaction of the institutions feeds the statements of the eurosceptic groups, as well as the negative myth of the 'european bureaucracy', creates uncertainty and does not facilitate investments, and, in the end, those directly affected are the citizens.
in writing. − the situation in turkey has worsened overnight since the outbreak of peaceful protests in gezi park in istanbul, with the response of the security forces leading to the rapid spread of protests in several cities. the violent police intervention resulted in four deaths and over a thousand injuries, mass arrests and severe damage to public and private property. i believe that turkey must respect the principles of a pluralistic and inclusive democracy in order for all citizens to feel represented in the decision-making process. the turkish authorities must promote tolerance and guarantee respect for the rights of all citizens to freedom of religion, freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and peaceful protest.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i too am concerned about the situation in turkey. until now, the country has been a pillar of stability in the region, and in the context of the syrian crisis, its role in humanitarian efforts has been very important. i would like to appeal to both the authorities and the protesters to refrain from any violent actions, which would only further strain the situation. i think we need to start a dialogue between civil society and the government to address the issues that have led to the current situation. both the european union and the states of the middle east need turkey to be stable.
in writing. - the situation in turkey is part of a complex regional context dominated by the civil war in syria. the causes of the protests in istanbul and other major turkish cities are much deeper and more serious than the simple rejection of a real estate project. turkey has enjoyed years of economic growth, but the growth has come at a political and social cost, and the fruits of that growth have been unequally shared. despite turkey's commitments in the process of negotiating its accession to the european union, the political regime in ankara is evolving towards authoritarianism, which is why the people on the streets in turkey are dissatisfied. the brutality of the turkish police has left many dead and wounded. violence may end the demonstrations, but it doesn't solve any of the problems the protesters claim. we must make it clear to the erdogan government that it will not solve anything by force, that it must enter into dialogue with the protesters and, above all, that it must respect its commitments made in the process of negotiating accession to the union. the eu and the middle east region need a democratic, stable and prosperous turkey, not a country gripped by a fever of protest and repression.
in writing. the compromise reached in turkey between the secularism of the state and the rule of political parties was the first step towards an islamic democracy. for example, former interim president mohamed hussein tantawia states: "turkey's experience is the closest to the egyptian people. turkey is a model to be inspired by. in the 14 days of protests in turkey, 4 people died and over 5,000 protesters were injured. but the authorities' violence against protesters in taksim square, prime minister erdogan's claims of zero tolerance towards protesters and calling protesters "extremists" are human rights violations that can only be cited as an example of "do not do". in a democracy there is a culture of protest and that is what turkey needs to show. being a democracy means having the right to free speech, the right to assemble and associate, the right to protest.
in writing. − the establishment of the european external action service (eeas) and the enshrinement of the function of high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy by the treaty of lisbon underlines the desire of member states to act together in a coherent manner in the various areas of the union's external action. this is a very important step for the whole of european construction, which is why every effort must now be made to exploit the potential of the union to act on the international scene. this requires an improvement in the efficiency of the functioning of the eeas, which is currently proving to be deficient in some areas. in order to ensure the full functionality of the eeas, i support a review of the organisation and functioning of this service. i believe that improvements can be made in the operational decision-making and implementation processes in the area of the common foreign and security policy, which are currently too slow. i support the simplification of the command structure of the eeas, as well as a strengthening of the role of its executive secretary-general by establishing a clear chain of command in support of an efficient decision-making process and a timely political response.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because i believe that the establishment of the eeas was a major step in defining a genuine foreign policy for the european union. i want to encourage the further development of the service as, in my view, the union needs to strengthen its external profile. however, i would like to point out that there are shortcomings in achieving a geographical and gender balance among the eeas staff. the new member states are still under-represented at all levels. that is why i believe that a medium-term solution for a fairer and more transparent recruitment procedure will have to be found. i also think that the gender balance issue will have to be addressed, especially in the top positions. but only with respect to the criteria of merit and performance.
in writing. − the eeas will need to become an efficient, results-oriented organisation as soon as possible. this seems to be affected for the time being by the current structure of the eeas, which is overburdened at the top and marked by too many decision-making levels. a more rational staff structure could make the eeas a flexible and adaptable instrument, capable of acting in crisis situations. as the report shows, the weaknesses of the service have become apparent in the context of recent events in north africa and the middle east, areas of interest to the eu where we should have been more present and more active in diplomacy. i also note the need for better coordination between institutions and good governance on international development issues so that the eu can adopt a unified vision and gain visibility. the eu has experience in designing, financing and managing development programmes in partner countries, some of them highly sensitive, that address the active fight against poverty. it is in no one's interest to draw parallels that lead to the waste of already limited resources.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european external action service (eeas) needs to be coordinated more effectively. the european commission and the eeas should also avoid overlapping their activities in order to make decision-making more efficient and to respond in a timely manner to international challenges. last but not least, the european parliament must have a bigger say in how the eeas operates.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation. however, i believe that the clear progress made in setting up the european external action service does not eliminate the problems of the functioning of the service. the crisis in mali and the situation in syria have highlighted a number of procedural and communication deficiencies in the eeas. the european external action service is an opportunity to pursue a coherent foreign policy. i support point 3 of this recommendation aimed at simplifying the hierarchical structure and defining the roles of eeas representatives for greater institutional coherence. this simplification is made possible by the unification of the external policy structures of the commission and the council secretariat. i stress the need for cooperation between national embassies and eeas delegations. this can be achieved through a system of joint political reporting between the two courts.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it very much echoes the concerns of the european parliament about the organisation of the european external action service (eeas). it makes it very clear that the eeas must make further efforts to make europe's voice heard in the world, and that this can only be done by improving synergy and cooperation between the institutions of the european union and the member states so that the eeas can respond quickly and appropriately to events in the world. a second reason for my vote is the definition of the objectives of the eeas and in particular the reaffirmation of the 'community' character of the neighbourhood policies. finally, the report proposes to achieve economies of scale with greater conciliation with the member states in order to reduce costs, particularly in consular services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report, but i appreciate that the recommendation should have stressed the issue of geographical balance in the selection and appointment of eeas staff. i recently asked the european external action service to answer the following questions: what is the number of staff of the european external action service; what is the provenance, by member state, of eeas staff; what is the provenance, by member state, of eeas staff in management positions; what measures will the eeas management take to achieve a more pronounced geographical balance in the selection and appointment of staff. the reply received referred only to the total number of persons employed by the eeas, avoiding to provide the specific information requested. i consider the reply to be a lack of transparency on the part of the high representative.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because, after the french military intervention, the situation in mali seems to have stabilised. but at the level of homeland security, there are still areas that present risks. i believe that holding the elections in july is a major test for the authorities in bamako, but also for the security of the country. the eu training mission will have an important role to play in the period ahead, especially in the context of the phased withdrawal of french troops from mali. but we need other kinds of support besides military training. in the past, there have been numerous reports of military personnel trained by foreign experts defecting to join rebel forces. internal dialogue and rule of law reform in mali must be encouraged to prevent such events from recurring. and the involvement of civil society is very important to legitimize the actions of the authorities.
in writing. − the stabilisation of mali following the french military intervention remains fragile without a process of national reconciliation and without a sustained effort to heal the region of its worst scourge: chronic poverty. the sahel would not have become a 'no man's land' conducive to extremist activities without the hunger in the region. mali has the second highest infant mortality rate in the world, after somalia. the armed conflict has exacerbated the situation of 4.6 million people affected by persistent food insecurity and forced half a million residents to flee their homes. the european commission's humanitarian response to the food crisis in the sahel has been swift and substantial. this effort must be reinforced by coordinated development assistance to ensure that the population has access to water, food, housing and basic health and education services. only a regional development effort can be the real stabilising factor, after the eradication of terrorism, which is fuelled by the conflicts in the ivory coast, libya and mali.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because eradicating global poverty must remain a priority objective of the union and of all developed countries. the millennium development goals remain a priority in the union's development assistance policy. but i must also point out that not all the targets will probably be met by 2015. promoting gender equality is still a problem in many countries. also, access to clean water sources or decent health services remains difficult in many areas of the world. i believe that after 2015, the union, as the world's leading aid donor, will have to focus on making poverty eradication efforts sustainable. assistance must be geared to job creation and decent education and health services.
in writing. − the post-2015 mdgs should include a number of specific objectives, emphasising their cross-cutting nature across development cooperation programmes. among these, i mention the need to accelerate global action to reduce maternal, infant and newborn mortality, with universal access to reproductive health services being key. research into more effective and sustainable prevention and treatment programmes, including research and development of effective medical interventions, including vaccines, medicines and diagnostics, should be further supported. i call for the implementation and enforcement of specific and effective policies to combat all violations of women's rights to life, bodily integrity, freedom of movement and choice of partner, including so-called 'honour' crimes, forced marriage and female genital mutilation, regardless of who commits them and where they are committed. all countries must ratify the united nations convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women in order to promote gender equality. quality basic education must also be ensured for marginalised populations, in particular in rural areas, conflict-affected areas, for children with disabilities and for children in employment.
in writing. − equality of opportunity is a key factor for sustainable development, yet discrimination persists in all countries of the world in women's access to education, the labour market, basic health services, especially reproductive and sexual health, and in decision-making. at the same time, domestic violence and physical abuse continue to be major obstacles to achieving gender equality, blocking women's opportunities for social assertion, economic initiative and personal development. in order to build on the progress made so far, we must take into account that women's empowerment, socioeconomic independence and gender equality are preconditions for achieving the mdgs. it is necessary to fully integrate gender equality into country strategies and development indicators by including the gender gap index in the criteria for measuring the achievement of the mdgs.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that poverty eradication and the achievement of global social and environmental sustainable development should be the priorities of the post-2015 development agenda. it is also important to include a specific target on the elimination of all forms of violence against women, and to recognise the right to abortion and contraception as universal rights, which are essential to achieving the mdgs. i therefore believe that the new framework should be a universal one, including a limited number of concrete objectives and measurable targets to meet the needs of the least developed countries, which face extreme poverty, a worrying infant mortality rate and a lack of natural resources.
in writing. − i believe that addressing malnutrition among mothers and children requires long-term development strategies at european level, focusing on sectors that influence malnutrition, such as health, education, water and sanitation and agriculture.
in writing. - i voted for this report. i stress the need for a concerted effort at european level, to be highlighted in the future framework document 'towards a post-2015 development framework'. furthermore, for greater coherence at european level, i support the alignment of the sustainable development goals with the post-2015 millennium development goals. the european union's common position must contain key development and sustainability issues. according to the study by the european parliament's foreign affairs department, the main challenges for the post-2015 framework are the so-called 'non-profit' dimensions of poverty: inequality, human rights issues, marginalisation and exclusion. it was decided to allocate 0,7% of the gross national income of the member states to official development assistance (oda) by 2015. i insist on the need to implement this directive at national level. the european union is the world's largest donor and must assume this role in the context of the redefinition of the post-2015 agenda. we need to take into account the disparities between underdeveloped and developing countries at international level in order to make the implementation of the millennium development goals more effective.
in writing. the european union must play a leading role in the achievement and definition of the post-2015 millennium development goals. this is the whole point of this report, it ensures that poverty eradication, respect for human rights in the interests of peoples' peace and security, environmental sustainability of the actions that can be carried out and the necessary strengthening of cooperation between donors to improve the financing of actions are taken into account. it is as a convinced european and believing that europe must give a voice to help the development of the planet that i gave a positive outcome to my vote.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report and stress the importance of references to agriculture and private sector development in achieving the millennium development goals. i regret that the issue of supporting small farmers to produce enough food has been distorted by a rather inappropriate feminist approach. as regards the votes on abortion, free access to contraception and sex education, i would point out that i voted in favour of these rights, which i support, especially in view of the tragedy that romania went through during the communist period as a result of the prohibition of these rights.

member of the commission. - madam president, as mr[nbsp ]seeber knows, it was not an easy negotiation. more than 10 council working party meetings, seven coreper meetings, three trialogues and two technical trialogues were held with a view to reaching the first reading agreement. you have done a very good job to make this possible. without the european parliament’s help, the deal on the watchlist and the strategy on pharmaceuticals would not be as good as they are. on the question of cost, which was raised today, whenever we make a proposal we do an impact assessment, and nothing comes for free. we always have to look at both sides of the question and determine firstly how much it would cost to remedy and secondly how much it would cost not to remedy. i can guarantee you that, if we do not remedy such problems, the next cost review in five to 10 years’ time and impact assessments will show that not remedying them will cost even more. so we would have even more reasons not to adopt that kind of solution. it makes all the more sense for us to compare the costs and benefits at all times. whenever we do that we try to be balanced because we understand that this has to be done in a way that benefits human health and the environment but that is also cost-efficient. concerning the science, all the proposals are science-based. we went through the whole list of proposals and, if i remember correctly, the list was very long. science is constantly advancing and we will take into account whatever new evidence and data is shown to us in the future, whether from interested parties, the business sector, academia or wherever. this is such a serious issue that it simply cannot be done any other way. what is important now is to implement the proposal and to work as closely as possible with the member states. that is exactly what the commission intends to do. i would like to thank you all, and the rapporteur, for giving your support to the proposal.

regional and social cohesion. one of the key elements of competitiveness is connectivity. the union is based on foreign trade. air transport, airports play an important role in connecting europe with the rest of the world. therefore, support is needed for a highly ambitious agenda for this sector. liberalisation is necessary and has its place. at the same time, however, the union must promote and defend its own standards and interests. particular attention should be paid to labour and environmental standards, safety and security, passenger rights and, in general, compliance with european regulations. the european commission must define a minimum set of requirements to be included in bilateral agreements, in order to defend european interests, values and good practices. at the same time, we must insist on comprehensive agreements at european level, based on european unity and authorised by the council. the agreements must include conditions relating to safety, security, passenger rights, staff training and certification. the efforts made over the last 7 years to implement an external aviation policy, even if at a high level, have proved insufficient. a common approach, coordinated at european level, is needed to increase the union's chances of penetrating new markets. air service agreements with brazil, australia and new zealand need to be finalised, agreements with emerging economies need to be negotiated: china, india, asean, the gulf states, and so on. the agreements with neighbouring countries such as ukraine, lebanon, tunisia, azerbaijan and algeria are development opportunities for regional and secondary airports and can at the same time help to decongest the main european hubs and increase their global competitiveness. the congestion of the main european airports is evident and creates disadvantages for new hubs in third countries. new infrastructure is needed and the existing infrastructure needs to be used efficiently. competition must be transparent and fair. there are still elements that distort the market, subsidies, lack of transparency, non-compliance with social standards, unequal approach to passenger rights. the external aviation policy must fully respect the principle of reciprocity, including market access, address all air services activities, fair and transparent competition and have two main objectives: the benefit of passengers and companies and supporting european companies and airports in their efforts to maintain their leading position on the world market. the european parliament calls on the commission and the member states to speed up the implementation of the two european projects of major importance to the aviation sector: ses and sesar. in this respect, i would like to welcome the commission's proposal, ses2+, which, although not ambitious enough, can be improved and can be a very big step forward for the efficiency of air transport within the union. we ask the commission to examine measures that can ensure reciprocity in the use of airspace between the union and the russian federation. the trade agreement between the united states and the european union will also affect air transport. the commission should consider the removal of restrictions on the ownership and control of airlines, both in relation to the united states and canada.

cooperatives are a very important community-based and proven management tool in the european union. in the central and eastern european region, their status and functioning were unfortunately somewhat compromised during the communist period. their role in dealing with the current protracted crisis is undeniable. their number and importance have increased in all member states. the employment rate in these companies is on the upward trend and, despite the complex crisis, they are more resilient than traditional companies and even have a strong role in integrating the workforce at regional level. cooperatives are more open than traditional businesses. their flexibility in new and innovative sectors demonstrates the adaptability that has enabled them to sustain their activities. their strategy is a collective solution. a single regulatory framework at union level could increase the competitiveness of a number of activities organised within the cooperative sector by harmonising the positive mechanisms inherent in the cooperative model.
in writing. in recent years, it has been observed that, despite the crisis facing the european economy, there have been and are a number of entities that have withstood the recession, namely cooperatives. by enabling small entrepreneurs, often groups of citizens, to take on entrepreneurial responsibilities, including in areas such as social and health services, school services, commercial services, communications, cooperatives have been able to effectively promote entrepreneurship on a micro-economic scale, especially in remote or disadvantaged areas. cooperatives thus represent a model of development capable of responding to new needs. they stimulate job creation better than other models due to their ability to adapt to change and keep their job at risk, are anchored in the local economy, contribute to sustainable local development and ensure that their business is not off-shored, even when operating internationally. in addition, cooperatives have been created in new and innovative sectors and there is evidence that such structures have been able to withstand the crisis, in particular with regard to cooperative banks and cooperatives in industry and the service sector (workers' cooperatives, social cooperatives and cooperatives formed by smes).

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, after excessive speed and non-compliance with the rules of the road, the technical condition of motor vehicles is the third cause of accidents in romania. regular roadworthiness testing can be an important tool in their prevention. moreover, the increasing mobility of people across the union justifies the need for harmonised legislation in this area. environmental protection issues must not be neglected, because 5% of the car fleet causes 25% of total emissions of pollutants, and a significant part is generated by vehicles with problems with the emission control system. finally, i would like to stress the need for better training of vehicle owners. basic checks such as tyre pressure are minor preventive measures but have a major impact on road safety.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it establishes eu minimum standards which are of the greatest importance for the union’s cohesion and road safety. if the member states want to go further, they will be free to set stricter rules. periodic testing should be used as the principle tool to ensure roadworthiness. this is why awareness campaigns will be developed in the eu to accustom vehicle owners to good practices and habits. if users are aware of the risks, they will certainly have better practices, and in consequence, tests that will detect deficiencies in a motor vehicle’s roadworthiness in time will also prevent many accidents. this report upholds the principle of free movement within the european union since the roadworthiness certificate issued in the original member state of registration should be mutually recognised among the member states for the purpose of re-registration. in the future, when the principles of this report will have been completed, provisions for full mutual recognition of roadworthiness certificates throughout the union should be applied, and the eu will reach a new level in terms of road cohesion and harmonisation.
chemical pollution, as we know, directly or indirectly affects not only the lives of aquatic animals but also the lives of the citizens of the european union, and water pollution cannot be stopped at the border, which is why i believe that a joint effort is needed to achieve positive results in combating pollution. the replacement, elimination or introduction of chemicals has a negative impact on all watersheds and should be a concern for national and european policies in the coming period. i am seriously concerned about the inclusion of three new substances in the list, used in the pharmaceutical industry, namely 17beta-estradiol, the synthetic hormone 17alpha and, last but not least, the non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug diclofenac, which have endocrine disrupting properties, and we should therefore do everything we can to remove these substances and to ensure the benefits of clean watersheds.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because water pollution is one of the problems of concern to european citizens, chemical contamination being a threat to the aquatic environment. unfortunately, there is no correct information in the field. the objective of the 2000 water framework directive is to achieve good environmental status by 2015. the updating of the list of chemicals presenting risks and the proposal to add new substances considered dangerous will improve the effectiveness of the directive. however, the decision to include substances used in the pharmaceutical industry in the list could have consequences for health policies in the member states. last but not least, i would like to inform you that a project to monitor the danube waters has recently been launched in romania, which will also include activities to inform the population about the correct management of waste.
in writing. − chemical pollution is one of the factors that increasingly affects the aquatic environment and the quality of safe and clean water in our society. therefore, taking appropriate measures to control chemical pollution of water is a central aspect of sustainable water management. the water framework directive (wfd), adopted in 2000, adopts an integrated approach to water policy, focusing on water management at the level of river basins, setting a sustainability target of achieving good overall ecological, chemical and quantitative status for eu water bodies by 2015. the dca sets out in particular strategies to combat water pollution. this report adds 15 chemicals and 33 pollutants to the list that are monitored and controlled in eu surface waters, including industrial chemicals, biocides, plant protection products and, for the first time, three substances used in the pharmaceutical industry. these substances have been selected on the basis of the available scientific information as they may present significant risks.
in writing. − water pollution is one of the main environmental concerns expressed by eu citizens. the water framework directive is our key tool to improve water availability and quality by reducing chemical pollution. in the current context, an amendment to the water framework directive is necessary to have a clearer and more effective water pollution control strategy, capable of ensuring the conservation of a balanced aquatic environment and preventing dramatic damage to the environment and human health. identifying the causes of pollution and tackling emissions at source as effectively as possible must be a priority. it is therefore very important to identify and monitor possible sources of pollution and to apply systematically the fundamental 'polluter pays' principle laid down in directive 2006/60/ec. the transboundary nature of water pollution is of particular importance. for this reason, it is appropriate to establish harmonised standards at union level for priority substances and to require member states to notify exceedances of these standards as soon as possible. i also consider it important to provide citizens with adequate, transparent and timely information on the state of the european union's waters and on the measures taken and results achieved in the context of strategies to combat chemical pollution.
in writing. − chemical pollution is one of the factors that greatly affects the aquatic environment and the availability and quality of safe and clean water in our society. i believe that appropriate measures should be taken to control chemical pollution of water under the water framework directive.
in writing. − i voted for this report as i agree with the added effectiveness it will bring to the commission proposal to amend the water framework directive (wfd). a 2012 survey revealed that 73 % of europeans think that the eu should propose additional measures to address water problems. these problems are largely the result of chemical water pollution affecting both aquatic biodiversity and public health, and so should be addressed as a matter of urgency. in particular, i sympathised with the principle that the polluter should pay the full amount of funds necessary to rectify the environmental damage they cause at source. it is part of the policy of preventive action as detailed in article 191 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. these measures are designed to improve, on an international level, the quality of the environment, rationalise the use of natural resources and improve public health. the ‘polluter pays’ principle is key to achieving these fair and sensible objectives, especially in the context of water policy.

in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy gives a strong place to european marine policies, with the aim of enabling the union to respond to the pressing and growing challenges facing humanity, including climate change. in addition, europe's long and strong maritime tradition is reinforced by new and developing activities such as wind energy, cruises and offshore aquaculture. these areas, as well as new technologies such as robotics and advanced marine equipment, require a constant encouragement of cooperation between industry and academia in order to prepare graduates for new professions that are constantly evolving and adapting. as such, i support the rapporteur's proposal on the establishment and funding of 'european sectoral employment and skills councils'. they will enable the relevant authorities to record new employment trends in order to develop new training initiatives to promote worker mobility.
in writing. − cooperatives, alongside other small and medium-sized enterprises, play an important role in shaping the social economy sector in the european union. their work contributes not only to economic development but also to the promotion of cohesion and solidarity, thus giving relevance to the european social model. at the same time, their work needs to be brought to the attention of national and european decision-makers as a result of their growing importance both in terms of the number of jobs they have created and their contribution to the growth of the european economy. european and national decision-makers need to stimulate this type of economic association, especially in the context of the recession, precisely because of the greater flexibility of cooperatives. they can be one of the points of affirmation of microeconomic entrepreneurship in a context that is extremely difficult for 'classic' enterprises. moreover, the transfer-to-employees solution should be more frequently considered by national authorities when seeking to ensure the continuity of an economic operator. i voted in favor of this resolution.

in writing. − cooperatives are a development model that can respond to new needs, especially since they are firmly anchored in the local economy and have very good results in terms of growth, employment, survival rate and opening of new businesses and development of new services. they also contribute to sustainable local development and ensure that their work is not off-loaded, which is significant in this time of crisis. in addition, cooperatives stimulate job creation better than other models because of their ability to adapt to change and to keep their business in case of risk. it is also beneficial that there may be groups of individual cooperatives organised into large entrepreneurial groups, covering sectors such as industry, agriculture, distribution, finance, research and development and higher education.

mr president, hungary’s troubling record on rights is putting europe to the test. this is the first sentence of the latest analysis of human rights watch and they are right. the debate today and the vote tomorrow is a test of how determined parliament is to defend eu fundamental values and principles. on several occasions we have had discussions about what has been going on in hungary. we started with media law, that incredible legislation and practice which comprised everything that was bad or controversial in different european countries without any check and balance. we continued with the changes to the judiciary and the constitutional court, aimed at limiting judges’ powers and making them less independent. we have stressed over and over again that the hungarian legislation and practice was against the letter and spirit of article 2 of the treaty. unfortunately, on all these issues and debates, the commission was rather weak, if not absent, as if the treaty and its article 2 were just recommendations. at the same time, many other european institutions have expressed harsh criticism – the osce, the council of europe’s secretary-general, the venice commission, the parliamentary assembly of the council of europe and, of course, the european parliament, as well as an impressive number of international and hungarian ngos and media associations. we cannot all be wrong or all be accused of being anti-hungarian, which means that now is the time for robust action. we have said again and again that what happens in a member state is an internal business of the european union. therefore i hope that the message we are sending through this report will be seriously considered by the eu institutions and the hungarian government. i truly hope that mr orbán will not answer in an arrogant style, questioning this house and its treaty right to express concern and ask for action on the undemocratic behaviour of a government.

in writing. the introduction of a financial transaction tax is a good initiative, provided it is practiced globally. if this tax is imposed in only 11 eu member states, we will face the risk of capital movements to other jurisdictions where this tax does not exist. in addition, the range of financial transactions to which this tax will apply is still limited. i believe that the european union must continue its efforts to convince other countries where important financial transactions take place of the need to introduce a tax on these transactions.

member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr vaughan, for his report. as is the case every year, this report will provide the commission with important input on its future work in fighting against fraud to the eu financial interests. the commission will of course reply in writing to all the concrete proposals in due course. however, i would like to say a few words about some of them now. firstly, i would like to provide you with a short update on the main initiatives that the commission has taken in order to improve the policy framework in the anti-fraud field. we have tabled a number of important proposals, and on some of them we have already been able to reach an agreement. there is, of course, the olaf reform on which we have just debated at length. in this context, let me stress that this report is not the right place to make judgments on the way individual investigations have been handled by olaf. furthermore, we proposed, in 2012, a directive on the fight against fraud to the union’s financial interests by means of criminal law. we are eagerly awaiting the parliament’s input on this proposal, known as the pif directive. we have also launched a number of successful initiatives related specifically to the revenue side. thus, the vat directive and the customs code implementing provisions were amended with stricter and clearer conditions as regards procedure code 42, which allows importers to suspend the payment of vat at import. we have launched a broad action plan to fight tax fraud and tax evasion, which has received strong support both at eu and international levels; in particular, we managed finally to achieve an agreement on the vat quick reaction mechanism, and, just last month, we adopted a comprehensive eu strategy against cigarette smuggling. our proposal for a new hercule iii programme is a continuation of our efforts to help member states improve their work in fighting fraud. hercule iii is the only programme specifically aimed at protecting the eu’s financial interests by organising training and providing technical assistance. in parallel, we have already implemented, to a large extent, the commission’s internal anti-fraud strategy adopted in 2011. moving away from the policy area, the quality of reporting by the member states remains a perennial problem. it is not exclusively due to a divergent application of the reporting regulations by the member states; it is also caused by very different legal, organisational and even cultural approaches that member states have in relation to the fight against fraud affecting the eu’s financial interests. in recent years olaf has deployed great efforts to provide member states with technical solutions, training, guidelines and instructions to improve uniformity in the reporting of information concerning irregularities and fraud. agreeing on a more uniform definition of fraud in the context of the proposed pif directive would bring additional improvements in this area. to conclude my comments on the first report, and without prejudice to my comments regarding the points on olaf individual investigations, your annual report provides a solid basis to further improve the protection of the eu’s financial interest and fight against fraud. the commission will pursue its efforts proactively to address those issues which put at risk the proper use of the european taxpayer’s money. let me turn now to the report on the commission’s integrated internal control framework. i would like to thank the rapporteur, ms andrea češková, for the constructive approach used in the report and the comprehensive analysis of the current situation. the report correctly indicates that the commission is still striving for a positive das, but there are conditions to fulfil before getting there. firstly, the commission services will continue implementing the audit and discharge recommendations issued every year in order to improve the management, control and protection of the eu budget. secondly, for all programmes under shared management, the member states must ensure that their management and control systems are functioning as required. they must also conduct effective controls at the level of final recipients of eu funds and report in a way that allows the commission to identify existing problems and to take any necessary action. thirdly, the post-2013 legislation must reflect the issues identified in the simplification agenda for the new multiannual financial framework and the simplification scoreboards adopted by the commission. finally, the commission’s action to protect the eu budget through its multiannual corrective mechanisms needs to be taken into consideration when assessing the effectiveness of its management and control systems. it should be put in perspective with the error rate estimated by the court of auditors. after the summer, the commission will take the next step by issuing a new report on the protection of the eu budget. with this report, the commission will give more inside views and explanations on the performance of its multiannual preventive and corrective systems. moreover, the commission welcomes the suggestion that an interinstitutional working group be set up to consider necessary measures aimed at establishing a performance-based budget and it will prepare an action plan in this regard.
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, as the ppe shadow rapporteur on the 2011 report on the protection of the union’s financial interests, i would like to recall some facts. the financial impact of fraud reported in 2011 decreased by 37% compared to 2010. however, the amount of fraud is still very high – eur 400 million, of which eur 77 million was fraud in agriculture and more than eur 200 million fraud in cohesion policy, with other figures adding up to eur 400 million. i would now like to say a few words on the fight against cigarette smuggling and illicit trade in tobacco products. between 2005 and 2010 illicit trade in cigarettes deprived the european union and the member states of more than eur 10 billion. this eur 10 billion lost in cigarette smuggling is used to support and enlarge organised crime networks. this is why i welcome the eu strategy against cigarette smuggling and the illicit tobacco trade published in june. i believe it comes quite late but it is good that we have it. vulnerable member states should be given stronger support to protect borders against cigarette smuggling. one way to do it is with hercule iii, a programme designed to fund detection of smuggling at the borders, for instance through buying and installing truck-scanning equipment. it should be very clear to all member states that, once tobacco is smuggled into the eu through a weaker border, we are all affected, including the member states who do not have external borders.
i am very pleased with the results of mr pargneaux's report. in crisis situations we need central coordination and, above all, we need improved communication and cooperation between member states. the prevention of critical situations such as avian influenza or e. coli is based on transparency between member states, their immediate capacity to react, individually or as a group, and cooperation between medical and veterinary units on a pre-crisis basis. when we talk about serious cross-border health threats, we must not forget poverty and the correlations between the health of the population and the social and financial problems it faces. poverty may not affect all of us today, but that does not mean that we can remain homeless in the future. right now, 19,000 children die every day before they're five years old. poverty is one of the primary factors in malnutrition and lack of access to health services and adequate treatment. our immune systems are essential to cope with crises and epidemics, but to do so, we must prioritize the proper implementation of nutrition plans and proper care for infants, children, and their mothers. access to appropriate medicines for those suffering from communicable and non-communicable diseases must be increased to minimise the number of people affected by the epidemic. and finally, let me congratulate the rapporteur on the work he has done on this exceptional report.

in writing. − i support this resolution as continuity and expediency must be restored, so that the revised 1958 agreement can effectively ensure that the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) is able to remove inconsistencies in technical requirements when the contracting parties engage in trade in motor vehicles. this resolution aims to modify and bring up to date the agreement to establish global technical regulations regarding which wheeled vehicles, equipment and parts can be fitted on wheeled vehicles, as introduced by council decision 2000/125/ec of 31 january 2000. the incompatibility lies with the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), which has since altered the procedure by which the union establishes its position in regard to unece and other international organisations. the original council decision must be brought into line with the new decision-making procedure, so as to be able to continue effectively with the parallel agreement in the framework of the unece.

in writing. − the european union has established, through the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), legislative and budgetary instruments to provide additional support to workers affected by major changes in the structure of world trade, aggravated by the economic, financial and social crisis. i believe that member states should be encouraged to take advantage of the exchange of good practice and to learn especially from member states that have already set up national egf information networks involving social partners and local actors, in order to have a good support structure when a situation falling within the scope of the egf would occur.
in writing. − i voted for the report on the mobilisation of eur 750 000 from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), covering technical assistance for the commission. i particularly support the allocation of eur 80 000 for the creation of a knowledge base, which increases information sharing through networks and expert groups. a detailed database of facts and figures from all the previous cases allows new applicants to better understand the functioning and implementation of the egf. processing of new applications is therefore simplified and speeded up. additionally, enhancing the sharing of know-how and the liaison between all those involved in the egf process reduces the misuse of the funds received.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) plays a key role in the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of structural changes in world trade. since its creation in 2007, some €464 million has been requested to support 97 000 workers. i welcome the commission's proposal to mobilise the egf to provide eur 750 000 for technical assistance. the measures proposed by the european executive regarding the use and evaluation of the egf in the member states will increase the efficiency, transparency and visibility of this instrument. the consolidation of the egf is all the more important as it will allow the application procedure to be simplified and the examination of applications to be accelerated. it will also contribute to the objective of reducing the administrative burden for member states. equally important is the strengthening of the promotion and information dimension through a website that will allow the exchange of knowledge and information on the egf. at the same time, the establishment of national egf information networks will stimulate innovation and economic growth, improving the quality of everyday life of european citizens.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the differences between the provisions on the obligations and liability of depositaries must be eliminated. the companies managing the collective investment undertakings need to have control and risk and remuneration management policies. therefore, harmonisation of supervisory practices by the european securities and markets authority and the european banking authority is vital and sanctions for breach of these rules should not be overlooked. in romania, the investment management company is responsible for the management of undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities. a legislative framework is also in place for actions that can be classified as infringements, as well as appropriate sanctions.
in writing. − the principles governing remuneration policies must recognise that ucits management companies have the capacity to apply those policies in different ways, depending on their size and the size of the ucits they manage, their internal organisation and the nature, scale and complexity of their activities. however, ucits management companies should ensure the simultaneous application of those principles in all cases. i consider that any financial instrument held in custody for a ucits must be distinguished from the depositary's own assets and must be identified at all times as belonging to that ucits; such a requirement must confer an additional level of protection to investors in the event of the depositary's breach of its contractual obligations.
in writing. − i voted for this report. undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) are investment funds that manage a market of almost eur 6 trillion in assets. scandals such as the lehman brothers’ bankruptcy or the bernard madoff fraud shook the integrity of this huge market. therefore it is necessary to ensure investor safety once more. this report regulates in particular transparency regarding the remuneration of investment fund managers and the proportion of their bonus payments, which should be no more than two times the fixed salary. for example, richard fuld, the former ceo of lehman brothers, was paid in 2007, so only one year before the collapse in 2008, a total of usd 22 million, which included a base salary of only usd 750 000, a cash bonus of more than usd 4 million and stock grants of more than usd 16 million. establishing the balance between an investment fund manager’s fixed salary and his/her bonus payment and ensuring that remuneration is disclosed in an accurate manner to all stakeholders involved are proofs of reliability, which aim at restoring the confidence of investors on the market.
in writing. − the european union is leading the global effort to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from human activities, which threaten to cause dangerous global climate change. the community emissions trading scheme (eu ets) developed by the european union is the cornerstone of its strategy to reduce its own greenhouse gas emissions cost-effectively. this system is based on the recognition that carbon pricing is the most cost-effective way to significantly reduce global greenhouse gas emissions, and that such reductions are necessary to prevent dangerous levels of climate change.
in writing. − one of the european union's most important objectives is to reduce industrial emissions. due to the large quantities of emission allowances, the carbon price is falling very noticeably from around 30 euro/tonne of co2 to around 7 euro/tonne of co2, and investments in technologies need to be supported. this decision to adapt the eu ets auction calendar only once, in the third phase of the eu ets trading, maintains a certain balance. i therefore believe that we need to take steps to strike a balance between carbon emissions and scientific innovation and i agree with the structural changes, considering that the volume of greenhouse gas emissions quotas requires special conditions.
in writing. − recent crossborder health threats, such as the h1n1 influenza pandemic (2009), the volcanic ash cloud (2010) or e. coli (2011), have led to the european union strengthening its response capacity by taking concrete measures to provide means, networks and structures complementary to those already in place to prevent and combat them. the proposal voted today extends the risk assessment and coordination measures applicable to communicable diseases to all threats to health from biological, chemical or environmental sources; strengthens the role of the health security committee to improve coordination of crisis response measures; and provides for each member state to develop, strengthen and update in a coordinated manner national health crisis preparedness and response plans, exchanging good practices with other member states. i believe that the proper functioning of the 'rapid alert and response system' and the system for recognising a health emergency' requires close cooperation between the member states and the eu institutions. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because, by harmonising and strengthening the union's capacities and structures, it will provide an effective response to major crossborder health threats. events such as swine flu, avian flu and the effects of the volcanic cloud in iceland have shown that member states have faced difficulties in trying to act unilaterally. the union therefore needs a coherent response framework and effective joint action. member states' efforts need to be multiplied, especially in view of the current crisis period. the economic effort of each member state will thus be reduced by coordinating actions and responding to a possible cross-border crisis. taking the example of the volcanic ash cloud in iceland, the paralysis of air traffic at european level caused significant losses to passengers and airlines. in romania, losses exceeded eur 7 million.
in writing. − building on the rapid alert and response system for communicable diseases established in 1998, the european commission's proposal sets out measures to strengthen the eu's response capacity to prevent serious crossborder threats to health by providing complementary means, networks and structures to combat these threats. by this decision, the commission proposes to 'extend the scope of the rapid alert and response system on serious cross-border threats to health'. the commission thus intends to address the shortcomings identified in recent years in the notification, surveillance, assessment and management of health risks. recent events have demonstrated that the european union has not responded adequately when faced with health crises resulting from medicines being used for purposes other than their original purpose or from the placing on the market of defective medical devices. an effective warning system would certainly have helped to prevent such tragedies.
in writing. − recent serious crossborder events such as the h1n1 pandemic in 2009, the volcanic ash cloud and the toxic red mud in 2010, the e. coli bacteria in 2011, have demonstrated the need for measures to strengthen the eu's response capacity and provide the means, networks and structures to effectively protect citizens across europe against a wide range of crossborder health threats. in this context, i welcome the commission's proposal for a decision extending the scope of the alert and response system, improving coordination of crisis response measures and ensuring greater efficiency in responding to serious cross-border threats to health. while member states have the responsibility to manage public health crises at national level, no country can cope with a cross-border public health crisis on its own. i therefore believe that the european union should complement and support national policies and encourage cooperation between member states, without, however, replacing their competence in this area. cooperation with third countries and international organisations, in particular the world health organisation, should also be given high importance in relation to the emergence or re-emergence of communicable diseases.
in writing. − i believe that this proposal for a decision on crossborder threats, particularly in terms of coordinating and ensuring the effectiveness of the response to serious health threats, certainly helps to prevent dramatic situations.
in writing. − the health threats that have affected the european union in recent years, such as h1n1 influenza or e. coli, have shown that the european union is not prepared to deal in a concerted way with these dangers, which are by their nature transnational. i therefore voted in favour of this report as it will lead to a strengthening of the european union's capacity to react and prevent such health threats, both in terms of risk assessment, improving the efficiency of existing structures and cooperation at european and international level, in particular with the world health organisation. the new framework defined by this decision will allow the eu to be better prepared to prevent and combat such health threats, which can have very serious effects on european citizens.
in writing. - i voted for this report. i believe that by introducing common procedures for the procurement of pandemic medicines and vaccines, member states will be able to respond more quickly and effectively to unforeseen events and pandemic threats to the health of union citizens. in addition, they support the establishment of the rapid alert and response system, consisting of the european commission, the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) and the competent and responsible national authorities. the rapid alert and response system will notify cases of serious cross-border threats at european level, and will act independently and in the interest of the union as a whole in establishing the necessary measures to protect public health.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution and draw attention to the fact that serious crossborder threats to health should not be seen solely as diseases affecting human beings. diseases affecting domestic animals, and even food plants, are equally important cross-border health threats, requiring equally coordinated and well-organised interventions and prevention actions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i think that the decision taken by the 11 member states to work together to implement the financial transaction tax is commendable. the tax could make a significant contribution to budgets and at the same time to the effort to exit the current recession and could become a disincentive to risky activities and speculation. i regret that the rest of the european union has not joined this initiative for the time being.
in writing. − i support the rapporteur's proposal to set up an expert working group, including representatives of the participating member states, the european commission, esma and the ecb, to properly monitor the way the financial transaction tax is applied in the eu countries, as it will not be applied uniformly in all 27 member states but only in 11. a core collection mechanism is essential, as the existence of weaknesses in a member state would undermine the success of the tax and could even lead to arbitration cases in the tff area.
in writing. - i voted for this report. the commission estimates that the financial transaction tax will bring between €30 and €35 billion to the eu budget, or about 1% of the union's gdp. the daily financial transactions of citizens and businesses will not be affected, with the tax only applying to financial institutions, which account for more than 85% of total transactions. the application of this tax by the 11 member states will lead to more transparency in the exchange of financial information between the participating countries and to a reduction in tax evasion. the financial transaction tax will also help to reduce tax differences due to the different tax systems in each country and thus reduce speculation on financial markets.

the evolution of the economic and financial crisis has unfortunately led to imbalances in the banking system and has had direct and indirect effects on economic developments in the european union. the rapid increase in the complexity of banks' activities before the crisis, and in particular those related to investment, led to a limitation of internal and external control over the organisations. in short, the real value of equity decreased, losses began to emerge and the banks' ability to absorb proved inefficient. all these problems could have been avoided if there had been a system of surveillance at national and european level. that is why, given the key role banks play in financing individuals and businesses, i believe that we urgently need new regulations to strengthen the capacity of the european banking sector to provide quality financial services and support economic development.
in writing. − as the european union's states and societies continue to face the effects of the economic crisis, banking sector reform is becoming an essential tool to prevent future such dynamics. at the same time, it should not be forgotten that the bailout of the banking sector cost european taxpayers no less than eur 1.6 trillion (equivalent to 12.8% of the eu's gross domestic product), costs which in several member states have exacerbated the problem of budget deficits and public expenditure systems. the construction of a european institutional framework is a key task in this context. it must, however, take account of both the imperative of maintaining the single market for goods and services and the specificity and particularity of the banking sectors in the member states. i support the commission's intention to draw up a directive for structural reform of the banking system many of the institutional problems that have been at the root of the crisis require effective and decisive solutions. it is also important to regulate the shadow banking sector in the same spirit.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because five years after the start of the crisis, the european union is still in recession, with consumer confidence in the european banking sector at a worryingly low level. moreover, state-financed bank bailouts have caused a massive increase in public debt in the member states. one of the final goals of structural reform should be to ensure that only essential services such as payment systems and overdraft facilities are provided by the state. these are essential for the proper functioning of the real economy. moreover, the costs of bankruptcy should be borne first by the shareholders, creditors and only then by the state. european taxpayers should not pay for the greed of banking systems. the reform must respect the integrity of the single market and transparency with regard to non-euro area member states.
in writing. − as the banking sector plays a critical role in the real economy, concern for its improvement has spread across the spectrum of society, from citizens to governments, bankers, the business community, experts, global financial management organisations, civil society, the media, etc. better regulation is important to reduce the chances of another major financial crisis, a key factor in restoring confidence in the financial sector. the fact that a country has been exposed to a financial crisis does not reduce the likelihood of being hit by another crisis. it is quite obvious that simply additional legislation is not enough. reducing risk will inevitably require a cultural change in the financial system.
in writing. − the concern of european citizens and their declining confidence in the banking system are understandable in the context of the new european measures to address the financial and banking crisis. it is clear that we need a more ambitious reform to ensure a stable, efficient banking system that can function satisfactorily in a competitive market economy. banks need to review their strategies to serve the interests of customers and consumers and eliminate activities that present excessive risks and have the sole objective of making a profit. in the event of future bank failures, retail customers need to be protected so that they no longer have to bear the burden of the recovery of banking systems. in order to support real economic development, banks must be held accountable when they take excessive risks and therefore retail banking activities such as deposits, bank accounts and loans must be separated from riskier activities such as trading in financial instruments and derivatives. discipline and transparency are essential in resolving this fundamental issue facing the european union at this time as efficiently and quickly as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on structural reform of the eu banking sector. among the most important changes it brings are the reduction of complexity and the limitation of interconnection between commercial and risk investment activities in the banking sector. a few months ago, i asked the commission a question for a written answer on the technical complexity of the financial market. i asked the commission whether a distinction should be made between commercial and investment banks to take account of the particularities of the different types of banking operations. the commission replied that it would 'take a decision on a possible legislative measure in this area in the second half of this year'. i therefore ask that the commission take account of the recommendations of this report when drafting its legislative proposal, in particular as regards the legal separation of financial activities. the union banking system needs to be less complex to serve the needs of the real economy.

in writing. − the economic viability of the european union depends crucially not only on safeguarding the efficiency of resource collection but also on the efficiency with which european funds are spent. the report on the protection of the european union's financial interests continues to be an important tool in this respect for both the european institutions and the member states. however, it is important to stress that, despite its importance, the report makes it difficult to assess the real extent of the problems at this level, as it contains only data reported by member states, which define fraud differently. it is important that national actors and the european institutions adopt a similar regulatory framework, which allows, as european legislation has called for on several occasions, the identification and penalisation of states that do not effectively combat fraud. it is also advisable in this context for the european union to provide additional funds to national law enforcement authorities. the efficiency of the public expenditure system is essential for the european union, both in the current highly restrictive economic context and to ensure the credibility and transparency of the institution among european citizens.
