mr president, naturally spying on one’s allies is not acceptable. however, unveiling such practices precisely at the crucial time of the initiation of talks on establishing a transatlantic free trade zone was done in an attempt to strike a strong blow, both to those talks and to the mutual trust between the two sides of the atlantic. it only benefits our competitors. however, the real problem is that after 9/11, and facilitated by the exponential advance of technology, the genie is out of the bottle. intelligence services have a completely free hand to satisfy their insatiable hunger for more and more data on practically everybody. how does that square with the full respect of people’s democratic freedoms? to those of us from the east this is even more disturbing. we fought to join the west precisely for the respect of those freedoms, not for their disrespect.

union is active in responding to these new threats, and this directive is a step forward. the new directive will harmonise not only the level of penalties but also the definition of criminal offences, on behalf of the alde group. – madam president, i consider that we need a better or real implementation of the council common position (ccp) but only in a manner that is sustainable and good for both the industry and the people that the ccp is supposed to protect. some parts of this initiative and some proposals are realistic in our opinion. we cannot ban weapon production or the sale of weapons, but we need to be able to have guarantees for all member states that no problematic regime, non-state actor or paramilitary group is behind any weapons contract with their country. we should not kill off an important industry for europe and we should not adopt a radical approach. it is important to promote better cooperation on the common position and enable the european defence agency to fully promote its implementation at council level. the problem is to achieve a balance between arms control and preserving and promoting the development and innovation of the european defence industry. the solution for me is the real integration and consolidation of our industry. for now, the compromise that we have reached on the common position is a step forward and we should be realistic before we blindly ask for more.
the arms industry is strategic for the european union and is also a source of substantial revenue for many member states. the union as a whole is in fact the second largest arms exporter globally, after the united states. the strategic nature of the matter is no excuse for lack of transparency. member states shall take into account the common reporting tools for the number of export licences issued in the field as well as the final destination of the exported products. the main problem when we talk about arms exports is the final destination of arms. even if export licenses are issued to certain states, as is known, weapons can be sold to other areas, thus fuelling regional conflicts. we must recognize the risk that arms exported legally from european countries could end up in the hands of authoritarian regimes, regimes that violently repress protests. the same must be said for the risk of corruption, which is unfortunately also inherent in the arms trade. in these circumstances, i would like to welcome the conclusion of the arms trade treaty, which will certainly lead to increased control and improve transparency in this very sensitive area. i am also pleased that 74 countries have already signed the treaty, 26 of which are member states of the union; i hope that the other two countries will follow the example of the member states as soon as possible. the arms trade treaty demonstrates that there is substantial reflection on the problems we have listed here and that important efforts are being made to address them.

member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank honourable members for their continued interest in the european emergency number, 112. the commission is ever vigilant and provides support to member states, as outlined earlier. we will keep the parliament updated as the experts provide us with eu-level solutions for the issues you have raised. allow me to take this opportunity to invite you to continue to encourage member states to ensure that the use of 112 is integrated in their policy and actions.
in writing. 112 is designed to reduce the response and reaction time of emergency services across europe. in addition, people travelling in the european union know that the same emergency number is valid in all countries. i would point out that council decision no 396 of 1991 on the introduction and implementation of the single european emergency number requires member states to ensure the application of the single emergency number procedures and the popularization of the 112 number throughout europe. an example of good practice is in romania. if in 2007 the european commission blamed shortcomings in the implementation of the decision, now, according to the 2013 flash eurobarometer, over 90% of the romanian population knows and uses the 112 number for emergency situations. financial infringement procedures for non-implementation of technical telecommunications directives imposed by the commission on, among others, italy and lithuania, do not solve the problem of the low level of popularity of 112 as a european emergency number. i call on the member states to underline that they have an obligation not only to implement the technical provisions but also to popularise 112 as the single european number so that people can access emergency services as quickly as possible.
in writing. on 12 september 2011, the european parliament adopted written declaration 0035/2011 on the need for a 112 emergency service that is also accessible to people with disabilities. this statement called on the commission to present legislative and standardisation proposals so that 112 services are also accessible to deaf, hearing and speech impaired users, and to propose a service using sign language through video and text-based technologies. unfortunately, the number 112 remains inaccessible to a large proportion of people with disabilities. i ask the commission to make efforts to implement and promote the eu-wide emergency call number. the commission should implement the use of next generation technologies for 112 and mandatory accuracy and reliability criteria for the location of the caller to the emergency services. last but not least, i ask the commission to present an action plan to support member states in their information and public awareness campaigns on the european 112 service.
member of the commission. − madam president, we welcome parliament’s report on connected tv. this timely report addresses a wide range of issues which reflect the complexity of convergence in the audiovisual sector. the commission has itself recently published a green paper on ‘preparing for a fully converged audiovisual world’, which is the basis of an ongoing public consultation. connected tv and the subsequent convergence of ict technologies presents opportunities and challenges which will impact those in the audiovisual sector and the values underpinning this policy area. we will assess mrs kammerevert’s report alongside the expected inputs of the green paper consultation. as stated in your report, we will also be analysing, amongst other things, how convergence will impact the relevance and usefulness of the existing regulatory mechanism. we are therefore looking forward to receiving feedback on this question in the public consultation. with regard to increasing convergence in the audiovisual sector and the impact on the audiovisual media services (avms) directive, we have already encountered a wide range of views. while some point to the need for adjustments, others argue that the directive – which was adopted not so long ago – still works well. the option of self- and co-regulation has also been mentioned. this is why we have included these questions in the green paper. the commission is open-minded regarding the necessity for a review of the avms directive in the follow-up to the green paper consultation. if such a review were to be identified, we would consider this for the future. the consultation is open until the end of august 2013. we look forward to good cooperation with parliament on the preparation of any future audiovisual policy initiatives, be it through legislative action or other measures. the commission’s goal in this area is to ensure economic growth and respect for european values, including the promotion of cultural diversity.

communicate after arrest. i would like to welcome commissioner viviane reding to this debate and thank her for her excellent cooperation in the work on this dossier and for supporting us throughout first two measures of the roadmap for strengthening the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, namely the right to translation and interpretation and the right to information, we are now about to adopt the most important of the regulations of this roadmap. access to an effective defence in criminal proceedings currently varies widely in the member states, depending both on the specific legal system and its practical applicability, which indirectly but significantly influences the union's policy on trust and mutual recognition. despite the existence of common minimum principles and standards, which derive from both the european convention on human rights and the charter of fundamental rights, the provisions governing the assistance provided by a lawyer differ significantly from one state to another. we therefore need legislation to ensure that the rights set out are guaranteed and we need a legal and professional culture to facilitate their exercise. practice shows that there is still a great deal to be done to achieve the effective realisation of procedural rights in criminal matters as an essential element of the right to a fair trial. the directive on the right to be assisted by a lawyer in criminal proceedings and the right to communicate after arrest is therefore an essential step in this direction. in the light of the union's desire to create a single area of justice, freedom and security, citizens must be satisfied that their rights are fully respected, that they are safe when travelling and that they enjoy the same guarantees in all member states. without the appropriate assistance of a lawyer, the effective exercise of other procedural rights may remain only illusory. once this directive is adopted, suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings, wherever they may be in the union, will have access to legal aid from the time they are informed by the competent authorities, by official notification or otherwise, that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence until the conclusion of those proceedings. the directive will be implemented uniformly in all member states, irrespective of the specificity of their legal systems, thus ensuring the same standards in the european union. that is why, in view of the permeability of borders and the freedom of movement within the union, the adoption of this directive is a remarkable achievement, i believe, which will improve the lives of millions of european citizens.
the right to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and immediately after arrest is a vital right in legal systems that ensure fair trials. we're talking about article 6 of the european convention on human rights, which guarantees a fair trial, including the right to a defence. i've won many cases at the echr when that right was violated, and that's why this project is so dear to me. the problem is that the right to a defence must be an effective and real one. for those who cannot afford to pay for a lawyer in a criminal case, the state has an obligation to step in and pay for a lawyer. unfortunately, this report has failed to include and ensure this right to defence for those who lack the financial means. i'd like to encourage by what i say today and pro bono defense. i think it's the duty of law firms, of lawyers to make that contribution to society.

in writing - the rules on property rights for international couples are very complex and very difficult to interpret. there are currently no common rules at european level. the european commission put forward two proposals for spouses and registered partners in may 2011 to alleviate future legal complications in cross-border cases. the proposed regulations set out the courts competent to settle disputes concerning the property consequences of marriage or registered partnership and the applicable substantive rules. i believe that these regulations will ensure the free movement within the european union of judgments, court settlements and all relevant authentic instruments.
650 000 of the approximately 16 million international couples, that is, spouses from different member states, divorce each year in the union. property rights after divorce, but also in the event of death, remain an obstacle in the way of citizens, who waste time and money looking for the applicable legislation and the competent court. the differences in legislation between member states lead to a breach of article 17 of the charter of fundamental rights of the union, which protects common property acquired during marriage. moreover, resorting to the most favorable court, usually in favor of the wealthier party, violates equality before the law and the right to non-discrimination. it is therefore imperative that discrimination be prohibited and the right of access to justice guaranteed. this report will simplify existing conflicts of laws and procedures for citizens by establishing common rules in the property rights regime.

in writing. − the report addresses a very important issue that is directly related to the guarantee of a fundamental human right, the right to defence. in doing so, the assistance of a defendant or accused person by a lawyer is essential, all the more so in situations where the acts under investigation are committed in a vast territory, the european union, where different legal systems, different criminal proceedings, different people coexist. it is essential that the right of defence be exercised and guaranteed in this complicated context. the report sets out specific measures to protect the rights of defence of accused minors, who must at the same time benefit from the general safeguards to safeguard the best interests of the child. however, i note the absence of measures to make this whole system more functional, such as the absence of provisions on cooperation between the bars of the member states to facilitate legal aid, and the need to set up bar associations to deal specifically and ex officio with these situations, many of which concern people who have no material means of hiring a lawyer.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it represents a major step forward towards democratizing access to justice for all our european citizens. the implementation of this directive in the member states will introduce better safeguards for persons in detention. it will guarantee access to a lawyer for anyone detained by the police, under arrest or simply suspected. the text, which was adopted by the european parliament today and is expected to enter into force in 2017, provides that anyone arrested in the eu will have access to a lawyer as soon as possible after being questioned by the police and deprived of liberty. one of the measures in the directive further states that any arrested person has the right to call a relative or another person, such as his employer or a consular authority. although i regret that the issue of free legal aid for people in financial difficulty was not included in the directive, i welcome the adoption of this text, which is an important step towards strengthening and harmonising procedural rights in europe.
mortgage payments amounted to around 52% of the gdp of the european union in 2011, i.e. over eur 6,5 trillion. this is of great economic importance. one of the main causes of the financial crisis was the excessive indebtedness of consumers and the processing of credit applications by banks without a careful check of applicants' income, and this was to the detriment of applicants. for example, in romania, at the end of 2011, 24% of loans were affected by arrears, i.e. 225 000 romanians could no longer pay their loans. i therefore support the imposition of responsible lending practices, the most important of which is the assessment under strict conditions of the consumer's ability to repay the credit. a minimum reflection period of 7 days must also be allowed before the loan is signed, so that the borrower can analyse all market possibilities.
in writing. - mortgages are often the most important and long-term financial commitment a family makes. mortgages are essential to be able to buy a home, almost 70% of properties in the eu are bought in this way. 'mortgage markets are of major importance in the internal market, but are only marginally or not at all integrated. in addition to the general obstacles to cross-border lending (even in the case of consumer credit), such as language barriers, different financial cultures and regional trust relationships, there are other obstacles to mortgage lending, in particular the major differences between member states' land laws, valuation provisions, legal regimes of land and mortgage registers and laws on enforcement.
i voted for this report. recent scandals of manipulation and leakage of information in the financial market have seriously damaged investor confidence. i'm reminded of the case of ian hannam, the former managing director of jp morgan, who illegally exposed the confidential information of clients and resigned after being fined £450,000. i assume mr. hannam has earned far more than the amount of this fine. i therefore call for the immediate opening of negotiations on the market abuse directive, in particular on criminal sanctions for market manipulation. by severely sanctioning misuse of financial information, the integrity of this market and the level of investor protection will be improved. it will also ensure a level playing field for everyone on the market at the same time.
in writing. - building a single market for financial services can help to boost european economies and create new jobs. the adoption of a system of strong and effective regulation will also make a significant contribution to the credibility of the financial system, which has been significantly damaged since the economic and financial crisis. there are several useful regulations at community level, but the pace of technological innovation, as well as the diversity of existing financial services, make it necessary to modernise legislation in this area. it is in the interest of european consumers and economic actors that problems such as insider dealing and market manipulation are prevented and tackled firmly. at the same time, european decision-makers must bear in mind that building a transparent financial system is essential both for the union's economic competitiveness and for the final recipients of financial services.
in writing. - in the current economic context a genuine internal market for financial services is essential for economic growth and job creation in the union. market abuse endangers the integrity of financial markets and public confidence in securities and derivatives. directive 2003/6/ec on market abuse introduced a general framework to combat market abuse. in its current form, the directive allows a latitude that can lead to legal uncertainty and create pretexts for infringements. therefore, i consider that the transformation of the current directive into a regulation is the right way forward to strengthen and update the measures to combat market abuse as it ensures uniform rules and definitions across the eu and ensures uniform implementation of the measures in all member states.
in writing. − i believe that the commission should propose a new and substantially amended draft regulation on the use of technical measures in the baltic sea and the belts and sound.
in writing. - the establishment of a genuine internal energy market is one of the measures which directly contribute to ensuring the union's overall energy security and sustainability. continuing this process must take into account that the accompanying benefits can also be felt at the level of competitiveness of economic actors in the european union. the completion of an internal energy market will not only boost the economic growth of european countries, but can also lead to job creation. i welcome the action and investment plan presented by the commission officials. i am confident that the start of the ambitious investment programme undertaken at this level can lead, in the medium term, to the achievement of real energy independence for the european union by developing its own potential and exploiting indigenous resources. i would also like to draw attention to the imperative of supporting the production of green energy as a decisive step in the fight against climate change by the union and its member states.
in writing. − energy prices will continue to rise as long as europe remains dependent on oil and gas imports and on insufficient investment to maintain and upgrade its energy systems. it is beneficial for europe to continue developing indigenous resources, which will lead to the emergence of new trading centres in the eu and give the union and the member states a real chance to set their own energy prices, including at regional and local level.
in writing. - i voted for the buzek report because it represents a step forward towards completing the single energy market. the report stresses the need to meet the commitments to achieve a single energy market by 2014 through better coordination of energy policies and cooperation between member states. for the moment, the eu's powers are limited, based on the principle of subsidiarity, with member states deciding how they use their energy resources and which sources they use. each government negotiates import contracts individually. some countries pay more, some countries pay less. one measure could be to centrise supply, by negotiating contracts at community level, for example for imported gas. the internal market for energy and gas should be fully operational by next year. it is estimated that without the single market, by 2035 the price of energy in europe would be 50% higher than in the us and 300% higher than in china. for consumers, the single market will mean more transparency in their energy bills and more choice. according to the commission, households could save up to €13 billion per year by switching to the cheapest supplier. for industry, the internal market will be an incentive not to leave europe, energy security will increase and costs will fall.
the european union imports more than 50% of its energy needs, which makes us dependent on relations with external partners and vulnerable to pressure from russia. in this context, diversification of energy sources is essential to maintain our independence in a future marked by energy crises. romania can become the largest wind energy producer in southern europe. romania's wind potential is 14,000 megawatts, the second largest in europe, and many investors have entered this market. a clear long-term strategy is needed and the difficulties faced by foreign investors in exploiting green energy must be removed. the government must also take measures to prevent possible imbalances in energy production and consumption. in addition, romania needs to reduce all obstacles to the way green certificates are managed and awarded.
in writing. - increasing the eu's energy efficiency is creating the conditions not only for a resumption of economic growth but also for the creation of new jobs, at a time when unemployment, especially among young people, has reached critical levels. at the same time, the european union must remain the leading global actor in the fight against climate change, driving global governance by example. in these circumstances, i support the conclusion of the report, which shows that investments in this area, as well as the allocation of european funds, are not expenditure but investments capable of reviving whole sectors of european economies and creating jobs. combining energy efficiency objectives with cohesion policies thus leads to both achieving the objectives set by the european states in the europe 2020 strategy and strengthening the bonds of solidarity within the union.
in writing. − at european level there is a large percentage of the real estate stock that is ageing. whether public or private, many of these properties have reached the end of their natural 40-year renovation cycle. they urgently need to adapt to new energy saving requirements and the european structural and investment funds play a crucial role in providing the necessary funding. on the other hand, there are rural and remote areas with ideal conditions for the development of efficient forms of decentralised energy production, which would result in significant reductions in energy losses associated with the transport of electricity over long distances. i believe that member states should make the greatest possible use of national and regional programmes for the design and construction of new energy-efficient buildings, but also for the phased upgrading of existing buildings to be energy-efficient, including buildings for low-income households.
in writing. − the new cohesion policy, which will come into force with the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, sets important objectives for both the member states and the regions, which will also benefit from significant european funding for the next seven years. in this context, we must not forget the european approach, which wants a europe at one speed and which is able to face efficiently the challenges that the future holds. in this sense, the reduction of energy waste and the use of alternative and/or renewable sources will have to find new impetus and not lose sight of the important objectives set. to achieve this, it is important that the activities are coordinated at european, national and regional level.
in writing. − cohesion policy is not only an essential tool for regional development, but also for ensuring the prosperity of the union as a whole. any political, economic and social entity is only as strong as the weakest link in the chain of the engine that runs it. at present, the energy efficiency of the european union is less than 50% of optimum capacity, which, at least mathematically, puts us on the mediocrity line. i encourage the report's initiatives to support the union 2020 commitment to impose a 20% energy efficiency strategy. thus, the effect of boosting energy productivity will be to reduce unemployment, help reduce budgetary expenditure in this sector and improve energy standards and networks in regional areas with socio-economic difficulties.
in writing. - the role of cohesion policy is to reduce economic, social and territorial disparities at union level. regions should prioritise their specific development objectives by identifying and developing their own energy efficiency measures according to their potential. academic research confirms that three years ago, 9% of european citizens were facing energy poverty. reducing the vulnerability of energy consumers can be achieved through investments in improving local energy generation capacity. currently, local and regional authorities have limited powers and responsibilities in terms of access to and use of energy resources. overcoming barriers to access to finance can be achieved by facilitating the use of innovative financial instruments and by removing budgetary constraints. a clear synergy between national energy efficiency targets and operational programmes is needed to ensure coherence in future partnership agreements. in romania, the change of the rules during the game in the case of green certificates for renewable energy production created imbalances and uncertainties. i support this report because i believe it is necessary to use the structural funds to finance sustainable energy projects and to attract private capital investment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and particularly welcome the approval of paragraphs 17 and 18, the text of which i proposed in the form of amendments during the committee debate. these points refer to the need for simple, unbureaucratic formalities for the use of funds intended for energy efficiency improvements in housing, and to the direct access of municipalities to these funds, within a decentralised system. implementation of these suggestions would lead to more efficient management of the funds available. i therefore hope that the member states will take account of the european parliament's suggestions in the interests of the citizens.
in writing. - any strategic vision for fisheries must take into account the importance of crossborder cooperation for the development of this economic sector and for the sustainable conservation of natural resources. the economic development of this sector is important for member states and job creation is a priority in the current socio-economic circumstances. the regional strategy must not ignore the danger of pollution the high number of endemic species in these areas, as well as the proximity of human settlements, are factors that must be taken into account by european decision-makers and economic actors. last but not least, it is extremely important that policy papers contain precise and effective provisions for the protection of water resources and the conservation of the hydrosphere.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report. in this context, i should mention that there are a number of similarities between fishing in the adriatic and ionian seas and fishing in the black sea, namely that the management of maritime activities and common resources is shared with several third countries. i would like to reiterate the need for a better coordinated and more intensive dialogue between the eu and its neighbours in the fisheries sector, and for the establishment of a separate body for the management of fisheries in the black sea.
mr president, we pay too much for interpretation. multilingualism is a principle of the union but its cost has become excessive. with 24 official languages, the european parliament’s interpretation services have to cover a total of 552 language combinations. in 2011, parliament spent nearly eur 57 million on interpretation services. the fact that for 2014 parliament plans to reduce interpretation expenditure by 23% compared with 2013 is encouraging, but it is not enough. for instance, interpretation should be done only on demand and unnecessary interpretation should be cancelled in due time to avoid situations in which there is interpretation, we pay for it, but no one uses it. i would also like to express my regret that the plenary adopted the amendment by the socialists, which would not help save taxpayers’ money in this area of interpretation.
in writing. - it is important that any initiative taken in this area contributes to the most effective implementation of the fundamental principle of the european institutions - multilingualism. the european parliament is par excellence an institution that must represent the diversity of ideas and identities in european society. moreover, multilingualism ensures that citizens and european legislators can communicate effectively and directly. at the same time, however, the european parliament must also take account of the financial constraints imposed by the current economic situation and the budgetary planning of the european union. reducing the costs of operating european legislation, including interpretation and translation, should not, however, affect the proper functioning of the institution and its relationship with citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the regulation of the online gambling market is a particularly sensitive subject. this is a specific economic activity and therefore the normal internal market rules should not apply to it. european citizens should be better protected against the serious risks of addiction linked to the development of these online games of chance. it appears that the development of such a consumer protection policy has so far been better executed at national rather than european level. that is why i support and encourage, as does the socialist and democratic group, the development of cooperation and coordination in this sector between the member states of the european union. in fact, despite our ambition to harmonise the online gaming market at european level, it seems that it is still too early to build a true pan-european online gaming market, because of the risk that the most vulnerable european consumers would face in the face of the risks of addiction.
in writing. - the practice of gambling, particularly online gambling, is now increasingly widespread and requires specific intervention by the legislator to counteract the negative effects of possible abuse and illegal gambling. the aim of the report is to regulate online gambling in the internal market and, specifically, to guarantee the rights of consumers in order to protect them more and more against any unfair practices. i would also like to add that i am firmly convinced of the need to carry out adequate information campaigns to raise public awareness of this sensitive issue and thus actively contribute to the action to combat the spread of the phenomenon.
in writing. − the growth rate of online gambling is 40% from 2011 to 2015, according to the commission's estimate. therefore, we need legislation to protect consumers who bet online. addiction and pathological gambling disorders are just two of the risks. another important aspect of gambling is fraud and money laundering. we must fight these criminal organizations and confiscate the proceeds of crime, even in the absence of a criminal conviction. i therefore call on member states to pay particular attention to online gambling and to increase cooperation between gambling regulators and consumer organisations.
madam president, the report we are debating today is tackling the most important problem confronting europe today. youth unemployment is a pan-european disease that destroys the social fabric and threatens the future development of our societies. the report stresses the importance of education as a key to delivering a generation of employable young people. i think this is undeniable, but not enough. youth unemployment says something about the strength of our economy, so if one wants to deal with this issue, one needs to create a better economic environment. yes, there is a need for better convergence of school curricula and ground realities. yes, early school leaving should be discouraged and, yes, we should encourage a mentality based on continuous learning. however, none of these will work in a frozen economic environment. a famous economist once remarked that in the long run we are all dead. it could also be said that in the long run we are all wiser and better educated. but what about today? because we have to do something about youth unemployment today. job creation only comes when the potential of the private sector is released. this can be achieved by courageous fiscal incentives, and particularly by cutting down the bureaucracy that hinders the creation and development of smes. i think this is a good report and i also think this is only the first step.
i want to see youth-led organisations, youth-led organisations, mobilized to address youth unemployment and build pathways to recovery. i'm trying to support a charity like this myself. every summer, in four countries, we teach entrepreneurship to high school students. the active participation of young people in society, especially when combined with prior experience abroad, is one of the conditions for a dynamic labour market. secondly, one of the key factors in the functioning and effectiveness of the european union (eu) is the capacity to learn, to be open to each other's achievements and to adapt. analysing the activities of regions with low youth unemployment and highlighting good practices in regions with high unemployment. thirdly, young workers should be informed by all possible means of the opportunities for traineeships and jobs in their region. it is in the eu's interest to make efforts to ensure that young people are properly remunerated for their skills, so that young professionals do not increase the competitiveness of other regions and countries.
i would like to draw attention to the serious problem of unemployment among young people in rural areas, a subject which is unfortunately not reflected in the motion for a resolution. in romania, the member state i represent, 6 out of 10 young people over 19 in rural areas have never had a job. very seriously, only 5% of rural youth have an income from agricultural work. i believe that, in these circumstances, the member states have an obligation to make the most of the possibilities offered by the european agricultural policy to support the establishment of young farmers. under the reform currently under discussion, the funds for them would increase from eur 40 000 to eur 70 000, along with other financial incentives. member states should also make the most of the possibilities for european funding for the creation of small businesses and new jobs in rural areas. i believe that the potential of agriculture to attract young people from urban areas, even the most qualified, who want to orient themselves towards agricultural work should not be overlooked.
in a europe that is failing to find the most effective solutions to overcome the crisis, with factories closing every month or relocating outside the union, choosing a profession or field of activity is becoming increasingly difficult not only for young people but also for parents and teachers who need to guide them in identifying the field that best suits their skills. the problem of youth unemployment is made all the more difficult by the growing number of those who drop out of school before obtaining a qualification or a diploma. the flip side of this is the problem of 'smart wasting', where highly skilled young people work far below their potential, which has negative effects on them, socially and psychologically. i believe that it would be beneficial to work more closely not only with the commission but also with the member states to implement instruments which have been tested in other member states for reducing youth unemployment and for improving youth mobility, especially as there are over a million vacant jobs in the european union that are not being filled because there are no people interested in those regions.
in writing. at european level, the unemployment rate has reached 23% and in crisis-affected countries (greece and spain) 55%, with the chances of an unemployed young person finding a job being low. through a series of actions, such as the employment package (including the youth guarantee), the eu is seeking to increase the employment rate of young people. the youth guarantee facility is a commitment by member states that, within 4 months of becoming unemployed or leaving formal education, young people under 25 will receive a good quality offer of employment, further education, apprenticeship or traineeship. the scheme was approved by eu ministers in april 2013 and is due to be implemented from january 2014. eu regions with a youth unemployment rate of over 25% are targeted , with three regions in romania where the youth unemployment rate exceeds 30%: centre, south east and south mountain. this initiative has been allocated eur 6 billion of european funds for the first two years of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020.
mr president, the truth about cybersecurity is that we are always one step behind technology and its users. it is time now to adapt and we must do so quickly. the most important thing is to be balanced. we need secure cyberspace, with rules and a degree of control, but we need also to protect openness and the free flow of information and communication. some member states understand cybersecurity only as the prosecution of hackers, but it is much more than that. it is the regulation of an ever-changing environment. we need to identify its vulnerability – on the one hand financial and in terms of infrastructure systems and, on the other, in terms of vulnerable users, such as children, who need to be protected. but we also need to draw the line there. we also need to change our mindset and to have the issue of cybersecurity in every single document we publish or work with. we need the member states to adopt national cyber-defence strategies. there is a lot of pressure involved in this but we must continue.
europe has been through a difficult time. the financial crisis has generated an economic crisis and created major problems in most member states. the commission has reacted and proposed the necessary legislation to prevent similar situations and to create the possibility of redress. the european parliament has supported these proposals, often against the council's position, and as a result we now have strong legislation that needs to be implemented. governments, under internal pressure, have often used populist measures. the austerity-development-jobs debate has led to the rise of populism. the commission now has two mechanisms at its disposal to encourage member states to take the necessary measures for development and jobs: the european semester and the partnership agreement. the european semester can steer national budgets towards a policy of wise spending and investment for development and jobs. the partnership agreement should create synergy between national budgets and european funds. member states need to develop clear strategies on development directions and priorities to make the most of this synergy. i believe that the commission has a very important role to play in the period ahead and should not hesitate to take all the necessary decisions, irrespective of the member state concerned, to implement these mechanisms which can redress the current situation and generate economic growth and stability throughout the union.
in writing. the debate on the state of the union is, unfortunately, the balance sheet of a lost fifth of a century for citizens and for the european project. the austerity imposed by the popular vote has increased unemployment, poverty and euroscepticism. at the same time, the step towards what we call 'more europe' has not been taken. the barroso commission lacked the vision and courage to push the european construction forward. there are initiatives such as the 'banking union' and the 'youth guarantee' that are stuck in a bureaucratic process that needs to be accelerated. in this respect, there are significant efforts by parliament to boost cooperation and transparency in decision-making, such as the agreement between the european parliament and the european central bank on the single banking supervisory mechanism and the interparliamentary agreement on the eu budget for the financial year 2014-2020. unfortunately, the council is still trying to downplay parliament's legislative role and the importance it attaches to growth and employment. although austerity has disappeared from the vocabulary of the european people, it is a reality at union level, reflected in the council's perception of the european budget for the next seven years. it is unacceptable to cut, at the last minute, by one billion euros the budgets allocated to job creation for young people and innovation.
in writing. the state of the union must be seen through the eyes of the 500 million european citizens and their confidence in their own future. the employment rate is only 68.4%, research and development spending is only 2.02% of gross domestic product (gdp), 12.8% of the 18-24 age group have left school early and 119.8 million european citizens are at the poverty line or social exclusion. the state of the union cannot improve without investing in education and health, in decent jobs and in a decent pension. the eu needs to develop an industrial policy capable of rebuilding european industry in an eco-efficient manner. the eu's industrial development must be accompanied by measures to finance the european economy, so as to ensure both jobs in the eu and the eu's global competitiveness. it is unacceptable that today there are still barriers to the free movement of workers and that member states are faced with a regression from the social model on which the union was built. the union must defend the european social model, increase the competitiveness of industry in all member states and safeguard jobs throughout the union.
in writing. − linguistic and cultural diversity is one of the fundamental principles of the european union, enshrined in article 22 of the charter of fundamental rights: 'the union shall respect cultural, religious and linguistic diversity'. since the death of the last speaker of a language is usually tantamount to the disappearance of that language, i believe that local authorities in particular must take remedial measures to this end, which can change this situation.
in writing. the language used by a given people is probably the most obvious and clear form of cultural identity. within the european union, where linguistic diversity is a fundamental principle, many languages are in danger of extinction. linguistic diversity enables european states to know and understand the cultural and social differences that coexist within the union, and the possible loss of these sources of tradition would undoubtedly damage the rich cultural and linguistic heritage of the european union. that is why i voted in favour of taking a step forward in the defence and promotion of all those languages which are in danger of disappearing, by implementing policies to revive them within the linguistic communities concerned and by allocating a sufficient budget to this end.
in writing. - i am in favour of protecting the unique diversity of the linguistic and cultural heritage of the european union. moreover, i draw attention to the romanian model, an example appreciated by colleagues in this forum, even in their interventions in plenary. i believe that the eu must adapt its joint programmes to support languages that are truly endangered. to do this, we have a multitude of financial instruments at our disposal: the programmes on documentation of these languages, for education and training, social inclusion, youth and sport, research and development, the culture and media programme or the structural funds. i stress the importance of new technologies and social communication platforms, which bring about changes in the paradigm of communication. learning at least two languages from an early age facilitates later learning and others, which supports the global and mobile society in which we live. i also support the intensification of the process of standardising languages which are predominantly oral in nature, which would subsequently help in the process of teaching that language. i also wholeheartedly support the protection of the linguistic heritage in the countries neighbouring the union, all the more so as these countries have expressed their option for a future within the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report. i would also like to point out that the european union should be equally concerned about endangered languages or dialects in the countries neighbouring the union, as exemplified by the different dialects of the romanian language still spoken by communities in countries such as serbia. the parliament should also not passively witness the attacks against the romanian language in the provinces of the republic of moldova or in ukraine.
in writing. − the cultural heritage of linguistic diversity is the key to the eu's unity in respect for tradition. the ep has committed itself by voting on the own-initiative report, as over the last 10 years, despite repeated warnings from experts and the strong demands of europe's indigenous minority and regional communities, it has failed to take a stand on behalf of the institution to ensure their adequate protection. 10-12% of the eu's total population speak an indigenous, minority or regional language. the sheer size of this population compels us to act. member states that have not yet ratified the 1992 european charter for regional or minority languages and the 1995 framework convention for the protection of national minorities should do so as soon as possible. i welcome the fact that the document although not legally binding calls on the governments of the member states to condemn all practices that are directed or directed against the identity and language use of endangered linguistic communities or against their cultural institutions through linguistic discrimination or forced/hidden assimilation. the report is relevant to the hungarian language and, importantly for the hungarian-speaking community in the union, states that the commission must be aware that the survival of languages within its borders is threatened by the policies of some member states and regions, even if these languages are not threatened at european level. you are protected by the status of an official language in a member state.
in writing. − i welcome the overwhelming majority recorded at the vote on the alfonsi report on endangered european languages and linguistic diversity in the eu. this is a strong endorsement given by all the political groups of the ep and a strong message to the european commission and the member states. the diversity of languages and cultures in europe is nothing less than the living heritage which secures the sustainable development of european societies. i fully share the view that ‘teaching in people’s mother tongue is the most effective way of learning’ and i urge member states to implement this principle in their education policies. the ec’s multilingualism policy has to be revitalised and properly funded in the next mff. the new policy actions have to take into consideration the proposals formulated by the minority intergroup of the ep. fully-respected linguistic diversity is a vital contribution to european soft power, enabling the eu to enforce its global significance. this house recently debated the cost-effectiveness of interpretation at the ep. while i support the sound financial management principles, i urge all of us to bear in mind that full multilingualism strengthens democracy in our parliament.
in writing. − today we adopted the regulation that the executive directors of the european environment agency will have to be heard by the european parliament before being appointed. this is a request i made in my capacity as rapporteur for the 2010 discharge of the european environment agency. today, my request has been granted and thus my goal has been achieved. i welcome the fact that the european environment agency is now aligned with the european food safety authority, the european medicines agency and the european chemicals agency. we must not stop there, but make it compulsory for all eu agencies to hold these hearings before appointing candidates to the post of executive director. however, i regret that under article 1 of the amended regulation the hearing will only take place before the committee on the environment, public health and food safety. in my opinion, this is not enough. the hearing should also take place before the committee on budgetary control. the members of the budget control committee will be going to these hearings anyway. an executive director must demonstrate managerial experience and knowledge, including in the field of public procurement. let's not repeat the mistakes of the past.
in writing. − private and public buildings, water supply and waste water disposal infrastructure, as well as businesses and agricultural land and forests were affected by flooding in large areas of the sava, kupa, mura and drava river basins in slovenia and the mura, drava and lavant river basins in austria, as well as on the territory of croatia, in 2012. as such, it is useful to mobilise the solidarity fund to support the efforts of local and regional authorities and private individuals and companies to remedy the effects of these floods, to show solidarity with all citizens affected by natural disasters.
in writing. − the use of biofuels has been steadily increasing over the last decade as a result of the eu's policy to limit the environmental impact of transport and reduce europe's dependence on petroleum-based fuels. the european parliament recognised the importance of promoting renewable energy. directive 2009/28/ec on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources and directive 98/70/ec on the quality of petrol and diesel are aimed at combating climate change and reducing the eu's dependence on external energy sources. however, the main purpose of the two directives is in danger of being undermined by the effect of indirect land-use change, which may offset the greenhouse gas emission savings of individual biofuels compared to the fossil fuels they replace. scientific work shows that indirect land-use change emissions can vary substantially from one commodity to another in relation to the fossil fuels they replace and that greenhouse gas emissions related to indirect land-use change are significant and could offset, in whole or in part, the greenhouse gas reductions from individual biofuels.
in writing. − the development of the first generation biofuel industry has now led to the sacrifice of agricultural land for food. at the same time, the multiplication of greenhouse gas emissions from the increasing use of agricultural land for biofuel production negates many of the benefits of biofuels. this is a clear signal that attention and efforts should be focused on advanced biofuels. i therefore welcome the european parliament's vote in favour of limiting the use of traditional biofuels and moving more quickly to advanced biofuels from alternative sources such as seaweed and waste. the european parliament adopted a resolution on the eu's future energy policy, which aims to limit first-generation biofuels, i.e. those derived from agricultural crops, to 6% of final energy consumption in the transport sector by 2020, as opposed to the 10% target in existing legislation. advanced biofuels, generated from seaweed or waste, will need to account for at least 2.5% of energy consumption in the transport sector. the legislative proposal has important economic and ethical implications and is essential for the integrity of the eu's climate change policy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft fuel quality directive and the renewable energy directive which the socialist and democratic group sought to adapt in order to respond more effectively to the environmental and food challenges ahead. the production of biofuels from food crops contributes to price volatility, which is why the increasing demand for biofuels in the european union has a negative impact, in particular, on the access to food of certain populations. this is a very worrying situation. it is essential that people living in poverty do not suffer from food shortages due to the proliferation of policies that give priority to the production of biofuels. according to the oecd and fao, the price of basic foodstuffs is likely to continue to increase between 2015 and 2019, by at least 27% for wheat, 48% for maize and 36% for oilseeds, compared to the levels of 1998 to 2002. the potential impact of biofuel production on the prices of food raw materials should therefore be given greater consideration by the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of a balanced approach to the food and fuel production dispute. i think this issue needs to be looked at with caution. the potential influences of crop plants for biofuels on food prices cannot be overlooked. at the same time, these crops play an important role in covering the proteinase deficit at eu level, which is of concern. my position was 'for' the final vote, to open the possibility of a second reading, where the excesses of the text could be eliminated.
in writing. − i supported the limit on the contribution of biofuels to renewable energy targets because of several major concerns about the unintended effects of biofuel production. we must not allow biofuel policy to cause the destruction of carbon sinks such as forests and wetlands, as this would only serve to undermine the co2 reductions which biofuels were intended to achieve.
in writing. - there is only one stock of european eel. i believe that a regulation is needed to put restocking in the right context, giving priority to the choice of spawning sites and to a correct assessment of the likelihood that restocked eels under 20 cm in length will reach sexual maturity.
in writing. − the customs union is an essential element for the functioning of the single market, which can only function properly through the uniform and consistent application of common and modern customs rules and systems. in order to support a dynamic environment for competitiveness and economic growth, while ensuring appropriate uniform levels of control of goods, i believe that modern and simple customs rules, based on state-of-the-art systems and allowing for the harmonisation of controls so that the economic operator is required to provide information only once, should be promoted.
in writing. − i believe that the further modernisation of the union's customs legislation should take due account of the views of economic operators in order to ensure effective administrative simplification.
in writing. − the farm accountancy information network was set up in 1965 to meet some of the requirements of the common agricultural policy, in particular those relating to income certification and the analysis of the economic activity of agricultural holdings. over time, it has evolved and the network has expanded to all member states. it is currently the only harmonised database containing microeconomic data, stating that the approach is the same in all member states. i consider it an important tool for framing and evaluating agricultural policies, as it collects data on income, inputs and outputs from a sample of farms representative of the eu each year.
in writing. − i consider it beneficial to extend the agricultural accounting information network on income certification to all member states, as this is the only harmonised database containing microeconomic data, but also that the data are public and can be consulted by any citizen of the union.
in writing. − the approach taken to the recent amendment of the fruit juice directive (directive 2012/12/eu), where the annex containing product names, definitions and characteristics was excluded from the scope of the delegation. i consider that such essential elements should not be amended by means of delegated acts.
in writing. − i voted to postpone the decision on the revision of the environmental impact assessment directive. i believe that such a decision cannot be taken without a thorough debate, which clarifies the commission's proposals and allows members to explain their views expressed in amendments.
in writing. i voted in favour of signing this agreement as it is an important step towards opening up european visa policy. in the context of the special partnership between the european union and cape verde, the union has undertaken a policy aimed in particular at promoting good governance, security and stability, sustainable development and the fight against poverty. cape verde is a democratic and stable country, which upholds the values and principles of democracy, respect for human rights and the rule of law. the high standards and practices of governance that the country can boast of give every reason to further develop its relations with the union. the agreement on the facilitation of the issuance of short-stay visas should contribute to achieving these objectives. it will facilitate, on a reciprocal basis, the issuing of visas to citizens of cape verde and of the union for intended stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. the agreement also implies the introduction of simplified conditions for the issuing of multiple-entry visas with a validity of 5 years.
in writing. - the impact of the crisis on young people should be tackled much more effectively, as youth unemployment has risen to unacceptable levels, especially in the south of the eu: for example in greece (59.1% in january 2013), spain (55.9%), italy (38.4%) and portugal (38.3%). member states should make full use of available eu funds and make full use of the options for finding viable solutions offered by the youth opportunities initiative for the benefit of young people who are not in employment, education or training. the eu youth strategy should help vulnerable young people by focusing on the overall participation of young people in civil society and mitigating the consequences of the current crisis on social inclusion and its effects on the health and well-being of young people. member states and the commission should focus more on developing cross-sectoral cooperation, with a particular focus on examining how approaches and methods of youth policy and youth activities can be used in other relevant sectors. at the same time, efforts in the field of employment and entrepreneurship should be encouraged, facilitating access to jobs and developing the innovative and creative capacities of young people.
in writing. i voted in favour of the conclusion of this agreement on the readmission of irregular residents which accompanies the signing of an agreement on visa facilitation between cape verde and the european union. the two agreements are interdependent and parallel and must enter into force simultaneously. they represent an important step in the relations between the union and the republic of cape verde. these are the first agreements between an acp country and the european union on short-stay visas and the readmission of irregular residents. these two agreements are of great political importance and represent an encouraging step forward and a strong signal from the union. cape verde is a stable and democratic country which upholds the values and principles of democracy, respect for human rights and the rule of law. the high standards and practices of governance that the country can boast of give every reason to continue developing its relations with the european union. the agreement on the readmission of persons residing without authorisation, which will operate on a basis of full reciprocity, will contribute fully to the achievement of these objectives.
in writing. − the report on the implementation of the eu youth strategy 2010-2012 proposes appropriate solutions to the most pressing issues facing the young generation today in the fields of education, employment, social inclusion and health. i welcome the fact that this report clarifies the issues that have not been addressed so far by the current eu youth strategy, and suggests ways to improve member states' own policies so that they achieve the best possible results and achieve the objectives of the future strategy. the european union must put in place tools, policies and mechanisms to respond to the challenges facing the young generation today and to offer them better opportunities for their lives.
in writing. − youth unemployment is a difficult problem, especially for those who leave school before obtaining a qualification or diploma, and their numbers are increasing. we must not forget the category of young people who 'waste their intelligence'. these are highly skilled young people working far below their potential, which has negative effects on them, socially and psychologically. i believe that it would be beneficial to work more closely together between member states to improve the mobility of young people, given that there are over a million vacant jobs in the european union that are not being filled because there are no people interested in those regions.
in writing. − the year 2013 has been declared the european year of citizens. we need to involve better young people, to give them a chance, to share their vision of the european union. this report identifies the problems of european youth suffer, such as unemployment, school dropouts, no access to education, health problems, etc. it also focuses on solutions such as the implementation of the youth guarantee, involving young people in policymaking and their active participation in society, increased investment in education training and youth work. in this difficult period, the eu should work on providing more opportunities in education and training, supporting youth initiatives, funding education programmes and employment initiatives. this has a very important effect on growth in europe.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis that has hit the union has led to an increase in unemployment among young people, with a negative impact on their well-being. the economic difficulties experienced by the union have increased the inability to employ young people and to disengage those already in the labour market. the youth strategy 2010-2012 was a good first step, improving young people's access to the labour market, education and training, but at the same time it is regrettable that some member states have not adopted any specific youth strategy. the european union has had nothing to lose from the lack of opportunities that young people have faced, which is why i believe that the budget for funding in the field of youth and education should be increased in order to effectively implement the union's strategy further. it is also important to introduce traineeships as part of vocational or university training to ease the transition from education to work.
in writing. - i voted for the papanikolau report because it sets out a framework for cooperation on tackling the problems of young people in the next decade and finding new opportunities for them. as the commission has proposed for the youth strategy, it will continue to focus on young people not in employment, education or training by encouraging the full use of european funds. we need to strengthen the policies undertaken by member states so that they achieve the objectives, but also the best possible results. the eu has called on member states to implement the youth guarantee as soon as possible and on those with regions with unemployment above 25% (including romania) to adopt a youth guarantee implementation plan by the end of 2013. the commission has sent country-specific recommendations to each member state. romania should therefore implement without delay the national plan for youth employment, introduce reforms in vocational education and training, align tertiary education with labour market needs and improve access for disadvantaged people; implement a national strategy to combat school dropout, with a focus on access to quality education, including for roma citizens.
in writing. - it is a well-known fact that unemployment among young europeans has reached unprecedented levels, reaching 59% in the case of greece. as we deplore the demographic crisis and its medium- and long-term impact on the pension system, a big question mark arises: why is the union trying to bring in labour from third countries when more than half of young people in some member states are unemployed? the phenomenon is that the qualifications of these young people do not match the requirements of the labour market, but are also overqualified in many cases, indicating a structural problem in european education. i would remind european decision-makers of the model of countries such as the united states, which have invested in education and training, investing considerable sums, even in budgetary constraints. i also draw attention to a worrying phenomenon that unfortunately occurs in eu countries: companies recruit young people for a trial period, and then after 3 months, when they should have hired them, they decide to terminate the contract. this can change if we make education and training strategic sectors, learning from countries like germany and austria, where youth unemployment is only 9%.
in writing. − young people are currently facing a very difficult labour market situation which requires decisive intervention and financial resources for appropriate investment. the unemployment rate among young people under 25 in the euro area has risen by around 50% over the past five years, from around 16% in 2008 to 23.9% in may this year, twice as high as among the working-age population. the effective improvement of the situation of young people depends both on state support and on enhanced cooperation between employment services, vocational guidance services, vocational training institutions and youth support services. actions to combat youth unemployment must be coordinated with those to stimulate economic recovery and reform employment policies.
in writing. − young people in the eu member states are currently facing a very difficult situation in the labour market. the unemployment rate among the working age population is 11%, while among young people it is twice as high (23%). the economic crisis that has affected and still affects eu countries to a greater or lesser extent has brought with it the cessation of new job creation and, more seriously, a reduction of jobs, as a result of the tendency of employers to save. i therefore believe that action to combat youth unemployment must be coordinated with action to stimulate the general economic recovery and reform labour policies. initiatives to promote entrepreneurship and to preserve as many existing jobs as possible are needed, and at the same time measures should be taken to encourage entrepreneurs to create new jobs.
in writing. - currently, young people are the most disadvantaged during the economic crisis, more than other vulnerable groups, and for many of them, current unemployment will most likely turn into long-term unemployment, with the risk of social exclusion. member states should develop a more specific approach, combining interventionist measures to combat early school leaving and the reintegration of young people who drop out of school with measures to ensure a smooth transition from education to employment and to increase the employment opportunities of young people. modernising education is necessary by making education policy a fundamental instrument for investing in the future of young people, by adapting the school curriculum to current and future labour market requirements. thus, a personalised career guidance system, which should be available from secondary education, would be useful in addition to a system of monitoring future job supply to ensure subsequent integration into the labour market. also, because of the impossibility of finding a job, many young people have been doing paid internships even up to 1 and a half years. it is important that training periods are recognised as seniority in the field of work.
in writing. − member states and the eu must continue programmes to support actions aimed at developing entrepreneurial and independent initiatives and individual talents of young people, to encourage and teach them how to set up their own business and where to seek help with administrative matters. as such, i consider it useful to promote a system of preferential conditions and benefits, in the form of tax exemptions or relaxations, which should encourage them in this direction.
in writing. this own-initiative report of the european parliament aims to respond to one of the greatest contemporary economic and social challenges for the european union. that's why i'm supporting it. youth unemployment is reaching dramatic levels across the union and should be placed at the top of the priorities of the european institutions. that is why i believe that this report is an important step in the fight against this problem. it is also a strong message to the council, the commission and the member states, stressing that all those involved in this matter must take responsibility and deploy all the necessary tools to do so. this action should include both educational institutions, enterprises and social partners at regional and national level, as well as other actors involved in this cause, such as youth organisations. jobs reserved for young people, apprenticeships and traineeships should meet a number of standards, in particular as regards salary guarantees. finally, the report makes it clear that austerity is not the way forward because it has contributed to the economic and social weakening of young people and to the increase in unemployment.
in writing. − youth unemployment is one of the biggest challenges facing europe today. member states and the commission need to provide far more money to fight youth unemployment. there is a link between austerity, endorsed by the right-wing governments, and youth unemployment and this report acknowledges that fact. the report identifies the major problems and focuses on several solutions. the report stresses that the involvement of all relevant stakeholders, at local, regional, national and european levels, and in particular student and youth organisations too, is essential for the successful implementation and monitoring of a variety of measures to foster youth employment. the report highlights the importance of education, youth programmes, self-employment, etc. in one of its main points the report mentions that the commission and the member states should support young entrepreneurs and young self-employed people by facilitating and simplifying access to finance, reducing administrative burdens and creating overall preferential conditions, which should include efficient counselling and mentoring and providing business incubators. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, but i consider it incomplete because it does not address the issue of rural unemployment. the proposed solutions also fail to mention the important contribution that european agricultural policies can make to job creation, in particular by supporting the establishment of young farmers and by financing small enterprises.
in writing. − supporting the tertiary sector at european level is of the utmost importance for the economic development of the european union. the services sector currently accounts for more than 65% of the union's gdp and provides a significant number of jobs in the member states. it remains the central element of the common market, ensures the continuation of the integration process and is the most important link between european societies and states. there is still a major potential for supporting growth and job creation in the services sector. at a time when the global competitiveness of european players is essential for economic success, the removal of unjustified restrictions on the services sector could lead to a 2.6% increase in union gdp over the medium term.
in writing. − the services sector accounts for more than 65% of eu gdp and is a dynamic, modern and future-oriented element of the european economy. various innovative ways of delivering services are constantly being developed. for all these reasons, a better functioning internal market for services is the cornerstone of a more competitive european economy as a whole. this resolution aims to confront member states with their responsibilities for the full and correct application of the services directive, in its letter and spirit. the economic crisis has made it even more urgent to act to unlock the full potential of the services sector for growth and jobs.
in writing. − the services sector in the european union is estimated at over 65% of eu gdp and is undoubtedly the future of the european economy. member states should have transposed directive 2006/123/ec on services by december 2009. however, 3 years later, implementation is far from satisfactory. this hinders member states from achieving optimal economic growth. member states must do everything possible to establish once and for all the functioning of the single market for businesses and consumers. i also voted in favour of the report on the internal market for services because it takes into account the measures needed to promote better enforcement and to strengthen transparency and accountability. all stakeholders, including national parliaments, the business community and the social partners need to join forces and work together to ensure that the services directive is properly applied. member states must adopt and implement long-term growth policies. the time has come for a new impetus and the removal of the remaining obstacles to the full implementation of the services directive. the european union and its member states need growth, and the services directive is one way to achieve this.

in writing. – syria is not only a real tragedy, with tens of thousands killed and millions of displaced people, but also an exercise in the limits of realpolitik itself. indeed, looked at from every angle, the situation in syria looks bad; no conceivable option seems to be working: the hatred against assad, the infighting within the opposition, russia’s intransigence, the lack of western unity, the ghost of iraq, all combine to create this impossible situation. however, due to its high negative potential, the crisis cannot be left to continue much longer. of course, there is no military solution. but the use of the military instrument is only meant to prepare the ground for a political solution. this is best illustrated by the slightly positive perspective of the latest proposal to the syrian authorities to place their chemical weapons under international control. if it was not backed by the potential us strike, i wonder if (1) russia would have come up with it in the first place and (2) the syrian authorities would have indicated possible acceptance. it is not much, but it is something and, therefore, it should be pursued accordingly.
