mr president, i would like to start by saying that i cannot share either the praise of mr bütikofer for the report of ms gomes or the optimism of mr van orden with respect to european defence. i will now talk about what i prepared about the report by ms giannakou. i will start by saying that a true arc of crisis has enveloped europe from south and east, once again bringing defence to our attention – except that, instead of increasing our defensive effort, we have already reduced it considerably. in comparison with the 1929-1933 world crisis, when defence spending and re-arming proved to be an efficient way of getting us out of that crisis (with the cost of throwing us all into the most destructive world war six years later), today we respond by slashing our defence budgets. true, even if today we do not envisage a new world war, the consequences of our current reductions might jeopardise our future all the same, because europe would be less and less capable of defending itself in the face of new and old challenges coming closer and closer to our borders. the report by ms giannakou has taken onboard all the major suggestions advanced by our group, a fact for which i hereby thank the rapporteur, ms giannakou, who approached her collaboration with the shadow rapporteurs in a very businesslike manner. among the important proposals advanced by the rapporteur are the request for a significant increase in the shared costs for rapid reaction operations; the invitation to the council to revisit and streamline the decision-making procedures to make the eu’s rapid reaction a reality; the creation of a fully-fledged eu operational headquarters within the european external action service, possibly through permanent structural cooperation; and the evaluation of the possibility that costs not related to the military operations per se be charged to the eu budget. in conclusion, we appreciate very much both the report and its proposals and the work done in preparing it, for which ms giannakou deserves to be congratulated and consider that, by adopting it tomorrow, parliament would significantly contribute to the december rio council devoted to defence and security.
if you ask european citizens what they think, a majority of them think that a common defence and security policy is needed. on the other hand, as we know, the treaties tell us that the union must work towards the progressive establishment of a common defence policy framework. however, recent history, and i am thinking here of the intervention in libya, the intervention in mali, shows us that we are far from a genuine common security and defence policy. the union has insufficient capacity to respond to international crises, national defence budgets are also continuously declining. the impact of the financial crisis on the defence sector is also not to be ignored. what can we do in these conditions? i think the budgetary problems can be countered by better coordination. i think they can come together and share capabilities. i believe that by developing a european defence equipment market, new ways of financing can be found at european level. the truth is that the main obstacle to a common security and defence policy is the political will of national leaders. we therefore encourage the european defence council of december 2013 to promote cooperation between member states, including, if not otherwise possible, between some of the member states. the meeting of this council is already an important signal - let's hope the results will be adequate.

madam president, recent developments in the east are not accidental. they are russian foreign policy. the break-up of the eastern partnership is a russian project. the reabsorption of our eastern partners is a russian project. the question is, why? why is russia so confident? unfortunately, we created opportunities for russia by lacking a resolute enough eastern approach. in the east, the eu has not achieved progress in solving the frozen conflicts. in the middle east, the eu and us management of the crisis has been disastrous so far. russia’s assertiveness was encouraged by our weak stance. russia can cynically ban moldovan wine and threaten to let moldovans freeze this winter, knowing it has to fear no consequences. our eastern partners are at a crossroads: moldova, ukraine, armenia are openly blackmailed. this is russia’s offer. our offer is free choice, but our partners need tangible political support. increased market access and political dialogue are good, but not enough. the eu should offer its eastern partners more than a hypothetical chance of joining the eu.
madam president, as the summit in vilnius approaches, with the expected signing-in of some important former soviet republics, moscow is intensifying its efforts to prevent another geostrategic loss. lately, the overt and covert pressure on the potential signatories has thus intensified considerably, demonstrating that moscow’s carrot is also a stick, albeit it not such a big one. armenia having already given in, moldova was immediately visited by russian deputy prime minister dmitry rogozin, a well-known figure in brussels, and by the russian patriarch kirill. the signal, direct and rather brutal from the former, convoluted from the latter, was the same: moldova should plan its future path very carefully by joining the other slavic orthodox peoples. the russian authorities immediately gave substance to such suggestions – first questioning the quality of moldovan wines and then embargoing them altogether. naturally, neither of our prospective signatories should bow to this pressure, now we have come so far. moreover, the eu should evaluate the adoption of concrete measures to alleviate the impact of such abrupt retaliatory moves against these countries.
in writing. the russian federation threatens the republic of moldova to prevent the initialling of the association agreement with the european union and by implication to stop its european path. on 10 september, the russian federation banned imports of moldovan wine on health grounds. the russian health service is elevated to the rank of minister of war to punish countries in the near neighborhood that do not respond to russian orders. the deputy prime minister of the russian federation, visiting chisinau on september 2, stated that the republic of moldova will lose the transnistrian region if it initiates the association agreement. he also threatened the moldovans that they would freeze in winter, so the russian federation is blackmailing the republic of moldova by blocking the gas supply. in addition, there are other threats to make formalities more difficult for moldovan citizens working in the russian federation. the chisinau government responded to this rhetoric with calm and courage. the efforts made to conclude the negotiations in record time and to initial the association agreement show the extraordinary will to integrate the european project. the signing of the association agreement must follow its initial signature as soon as possible, because the european union will not accept being blackmailed by the russian federation.
in writing. after ukraine and armenia, moldova becomes the third country against which russia is pressuring. moscow does not welcome the eastern partnership and the conclusion of association agreements between the european union and the countries of the queens. this is not the first time that russia has used the weapon of banning wine imports from moldova in order to influence the politics of this country. the european union has a responsibility to protect its partners and moldova must not give in to these pressures, which are illegal in view of russia's membership of the wto. finally, i would point out that the association agreements are not intended to undermine trade between the eastern partnership countries and russia, but that, on the contrary, they will boost the competitiveness and performance of the countries in the area and improve their trade with all partners.

i voted for this resolution. the european union currently spends about 10 billion euros a year in subsidies to promote biofuel production. this cost is not justified. on the one hand, burning biofuels increases carbon emissions and contributes to global warming, on the other hand, biofuel subsidies particularly favour large farms operating on a monoculture basis. i think the targets for farm subsidies should be small farmers. we supported the proposal to reduce the target from 10% to 5.5% (well, the 6% compromise was voted on) because it is also in romania's interest. in the absence of sufficiently developed production capacity, romania would have had to import biofuels to meet the target of strategy 2020. but of course, biofuel producers need to develop the ability to process waste and non-food woody plants.
the economic losses caused by the disengagement of young people from the labour market were estimated in 2011 at eur 153 billion, or around 1,2% of the union's gdp. moreover, in 2011, some 7.5 million young people, or about 13% of all 15-24 year olds, were not in employment, education or training. the union is making structural funds available to remedy this serious problem, but these funds have only been partially used. for example, in 2012, €30 billion from the european social fund remained unused. i don't want to comment. this has to change.
although young people represent 13% of the union's labour force, it is estimated that in 2012 they accounted for 42% of temporary work contracts and 32% of part-time contracts. unfortunately, the attitude of many employers is to disregard those without work experience and to dismiss, especially those with temporary or part-time contracts, so that young people are by default the most disadvantaged. in addition, 2 million jobs have been left unfilled in the union because of the education system, which is not in line with the market requirements, the requirements of today and tomorrow. we produce educated young people who are not prepared for a market where there are jobs, but for a market where there may not be jobs. i hope that the resolution that we're voting on now will lead to change, because young people are the priority of any society that wants to progress.
the services sector in the union is estimated at over 65% of the union's gdp and is undoubtedly the future of the european economy. member states should have transposed directive 2006/123 on services by december 2009. however, after 3 years, the implementation was not completed. this clearly hinders member states from achieving optimal economic growth. the remaining obstacles to the implementation of the services directive must therefore be removed, otherwise we cannot grow economically. that is the first need we have: economic growth, and the services directive is, i repeat, a way of achieving that growth.

in writing. − changing the reciprocity mechanism in relation to the common visa policy has emerged as an important need in recent years, requiring a third country benefiting from visa exemption to adopt the same measure in favour of eu citizens. the current situation with regard to the visa requirements for canadian and us citizens undermines the eu's common visa policy, which should be based on reciprocity and promote freedom of movement for all eu citizens. the reciprocity clause is a step forward and so is the promise to act effectively against certain third countries which continue to ignore the basic principle of equal treatment between member states.
in writing. − i believe that this is a major improvement to the eu's visa policy in that the reciprocity rule will be truly enforceable, thus creating de facto solidarity both within the union and in relations with its partners. more than 100 million citizens in 6 member states could benefit directly and immediately from the new visa rules. it is a necessary step towards the end of the us and canadian visa regime for our fellow citizens from romania, bulgaria, the czech republic, poland, cyprus and croatia.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this text because it is my responsibility to fight for the visa rights of my fellow eu citizens. the proposed text reinforces the ‘reciprocity mechanismʼ, a political mechanism which would be activated as an act of solidarity when a third country whose nationals do not need a visa to come to the eu applies or maintains a visa requirement for nationals of one or more eu member states. secondly, it creates a suspension mechanism which would temporarily suspend the visa waiver for a third country in the event of an emergency situation related to its migratory situation. this mechanism will put an end to the unacceptable situation concerning citizens from six member states: romania, bulgaria, poland, the czech republic, cyprus and croatia. this text will improve the euʼs visa policy because the reciprocity rule will be truly enforceable, creating solidarity both within the union and in its relations with its partners. over 100 million citizens from six member states would benefit directly from the new visa rules.
in writing. − in 2008, when the financial crisis spread across europe, there were 27 different systems of bank regulation in the european union, all based on national rules and national rescue mechanisms. although some form of coordination existed at eu level, it was concerned with relatively informal exchanges of information and cooperation procedures. this was not sufficient to react to the financial sector crisis felt in the union in recent years. initial steps have therefore been taken to address these issues both through the introduction of stricter rules for financial services and through the establishment of new financial supervisory agencies, including the european banking authority. the european banking authority was established in 2011 to help coordinate the activities of national regulators and ensure the consistent application of eu-wide rules. however, effective supervision of banks remained mainly the responsibility of the national regulatory authorities.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this text to establish a european banking supervisory authority in connection with the specific tasks of the european central bank relating to policies on the prudential supervision of credit institutions. this decision, which gives the ecb the power to supervise the banks of the eurozone and establishes a single supervisory mechanism, will have to be translated into reality as soon as possible in order to move towards the creation of a real banking union. while there is still a long way to go, this vote is a step in the direction of transparency in the european banking sector, which is a very good thing. it is, however, only a step towards holding european bankers fully accountable, to ensure that their speculative activities, which have contributed to the economic and social crisis we are currently experiencing, come to an end. i would also like to highlight the role of the socialist and democrat group in the european parliament in ensuring that any transfer of power from the national to the european level will have to be accompanied by greater democratic oversight by the european parliament.
in writing. - today we have approved, despite a difficult path, the report calling for the european central bank to be given specific tasks in relation to policies on the prudential supervision of credit institutions. the ecb's policy, especially in recent times, has been subject to the magnifying glass of public opinion, politicians and financial operators. this means that its role is becoming increasingly decisive and that the decisions it takes are decisive, especially those concerning monetary policy. in a context of a feared credit crunch and difficulties in accessing credit for public authorities, businesses and public administrations, the ecb's new specific tasks in the field of prudential supervision should be welcomed as a positive sign of a union that wants to move at a single speed and not, instead, as an additional 'cap' that the ecb wants to place on the sovereignty of states. to give in to this interpretation would mean giving europe over to the anti-europeanists, and that is something we cannot afford.
in writing. − the evolution of the economic and financial crisis has brought the european banking system to the brink of collapse, which has undermined the integrity of the single currency and the single market, endangering the union's entire economic development. the rapid increase in the complexity of the activities carried out by credit institutions before the crisis led to a limitation of national control and the inability to have a comprehensive picture of the entire internal market in financial services. the fragmentation of financial markets placed a heavy burden on public finances during the crisis, which were already under pressure. all these problems could have been avoided, however, if there had been proper supervision. that is why, in the light of the european central bank's experience with financial problems, i believe that we urgently need new regulations to strengthen the capacity of the central bank to prevent and limit the risks specific to the activities of these institutions, thus protecting the stability of the european financial system.
in writing. − if we want the eu to meet its long-term renewable energy targets, we need to consider microgeneration. this contributes to increasing the total share of renewable energy in the eu energy mix and allows for efficient consumption of electricity close to the point where it is generated, thus also avoiding losses during transport. i would like to mention that the efficient use of microgeneration is influenced by several factors, such as: a functional european internal energy market; the technical development of microgeneration units; the realisation of an intelligent energy infrastructure, especially at the distribution level, and, not least, short, medium and long-term policies and effective support mechanisms to stimulate microgeneration at european, national and local level.
in writing. − access to enough energy for a decent standard of living is a fundamental right for all citizens and, as energy prices have risen significantly in recent years, i believe that the role of research and technology in improving efficiency and reducing the costs of microgeneration is essential.

in writing. − the gender pay gap is still a persistent problem and currently stands at 16.2 % across the eu. the implementation of the principle of equal pay for the same work and for work of equal value is crucial to achieving gender equality, bearing in mind that the negative effects of the gender pay gap on women extend into their retirement age and women receive pensions which are, on average, 39 % lower than those of men. reducing gender inequalities by closing the gender pay gap will bring benefits not only for women but for society as a whole, and this should be seen as an investment. the commission should strongly support member states in reducing the gender pay gap by at least five percentage points annually with the aim of eliminating the gender pay gap by 2020. the commission should review directive 2006/54/ec on the implementation of the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment and occupation, at least in relation to some aspects of the gender pay gap issue: work evaluation and job classification, equality bodies and legal remedy, social dialogue, prevention of discrimination, gender mainstreaming, sanctions, streamlining of eu regulation and eu policy.
in writing. − slow progress in closing the gender pay gap has significant demographic, social, legal and economic consequences. therefore, i believe that reducing gender inequalities by eliminating unjustified pay gaps between women and men will benefit not only women but also society as a whole and should not be considered a cost but an investment.

the carbonated products that can be found in schools, kiosks, playgrounds and are used to quench our thirst, as we hear from advertisements, not only have the opposite effect, causing dehydration in the body, but have been shown to lead to various harmful diseases, such as obesity, cellular damage, osteoporosis, tooth decay, liver disease and so on. in addition, a study called nomas clearly states that dietary carbohydrate juices increase the risk of stroke by up to 61 percent. i therefore ask the european commission to take urgent action to protect the health of minors in the european union by treating the marketing of carbonated juices in a similar way to cigarettes and alcoholic beverages, by carrying out concrete information campaigns and by detecting harmful substances in carbonated juices.
given the need to develop a new strategy and action plan on hiv, aids and other communicable diseases for the period 2014-2020, i thought i would bring to your attention today some key elements on this topic. first, access to quality medicines at affordable prices must be improved. the pharmaceutical industry plays a very important role here. it should facilitate access to low-cost treatment and enter into beneficial partnerships with both the private and public systems for drug availability research/development and technology transfer. pharmaceutical companies should be encouraged to get more involved in middle- and low-income countries and register their products in these needy countries. the european commission must delay the implementation of trade-related intellectual property rights in least developed countries in order not to impair people's access to health services and their access to appropriate treatment. the commission must continue to take into account in all its bilateral agreements the importance of ensuring access to public health services for the population.
in writing. i believe that the partnership between central and regional and local authorities is essential to set priorities and to ensure the co-financing needed to implement programmes supported by the structural funds. these partnerships will ensure an important role in achieving the europe 2020 objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, but the need for thematic focus on a small number of priorities must be taken into account. in addition, i support the need for flexibility which will enable member states and regions to respond most effectively to common objectives, while respecting territorial, economic and social characteristics as well as regional and local needs. it should be borne in mind that regional and local governments account for 60% of public investment and 38% of consolidated government expenditure on 'business' and this includes most of the expenditure that can influence regional development, such as trade and jobs, agriculture, transport or research and development.
in writing. an ambitious health promotion policy also requires smart regulation of tobacco products. for this reason, i welcome the commission's proposal, which contains many elements that will make tobacco products less attractive, especially to young people. i think, however, that a degree of proportionality must be maintained in the sense that we cannot go too far with the prohibitions. as long as the sale of cigarettes remains legal, we must recognize that there is an industry that we cannot stop from operating. i therefore sympathize with the introduction of health warnings on 75 or 65% of the surface of the package, but i do not think that the introduction of standard packaging is appropriate. i would also like to make a comment on electronic cigarettes. it is well known that they are less harmful than regular cigarettes and can help smokers to quit. however, since they are not completely harmless, it is illogical to classify them as drugs. this would mean that smokers would have less access to a less harmful product than cigarettes, which are widely available. i think it is more balanced that they are considered to be tobacco products and that they carry the appropriate health warnings.

i voted for this report because it is very important in the fight against corruption. the report draws attention to the effects of corruption on people, on budgets. according to the world bank, corruption accounts for 5 percent of global gross domestic product and more than $1 trillion is paid in bribes each year. corruption adds 10 percent to the total cost of doing business and 25 percent to the cost of government procurement in developing countries. corruption, even at the highest levels, affects everyone because it reduces the amount of money that needs to reach people. with that money, we could build schools, hospitals, roads, raise wages or pensions. so everyone needs to understand that even those who are not directly involved in corruption are affected by the material costs of corruption.
in writing. - the problem of corruption does not only bring to the fore the economic impact of illicit activities. corruption raises numerous questions about the institutional capacity of developing countries and societies. the scale of the phenomenon also allows for the maintenance of various stereotypes and the practice of a widespread system of discrimination, significantly limiting the possibility of sustainable development. we can also say that, at institutional level, the european union has both the capacity and the know-how to drive political and social transformation in these countries. in encouraging the transition to democracy and to market economies in the former communist states, the union has demonstrated its ability to steer and accelerate the pace of change towards good governance. i believe that in these circumstances respect for transparency must become an essential principle of the european union's policies, both internally and in its external policy, and that the phenomenon of corruption must be treated with the same intransigence.
in writing. − according to the world bank, corruption accounts for 5% of global gdp (usd 2.6 trillion), and over usd 1 trillion is offered as bribes each year. corruption accounts for 10% of the total cost of doing business worldwide and 25% of the cost of public procurement in developing countries. the eu can only become a credible and influential leader in the fight against corruption if it properly tackles organised crime, corruption and money laundering within its own territory. i hope that the 'eu anti-corruption report' to be presented by the commission will identify areas vulnerable to corruption in the member states and help to step up anti-corruption efforts by facilitating the exchange of good practices.
in writing. − the future of the european union, in a global context, offers both the prospect of opportunities that we must seize and a perhaps unprecedented set of challenges that we must recognise in advance in order to be able to pursue our policy of economic consolidation and development. in this last aspect of the obstacles we will face, the ability to identify and study trends developing worldwide is extremely important in order to be able to develop forecasts that help us achieve the major objectives of the european union. in a world of constant change, access to information remains essential. the european union cannot be content with being a mere pawn on the world chessboard, but must play an important political, economic and decision-making role. this is why it is important to anticipate all those global trends, the movements of the other actors, which will support the decision-makers at european level. i think it is extremely opportune to support the espas effort and even to strengthen this mechanism for interinstitutional information exchange in the period ahead.
in writing. − the european union is facing a period of rapid transition and transformation, particularly in terms of power, demography, climate, urbanisation and technology. the coming years will be characterised by increasing complexity and uncertainty, the multipolar nature of a more globalised world, a multi-level nature of governance and more actors interacting in policy and law-making, all of which contribute to a new global context that will present greater challenges. this new global context will evolve with a higher level of uncertainty than usual. following global trends will be a fundamental aspect of europe's ability to prepare for and respond to future challenges. it is therefore increasingly important for policy-makers to invest in monitoring, studying and analysing important trends and to engage in forward-looking policy analysis, while seeking solutions to new and complex challenges.
in writing. − the harmonious development of all regions that the european union wants is closely linked to the existence of efficient administrative structures, which can effectively implement the different european policies and properly manage eu funds on the basis of well-founded and forward-looking strategies, but which must also take into account the specificities of the regions. however, i believe that improving the administrative capacity of regions and local government structures should not lead to the creation of new mechanisms or institutions, but should make more efficient use of existing administrative processes, and e-government can play a fundamental role in capacity building, administrative modernisation and better horizontal and vertical coordination between different bodies at national and european level.
in writing. − the effects of the economic crisis include the intensification of conflicts between employees and employers, as well as the denunciation of problems related to employment contracts. situations in which employees in the shipping or road transport sector have sought to take their employer to court have become increasingly common. many of them were caught in a legal deadlock, in that they were from an eu country, were based or working in another country and their employer was from a third member state. although the brussels i regulation has brought significant improvements in the rules governing jurisdiction, both civil and commercial, practice shows that both in trade union action and in individual contracts of employment, various disputes continue to arise in obscure legal contexts that do not allow them to be clarified in the shortest possible time. i welcome and support the rapporteur's proposals and i believe, for my part, that these amendments are intended to protect employees, collectively and individually!
in writing. − labour law is an area in which the european union exercises only a relatively minor influence. different member states have set the balance between workers' rights, trade union activity and the freedom to conduct business in different ways. for the free movement of workers and capital, the european union has developed rules which govern, in crossborder situations, which member state has jurisdiction to settle disputes, including in the field of labour law. labour law is a particularly sensitive area and the specific rules in the brussels i regulation on individual employment contracts reflect this.
in writing. − in december 2012, the reformed brussels i regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters was signed. it is important to ensure, as far as possible, the jurisdiction of a member state in disputes to which its own labour law applies. as far as possible, jurisdiction and the applicable law should belong to the same state. the rules on jurisdiction in disputes relating to employment relations must be aligned with the rules in force on the applicable law. the court of the member state in which the trade union action is being or is to be brought should therefore have jurisdiction to rule on disputes relating thereto. it is essential that there is an exclusive forum for disputes concerning trade union actions, in accordance with the rome ii regulation, located where the trade union action is or has been brought. in cases where an employee is suing the employer, the safety clause that applies when there is no regular place of work should be reworded to refer to the place of work from which the employee receives or has received daily instructions and not to the place of employment of the company.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to improve private international law by establishing rules of jurisdiction applicable in the field of employment. the report proposes to make important amendments to the 'brussels i' regulation on jurisdiction in the field of labour law. it shall establish a court for disputes concerning the class action, namely that of the place where the class action is to be or has been brought. in addition, when the worker takes legal action against the employer, the withdrawal clause, when there is no habitual place of work, should be reworded to refer to the establishment which gives or has given the worker his daily instructions rather than to the place where he was employed. i welcome these amendments, which are intended to protect workers collectively and individually, who are usually the weakest party in an employment relationship, and to ensure legal consistency and avoid undermining national legal traditions in the field of labour law by ensuring, as far as possible, that jurisdiction and the applicable law overlap.
in writing. − this proposal for a directive is part of a wider framework of european legal measures set up to implement several rules of the maritime labour convention adopted by the ilo in 2006 in geneva. at present, 30 countries have ratified the convention, representing 59% of the world fleet tonnage, meeting the requirements for the entry into force of the convention, namely 30 countries representing over 33% of the world fleet tonnage. the convention covers essential aspects such as minimum requirements for seafarers to be able to work on board a ship, conditions of employment, accommodation, recreational facilities, food and catering, health protection, medical care, social services and insurance, and its compliance and implementation to ensure decent working and living conditions on board ships, and procedures for the implementation of these provisions. each member state shall require ships flying its flag to obtain and maintain at all times a maritime labour certificate attesting that the working and living conditions of seafarers on board have been inspected, including measures of continuing compliance to be included in the maritime labour declaration of compliance.
in writing. − i believe that each member state should set clear objectives and standards for the management of its inspection and certification systems, and appropriate general procedures for their evaluation, to the extent that those objectives and standards are met.
in writing. − the european parliament's proposal for a directive on tobacco products was mainly aimed at discouraging smoking among young people. statistics show that the incidence of smoking among young people is increasing, with 70 percent of smokers starting before the age of 18 and 94 percent before the age of 25. preventing smoking among young people must be a priority as smoking is the most important cause of premature death in the eu, accounting for almost 700 000 deaths a year. i voted along the lines of the socialist and democratic group, which supported the revision of the tobacco products directive, but on certain aspects i took account of the position of the romanian government in order to avoid that, in the current crisis period, romania should suffer job losses as well as significant losses to the state budget. i believe that we need a european union strategy to tackle smoking among young people in a comprehensive way, including, in addition to legislative measures, actions to address the multifactorial causes of young people starting and continuing to smoke. such an approach is likely to enhance and maximise the impact of legislative measures and produce lasting changes in the smoking mind-set and behaviour of young people.
in writing. all studies show that smoking remains the number one preventable cause of death in the european union, killing nearly 700 000 people a year. while it is a welcome acknowledgement that the measures taken over the past decade to combat smoking have borne fruit and have reduced the number of smokers, much remains to be done to prevent the scourge. that is why i voted in favour of this report. the main objective of the directive is to place a strict control on the use of tobacco products in order to make them less attractive to young people, while preserving jobs and income from the tobacco industry in this time of crisis. we have, for example, voted in favour of a measure to make tobacco warnings more visible: they will have to cover 65% of cigarette packs and will be printed on the top of the pack. i also welcome the continuation of e-cigarettes as a consumer product accessible to the public as this tool has been proven to be particularly effective in helping smokers to quit.
in writing. − the european union has established itself as one of the most important political forums in the world in terms of combating gender discrimination. but despite these efforts, we must admit that the gender issue is a much more nuanced and complex one, which requires the attention of national and european decision-makers. the persistence of gender discrimination, intolerance and the maintenance of double standards are unfortunately still commonplace both within and outside the european continent. in particular, it is necessary to adopt measures by which the union contributes to discouraging the practice of selecting children on the basis of sex. this is an unacceptable practice! the existing gender imbalances have reached a level in many countries and regions that calls into question both the effectiveness of anti-discrimination policies and the creation of a social context conducive to democratic development. the union's external action should be geared to the needs of women and girls, and should be based on the principles of non-discrimination and gender equality.

in writing. − killing people systematically and deliberately because of their gender is a severe violation of human rights that must be addressed without delay. around 200 million women are estimated to be ‘missing’ due to male/son preference and sex selection at birth according to recent research, 100 million more than in 1990. gendercide is a global phenomenon touching not only asia but also countries in europe, north america, latin america and africa. in china, 113 boys were born for every 100 girls in 2011 while the normal ratio is 106 males to 102 females. fighting such a global and complex phenomenon requires a full set of measures. we need better and more reliable data on sex ratios at birth, child mortality, and recognized sex-selective practices at micro, sub-national and national level. in addition, we need more efficient legislation and policy frameworks to address the root causes of gender inequalities and gendercide. i also call on the commission and the eu delegations worldwide to integrate gendercide into the political dialogue agenda with the relevant third countries.
in writing. − the economic crisis has not only affected the living standards of european citizens, but has also called into question one of the major objectives of the european union the social, economic and territorial cohesion of the eu. regional disparities have widened, while budget deficits, especially at local level, have increased significantly. at the same time, access to credit has become increasingly difficult for local authorities, and the impact of austerity policies has left little room for public investment. it is important that cohesion policy should once again become the union's investment instrument. this process can offer effective prospects for tackling the crisis, reducing imbalances and strengthening the european union's sustainable growth. i also believe that the development of the union, even in the face of economic upheaval, cannot take place without respecting the objectives and commitments undertaken by the member states and the european union in the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − the current economic context has placed significant constraints on the public finances of the member states. at the same time, regional and local authorities are increasingly facing particular problems in their ability to finance cost-effective investment. on the one hand, they face a sharp decline in their disposable income as central budgets reduce allocations and require local and regional authorities to contribute to austerity measures, and on the other they have to provide increasingly demanding social services as a result of the crisis, putting increased pressure on their disposable funds. in the light of the above, i believe it is important to put forward concrete proposals to allow for all the flexibility needed for national co-financing of eu development spending, while also taking into account the strict application of the stability and growth pact.
in writing. − in the context of the current economic and financial crisis, regional and local authorities are facing a sharp decline in their disposable income as central budgets reduce funding allocations and require local and regional authorities to contribute to austerity measures, and on the other hand they have to provide social services that are increasingly demanding as a result of the crisis, putting an increased pressure on their available funds. public expenditure implementing programmes co-financed by the structural and investment funds should be excluded from the definition of structural deficits in the stability and growth pact, as this expenditure is dedicated to supporting competitiveness, growth and job creation and in particular to job creation for young people. it is important to rebuild and improve financial capacity at regional level and to provide appropriate technical assistance, in particular in the implementation of complex and locally managed joint projects, in order to secure public investment for programmes and projects aimed at boosting sustainable growth, combating social exclusion and restoring social fabric by providing adequate social and health services and creating jobs, especially at regional and local level.
in writing. − i believe that it is beneficial to extend the use of financial instruments under cohesion policy to all thematic objectives and all european structural and investment funds, but that the eib and the commission should propose new measures to finance long-term investments by local and regional authorities, including through the attraction of private capital.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to draw attention to the effects of budgetary constraints on regional and local authorities in the context of eu structural funds expenditure in the member states. in the context of the current financial and economic crisis, local (regional and local) authorities are increasingly confronted with the financial constraints on member states and the difficulty of securing productive investment. on the one hand, they are seeing a sharp decline in their incomes as central governments reduce transfers and ask regional and local governments to contribute to austerity measures; on the other hand, they are increasingly required to provide, because of the crisis, essential social services which impose additional pressures on their public finances. in this particular context, it is essential to make concrete proposals to ensure the greatest possible flexibility in the national co-financing of the union's development expenditure. we must make sure that we suggest practical and viable ways of improving the financial capacity of local and regional authorities for productive investment for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. − this report is a wake-up call to the difficulties local authorities are facing during the crisis. local and regional authorities are key players in local development in the european union. the actions of these authorities represent 60% of public investment and 38% of consolidated budget expenditure. reducing funding for local communities has a two-fold effect: on the one hand, savings are made during the crisis, and budget lines are cut, especially for public investment and renovations. austerity also affects the implementation of projects financed by the structural funds. local authorities no longer have the capacity to cover the co-financing needed to continue projects and are in long-term debt. where authorities have the capacity to borrow short-term, borrowing the banking system does not allow them to find low-interest loans. austerity is particularly affecting the poorest regions, which were already having difficulties absorbing european funds and implementing projects.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has significantly affected local and regional authorities, with local public budgets being directly targeted through drastic cuts. efforts to overcome the economic crisis must focus on investments in key areas for growth and job creation. at the same time, greater involvement of local and regional authorities in the planning of european union structural funds programmes is needed. the role of cohesion policy must remain decisive in reducing development inequalities. i therefore believe it is essential that local actors, even in times of crisis, have the financial resources to use the structural funds. i would like to raise the alarm about the need to strengthen administrative capacity, which is a key condition for reducing bureaucracy and making more efficient use of european funds. the development of the european union must be thought of from the bottom up, in order to ensure a fair economic balance so that no european region is economically discriminated against.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on 'budgetary constraints faced by regional and local authorities in spending eu structural funds in the member states' because one of the biggest problems facing local and regional authorities in this period is the major budget cuts in important areas and sectors. by enhancing financial capacity at local and regional level and providing appropriate technical assistance, we will secure public investment for programmes and projects that boost sustainable growth, combat social exclusion and create new jobs. member states should promote measures aimed at both strengthening the administrative capacity of regional and local authorities and reducing red tape, in order to boost their capacity to implement projects financed by european funds. i would like to express my opposition to the introduction of macroeconomic conditionality in the future cohesion policy, 2014-2020, as it would mean penalising, first of all, the beneficiaries and the regions already vulnerable to the crisis. any suspension of payments for purely economic reasons would have disproportionate effects in the member states, despite their full participation in efforts to balance public budgets.
in writing. − i welcome the european parliament's motion for a resolution on a comprehensive union strategy for fisheries in the pacific region, as i believe it is in the european union's interest to develop relations with the pacific region and cooperate in order to achieve its development objectives, based on the premise of conserving fisheries resources, promoting sustainable fisheries development and encouraging transparency in fisheries management. such a strategy in the pacific region is of the utmost importance, given the fisheries relevance of this region and its importance for the union fleet and for the european union fisheries processing market and industry. the commission must ensure the coherence of all community policies concerning the pacific region, in particular fisheries, trade and development, and promote the eu's visibility in the western and central pacific in such a way as to maximise the benefits for both pacific states and eu member states.
in writing. − the mediterranean and black seas have specific oceanographic, fisheries, environmental and socio-economic characteristics that need to be taken into account in a sustainable resource management strategy. in this context, i welcome the european parliament's motion for a resolution which aims at more efficient and sustainable management of marine resources in the mediterranean and black seas by promoting cohesion and cooperation between the coastal member states involved. all coastal states need to step up their efforts to phase out overfishing in the mediterranean and black seas, as declining fish stocks increase the potential for conflict in these regions. the european union should provide appropriate guidance, coordination and support to the member states in this regard, with a view to ensuring the coherence of the common fisheries policy and the integrated maritime policy. given that most of the states in the black sea and the mediterranean are not eu member states and are therefore not obliged to comply with eu legislation, i believe that bilateral cooperation and international agreements play an important role in promoting consistent management of marine resources in these seas under fair competition conditions.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to regulate practices and resolve conflicts concerning fisheries and territorial waters in the mediterranean and the black sea. the management of maritime and coastal areas is a complex issue involving the participation of different private and public authorities. it requires greater cohesion and political cooperation between the coastal states concerned. i share the concern expressed in the report about increased competition for dwindling marine stocks and resources, which is creating regional tensions and may lead to disputes between states over maritime zones. in this context, efforts at regional, national and european level to improve the regulation of access to resources must be intensified, and it must be ensured that all coastal states are urged to intensify their efforts to phase out overfishing. i share the call for the establishment of a strengthened system of monitoring, control and surveillance of fishing activity in the two basins, with an integrated approach to improve the conservation of the ecosystem, in accordance with european and international law.
the difficulties encountered this time in the discharge of the council are regrettable. for several years now, we have been facing the same set of problems, whose resolution stage remains constant. it was not possible to establish an open dialogue between the council and the committee on budgetary control on a transparent manner of cooperation. every year we find ourselves in a similar situation where we have to react to the council's refusal to answer further questions from parliament. questions and requests for additional information or documents from parliament are a legitimate part of the discharge procedure. under the treaty, the european parliament, through its committee on budgetary control, has a specific and well-defined role in the discharge process, with responsibility for granting discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the union. the council, by virtue of its status as a european institution, must be subject to this procedure in its entirety, since it is one of the beneficiaries of the european budget. i would reiterate that effective monitoring of the implementation of the budget depends on unconditional interinstitutional cooperation between parliament and the council. it is true that parliament has the right to refuse discharge, a right which it has applied to the council since 2009. however, there is a risk in repeatedly refusing to grant discharge where there are no direct results or repercussions. the absence of a concrete result following the decision to refuse to grant him management risks discrediting the procedure itself, with undesirable effects over time also on other union institutions or agencies.
public opinion and taxpayers have a right to know how public money is spent by the european institutions, including the european council and the council; they are not, nor should they be, an exception to this principle. their expenditure must be scrutinised by the european parliament, just as the european parliament scrutinises the expenditure and management of all the other european institutions. since 2007, the council has refused to cooperate with the european parliament on the discharge procedure. this situation is unacceptable and that is why, once again, and i agree with this, we are not giving the discharge to the council for 2011. the council constantly invokes a tacit agreement, the so-called gentlemen's agreement, which dates back to 1970. for god's sake, the world has changed, you can no longer invoke this agreement, it's time to show publicly what you do with the money and we do our job as the european parliament and check this.
madam president, the eu’s economic downturn is not just another unfortunate consequence of the financial crisis. the european union’s ability to compete in research is part of the problem. since 2009 the debate has focused on regaining lost competitiveness in business and labour terms. this message is right, but it is not enough. to my knowledge, the great economic powers of the world have achieved success by regarding research as a long-term investment with high returns. it does not make sense for the eu to try to prove them wrong. the eu needs to get its act together and support the completion of the european research area. thirteen years have passed since the project was launched: thirteen years of half measures and partial commitment. for a better evaluation please consult the statistics on the world ranking of research institutes: the eu does not appear very often in the top 50 positions. only cern makes the top five. the us and japan dominate. we have to understand that the future is built today and that research gives a cutting edge to those who do not hesitate to invest in it. we keep on generating debates on economic recovery but we have lost sight of the fundamental role of research. we will not be able to restart our economies counting on the available research. the european research community should become a functional reality that disseminates its achievements to the benefit of the eu.
it seems that you have a much more theoretical approach than universities have to research and development at european level. at the moment we are dealing with a rather unresolved situation as regards the stimulation of research in the european union. the vast majority of r&d funding in the 2007-2013 period was not allocated because of a lack of knowledge among those who are eligible and have the opportunity and ability to do r&d and innovation at european level. secondly, there is no concrete link between the education system or education systems in the eu member states and the labour market in this field at european level. we are dealing with an emigration of intelligent labour from the european union to the great research powers like america, japan, but more recently also to china, which we cannot stop. we're going to go very soon and buy the science generated by europeans in china back to europe, then we'll produce and we'll license the chinese products to the european level. of course, my question is very specific: commissioner, is the european commission planning to standardize national research programmes?
the european research area is one of the best examples of the significant added value of cooperation between member states. without joint action, it is virtually impossible to achieve the objectives. unfortunately, it is no longer news that europe is lagging behind in the global search competition. in other parts of the world, there is a much greater emphasis on research, and this points to dangerous trends in the medium and long term. i am convinced that eu action is needed alongside the efforts of the member states. i'm not going to list them, i'm just going to mention them, my colleagues have listed them, europe 2020, the pay gap between researchers, mobility, the problems of women, the problems of researchers in third countries, all of these things show, i would say this, especially to my eurosceptic colleagues, that today it is no longer possible to claim that education, research, even minority issues, human rights issues are only a matter for the member states. there are countries, my country, where the education law is not enforced by universities, just because of the anti-minority sentiment, and you can imagine the kind of research that goes on at that university. in writing. − the directive on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment establishes the simple but fundamental principle of 'informed decision': before authorising the implementation of a public or private project likely to have an impact on the environment, the competent authorities of the member states are legally obliged to gather the information necessary to carry out an environmental impact assessment. in its 28 years of application, this legislation has been relatively successful in harmonising the principles of environmental impact assessment at union level. during this period, some shortcomings were identified which have given rise to a significant number of legal disputes at national level or before the court of justice of the european union. in line with the union's priorities, the proposal introduces biodiversity, the use of natural resources, climate change and the risks of natural and man-made disasters among the factors to be considered in environmental impact assessments. i consider that the decision to analyse projects in terms of cumulation with other projects or activities was necessary, as this will prevent the harmful practice of fragmenting works into batches in order to reduce the identified environmental impacts.

in writing. − the proposed revision of directive 2011/92/eu on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment aims to introduce new environmental impact assessment factors for certain activities and to streamline procedures in this area. in this period of economic crisis we must not put additional and unfounded obstacles to industrial projects which are important sources of economic growth and job creation for europe. i therefore believe that introducing preliminary stages in the evaluation procedure will lead to a delay and administrative burden in the implementation of industrial activities. i also do not think that additional measures for shale gas exploration are necessary. the european commission has already taken a first initiative in this regard through the 'environmental, climate and energy assessment framework to enable safe and secure unconventional hydrocarbon extraction' work programme introduced in 2013, which aims to provide a risk management framework, address regulatory gaps and provide maximum clarity and predictability of the legal framework for both citizens and market operators. the content of the directive needs to be simplified to avoid prolonging the time and administrative procedures involved in the implementation of industrial projects.

clear. i am not going to repeat what i have already said and what many of you have underlined. let me just respond to some questions which were asked. mrs járóka – who, by the way, is a roma and, i positive examples of integration. i know about these too, because i have visited them in our member states, and i know perfectly well how difficult it is for mayors, for instance, living in a small village, when a large number of people come to the village and try to establish themselves, to keep things in balance. we have to help those mayors so that they can maintain a balance. i believe we also need to put more emphasis on dedicating the money in the social funds to poverty and integration. these funds today have a threshold of 15 %, but member states are free to decide whether to use them or not. i would like to have a 20 % threshold with more dedicated rules ensuring this money is used in order to combat poverty and promote integration, because we must know something. if we – and i mean all of us, in the countries of origin and the countries of destination – do not manage, for instance to get roma children into schools, the next generation will be confronted with an even bigger problem to solve. here i think we have a real responsibility as politicians today to get things right. but we also have a responsibility to look at things as they are and not to make a reality from perceptions. that is exactly what i was discussing yesterday with the ministers of the interior. we had the question of the free movement and non-discrimination directives on the table, and i asked everybody not to confuse immigration with free movement, which is one of the most cherished rights of all european citizens. but, like all rights, it also comes with obligations. you not only have the right to go to the neighbouring country, you also have the obligation not to depend heavily on the social security of this neighbouring country. you have the obligation to obey laws, and governments have the obligation to ensure that these laws are implemented. it is the responsibility of national governments to enforce laws and to combat fraud and criminality, whatever the nationality of the european citizen who commits the fraud or the crime. we must stop stigmatising citizens because they are from another ethnic background. i would also like all members of parliament to have this document. i presented the ministers of the interior with an initial analysis on the basis of data which the governments gave us to see what free movement in europe actually is. in fact this free movement in europe is not utilised by our citizens. only 0.29 % of european citizens take advantage of free movement. so let us not behave as if it was an invasion. there will not be an invasion on 1 january 2014 either, because nothing will change. free movement will continue as it is now. so let us stop doing what politicians should never do. we have heard it on occasion today. i president-in-office of the council. − mr president, madam vice-president of the commission, honourable members, the council is grateful to the european parliament for its substantive work in support of the social integration of the roma people. this afternoon’s debate has provided us with a valuable opportunity to exchange views on this very important issue. it is not an abstract point. it concerns the future of millions of our fellow eu citizens and i have heard a number of specific cases this afternoon in which roma people have been discriminated against. i would like to once again stress that all ethnic groups, including the roma, are protected by the eu anti-discrimination directive that prohibits discrimination on the grounds of racial or ethnic origin in a number of areas, including conditions for access to employment, access to vocational training, social protection, including social security and health care, education, and access to and the supply of goods and services, including housing. the directive also includes a positive action clause that allows member states to maintain or adopt specific measures to prevent or compensate for disadvantages linked to racial or ethnic origin. i look forward to continuing the excellent cooperation between the council, commission and parliament in this important area.
in writing. the present debate on the roma comes amid complaints from some member states about the influx of this ethnic group nomadic by historical definition and the problems caused by the different lifestyles of the members of the ethnic group. i would like to stress that roma are european citizens and, with or without the barriers of the schengen area, they can move freely within the eu. i welcome the commission's initiative and the existence of european funds as much as is allocated to the social inclusion of the roma. i remind you that my country, romania, has made efforts to integrate this ethnic group, efforts that no one appreciated, wrongly considering that lack of effect equals lack of effort. i look forward to the methods found by the states promoting multiculturalism and i am convinced that they will have spectacular results. in conclusion, i would stress that social inclusion must be achieved in the state of residence which roma have chosen by virtue of their right to free movement and not in the state of origin which they will leave immediately after a possible 'repatriere' in order to return to where they feel better, where they want to live, work and study. i end by wishing these states much success.
in writing. unfortunately, we have been discussing roma issues for years, we have been talking about a european roma strategy, but the situation remains the same, too much talk and too little action. roma remain the most discriminated population, they are still expelled from eu countries to other countries, denied the right to free movement, demonized and marginalized. i would also like to express my concern about the voices being raised in some member states which automatically associate roma with criminal phenomena and which use this false argument in a populist manner in domestic political discourse. the problems facing the roma population are not the problems of a single member state, and a european response is therefore needed to ensure the integration of this minority and to combat discrimination and xenophobia.
in writing. many roma citizens in europe face prejudice, intolerance, discrimination and social exclusion in their daily lives. they are marginalized and live in very precarious socioeconomic conditions. on average, only one in two roma children attend pre-school or kindergarten; school attendance falls considerably after compulsory education, and only 15% of roma young people complete upper secondary education; on average, less than one in three roma citizens report being employed; 20% of them do not have health insurance, and 90% live below the poverty line. the european union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. roma citizens are european citizens and have equal rights with all other european citizens, including the right to move freely and to settle and work in any of the member states. the integration of roma citizens is a european problem and not one of any particular member state. we call on the commission and the member states to ensure the integration of roma citizens and to stop discrimination against them on the basis of their ethnicity.
in writing. the far right is growing alarmingly in europe, amid the economic and social crisis and the crisis of confidence in the democratic system. the facts show that extremist discourse is doubled by violence that has escalated to murder, as happened recently in greece. unfortunately, some traditional parties believe they can avoid losing popularity by embracing radical ideas. for the first time since the fall of nazism, europe is facing the threat of the far right in a serious way. an extreme anti-european, anti-semitic, anti-islam, anti-immigration, anti-roma, racist and brutal, who propagates the primitive thesis of the danger of foreigners taking the jobs of locals, commits crimes, therefore must be expelled and eliminated. in the 1930s, from this point, it was just a step away from the ovens of auschwitz and a devastating conflagration. at least in the last hour europe must show that it has learned something from a history of bloody fanaticism.
the essence of intelligence cooperation is to carry out covert, covert, multi-state coordinated actions to ensure our security. i think that no one is questioning the need for the activities of the secret services, the cooperation between them, the joint action with allied services in the fight against terrorism. but we are talking about practices on the territory of european states that are in sharp contrast to the human rights system that we have developed over decades and of which we are proud. i've said it many times: if we don't take our own rules seriously, how are we going to take them seriously in other parts of the world? this case has symbolic significance. can a breach of a series of international conventions, committed with the knowledge of the public authorities, be allowed to go unpunished in the european union? i think the most basic requirement is that european citizens have a clear view of the matter. president-in-office of the council. − mr president, let me state again that the council fully shares the view that respect for human rights and international law in the fight against terror is fundamental. a number of speakers this evening have called on the council to investigate allegations of member states’ involvement in a programme of transportation and illegal detention of prisoners by the cia. the council consists of the representatives of the governments of the 28 member states. even if it had the legal basis to do so, the council would never have the political support of all 28 member states to issue a statement about such involvement, let alone initiate investigations. i realise that may be frustrating to members of this house to hear, but we also operate within the framework of rules which have to be respected. if there are allegations of inappropriate involvement by member states in such activities, this is first and foremost an issue of scrutiny by national parliaments, by national authorities, by national legal authorities, and there are channels at the national level for holding national executives to account. these can, of course, also go wider than national level, because all member states are contracting parties to the european convention on human rights and fundamental freedoms. so mechanisms do exist, but they are not mechanisms which are under the control of the council. that is why the council has been unable to follow up on the recommendations in your resolution. it has nothing to do with an absence of loyal cooperation. it has everything to do with the legal and constitutional framework within which we all operate. i therefore ask for your understanding and thank you for your attention.
in writing. the resolution on the alleged use of european countries by the cia for the transport and illegal detention of prisoners, adopted by the ep, again calls on the eu institutions and member states to investigate in detail the cia's operations. in 2007, the final report of the tdip interim committee recommended, among other things, the monitoring of the cia's actions at a later stage, followed by the resolution adopted in 2012 asking the ep to return to the subject after one year. the resolution does not introduce any new elements and, moreover, makes recommendations that go beyond the powers of parliament and the eu. in addition to the legally incorrect paragraphs (which call into question the right of the italian head of state to grant a pardon), there are also false elements such as the responsibility of the member states for the existence of the guantanamo prison, due to their refusal to accept prisoners on their territory. the resolution addresses 13 member states, including romania, with a view to the prompt launch of an 'independent, impartial, thorough and effective' investigation into their involvement in the cia prison programme. the european parliament's right to investigate violations of fundamental rights by eu member states is strengthened, with the parliament reiterating its recommendations to the council, asking it to make a statement recognising the involvement of states in cia programmes.
in writing. i disagree with the reopening of the discussion about alleged cia prisons: since there is no new element, to debate again about the allegations seems like a pure electoral gesture. i also object to the re-launching of criticism of the romanian authorities in this case. there is no evidence whatsoever that there were secret cia detention centres on romanian territory or that romanian airports were used by the cia to transport or detain prisoners suspected of terrorist acts. in romania, a special committee of inquiry was set up at the senate level, which reached this conclusion as early as 2008. in addition, romania has cooperated transparently with all international investigative mechanisms. the paragraphs in the resolution on romania can only cast parliament in a bad light through the dubious sources used. we cannot rely on a tv broadcast of a former security official currently on trial for money laundering, nor on the statements of the former head of the foreign intelligence service during the neo-communist iliescu government. i vote against this text.
i agree with my colleague pirker. in the last 25 years, nearly 20,000 illegal migrants have drowned in the mediterranean sea. so far 231 bodies have been discovered in lampedusa. this tragedy shows us once again that regret is not enough to stop the lives lost. illegal migration not only costs lives but also increases human trafficking and smuggling of cigarettes and other contraband. eurosur, a european border surveillance system, aims to strengthen the external borders of the schengen area and ensure internal security by preventing crime. the union must increase its capacity to react by introducing a centralised system of cooperation between member states. in addition, we need to provide a common technical and operational framework for surveillance tools and also clear competences for all member states. only in this way can we protect the lives of migrants and ensure a european security area. and finally, let us not forget that extradition of persons to a state with a high risk of capital punishment or other inhumane punishments or torture is prohibited by the charter of fundamental rights of the european union.
first of all, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and wish him a very happy birthday. i am very grateful to the eurosur system, i am grateful for the work done and, of course, for the welcome from the commission. we talk a lot about the effects, we talk a lot about what happened and how tragic it is, but we talk far too little about the causes. at the moment we are dealing with, rather, with deficient systems in border control, particularly at maritime borders, with deficient cooperation on security between the member states of the european union or between the european union as a whole and african countries, and often with a lack of funds and intervention apparatus. i'll give you an example: i was recently on a delegation somewhere in the gulf of aden, to find out that there is a desire to combat piracy in an area of over 2,000 square kilometres, but without a monitoring system. the maritime police have no way of reaching the scene in record time to catch the perpetrators. so i think we need much better cooperation in terms of fighting piracy and we need better cooperation between the governments of the member states, the african states.
for national authorities to cooperate in combating crossborder crime, there must first be harmonisation of information channels between member states and, of course - i agree with my colleague - common standards in the member states. as rapporteur for the eurodac regulation, i know how the tools for exchanging information between member states work. the eurodac database - that is, the fingerprints database - allows national authorities to access information for the prevention of very serious crime and terrorism, for the identification of perpetrators, witnesses or victims. investigators can check whether organised crime networks or terrorist movements are trying to bring their members into the eu under false identities to allow them to stay legally in the eu and possibly commit serious crimes. that's why i argue that access to this data is very useful in the fight against cross-border crime. but member states cannot access the eurodac database unless they first search for information in another database, namely prüm, which now only operates in 11 member states, reducing access to information from the two systems, eurodac and prüm. member states that have not yet implemented the prüm decision must do so as soon as possible and thus put into practice the requirements of the european commission in order to be able to use information that is essential in the fight against cross-border crime.
we talk a lot about data protection, we talk a lot about transparency, we talk a lot about the desire to make as much information available to citizens to be successful in whatever direction we're talking about. we talk about free movement, but we fail to develop common standards, we fail to link existing institutions, and i tell you that recently i had the honour of hosting in the european parliament the so-called euhackathon event, where experts from 17 eu and non-eu countries analysed the transparency of data made available in the online spectrum versus the security of citizens. i tell you that in some cases the situation is still catastrophic within the european union, not to mention the relationship between the european union and other states. that is why i believe that the european commission must better link up the existing european systems, whether it is schengen, whether it is sis ii, whether it is eurodac and so on - europol, eurojustice - and secondly, we must provide concrete programmes for their implementation.

the 2006 battery directive sought to ban the use of cadmium, allowing only a few exceptions, because of the risks to the environment, but also because it has been associated with the risk of serious diseases such as cancer and cardiovascular disease. similarly, the use of mercury is restricted by european legislation, being classified as an occupational hazard with known physiological and psychological effects. the european union has a responsibility to protect both the environment and public health, but health, safety and environmental concerns often conflict with the needs of industry and even the individual needs of citizens for goods and services. that is why a balance in regulation is needed, and in this case i believe that balance has been reached. the current regulations have reduced the presence of these toxic substances in household products, thereby reducing the harmful effects on the environment and, consequently, our exposure to these substances. alternative and innovative technologies as well as environmentally friendly products were encouraged at the same time. this new inter-institutional agreement shows the success of these solutions, which means reducing pollution and health risks. i particularly welcome the council's acceptance of parliament's proposal on the design of household appliances, which encourages easy battery replacement. today, too many parts, even whole machines, are thrown away too easily. we have become a society that wastes a lot of goods and resources.
