in writing. − the european union is now the most important economic and trade player in the world. both in the light of the external trade developed by the member states of the union and in the light of the ever-increasing dynamics of trade relations between the member states, it is safe to say that the issue of trade rules and regulations is of the utmost importance to the european union. but this must be done in a moderate and effective manner. it is true that the union promotes the rule of law and is committed to supporting trade freedoms. at the same time, however, we must also take into account the social impact of the proposed changes and the need to meet the expectations of european consumers as fully as possible.
in writing. − as the eu does not currently have a horizontal legislative framework to ensure the exercise of its rights under the wto and other international trade agreements, i believe that the proposed instrument is intended to strengthen the exercise of eu trade rights and eu credibility and to convince our economic partners to respect the rules of the game laid down in trade agreements, with the aim of opening up new markets for the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the regulation on the application and enforcement of international trade rules. i consider it necessary to include the services sector within the scope of the concession suspension measures as provided for by the world trade organisation. it is also necessary to inform the european parliament of commercial disputes.
in writing. − we have believed and continue to believe in an open market and the economic added value of international trade. the eu is probably one of the most open markets in the world with a liberal trade policy. having an open market does not mean, however, that there are no rules. an open market is neither naive nor passive when our trading partners do not respect the commitments they have made and the rules of the game set at the world trade organisation, of which the eu is a member. therefore, in order to defend our commercial interests effectively and to ensure our credibility with our partners, i can only support the instrument proposed by the commission. in order to be able to react quickly to possible restrictive trade measures imposed by the union's trading partners, we need a clear framework, and the proposal adopted by parliament meets this requirement. obviously, adopting this framework does not mean that we will have to use retaliation systematically or more often than we have done so far. i still believe that the union's trade interests must be defended in a first phase through negotiation and only when it fails to move to restrictive measures.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report establishing the european maritime and fisheries fund for the period 2014-2020 and i welcome its adoption. the text adopted took into account a large number of requests from the socialist and democratic group, including the creation of new jobs instead of using the funds available to finance the purchase of new boats without a sustainable economic strategy. the fisheries fund will provide €6 billion to fund almost 60% of the subsidies to support fishermen during their forced inactivity, to encourage a gradual reduction in the fleet of active fishing vessels, and to build safer and more environmentally friendly vessels. the vote is an important step towards the development of a socially and ecologically sustainable european fisheries, which will also allow for a better distribution of european funds and a stricter control of their use. finally, it is a fundamental text to help preserve fish stocks which have been severely impacted by the growth of 'overfishing', which is a good signal from the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report. however, i regret the rejection of amendments which would have contributed significantly to the modernisation of small boats, which represent, for example, 95% of the romanian fishing fleet. i welcome the provisions favourable to coastal and small-scale fisheries. i also consider the provisions on support for aquaculture to be particularly important, given that only 6% of eu aquaculture products are produced in the member states, the rest being imported.
in writing. − i believe that the eu should remain at the forefront of developing technologies for a future green economy, with the aim of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 50% by 2030. the warsaw conference (cop 19) will be crucial for the preparation of commitments and the conclusion of a legally binding global agreement by 2015 in this area, placing the responsibility on governments to provide an adequate response to the climate challenges facing humanity.
in writing. − climate change is an urgent and potentially irreversible threat to human society, biodiversity and the planet, and therefore solutions must be found at international level. the warsaw conference (cop 19) will play a crucial role in ensuring the progress needed to move the durban platform forward, paving the way for the preparation of commitments and the conclusion of a legally binding global agreement by 2015, at the paris conference. it is very important that the european union, as a major player, has a unified position at the conference with a view to making progress towards an international agreement and remains united in this regard. the current economic crisis clearly demonstrates that only a sustainable economy can ensure long-term prosperity and that climate protection is one of the main pillars of such a sustainable economy. the challenges of climate change cannot be viewed from a separate perspective but must always be addressed in the context of sustainable development, industrial policy and resource policy. in this regard, i believe it is essential to explain climate change policies to citizens and change their mindsets.
in writing. − i believe that cooperation at regional, national and international level is essential to develop a coherent approach to climate change which threatens the ability of a large number of regions to provide the food their populations need. the european union needs to promote rural development, sustainable development, the productivity of agricultural systems and food security, especially in developing countries, to reduce their dependence on costly fossil fuel-based agricultural production factors, which will improve the livelihoods of poor rural communities. we must not forget that the production of agrofuels from oilseeds, palm oil, soybeans, rapeseed, sunflower seeds, sugar cane, sugar beet and wheat could lead to a very high demand for land and endanger people in poor countries whose livelihoods depend on access to land and natural resources.
in writing. − the security of citizens and consumers, freedom of movement, protection of businesses, free and fair competition, the need to avoid the distorting of the legal economic cycle by the accumulation of illicit funds and financial acquisitions, and the fundamental democratic principles underpinning the eu and the member states are all seriously threatened by the spread of organised crime, corruption and money laundering. excessive bureaucracy can also discourage legitimate economic activity and encourage corruption among public officials. corruption can undermine economic development through the misallocation of resources, in particular to the detriment of public services and, in particular, to the detriment of social services and assistance. it is important to establish stronger mechanisms to ensure transparency and integrity and to eliminate red tape in ministries and other public structures, including full access to information on every aspect of administrative organisation and activity, the exercise of institutional functions and the use of public resources, including by guaranteeing the right of citizens to access documents (starting with the very sensitive sector of public procurement procedures). the culture of legality and integrity in the public and private sectors should also be promoted, including through an effective whistleblower protection programme.
in writing. i would like to welcome the adoption of the report on organised crime, corruption and money laundering, which brings to a close the work of the european parliament's special committee for the study and analysis of these forms of organised crime. this text has sent a strong signal from the european parliament in the fight against these scourges. it called for the implementation of several major measures, such as the creation of a european public prosecutor or the introduction of stricter sanctions in the area of illegal sports betting. this text concerns the interests of european citizens. corruption and organised crime are serious violations of fundamental rights, such as the right to freedom of movement and to privacy. they involve serious consequences for the lives of thousands of victims. corruption and organised crime are also major economic problems, which lead to large financial losses, and this battle must be a priority in these times of crisis. a european approach is needed to organise a coherent legislative and legal framework. this report is part of that dynamic and should be welcomed.
in writing. − corruption and organised crime are a worldwide phenomenon, affecting eu countries as well, with a hugely negative impact both economically, with losses in the billions of euros, and humanly, when we think of the hundreds of thousands of victims of human trafficking, forced labour or sexual exploitation. organised crime also poses a threat to the safety of our citizens, as confirmed by the estimated 10 million illegal weapons circulating in the eu. despite their usefulness in everyday life, new technologies have brought new opportunities for organised crime, with cybercrime on the rise and causing significant material damage to internet users. a european action plan to combat corruption and crime is therefore needed, as suggested in the crim final report. many of the report's recommendations are quite ambitious and call for strong political will and much closer judicial and police cooperation between member states. however, in the face of a cross-border phenomenon of such a scale, tailor-made solutions and, above all, joint solutions are needed, as member states will not be able to defeat organised crime through individual actions.
in writing. − the eastern partnership is one of the most important elements of european foreign policy. beyond the specific interests or problems of the member states or even of the union at this level, it is important to remember that the union is first and foremost a forum for democratic principles and a space for sustainable development. the eastern partnership, in this perspective, is the instrument through which this political vision of governance and development of the european continent can be encouraged and effectively implemented. the european union has, over the past two decades, demonstrated its ability to build democratic formulas of supranational governance and to encourage democratic transition and development. we must not forget that, in the context of the evaluation of the eastern partnership, the commitment to democratic principles is the final benchmark in the evaluation of this foreign policy direction.
in writing. − the eu revised the european neighbourhood policy in 2011 to provide more support to partner countries, create a deep and sustainable democracy and support inclusive economic development. the eu's external financial instruments and in particular the european neighbourhood instrument should support the objectives of the neighbourhood policy, and strong and clear links need to be established between the policy framework and the support provided under those instruments. the government of moldova needs to continue to make sustained progress in implementing the necessary measures, political stability and lasting consensus on reforms, in particular on the rule of law and the independence of state institutions, are of fundamental importance for moldova's european aspirations. the initialling of the association agreement, including the deep and comprehensive free trade agreement, at the vilnius summit should be encouraged and i express my hope for a swift conclusion of the visa dialogue. the association agreement should be signed quickly in the near future (after the vilnius summit) if the current compatibility with the requirements is maintained. the opening of a new pipeline between moldova and romania is essential and continued efforts and resistance to pressure from russia to withdraw from the association agreement should be encouraged.
in writing. − despite pressure from the russian federation, the republic of moldova continued reforms this year to meet the european integration criteria, finalising ahead of schedule the negotiations for the association agreement and the deep and comprehensive free trade agreement. the republic of moldova has also implemented the necessary measures of the visa liberalisation action plan. the first commission report on the monitoring of the concrete measures in the action plan was positive, the next one will be published this year. if it is positive, i ask the european commission to give its opinion to lift the visa requirement for citizens of the republic of moldova. visa liberalisation is a concrete measure that will reward the efforts and determination of recent years and motivate the population to further support european integration.
in writing. − i very much welcome the content and especially the timing of this report. the vilnius summit will be a major test for eu’s neighbourhood. it is high time for the eu to show firm commitment towards its eastern partners. however, the report mentions that the unsatisfactory progress made by some eastern partners is caused by a failure by the eu to show its eastern partners a sufficiently motivating european perspective. i would put it more bluntly and say that the unsatisfactory progress is linked to the lack of a clear membership perspective. we have shied away from this issue long enough. i believe it merits discussion after vilnius.
in writing. − the european union continues to face many challenges. the effects of the economic crisis have not yet been fully overcome and their social impact remains high. furthermore, the consolidation of a stable economic and monetary union remains an objective that is not fully achieved. equally, the political and economic support of small and medium-sized enterprises is essential for the union's economic success, as 75% of the workforce and 60% of the value added is generated at this level. politically, the most difficult problem that coordination and planning efforts reveal is the need for the european institutions to work together more effectively. for the european project to remain legitimate among european citizens, respect for the legislative framework, but above all involvement in the political debate of the european parliament, alongside the other institutions, remains essential.
in writing. − the commission and the council must continue to improve the indicators for monitoring the social dimension of the europe 2020 strategy in the context of the european semester. several member states have undertaken major labour market reforms to increase labour market resilience, introduce more flexibility at home and abroad, reduce segmentation and facilitate the transition from one job to another. member states with low levels of labour market participation should, in consultation with the social partners, step up active, comprehensive and inclusive labour market measures and introduce other reforms to facilitate access to quality jobs, prevent early withdrawals from the labour market, combat labour market segmentation and align workers' skills with labour market requirements. as regards youth unemployment, the adoption by the council of the youth guarantee and the allocation of eur 6 billion for the youth employment initiative as part of the next mff is a positive development, as member states now need to urgently introduce youth guarantee schemes and make efficient use of available resources.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies and i welcome its adoption by the european parliament. this report constitutes the european parliament's study of the second stage of the 2013 half-yearly cycle on economic coordination. it contains country-specific recommendations (csrs) issued by the commission and the council for the year 2013. it stresses the fundamental need to improve economic coordination within the european union, that the slowdown in fiscal consolidation has produced satisfactory results, and that all eu member states have a particular role to play in correcting the imbalances in the euro area. i am pleased to note that this report calls for better coordination of the eu's objectives around the eu 2020 strategy, particularly with regard to its social inclusion objectives in country-specific recommendations. finally, it stressed the need to develop coordinated investment in job creation, which is a crucial issue in order to revive growth in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on mediterranean migration flows. in the light of the tragedy in lampedusa, the union must review its migration policy. better coordination at european level and common tools are needed to save lives and help those seeking asylum.
in writing. the recent tragedies in the mediterranean should be a turning point for the european union and its migration policy. the only solution to these successive tragedies is a coordinated approach based on the principles of solidarity and responsibility, supported by existing and recently adopted instruments. the european parliament's position on the proposal for a regulation establishing a european border surveillance system (eurosur), adopted at first reading on 10 october, is a step forward in european coordination in this field. the eu and its member states must also continue to push for new measures to promote legal immigration and prevent further tragedies. the european union must continue to guarantee the human rights of migrants, asylum seekers and refugees, especially unaccompanied minors. i welcome the adoption of this resolution and the growing attention of the eu and the member states to this central issue which should enable us to develop a comprehensive strategy that places labour migration in the context of the social, economic and political development of the union's neighbourhood.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the intolerable living conditions in the countries of origin have caused a major increase in the number of immigrants in the european union. in their attempt to enter the union, they travel by sea in small and inadequate vessels that pose a danger to their own lives. the tragedy that took place in southern italy, where more than 360 people lost their lives trying to reach the continent, is a european drama and it is regrettable that such an event took place and that the union could do nothing to prevent it. i therefore believe that a european programme is needed that has the financial and human resources to detect such ships in good time. the increase in the budget for easo and frontex is necessary to prevent such an incident from occurring in the future and to protect the lives of people who for various reasons are exposed to very high risks. thank you !
in writing. − the swift agreement is a particularly important instrument in the fight against terrorism, which unfortunately still poses a threat to member states. this agreement received the support of parliament after lengthy discussions on the guarantees it offers in the field of personal data protection. therefore, i do not believe that the agreement should be suspended without having certainties about practices that are contrary to the principles agreed between the us and the eu. nor can we remain indifferent to the newly revealed elements of surveillance by the us national security agency. but i think that a serious investigation by the european commission is needed so that we have clear data on what actually happened. in my view, these data do not exist at the moment and therefore we do not have sufficient solid grounds to take a suspension decision that will have serious consequences. we must not lose sight of the fact that, to protect our own citizens, we need a policy of tracking terrorist financing. suspending the agreement without the eu having its own capacity to extract this data would leave us completely unprotected and i don't think it's in the best interest of european citizens.
in writing. - the terrorist attacks of 11 september 2001 in the usa, but also those on the territory of the european union in madrid in 2004, london in 2005, and those planned by the extremist breivik on the island of utøya in 2011 show us that europe is not immune to terrorist attacks either. the eu-us agreement on the processing and transfer of financial messaging data from the eu to the united states protects european citizens from possible terrorist acts through the terrorist finance tracking program (tftp) and the swift network, respectively, as of 1 august 2010. the agreement contains important safeguards with regard to confidentiality and protection of personal data. the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms and council convention no 108 provide for the protection of individuals with regard to the automated processing of personal data. for this reason, the allegations of espionage and financial data theft by the nsa that have appeared in the press must be taken seriously. if there's a breach of the agreement, action must be taken. the european union needs a strong security system to protect its citizens. until we have credible explanations and evidence of these facts it is irresponsible to suspend the agreement and put the protection of citizens at risk.
in writing. − this legislative proposal from the european commission intends to introduce the 7th environment action programme for the period 2013-2020. among other things, it would require third countries to be as involved as the union is in environmental and climate issues. it is important that the eu does not remain isolated in its efforts and can rely on strong partners. the eu must better define the conditions for access to its market and not open it up unless third countries protect the environment, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and ensure that european businesses are not disadvantaged by unfair competition. in my view, the development of environmental civility should be a priority, a factor of progress.
in writing. − the environmental challenges we face today (climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution, waste, public health risks, etc.) remain significant and cannot be ignored or treated lightly. i am confident that the new general programme of action of the union will ensure a high level of environmental protection and guarantee quality of life through equitable and sustainable welfare for citizens. the new eu environmental policy framework proposes an ambitious and realistic approach to environmental problems and also includes solutions to overcome the crisis by promoting green economic growth. we can and must have economic growth and create new jobs while respecting the environment, using resources efficiently and focusing on innovation and business competitiveness. the proposals in the new action programme will ensure that european environmental legislation is based on sound scientific knowledge, is more coherent and simpler, and is therefore better accepted and applied. i also welcome the attention paid to the need and importance of raising awareness, informing and involving european citizens in the european union's environmental policy so that they become actors in the protection, conservation, enhancement and exploitation of natural capital.
in writing. − the european union is and wants to remain an important player in environmental protection and as such should send a strong political message to third countries to help create international environmental governance and combat climate change.
in writing. − this proposal for a revision of the directive is a step towards improving the protection of citizens against exposure to ionising radiation. the amendments were based on the latest scientific data and knowledge in the field and will remove contradictory and outdated provisions in existing legislation. in addition, in order to ensure better protection of the public, the provisions of the directive will also take into account natural radiation sources as well as naturally occurring radioactive materials. i supported the adoption of the amendments.
in writing. − the proposal to reform the council's basic safety rules directive is another step towards improving protection against exposure to ionising radiation, mainly by removing contradictory provisions from existing legislation and incorporating the latest scientific data and knowledge into current legislation. i welcome the fact that natural radiation sources are taken into account for the first time in the directive on basic safety standards, in order to guarantee better protection for the general public. the presence of radioactive substances in the environment has consequences for the protection of public health. in addition to the direct routes of exposure, environmental protection as a whole must be considered in a general, comprehensive and coherent framework. in this context, i believe that more resources should be allocated to examining in detail the consequences of ionising radiation on both the population and the environment. it is important to ensure a high level of protection, but without imposing disproportionate burdens on member states in terms of implementation. regulatory regimes in the member states are very different from each other and a uniform approach is therefore not appropriate. member states need an appropriate degree of flexibility to implement legislation in accordance with their own practices.
in writing. − the european union cannot define its foreign policy without remaining faithful to the principles of democracy and the rule of law. the union is built around these principles, which is why it cannot afford not to pursue their promotion in its own foreign policy or their inclusion as a fundamental element of the emerging international order. it is equally important that the union demonstrate, through a robust and effective policy, its capacity to act decisively to protect the security and interests of its citizens. last but not least, the union and its member states need to show additional flexibility to deal with the security challenges we face, ranging from the impact of climate change to issues such as food security or energy security.
in writing. − the global financial crisis is creating major political, economic, social, cultural and environmental challenges, including domestic issues, for all parties and addressing such challenges requires collective and united eu action and the creation of alliances, in order to promote peace, security, social progress, prosperity, the rule of law and respect for human rights. in this context, i believe that european external action must be understood and supported by eu citizens.
in writing. - i voted for this report. i regret, however, that another year has passed without any progress in resolving the frozen conflict in the transnistrian region. the russian federation is using this situation to blackmail the republic of moldova and prevent it from moving to europe. this year, tension increased in the region when, in april 2013, the so-called 'transnistrian authorities' tried to introduce checkpoints on the so-called administrative line on the dniester river. another challenge came in july 2013 when a russian federation government publication announced that russian forces in the transnistria region would be reinforced by helicopters. on october 11, the vice president of the russian federation threatened that "transnistria is preparing a tough response to the authorities in chisinau in case of the republic of moldova's accession to the eu". despite these direct threats to its territorial integrity, the republic of moldova is determined to continue on its european path. its efforts to implement the reforms needed for european integration must be rewarded with concrete action at the right time. the signing of the association agreement and the deep and comprehensive free trade agreement is to take place before autumn 2014.
in writing. − one of the most important problems facing the european electronic communications sector is the major differences between the implementation and enforcement of the european legislative framework. these gaps are one of the most important obstacles to increased investment and the development of european communications. the important technological advances of recent years also make it imperative to adapt european legislation to the new realities in this field. i support the adoption of the report because many of its recommendations can contribute to the development of a competitive european electronic communications sector, based on innovation and investment, which offers high benefits to both european consumers and businesses. i also agree with the importance of closer and more efficient cooperation between national regulators in the field of electronic communications and national competition authorities.
in writing. − the roaming regulation was adopted only last year, imposing a series of structural measures on transport operators, designed to create competition and thus push down the prices of roaming services at national level. considering that the regulation is to be revised in 2016, i would like to mention that i am in favour of the abolition of roaming charges and hope that this measure will gain the support of parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mrs trautmann on the communication system, access to services, networks and guarantees of the competition regime. the evolution of the technological spectrum at our disposal requires a thorough review of the regulatory framework governing access and competition rules in the electronic communications market. such review should be carried out with the involvement of stakeholders to ensure that a stable and durable framework can be provided.
in writing. − the internal market for electronic communications is a necessity in the union today. it is therefore necessary that the commission's regulations are applied by the member states in a uniform manner and within the relevant time limits. different implementations by member states only fragment the internal market for electronic communications, directly affecting innovation, economic growth and the provision of competitive prices for all european citizens. in view of the technological developments of recent years, a review of the framework is necessary to further promote an ecosystem of competition and investment for the benefit of final consumers. it is necessary to include broadband internet access at a fair price in the universal service. it is also necessary to confer powers on national regulatory authorities in all respects to ensure the proper implementation of the framework.
reporting for opinion of the committee on industry, research and energy. − mr president, commissioner, investment in education, research and innovation is essential for industrial policy and for the union's competitiveness. as rapporteur of the itre commission, i supported the commission's proposal and called for the inclusion of the european union's industrial policy among the relevant union policies for the 'erasmus for all' programme. the itre committee requested the inclusion of the mobility of persons for educational purposes, including in the field of entrepreneurship, among the objectives and actions of the programme and supported the eligibility of phd students pursuing a phd in another participating country for the guarantee of loans to phd students resident in a participating country. i consider it important to ensure access to the programme for non-governmental organisations, especially youth organisations, in areas such as education, training, youth and mass sport. i believe that there is a need to increase the number of people over 35 years of age who benefit from lifelong learning. for the sake of transparency, i consider it important to define the performance criteria in an annex to the regulation, rather than by delegated acts.
mr president, we have spoken a great deal in recent years about an inclusive economy, a knowledge-based economy, a sustainable economy, we have spoken about fighting unemployment. finally, we have, especially among young people, a very coherent programme, a programme that celebrated its 25th anniversary last year, a programme that is now much better structured and has much better funding. we cannot think of a single economy, a single european market, if we do not talk about a single labour market, if we do not talk about the mobility of young people within the borders of the european union, if we do not talk about the exchange of experience between universities, if we do not talk about the same workforce with uniformly developed skills, if we do not talk about higher education graduates who have the same preparation for the labour market throughout the european union, and of course if we do not talk about lifelong learning. i think that this project should be welcomed and the way in which the committee on budgets supported the funding of this project should be welcomed.
thank you very much, mr president, and i would also like to congratulate my colleague, mrs doris pack, on her contribution to the improvement of this programme. i really appreciate this report because it is the first time that all the education programmes will be brought together in a common framework. the over eur 14 billion allocated to the programme is a signal that the union is supporting educational mobility, especially in the context of high youth unemployment. the benefits of an erasmus grant are not limited to the period spent in a particular country. it can open up the way to professional mobility after graduation or it can give rise to business ideas in the home country. i also believe that more attention should be paid to the mobility of students from the eastern neighbourhood and that next year more scholarships should be awarded to students from the republic of moldova.
erasmus is one of the best-known and most successful european union programmes, regardless of what we mean by it. for millions of students, it is not just about studying abroad, acquiring new knowledge, but also about discovering the continent, experiencing european identity in practice, respecting otherness and taking on new challenges. nothing serves the idea of a common europe better than erasmus, because these young adults will shape the future of the continent. it is therefore important to address possible financial obstacles through erasmus and its sister programmes and to avoid any question of the eligibility of programmes during the next seven-year planning cycle.
mr president, i support the proposal of the european commission and the rapporteur to change the structure of the regulation, to identify more precisely the sub-programmes corresponding to the different sectors of education and training, to define more clearly the specific objectives assigned to the different sub-programmes, and to include a programme for sport. i believe it is important to strengthen the links between education and employment, between education and poverty reduction, and lifelong learning by addressing unemployment, especially youth unemployment, and poverty by promoting active citizenship and active ageing. it is also necessary to improve the accessibility of the programme, i.e. to promote greater participation of persons with special needs or educational, social, gender, physical, psychological, geographical, economic or cultural difficulties.
reporting for opinion of the committee on industry, research and energy. − thank you, mr president, commissioner, the creative and cultural sectors make an important contribution to employment and economic growth, providing 4.5% of europe's total gdp and 3.8% of its workforce. as rapporteur for the itre commission, i supported the introduction of new specific objectives of the programme, which strengthen its components relating to the adaptation of the creative and cultural sectors to globalisation and digitalisation. the digitisation of products of the creative and cultural sectors offers economic opportunities and is a key condition for the future development of europe's cultural and creative capacities. the accessibility of cultural material online will allow citizens across europe to benefit from it. a public-private partnership is needed to create new ways of financing. we called for better, legal and attractive online offerings to encourage artistic creation and protect copyright, and for a clear budget allocation for each of the three components of the programme. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs silvia costa.
rapporteur. − mr president, i am very satisfied at this successful outcome for the connecting europe facility (cef) after a year and a half of hard work and good cooperation with my co-rapporteurs on transport, ms ayala sender and mr riquet, whom i warmly thank for their constructive approach to this complex issue. tomorrow we will vote on this new european instrument which will earmark eur 33 billion for investment to improve europe’s transport, energy and telecommunications networks. this new funding instrument is potentially a real revolution and, at the least, a shift of paradigm. it is the only growth policy in the eu budget for the coming seven years. in times of crisis we are obliged to be creative in order to respond with limited means to the challenges we face. with the cef, public money will be spent in the most efficient way by maximising the use of innovative financial instruments. these instruments have the capacity to create a leverage effect by attracting private funding that is available on the world capital markets, and thereby to multiply by up to 15 or 20 times the initial budget. through the cef, we are sending a positive message to world investors, telling them that europe is still an attractive and innovative capital market. it is ever more important to invest in our infrastructures, for they are the primary growth generators in all sectors of the economy. however, they are on the verge of becoming outdated and are insufficiently interconnected. as a consequence, there is a real risk of market fragmentation and renationalisation of energy, transport and telecommunications policies if the current state of play is maintained. when we know that our needs for upgrading and interconnecting our infrastructure amount to eur 1.5 trillion, we have no choice but to work alongside the private sector so as to leverage financial resources on a massive scale. the cef also marks a shift in mentality as it focuses on financing projects which have european added value only. this requires us to envisage the common good for europe and to shift away from the traditional nationalist behaviour pattern of 28 member states each fighting over the financial envelope. with a total budget of eur 33 billion, it is still necessary to decide what political priorities are to be financed. that is what parliament has discussed in depth with the council, and i am satisfied we have agreed in broad terms that, with eur 5.8 billion, the european union will make substantial improvements in order to complete the internal energy market, interconnect our member states’ and regional submarkets and ensure security of supply. a number of european projects of common interest have already been identified and they will be given priority in relation to permits and funding. for countries in eastern europe, this is a much awaited response to investment needs. to take romania as an example, projects like white stream will allow better interconnection and integration within the european energy market. as key growth drivers, the digital economy and the telecoms sector will benefit from eur 1.1 billion to support investment in a pan-european digital service. this should allow the deployment on a large scale of online and cross-border services of public interest, benefiting european citizens and businesses. in today’s world it is crucial for europe to create an environment defined by competitiveness and smart growth, and to make the eu market attractive to investors once again. i am convinced that the connecting europe facility is, above all, the right tool for boosting our competitiveness and creating a basis for growth.
thank you, madam president. the competitiveness of the union depends on the provision of an integrated trans-european transport network. the disparities between the eastern and western parts of the union in transport infrastructure can be reduced by implementing the projects identified in the ten-t and the connecting europe facility regulations. both regulations provide for annexes and maps in which romania is present, but i consider that important regions of romania are not included in the core network. i welcome the fact that the amendments were adopted, which have led to the inclusion of the sebeș - alba iulia - turda - cluj napoca - dej - suceava - pascani - iași route on the central railway network for freight and passengers, the carrying out of studies and works for the high-speed railway network on the bucharest - constanța route, the inclusion of the port of galați in the central ten-t network and the development of multimodal platforms for the ports of giurgiu and galați, the inclusion on the central network of the hungary - iași - târgu mureș - sebeș - turdaș connection, the calafat - craiova - bucharest section and the global network of the constanța - galați - brăilați section. i ask the plenary to support amendments 200 and 199 to the ten-t regulation and amendments 136 to 139 to the connecting europe facility regulation, in which i have asked for the buzău - brăila - galați section to be included in the central road and rail network and for the via carpathia route to be added to the list of transport corridors and also for the galați - giurgiulești section, including the bypass of the municipality of galați, to be included in the central road network. finally, i regret that the methodology used by the commission for identifying ten-t projects is not part of the annex to the ten-t regulation. thank you, madam president.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, thank you very much for the overwhelmingly positive comments about this very big plan. taken as a whole, the trans-european networks, in conjunction with the connecting europe facility financing mechanism, may even constitute the biggest overall project under this multiannual financial framework, so it really is a big plan. we can be satisfied that we have now reached a certain final point in decision making concerning this plan. of course, a lot of specific ideas were aired, which is not surprising, and they were not new to me. but if we want to create a real european infrastructure network, we need a plan and that plan should avoid a patchwork of national projects. this was the main aim. the first step was to create a methodology. together with parliament we adopted a methodology for creating a plan, a map. on the basis of that methodology, we now have a trans-european networks plan following, as you all know, three years of negotiations: first of all with the governments and then with parliament about the proposal by the commission. now this plan is more or less ready. the great thing is that we now have not only a plan but also money for financing the plan. we have the connecting europe facility, which is a real major novelty. it started three years ago, from the proposal to create a transport infrastructure fund, and we now have the connecting europe facility. of course, the needs are much greater. nonetheless, we should appreciate the decision to increase substantially the financing for the transport networks and also the energy networks. so it is now a big plan, and clearly this is not the end of the story. the next stage will be the implementation of the plan, and no one should underestimate the difficulties along the way. there will be delays and conflicting views but still, with regard to the main aim and what we have achieved together, we have a much clearer framework of rules about how this infrastructure should be developed. that is a great achievement, so i hope there will be a positive vote on these two regulations tomorrow, and that we can then continue to push for implementation, to follow what governments are doing and to ensure that society reaps full benefit from this plan.

thank you, mr president, and colleagues. allergies are among the most common diseases in the world, affecting over 150 million europeans. it is estimated that this so-called 'modern disease' will affect one in two people in the future. allergies are becoming more common and more aggressive. they occur quite early in life and are caused by a variety of factors, cumulative, that can be prevented to some extent. allergies affect mainly children and adolescents and represent a socioeconomic risk factor due to the impact of these conditions on school performance, social life and overall quality of life. in this context, i would like to ask my colleagues for their support for a more active involvement of member states in actions to reduce the impact of allergies on society. we need preventive action in this area, as we need national multidisciplinary programmes to effectively manage this disease. educational programmes for children, their families and teachers are needed, as well as investment in research and adequate training of healthcare staff.
mr president, the final agreement on the multiannual financial framework, which came after a long period of extremely difficult negotiations, can be considered a success. it is true that the council won the case, succeeding in imposing the budget reduction. this was mainly due to the current context, still marked by the crisis, complemented by the budgetary difficulties faced by member states and the financial discipline imposed by the new european regulations. parliament has secured two very important instruments from the negotiations that can be used in the long term - full flexibility between years at the level of payments and increased flexibility between years and headings at the level of commitments - and that will facilitate a much more efficient use of funds, as well as the review clause, which will allow it to reassess the union's budgetary priorities in the light of the economic situation at the time. i congratulate parliament's negotiating team on the results achieved, in particular on securing all outstanding payments for 2013, and equally the rapporteurs on horizontal policies, who have finalised the agreements on legal bases, in particular for the cohesion and agriculture policies, using the codecision procedure successfully. the agreement reached is far from meeting parliament's expectations, but a further delay in the vote would have irreversibly damaged the continuity of many programmes financed from the union budget, especially in cohesion policy, and would have generated instability at union level.
in writing. the draft multiannual financial framework is a compromise. unfortunately, we cannot speak of a real success of our legislative forum: it is the first time in the history of the european union that the european parliament votes for a budget that is reduced compared to the previous multiannual framework. the council has also succeeded in imposing a policy of austerity at european level, to the detriment of the interests of european citizens. the amount of eur 908 billion for payment appropriations does not correspond to the eur 960 billion for commitment appropriations. however, i cannot but welcome the efforts of my colleagues on the negotiating team to introduce more flexibility in the use of funds so that more funds can be allocated to tackling youth unemployment, the 'erasmus for all' programme and supporting small and medium-sized enterprises. i also welcome the allocation of an additional eur 1 billion for the fund for european aid to the most deprived. i hope that the next european legislature will use the review clause to reassess budgetary priorities so that they are focused on growth and investment in human capital.

in writing. − the agreement reached on the multiannual financial framework is a cornerstone for the future of the european union, as it is, in effect, an investment plan that supports growth for the next seven years. this long-term budget, which will be implemented from 1 january 2014, supports and encourages investment in jobs, research and education, while focusing on supporting small and medium-sized enterprises. young people are one of the groups most affected by the crisis, with acute unemployment in many eu member states. i therefore welcome the fact that the union budget for 2014-2020 provides for a special flexibility in the allocation of money to address youth unemployment as effectively as possible. the flexibility clause will allow for an assessment of the functioning of the mff by the end of 2016 and, depending on the economic situation at that time, the commission may come forward with a legislative proposal to revise the mff. by introducing this clause, the european union is demonstrating its ability to respond to the real needs of citizens and businesses by directing existing funds in the most effective way.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. the new financial framework introduces for the period 2014-2020 a special flexibility to address youth unemployment and strengthen research (article 15) and sets the contribution to the financing of large-scale projects (article 16). thus, under article 15, an amount of up to eur 2543 million (2011 prices) may be concentrated at the beginning of the period, in 2014 and 2015, as part of the annual budgetary procedure, for certain policy objectives relating to youth employment, research, erasmus, in particular for apprentices and small and medium-sized enterprises. as regards large-scale projects, from the general budget of the union for the period 2014-2020, a maximum of eur 7 billion shall be made available to the european satellite navigation programmes (egnos and galileo), a maximum of eur 2 707 million to the iter project (international thermonuclear experimental reactor) and eur 786 million shall be made available to the european earth monitoring programme (copernicus). the new financial framework also introduces a compensation mechanism for budget reduction, maintains the level of funding of the fund for the most deprived persons and maintains a high financial commitment for the european social fund.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament decision on the conclusion of an interinstitutional agreement between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline, cooperation in budgetary matters and sound financial management. the objective of the agreement adopted in accordance with article 295 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union is to implement budgetary discipline and to improve the functioning of the annual budgetary procedure and the cooperation between the institutions on budgetary matters, as well as to ensure sound financial management. budgetary discipline covers all expenditure and the agreement is binding on all institutions for the duration of its validity. it is composed of three parts: part i contains supplementary provisions on the multiannual financial framework (mff) and provisions on special instruments not included in the mff; part ii concerns interinstitutional cooperation during the budgetary procedure; part iii contains provisions on the sound financial management of union funds. under the agreement, in 2017, the commission shall update the forecasts for payment appropriations for the period after 2020. that update shall take into account all relevant information, including the actual implementation of the commitment appropriations and the payment appropriations, as well as the forecasts for implementation.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the protocol amending the agreement on government procurement approving the conclusion of the protocol. the government procurement agreement (gpa) is, to date, the only legally binding world trade organisation agreement on government procurement. the current version (aap 1994) was negotiated in parallel with the uruguay round in 1994 and entered into force on 1 january 1996. the parties to the 1994 gpa are: armenia, canada, the european union with respect to the 27 member states, hong kong (china), iceland, israel, japan, korea, liechtenstein, the netherlands with respect to aruba, norway, singapore, switzerland, chinese taipei and the united states. the revised gpa text provides for a higher level of clarity and transparency and guarantees equal treatment in public procurement procedures between suppliers, goods and services originating in the states parties to the gpa. to this end, the eu has succeeded in getting the revised gpa text restructured to follow the sequential order of a public procurement procedure and to align the text with the eu public procurement directives. the revised text contains entirely new provisions, which constitute an improvement in the conditions for the participation of eu suppliers abroad.
in writing. −'erasmus for all' brings together all current eu and international systems in the fields of education, training and sport, replacing seven existing programmes with one. this will increase efficiency, facilitate the application for grants and reduce duplication and fragmentation. the new programme will focus on eu added value and systemic impact, with support for three types of actions: learning opportunities for individuals both inside and outside the eu; institutional cooperation between educational institutions, youth organisations, businesses, local and regional authorities and ngos; and support for reforms in the member states, modernisation of education and training systems and promotion of innovation, entrepreneurship and employability.
in writing. − the proposed programme integrates all current programmes and actions in the field of education: higher education (erasmus, erasmus mundus, tempus and bilateral programmes between the eu and third countries), school education (comenius), vocational education and training (leonardo da vinci), adult education (grundtvig) and youth (youth in action). it also includes provisions on jean monnet activities and a separate chapter on sport. activities under the 'youth in action' initiative should continue and be adequately funded. for reasons of transparency and independence, it is essential to have both a chapter and a separate budget line for youth. if the eu wants a smart, sustainable and inclusive economy, it must also take into account the personal development of young people, their social integration and their active involvement in society. student mobility is important to introduce 'social criteria' in the award of erasmus grants, allowing students with low income to benefit from mobility periods without fear of lack of sufficient financial resources. for students working abroad, the combination of erasmus mobility for traineeships (part-time activity) and for studies with an increased grant would allow for a combined social, professional and academic integration in the host country.
in writing. − the 'erasmus for all' programme aims to contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and the strategic framework for vocational education and training in 2020. i believe it is important to strengthen the links between education and employment, between education and poverty reduction, and lifelong learning, by addressing unemployment (especially youth unemployment) and poverty, by promoting active citizenship and active ageing. there is also a need to improve accessibility to the programme, i.e. to promote greater participation by persons with special needs or educational, social, gender, physical, psychological, geographical, economic and cultural difficulties.
in writing. i voted in favour of the new erasmus for all programme and i welcome its adoption by the european parliament. it builds on previous eu initiatives to promote exchanges and the development of a european programme for education, training and employment of young people. the aim of this new system is to improve efficiency, accessibility and simplify the rules and procedures necessary to submit an application. erasmus is a major eu programme which has enabled millions of young people to have a rewarding travel and learning experience. it is one of the most successful initiatives, which has managed to gain a good deal of publicity, and i therefore welcome its longevity and the renewed dynamism of this new programme. in particular, i would like to emphasise that the new erasmus programme will have a stronger social dimension, by improving opportunities for education and training for young people from low-income social backgrounds and vulnerable groups. finally, it is good that the socialists and democrats have fought for continued support for non-governmental organisations in the education and youth employment sectors.
in writing. - with the approval of the new erasmus package, we wanted to strengthen one of the most successful programmes of the european union. with an allocation of some €15 billion over the next seven years, we expect to involve over 5 million students and to allow the most deserving to benefit from scholarships of up to €18,000 for master's degrees at the most prestigious european universities. it is one of the eu's most successful programmes and we are rightly proud of it. the new erasmus programme will provide more training and cultural enrichment opportunities for many young people of merit, who will be able to compare themselves with one another and grow up in a truly european atmosphere.
in writing. − i welcome the commission's intention to reduce the administrative provisions that exist in the current 'continuing education' programme, but at the same time i consider it inappropriate to change the name of the programme to 'erasmus for all' in the next multiannual financial framework. the name proposed by the commission could be misleading, as the name erasmus is well known and associated with the mobility of students in higher education. this could give citizens the impression that we have neglected areas such as school education or vocational education and training, while also having a negative impact on the success of the new programme and creating confusion among users. the new programme should focus on reducing barriers to accessing funding and administrative costs, while maintaining and strengthening the current names of the fields of education. this would give continuity to an already successful programme.
in writing. - i voted for this report. in its 26 years of operation, the erasmus programme has provided educational mobility for 3 million young people. since its launch in romania 16 years ago, over 41 000 people have benefited from this programme. i support replacing the current seven education programmes with one that brings together all european initiatives in the fields of youth, education and training and sport. this will reduce the existing overlaps and fragmentation. among the key actions, i consider the most important one to be 'cooperation for innovation and good practice', which aims to promote entrepreneurship. the formation of 'knowledge alliances' and 'sectoral skills alliances' between education institutions and enterprises will stimulate innovation among young people and long-term employability. partnerships between schools and businesses will produce the specialists the economy needs.

in writing. −'creative europe' (2014-2020) is the community funding framework which will continue the current culture (2007-2013), media (2007-2013) and media mundus programmes. the programme will have three distinct components: media, culture and a cross-sectoral component dedicated to guaranteeing bank loans to the cultural and creative sectors and cooperation in the field of cultural policies. the new loan guarantee mechanism should lead to the creation of new financing opportunities for micro-enterprises and smes in the cultural and creative sectors. all potential project developers including video game creators, small theatre groups or individual artists will be able to access loans contracted with european banks and partly guaranteed through this programme. the culture strand of the creative europe programme will in particular encourage the professional capacity building of cultural workers, the operational capacity building of organisations offering international professional development opportunities, the transnational circulation of cultural works and the long-term development of audiences for these european cultural works.

in writing. − the rise of populism and euroscepticism in the european union in recent years is triggered by the economic, financial and social crisis and is at the root of a crisis of citizens' trust in the european union. to counteract extremist political currents, the european union must act and engage in a real dialogue with its citizens. article 10 of the treaty on european union stresses the principle of representative democracy and the right of every citizen to participate in the democratic life of the union. in addition, article 11 of the treaty sets out the union's obligation to have an open, transparent and constant dialogue with civil society. the 'europe for citizens' programme for 2014-2020 consists of two major components: (a) historical memory and european citizenship and (b) democratic engagement and civic participation. the aim of the programme is to strengthen european identity and increase interaction between citizens and the european union on concrete issues. the added value of the new programme is that it establishes a closer link with citizens by building transnational structures, without duplicating the consultation process at union level.
in writing. − at a time when citizens are expressing a high level of distrust in eu institutions and policies, the union must show vision and support civil society projects. the 'europe for citizens' programme is one such example, the overall objective being to enable all citizens to get to know each other and interact by engaging in common projects that strengthen the sense of belonging to the community. although the funds allocated to the programme are limited, i hope that we will be able to finance even small projects, supporting solidarity and the idea of volunteering in matters of common european interest. coming from a country where regionalization has many more steps to go, i support the importance of public decisions being taken as transparently and as closely as possible to the citizen. i want people to be able to express themselves freely, in any situation, on all issues of european, regional or local policy. also, in a context where euroscepticism is gaining ground, i believe it is important to remember europe's common past through debates on our history, our values and the future objectives of the union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft council regulation establishing the 'europe for citizens' programme for the period 2014-2020. the programme has a budget of eur 185 468 000 and is implemented by the commission through the adoption of annual work programmes. the objectives of the programme are to contribute to european citizens' understanding of history and its diversity and to promote european citizenship and improve conditions for civic and democratic participation at union level. the programme shall finance the following types of actions, implemented at transnational level or with a european dimension: - mutual learning and cooperation activities (citizens' meetings, twinning of cities, networks of twinned cities; projects implemented through transnational partnerships; projects on historical memory with a european dimension; exchanges based on the use of information and communication technologies and/or social platforms); - structural support for organisations; - analytical activities at union level; - awareness-raising and dissemination activities aimed at the further use and exploitation of the results of the supported initiatives and at highlighting good practice. the programme is open to all stakeholders promoting european integration and citizenship, in particular local and regional authorities and organisations, twinning committees, european public policy research organisations, civil society organisations, as well as cultural, youth, education and research organisations.
in writing. − i would like to express my support for the regulation proposing to set up the connecting europe facility, which will finance investments that will help achieve the objective of economic growth and competitiveness in the fields of transport, energy and telecommunications. through the connecting europe facility, eur 50 billion will be invested over the period 2014-2020, of which eur 31,7 billion will be for the modernisation of transport infrastructure, eur 9,1 billion for the modernisation of energy infrastructure and eur 9,2 billion to support investments in fast and ultra-fast broadband networks and pan-european digital services. the european union will in the near future have robust, high-performing and reliable transport, energy and telecommunications systems and infrastructures that contribute to the competitiveness of its economy, the dynamism of its economic and industrial sectors and sustainable, balanced and inclusive economic growth.
