in writing. − i support the rapporteurs' view that there is a need for a european union-wide vision of a long-distance corridor that crosses national borders. there are currently a number of obstacles (technical, administrative and infrastructure) to achieving fluid, interoperable and intermodal transport, and these have negative effects on competition in europe by increasing costs and reducing the reliability of the supply chain. in addition, the more peripheral countries are affected, which leads to discrepancies in terms of territorial cohesion in the eu, and projects in cross-border sections are neglected.
in writing. − we talk more and more about europe 2020 and efficient growth, but we forget that only a small part of the key points of economic development (such as airports or ports) are directly connected to the rail network. without interconnection and integration of all regions in the union, in particular in the areas of transport, energy and telecommunications, the union's economic growth will rapidly plateau, preventing us from achieving the objectives we set out to achieve. only through smart investment in infrastructure will we be able to move towards sustainable economic growth. i therefore consider it necessary that investment in union infrastructure focuses on a few key projects that provide maximum added value and i welcome the adoption of the connecting europe facility.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing the connecting europe facility (cef). the cef will invest eur 29 billion over the period 2014-2020, of which eur 23 billion for the modernisation of transport infrastructure, eur 5 billion for the modernisation of energy infrastructure and eur 1 billion for investments in fast and ultra-fast broadband networks and pan-european digital services. the cef will be centrally managed and for the transport sector, eur 10 billion will be earmarked under the cohesion fund for the cohesion member states, including romania. the regulation includes amendments supporting the development of waterway transport, in particular on the danube. they support investments in the development of shipping, in particular for works and studies on a number of sections and the removal of existing blockages, the modernisation of ports on inland waterways, the provision of connections to the hinterland for the main-danube canal (kelheim-constanța/midia/sulina). i regret that amendments nos 136 to 139 were not put to the vote. with these amendments i asked for the buzau - brăila - galați section to be included in the central road and rail network and the via carpathia route to be added to the list of transport corridors and i also asked for the galați - giurgiulești section, including the bypass of the municipality of galați, to be included in the central road network.
in writing. − an accessible and efficient transport infrastructure is essential for the provision of operational transport services, is fundamental to free movement and is vital to the ability of all regions of the european union to remain competitive within the european single market. resource-efficient infrastructure use, intelligent transport systems, satellite navigation, the development of better logistics (today 25% of heavy vehicles still have to run without a load), completing 'missing links' such as cross-border connections and avoiding bottlenecks are some of the solutions to a well-functioning and efficient transport system. another prerequisite for a well-functioning transport system is the presence of an intelligent infrastructure. infrastructure investments have a very long payback period, providing benefits over several generations if built or designed correctly. i believe that the purpose of the guidelines is to improve the interconnection and interoperability of regional and national transport networks and, by implication, the functioning of the single market, by creating the conditions for economic growth and mobility, which are essential for the quality of life of european citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report and believe that the trans-european transport network has a major potential for economic growth at union level. my country still suffers from infrastructure, which sometimes discourages foreign investors, despite the competitive advantages romania offers. the development of new road and rail links in the period 2014-2020 could therefore contribute to a higher competitiveness of the romanian economy and ultimately to more jobs for romanians.
in writing. − the trans-european transport network (ten-t) is one of the key projects of the european union. it is the backbone of the internal market and is indispensable for the mobility of eu citizens, for economic, social and territorial cohesion and for generating growth and jobs. the current challenges in the ten-t are well known: significant delays in the implementation of many ten-t projects, difficulties in project financing in this period of economic crisis, lack of coordination between the various centrally or decentrally managed financial instruments, and lack of information and statistics on project financing, in particular on financial aid from the structural and cohesion funds and the eib. in view of the above, i believe that ten-t policy must provide a solid basis that will guarantee efficient and safe transport in line with the future requirements of citizens and economic operators.
in writing. − the free movement of passengers and goods within the eu would not be possible without the trans-european transport network (ten-t), with half of all passenger and freight transport taking place via the means of transport on the network. with a significant contribution to economic, social and territorial cohesion and job creation, the development of the ten-t requires access to, interconnection and interoperability of national transport networks. as such, it is beneficial for europe to establish a methodology with common criteria for the entire network and all its modes of transport. it is also important to promote strategic planning for the equal integration of all regions, taking into account their transport needs, which must be linked to the european dimension in order to avoid bottlenecks and to achieve the missing cross-border links.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of the report on the new transeuropean transport network. the text voted at the plenary session aims to transform the transport infrastructure in europe into a true european network. the guidelines in this report propose two major changes to the current policy framework, involving a real method of programming european infrastructures and strengthening the tools for implementing the transeuropean transport network. this two-step approach, consisting of a comprehensive network and a strategic core, should ensure the design of coherent infrastructures across the european union. in addition, this new network offers hope that a strong policy framework will produce appropriate governance structures that should lead to a commitment by member states to deliver these critical infrastructure projects by 2030. the socialist and democratic group has particularly stressed the need to involve regional and local authorities and civil society in european infrastructure planning, and i welcome this.
in writing. − the increase in the mobility of citizens and goods in the european union has also meant an increase in transport volumes. in this regard, the european ten-t transport network must respond to new needs and present new approaches, according to priorities. i believe that member states should have a degree of flexibility to allow them to target their investments in the transmission network according to their needs. projects of common interest aiming at interconnection at regional level must take into account the development objectives set by the regional authorities. it is also important that projects of common interest take into account regional disparities in order to prioritise investments in areas where they are lacking. closing the transport infrastructure gap contributes significantly to strengthening cohesion at european level. i would like to emphasise that the development of crossborder projects by connecting transport networks brings significant economic benefits to these regions and beyond. the pan-european corridor 4 crossing my region is the main east-west road access route, which is why i insist that the romanian authorities overcome the obstacles to completing this corridor and, by implication, strengthening cross-border links.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the union's guidelines for the development of the trans-european transport network. the regulation contains important projects concerning the development of the romanian transport network. the amendments were included, whereby i requested the inclusion of the sebeş-alba-iuliaturda cluj-napoca - dej suceava pascani iaşi route on the central railway network for freight and passengers; the inclusion of the port of galaţi in the central ten-t network and the development of multimodal platforms for the ports of giurgiu and galaţi; the inclusion in the central road network of the ungheni - iaşi - targu-mureş - turda - sebeş connection and the calafat - craiova - bucharest section; and the inclusion of the constanţa - tulcea - galaţi - brăila section in the global road network. i also supported and called for the inclusion of a provision on bicycle lanes in the regulation. i regret that the amendments nos 199 and 200 which i tabled to the ten-t regulation were not put to the vote. these amendments called for the buzău - brăila - galați section to be included in the central road and rail network and for the via carpathia route to be added to the list of transport corridors. the galați - brăila - măcin area is the second largest urban agglomeration and an important industrial area of romania. galați is also a border crossing point with the republic of moldova and ukraine.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because simplification of the european statistical system was a necessity, especially as regards agricultural and fisheries statistics, in order to align these areas to the new institutional context. although it is a strictly technical-administrative change, it was necessary to ensure interinstitutional cooperation. the delegation of powers to the commission will ensure a more rapid and effective application of the provisions in this area.
in writing. − the commission has undertaken, in relation to regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council of 16 february 2011 laying down the rules and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers, to review legislative acts containing references to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny, taking into account the criteria laid down in the treaty. to this end, the commission aimed to amend nine legislative acts in the field of agricultural and fisheries statistics to align them with the new institutional context and also pursued the simplification of the european statistical system. the commission proposes a new structure of the european statistical system committee in order to improve coordination and partnership, in accordance with a clear pyramid structure, where the ess committee would represent the highest level strategic body. by voting in favour today, parliament has ruled in favour of this alignment exercise, but parliament has also ensured that the delegation of power is not indefinite but limited to a period of 5 years, tacitly extended by identical periods of time, unless the european parliament or the council opposes the extension.
in writing. − i agree with the general objective of eliminating all provisions relating to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny from all legislative instruments by the end of parliament's seventh legislature (june 2014) and also with the commission's proposal to simplify the european statistical system.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on agricultural and fisheries statistics. the objective of the regulation is to simplify the european statistical system (ess). regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics defined the european statistical system as a partnership between the european statistical authority, which is the commission (eurostat), and the national statistical institutes (nis) and other national authorities in each member state responsible for the development, production and dissemination of european statistics. the commission proposes a new ess structure aimed at improving coordination and partnership in line with a clear pyramid structure within the ess, where the ess committee would be the highest-level strategic body. the commission should also ensure that the delegated acts provided for in the legislative acts do not impose significant additional burdens on member states or on the respondents. in the framework of the strategy for a new structure of the european statistical system, the ess committee established by regulation (ec) no 223/2009 should have an advisory role and should assist the commission in the exercise of its implementing powers. to that end, the legislative acts should be amended by a reference to the esc. before submitting a proposal to the esc, the commission should consult experts in agricultural and fisheries statistics.
in writing. − the convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes (unece convention) provides a legal framework for cooperation on the common water resources of the states in the unece region through integrated management of these resources. the purpose of this convention is to establish a framework for bilateral or multilateral cooperation in the prevention and control of pollution of transboundary watercourses and the rational use of water by the countries belonging to the united nations economic commission for europe. i support the recommendation made by the rapporteur to accept the amendments to articles 25 and 26 of the convention to allow non-unece countries to accede to it if they so wish.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because the acceptance by the european union of the amendment to articles 25 and 26 of the unece convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes was necessary. this is all the more important as the european union is one of the few parties that has not formally accepted the amendment. the rational and responsible use of water resources is absolutely necessary, especially in relation to transboundary watercourses. another objective of the convention is to prevent pollution of these waters. in the context of the european union's global role model in environmental protection, acceptance of the amendments to the convention is a natural thing.
in writing. − the european union has been a party since 1995 to the unece convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes, which aims to establish a framework for bilateral or multilateral cooperation for the prevention and control of pollution of transboundary watercourses and for the rational use of water by countries belonging to the united nations economic commission for europe (unece). the parties to the convention have expressed their desire since 2003 to allow states outside the unece region to become parties to the convention, with the aim of promoting cooperation in watersheds worldwide. the eu is currently one of the few parties that has not yet formally accepted the amendment of any un member state to accede to the convention, subject to the approval of the parties. the european parliament has already expressed its position on the amendment in its resolution on the sixth world water forum adopted on 15 march 2012. by voting today, the european parliament approved the amendment to articles 25 and 26 of the convention to open it up globally and allow non-unece countries to accede to it if they so wish.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the acceptance, on behalf of the european union, of the amendment to articles 25 and 26 of the convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes. the main purpose of this convention is to establish a framework for bilateral or multilateral cooperation in the prevention and control of pollution of transboundary watercourses and in ensuring the rational use of water resources in the countries members of the un economic commission for europe (unece). the amendment to articles 25 and 26 of the convention allows for the accession to the convention of any state which is a member of the united nations, subject to approval by the meeting of the parties. the amendment will enter into force after acceptance by all states and organizations that were parties to the convention on 28 november 2003. once the amendment is in force, the convention will be of particular importance for the countries neighbouring the unece region, such as afghanistan, china, iran and certain countries in central asia. it is therefore necessary for the european union to accept the amendment now in order to open the convention globally and to allow non-unece countries that wish to accede to do so.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the iter project has the potential to revolutionize research in this field. as the european union has set itself, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, the objective of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, the development of alternative energy sources, such as that resulting from nuclear fusion, could contribute to achieving such an objective. looking beyond 2020, further research in this sector could gradually replace traditional energy sources such as oil and natural gas, thus ensuring the energy security of the european union.
in writing. − europe must implement an appropriate industrial policy, allowing the participation of as many industrial companies as possible, including small and medium-sized enterprises, in order to encourage competition, prepare the european system for the fusion era, but also to enable them to develop adequately and develop reliable standard solutions and equipment. i also believe that europe needs to take action to support training and education in fusion science and technology in order to have the necessary skilled and experienced workforce later on, and to involve scientists more strongly in order to achieve the desired results in fusion.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a council decision adopting a supplementary research programme for the iter project (2014-2018). the proposed additional research programme shall include contributions to the construction of the iter facility, the purchase of equipment and facilities, as well as general administrative and technical support for the project during construction, participation in the initial commissioning and operation and other iter-related activities such as those under the expanded collaboration programme agreement. the programme shall be financed by a maximum contribution of eur 2 573 million (currently). i consider it important to achieve the main objective of the iter project to build and operate an experimental fusion reactor because fusion has the potential to make a major contribution, decades from now, to achieving a sustainable and secure supply of electricity to the european union. the agreement on the establishment of the iter international fusion energy organisation for the joint implementation of the iter project was signed on 21 november 2006 by the european atomic energy community (euratom), the people's republic of china, the republic of india, japan, the republic of korea, the russian federation and the united states of america. the iter agreement establishes the iter international fusion energy organisation, which has full responsibility for the construction, operation, operation and decommissioning of the iter facilities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the research and innovation opportunities offered by the 'horizon 2020' programme are very numerous. therefore, its extension to the field of nuclear research is welcome. nuclear research is not just about the ability to produce nuclear energy. therefore, regardless of the options of the member states in this sector, i consider that nuclear research can bring competitive advantages to the union. i also believe that the involvement of the private sector in the programme is one of the conditions for its success. it will therefore be necessary to establish an appropriate framework for cooperation between public and private authorities.
in writing. − horizon 2020 offers the union numerous research and innovation opportunities, benefiting not only nuclear research but also other areas of research in the union. existing fusion projects such as joint european torus, which continues to provide the most accurate information on the work done so far in europe on fusion energy, should be further supported. existing programmes for sme funding, such as eureka star and some components of the marie curie actions, should be accessible to nuclear researchers. as regards funding, smes should not only have access to certain sme-specific instruments; all innovative funding instruments should be made available to smes participating in nuclear research. the leveraging of innovative financial instruments will be of key importance for all components of the horizon 2020 framework and access to these instruments by smes should not be hampered. the joint research centre should consider it its direct duty to undertake actions aimed at increasing the uptake of euratom funding by smes and to develop communication strategies to that end.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a council regulation on the european atomic energy community research and training programme (euratom programme) - 2014-2018 supplementing the framework programme for research and innovation horizon 2020. the euratom programme covers research activities in the field of nuclear energy (fusion and fusion) and radiation protection. the proposal is an integral part of the horizon 2020 framework programme for research and innovation. it shall establish the total budget for direct and indirect actions, set the objectives of research and development activities and specify the instruments to support them. the financial envelope for the implementation of the euratom programme is eur 1 603,329 million, which is allocated as follows: (a) indirect actions for the fusion research and development programme eur 636,095 million; (b) indirect actions in the field of nuclear fission, security and radiation protection eur 318,048 million; (c) direct actions eur 649,186 million. i support the overall objective of the euratom programme to improve nuclear safety, physical and radiation protection and to contribute to the long-term decarbonisation of the energy system in conditions of safety, efficiency and security, to contribute to other areas of research related to nuclear research such as medical research, and to secure the long-term future of european nuclear research.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because romania, as a country producing nuclear energy, has a direct interest in ensuring safety in this area. the nuclear accidents at chernobyl in 1986 and fukushima in 2011 have confirmed that there are a number of risks that this technology entails. romania applies the highest safety standards in the field, as proven by the results of the stress tests carried out by the european commission. however, further reducing these inherent risks requires both adequate funding and better cooperation between national authorities and facilitating the exchange of good practice in this area. i believe that this instrument will be able to lead to the achievement of these objectives.
in writing. − the instrument for nuclear security cooperation will build on the existing framework for nuclear security cooperation that the eu has gradually developed since the 1990s. the instrument shall aim to provide the union with sufficient resources to promote human and strategic security. in addition, it will effectively translate some of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy externally by promoting regulatory and other cooperation with emerging economies, as well as by exchanging best practices and standards. despite the proposed improvements, the need to ensure better coordination, consistency and complementarity of nuclear security efforts at eu and national level, as well as at the level of other international, local and regional organisations, in order to avoid overlaps and maximise the effects of funding, should be highlighted. the necessary safety conditions should also be created to eliminate risks to public life and health and to ensure that nuclear materials are not used for purposes other than those for which they are intended.
in writing. − nuclear risks are inherent in any reactor in any eu country or outside, as evidenced by the 1986 chernobyl accident and the 2011 fukushima accident. as such, i believe that europe must continue its efforts to enhance nuclear safety, in collaboration with other countries on other continents and with other professional structures. this will be beneficial to achieve the highest standards of nuclear safety as long as existing nuclear power plants remain in operation and new ones are built.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a council regulation establishing an instrument for cooperation in the field of nuclear safety. i support the promotion of an effective nuclear safety culture and governance and the implementation of the highest standards of nuclear safety and radiation protection. i also consider it important to manage spent fuel and radioactive waste responsibly and safely, and to decommission and rehabilitate former nuclear sites and installations in third countries. under this regulation, the european union finances measures to support the promotion of a high level of nuclear safety, radiation protection and the application of efficient and effective safeguards systems for nuclear material in third countries. the union cooperation actions provided for in the regulation shall be implemented on the basis of multiannual strategy papers. the multiannual strategy paper shall be drawn up for a period of up to seven years. the document shall set out the union's cooperation strategy, taking into account the needs of the countries concerned, the union's priorities, the international situation and the activities of the main partners. multiannual indicative programmes covering a period of 2 to 4 years shall be drawn up on the basis of the strategy papers. the budget voted for the implementation of this regulation for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 631 100 000.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that it is necessary to provide financial assistance from the european union for the closure of nuclear reactors. in the current context of the economic and financial crisis, where the resources available to member states are limited, the union's financial assistance is intended to ensure a standard-compliant decommissioning. all the expenditure for the decommissioning of these three plants is exceptional expenditure for the states concerned and in order not to jeopardise the steps already taken and to complete the procedures, an amendment of the existing legislation was needed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a council regulation on union support for the nuclear decommissioning assistance programmes in bulgaria, lithuania and slovakia. this regulation establishes the multiannual nuclear decommissioning assistance programme 2014-2020, which lays down rules for the continuation of the implementation of union financial support for measures related to the decommissioning of the nuclear power plants at kozloduy (unit 1 4), ignalina (unit 1 and 2) and bohunice v1 (unit 1 and 2). in accordance with the treaties of accession, bulgaria, lithuania and slovakia have closed their nuclear power plants or relevant units thereof and have made significant progress in their decommissioning. based on available estimates, the completion of decommissioning works will require considerable additional financial resources. the aid covered by the regulation must ensure the continuation of the decommissioning without interruption and focus on the measures necessary to implement the constant process aiming at the irreversible final stage of decommissioning, while ensuring the application of the highest safety standards. the financial envelope for the implementation of the programme for the period 2014 to 2020 shall be eur 969 260 000 in current prices: eur 293 032 000 for the kozloduy programme; eur 450 818 000 for the ignalina programme; eur 225 410 000 for the bohunice programme.

in writing. we have been fighting for over a decade to ensure gender balance in senior management positions in large european companies. self-regulation attempts, which have failed in several eu member states, have led to the inertia of legislative constraints. that is why i am pleased that we are discussing today in the plenary the proposal for a directive which has been so long negotiated by the european parliament. built entirely on the principle of meritocracy, the proposed directive addresses sectors where women are underrepresented and the achievement of gender balance on the basis of equal competences and qualifications. priority will therefore only be given if the candidate is as qualified as his male counterpart, which will eliminate the risk of positive discrimination. the directive also gives national authorities the choice of the means to achieve the objectives, as well as the option of imposing appropriate penalties on companies that breach the provisions. the gender imbalance in business management is not only undemocratic and inefficient, but is a real obstacle to economic growth. i consider it essential to use all human capital, skills and capacities to respond effectively to the challenges posed by the current economic crisis.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation no 723/2009 on the community legal framework for a european research infrastructure consortium (eric). the eric regulation was adopted in 2009 to facilitate the establishment and non-profit-making operation of european research infrastructures. the regulation created a new legal instrument at eu level for the establishment of european research infrastructures with legal personality, recognised in all member states. article 9 (1) of the eric regulation distinguishes and provides for a difference of treatment between member states, associated countries, third countries other than associated countries, and intergovernmental organisations. in an eric, at least three member states must have the membership (article 9 (2)) and the member states must hold a majority of the voting rights in the assembly of members (article 9 (3)). however, an eric may be hosted by a member state or an associated country (article 8 (1)). the objective of the proposal is to avoid associated countries being unable to become host or member of an eric because, as it stands, their voting rights do not have the potential to reflect their financial support for eric projects.

in writing. − economic, social and territorial cohesion is indispensable for the smooth functioning of the internal market, the economic and monetary union and the harmonious development of the eu as a whole. this agreement paves the way towards a more pragmatic, effective and strategic-priority-oriented cohesion policy in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the new cohesion policy will also foster synergies with other policies, such as research and innovation, thus encouraging more efficient spending of funds. grouping all funds under a common strategic framework with common rules is a smart approach which i believe will better meet the needs of the regions than the cohesion policy of so far, which is perceived as being highly bureaucratic. the elimination of unnecessary red tape will undoubtedly increase the absorption capacity of european funds and facilitate the participation of smes in the projects financed, which will have positive consequences for the economy. finally, even if the idea of macro-conditionality is based on a good and legitimate intention, i believe that in the form originally proposed, it could have had perverse effects. i am therefore pleased that the possibility of cutting funds in the event of macroeconomic mismatches has been strictly limited, while at the same time preserving the incentives for member states to have responsible macroeconomic policies.
in writing. − proposal for a regulation laying down common provisions on the european regional development fund (erdf), the european social fund (esf), the cohesion fund (cf), the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) and the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) which are subject to the common strategic framework, and laying down general provisions on the erdf, the esf, the cf and repealing the regulation. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the application of regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 to the new legislation. the new regulation on the use of european funds brings a number of novelties which i regard as promising. for example, focusing investments on the europe 2020 objectives, simplifying procedures, reducing red tape, and greater flexibility in combining different funds at the operational programme and project level. the ex ante conditionalities are also necessary preconditions in the programming phase and will have positive effects in the implementation phase. i do not, however, entirely agree with all the elements of this new regulation. i am referring here mainly to the macroeconomic conditionalities, even in the current version containing the safeguard clauses.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the amended proposal for a regulation laying down common provisions on the european regional development fund (erdf), the european social fund (esf), the cohesion fund (cf), the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) and the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) which are subject to the common strategic framework (the so-called 'european structural and investment funds - esifs') and laying down general provisions on the erdf, the esf and the cf and repealing regulation no 1083/2006. this regulation is organised in five parts: - the first part sets out the subject matter and definitions; - the second part contains the rules applicable to all esi funds; - part three sets out the general rules for the erdf, the esf (the 'structural funds') and the cohesion fund concerning tasks, priority objectives and organisation; - part four sets out the general rules for the structural funds and the cohesion fund and the emff concerning management and control. the resources for economic, social and territorial cohesion available for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 325 145 694 739 in 2011 prices, of which eur 322 145 694 739 shall be the global resources allocated to the erdf, the esf and the cohesion fund and eur 3 000 000 000 shall be a specific allocation for the youth employment initiative.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the european social fund (esf) and repealing regulation no 1081/2006. the regulation lays down the mission of the esf, including the 'youth employment' initiative, the scope of the support provided through it, specific provisions and the types of expenditure eligible for assistance. the beneficiaries of the esf are persons, including disadvantaged persons, such as long-term unemployed persons, persons with disabilities, migrants, ethnic minorities, marginalised communities and persons of all ages, who are facing poverty and social exclusion. the esf shall also provide support to workers, enterprises, including social economy actors, and entrepreneurs, as well as systems and structures, to facilitate their adaptation to new challenges, including the reduction of skills gaps, and to promote good governance, social progress and the implementation of reforms, in particular in the fields of employment, education, training and social policies. the esf shall support the following investment priorities: promoting sustainable and quality jobs and supporting labour mobility; promoting social inclusion, combating poverty and any form of discrimination; investing in education, training and vocational training for skills and lifelong learning; increasing the institutional capacity of public authorities and stakeholders and the efficiency of public administration.

in writing. − cohesion policy is one of the main investment instruments to support the union's key priorities set out in the europe 2020 strategy. in accordance with articles 174 and 176 tfeu, the european regional development fund (erdf) is intended to reduce disparities between the levels of development of regions and the degree of backwardness of the least-favoured regions, so that its actions must be channelled in particular to the countries and regions where needs are greatest. the commission proposal for the 2014-2020 erdf regulation introduced a new element by introducing a thematic concentration and by strengthening the urban dimension. the proposed thematic focus has meant focusing on a limited number of thematic objectives, further detailed in investment priorities. these improvements will ensure flexibility and allow for better tailoring of erdf support to the different needs of regions across the eu.
in writing. − cohesion policy is one of the main investment instruments to support the union's key priorities set out in the europe 2020 strategy. as environmental protection and sustainable development are major elements of these priorities, european cohesion policy is the most appropriate means to support the transition to a competitive, low-carbon economy and investment in climate change mitigation and adaptation measures, as well as environmental protection and biodiversity and sustainable urban development. the allocation of 6% of the available resources to less developed regions for the transition to a low-carbon economy in all sectors cannot be considered sufficient, as it is precisely in these regions that more investment is needed to reduce emissions. it is therefore essential to increase the percentage to 15%. particular attention shall be paid to common indicators for the erdf, which shall be clearly defined and in a manner that allows an objective quantitative assessment of the results achieved on environmental priorities. with regard to the prevention and management of climate change risks, the focus should not be exclusively on civil protection measures, but more attention should be paid to increasing the prevention capacity and resilience of ecosystems.
in writing. − i believe that introducing thematic concentration and strengthening the urban dimension are two important elements of the commission's proposal for the 2014-2020 erdf regulation. the thematic concentration will thus facilitate the identification of a limited number of thematic objectives, which will subsequently be identified as investment priorities, with the aim of contributing to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. on the other hand, the inclusion of the enhanced urban dimension will support the allocation of a 5% part of the erdf resources for the management of cities and the implementation of innovative actions in the field of sustainable urban development. in addition, flexibility will be ensured to better tailor erdf support to the needs of european regions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation on specific provisions for the european regional development fund and the investment for growth and jobs goal (erdf) and repealing regulation no 1080/2006. the regulation sets out the scope of the erdf's intervention and also defines a list of activities which will not be eligible for support. it defines the investment priorities for each of the thematic objectives. the regulation also provides for the following mechanism: - more developed regions whose gdp per capita is more than 90% of the average gdp of the eu-27 will spend at least 80% of resources on energy efficiency and renewable energy, research and development and support for smes, of which 20% will be devoted to energy efficiency and renewable energy. - transition regions whose gdp per capita is between 75% and 90% of the average gdp of the eu-27 will use 60% and 15% of the above resources respectively; - less developed regions whose gdp per capita is less than 75% of the average gdp of the eu-27 will use 50% and 12% of the above resources respectively.

in writing. − the adoption of the european parliament resolution on european groupings for territorial cooperation (egtcs) will facilitate the implementation of projects financed under objective ii, territorial cooperation. as an implementation tool, egtcs are not widely used, mainly because of their complexity and legislative vacuum. the legal clarifications introduced by the new regulation are therefore welcome. for example, the fact that the new regulation makes a clear distinction between the statute and the convention, by stipulating that only the convention, not the statute, will be subject to formal approval. i also welcome the clarifications concerning egtc staff, whereby members of a group can choose between the law of the headquarters country, the law of the place where the employees work or the national law of the respective employees. this provision was also available until now but was not fully understood due to the incomplete wording. i consider it beneficial to extend the egtc eligibility to non-eu countries. this provision will make it possible to combine different sources of funding, alongside the structural and cohesion funds, and to implement instruments of common interest, including in the framework of the danube strategy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending regulation no 1082/2006 on a european grouping of territorial cooperation (egtc) with regard to clarifying, simplifying and improving the constitution and implementation of such groupings. i consider that egtcs have the potential to encourage the promotion and achievement of the harmonious development of the union as a whole and the economic, social and territorial cohesion of its regions in particular, and to contribute to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. they can also contribute positively to reducing barriers to territorial cooperation and can be useful in strengthening cooperation between third countries, overseas countries and territories and union border regions, including through the use of eu external cooperation programmes. the amendments introduced by this regulation aim, on the one hand, to comply with the terminology introduced by the treaty on the functioning of the european union and, on the other hand, concern the composition, content of the convention and the statute of an egtc, its purpose, the authorisation process by national authorities, the applicable employment and procurement legislation, the approach to egtcs whose members do not have the same responsibility for their actions and more transparent communication procedures.

in writing. − i welcome and support the rapporteurs' proposal for a clear target of 40% of the under-represented sex in non-executive directorships in all listed companies by 2020 and in listed state-owned companies by 2018 to promote gender balance in the boards of all listed companies. this will provide women with greater opportunities to assume leadership positions and contribute with their skills to the economic performance of societies. it is also useful to introduce a series of sanctions for failure to comply with these provisions.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of this proposal to improve equality between men and women in the most highly skilled jobs. the objective of having 40% of women on the boards of publicly listed european companies by 2020 is ambitious and necessary. today, only 17.6% of non-executive directors are women, and only 2.4% of managing directors. this is not only discriminatory, it is also a hindrance to growth. this text is a step forward in ensuring equal opportunities for men and women in the highest positions in companies. there are still too many competent, skilled and talented women excluded from the boards of large companies. however, we know that a better gender balance in boards is particularly positive for economic success and business management. the text should make recruitment procedures more transparent, so that they are based solely on merit. they will be accompanied by sanctions for companies that are not compliant. i welcome the outcome of the vote, in which the socialists and democrats played an important role.
in writing. − gender equality and non-discrimination are part of the eu's core values. there is certainly still room for improvement in achieving full equality, whether we are talking about equal pay for equal jobs or the representation of women in decision-making structures in both politics and private enterprise. the objective of gender equality must therefore remain a priority on the european and national agenda. the commission's present proposal and the amendments adopted in the parliamentary committees do not, in my view, constitute a reasonable solution. i believed, and i still believe, that board seats in companies should be filled on the basis of competence and merit, and that the decision belongs to the shareholders who invest in those companies. legislative quota setting, even if it is based on a legitimate intention, will have perverse effects, preventing the companies concerned from appointing the people they want to their boards of directors, forcing them to take into account the sex of the candidates, which is absolutely irrelevant from a qualitative point of view and even discriminatory towards candidates of the opposite sex. last but not least, i cannot support a text that introduces disproportionate sanctions such as exclusion from public procurement procedures or even the dissolution of the company.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the strengthening of the gender balance among non-executive directors of listed companies and related measures. in january 2012, women occupied on average only 13,7% of the available positions on the boards of the largest listed companies in the member states. the number of highly qualified women willing to serve on a board of directors is increasing, but many obstacles remain. i believe that if half of the talent pool is not considered for management positions, the process and quality of appointments itself is compromised, which leads to an increase in distrust of the power structures of the business environment and leads to a decrease in the effective utilisation of available human capital. i support the objective of the directive to substantially increase the number of women on boards of companies across the eu by setting a minimum target of 40% of the under-represented sex among non-executive directors of listed companies and achieving that proportion by 1 january 2020 or by 1 january 2018 in the case of companies that are publicly traded.
after long debates, many welcome the agreement on the reform of the common agricultural policy, and the fact that after the transition period, the story of one of the european union's most successful policies can continue under the new rules. at the same time, it should be emphasised that, for the first time in the cap reforms, the european parliament succeeded in achieving substantial amendments in negotiations with the council, and as a result, in significantly improving the initial proposal. it is of the utmost importance that the balancing of direct payments between member states has also been agreed. the level of payments will thus clearly converge, resulting in a fairer distribution. support for young farmers will also increase, which is essential for the pursuit of sustainable and profitable agricultural activities, especially in member states with a very high share of the population living off agriculture.
in writing. − the common agricultural policy is not only one of the european union's most important economic objectives, but also one of the instruments with a key role in reducing intra-regional disparities and preserving a historically relevant way of life for european societies. it is therefore necessary that the amendments made take account not only of the economic effects but also of the impact and social importance of this area. i believe that improving the control and sanction system, reducing bureaucracy and making the evaluation and monitoring system more efficient are important steps towards improving the common agricultural policy. i also believe that these changes can increase the competitiveness of member states' economies by providing a growing number of jobs in a sector that is essential to the economic success of the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which i consider to be a particularly important part of the process of reforming the common agricultural policy. in the present context, but also as a precautionary measure, i would like to insist on budgetary discipline which requires compliance with the annual ceiling for expenditure. they also consider that the new payment and monitoring systems, as well as the related sanctioning systems, are welcome. the only condition is that they do not generate more bureaucracy or complicated additional procedures for local administrations. finally, i would like to express my support for the agricultural advisory system for beneficiaries. i believe that this is both important and necessary in terms of management, farming practices, environmental standards and public health measures.
in writing. − i believe that a reserve for crisis situations should be established to support the agricultural sector in the event of major crises affecting agricultural production or distribution.
in writing. i voted in favour of the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap) for the period 2014-2020. this fairer reform introduces new and more transparent criteria for the distribution of subsidies to member states and european farmers. the total amount of the cap for the next six years was set at 408 billion, or almost 38% of the union budget. the introduction of codecision has enabled the european parliament to impose a number of its demands, notably on the necessary transparency of the process of allocating funds, which is a notable development. the reform introduces the principle of publication of beneficiaries, who will have to be able to prove continuous activity: non-productive sites, such as airports or golf courses, will be excluded from the reform. the new payment system will give priority to small farms over large companies. finally, it is important that a limit has been set for at least 30% of the union rural development budget and 30% of farm subsidies to be dedicated to organic farming, agri-environmental measures and other climate adaptation measures.
in writing. − the reform of the common agricultural policy has been a long process and, for the first time since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament has played a leading role in the formulation of one of the most important european policies. the report i have dealt with is an attempt to improve the commission's proposal by ensuring that our farmers have more simplification and less red tape, both in the system of direct payments and in the system of controls and penalties. finally, with the definition of the 2014-2020 mff, we were able to define the framework that allowed us to establish the financial allocation of the new cap.
in writing. − the common agricultural policy has the potential to contribute to the europe 2020 strategy by ensuring sustainable agriculture and by increasing coherence between the common agricultural policy and environmental and public health policies. the monitoring and evaluation system is of particular importance as it will help to assess progress made and to make policies more effective in achieving the proposed objectives by providing timely access to relevant information received from member states. i believe that we need a system that is able to monitor and evaluate the performance of the cap as well as the main instruments of the programme (direct payments, market indices, rural development indices, etc.) and that also involves all stakeholders from the outset.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution because i strongly believe we need a modern legislation in order to increase the competitiveness of eu agriculture. the new rules will make farming more competitive, they will enhance support for young farmers and for those who are genuinely engaged in agricultural production. with these new rules we have paved the way for a green, modern agriculture that will ensure the best results for the consumers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the financing, management and monitoring of the common agricultural policy (cap). it lays down rules on: the financing of cap expenditure, including rural development expenditure; the agricultural advisory system; the management and control systems to be set up by the member states; the cross-compliance system; the verification and closure of accounts. i would stress the importance of introducing the article on the reserve for crises in the agricultural sector. a crisis reserve is thus established to provide additional support to the sector in the event of major crises affecting agricultural production or distribution by applying, at the beginning of each year, a reduction to direct payments through the financial discipline mechanism. the total amount of the reserve is eur 2800 million, with annual tranches of eur 400 million (at 2011 prices) for the period 2014-2020. i would point out that the amounts not made available for crisis measures by the end of the financial year are paid to final beneficiaries who, during the financial year for which the appropriations are carried over, are subject to the adjustment of direct payments. the reimbursement shall only apply to final beneficiaries in member states which were subject to financial discipline during the previous financial year.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report. i think we are dealing with a very useful and necessary report on how to inform and protect investors. although the range of investment products is becoming wider, they are becoming more complex and more difficult to understand. investments are often made in ignorance, with risks and costs that investors do not understand and that can lead to unforeseen and unbearable losses. i consider that this report brings improvements in terms of transparency and information provided to retail investors. last but not least, such measures aimed at regaining investor confidence in financial markets are necessary in the current economic context.
in writing. − i voted for the amendments adopted by the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation on key information documents relating to investment products. i consider that improving the transparency provisions for investment products offered to retail investors is an important measure to protect investors and a necessary condition for restoring their confidence in the financial market, especially in the context of the consequences of the financial crisis. different rules for the different sectors offering investment products and national regulations in this area create unequal conditions of competition between different products and distribution channels, thus raising new obstacles to a single market for financial services and products. this regulation complements the measures on distribution (including investment advice, investor protection measures or other sales services) provided for in directive 2004/39/ec and the measures on the distribution of insurance products provided for in directive 2002/92/ec of the european parliament and of the council. the regulation lays down uniform rules: - on the format and content of the key information document; - the annex to the key information document; - on insurance intermediation, and uniform rules on the provision of such documents to retail investors.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on support for rural development from the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd). it lays down: - general rules governing union support for rural development from the eafrd; - defines the objectives to be contributed to by rural development policy and the relevant union priorities for rural development; - highlights the strategic context for rural development policy; - defines measures under rural development policy; - lays down rules on programming, interconnection, management, monitoring and evaluation, based on the sharing of responsibility between member states and the commission, and lays down rules to ensure coordination of the eafrd with other union instruments. the creation and development of new economic activities, diversification into non-agricultural activities, including the provision of services for agriculture and forestry, activities related to healthcare, social integration and tourism are vital for the development of rural areas. the eafrd intervenes in the member states through rural development programmes. in order to contribute to the achievement of the union priorities for rural development, member states may include in their rural development programmes thematic sub-programmes addressing specific needs. such thematic sub-programmes may relate to, inter alia, young farmers; small farms; mountain areas; short supply chains; women in rural areas; climate change mitigation and adaptation and biodiversity.

in writing. − i voted to amend regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 on certain provisions relating to financial management for certain member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability, the rules on disengagement for certain member states and the rules on the payment of the final balance. the global financial crisis has seriously damaged economic growth and financial stability and deteriorated financial, economic and social conditions in several member states. in order to facilitate the management of union funding, to accelerate investment in member states and regions, and to improve the availability of funds to finance the economy, regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 was amended to allow for an increase in interim payments from the funds by an amount equivalent to 10 percentage points above the actual co-financing rate for each priority axis in the case of member states experiencing severe financial difficulties and having requested this measure. the union contribution, by paying the final balance for each priority axis, shall not exceed by more than 10% the maximum amount of assistance from the funds granted for each priority axis. the co-financing rate increased by 10 percentage points shall apply to the 2014-2020 programming period until 30 june 2016, when the possibility of such an increase is to be reviewed.

on behalf of the alde group. madam president, commissioner, we are debating two important reports tonight, but i believe that mr gahler's report is the solution for a common security and defence policy. it is a substantial report, showing us where our limits are and how those limits correspond to the ambitions of a common strategy and policy conceptualisation. the security situation, particularly in the mediterranean area, the situation of reduced budgets in almost all member states, the situation of the 28 different defence markets, far from having a single market, clearly tell us that we have a reduced capacity to react to the risks and vulnerabilities of an increasingly precarious security situation. the solution is to use the slogans, that famous 'pooling and sharing', in an effective way: member states to collaborate; member states to try to make their defence compatible; to try to make european joint undertakings, as a solution both to strengthen defence capacity and to strengthen employment; to standardise, certify and use the institutions we already have. we fully agree with mr gahler's proposal that the european defence agency should be the pivotal coordinator of these policies of compatibility, which must also generate greater competitiveness for the defence industry, because beyond what we are proposing, we have seen the limits. we've seen what's happened in libya, we've seen our inability to react and to support a common ambition. we cannot each, individually, respond to global challenges. instead, we can together, by putting our capabilities together, react effectively and make the european union not just an ambitious player in security policy, but an effective player, which would bring much more visibility and respect to defence policy. that is why i believe that in achieving our common ambitions defence capabilities and industry constitute the answer to a true cohesion of our common policy.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the fiscalis 2020 tax action programme aims to improve the efficiency of national tax administrations, to cooperate at european level, to simplify procedures, and to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. the programme was very favourably received by the national authorities, who requested that it continue in 2014. in this context, i welcome the proposal for an extension for the period 2014-2020. i believe that reducing administrative burdens and training of staff responsible for tax matters are important elements of the regulation, which will benefit both citizens and companies, while improving the functioning of the european internal market. according to the european commission, most member states face difficulties in the field of tax collection and the functioning of the tax administration. tax fraud and evasion cause considerable losses, estimated at €1 trillion a year in the european union. in romania, tax evasion accounts for about 15% of gross domestic product, the equivalent of €20 billion annually, according to the fiscal council. this money is a disservice to citizens, as it could be used for economic recovery and unemployment programmes. i also support the extension of the action programme for taxation to countries outside the european union, including candidate and potential candidate countries and neighbourhood policy partner countries. the programme will enable them to reform their tax administration and move forward on the path of european integration. finally, i would like to congratulate mr stolojan on his excellent report.

in writing. − i voted for the resolution on the proposal for a decision on the 'strategic innovation agenda' of the european institute of innovation and technology (eit): the eit's contribution to a more innovative europe. the eit was established to contribute to sustainable economic growth and competitiveness by enhancing the innovation capacity of the union and its member states. to achieve this, the eit combines strategic orientation at eit level with a bottom-up approach through the knowledge and innovation communities (kics). kics are integrated partnerships that bring together long-term leading universities and research centres, small and large enterprises and other actors of excellence in innovation. in 2010, the kics were established: sustainable energy (kic innoenergy), adaptation to and mitigation of climate change (climatekic) and the information and communication society of the future (eit ict labs). in the next step, new kics will be developed and calls for proposals will be launched for five new kics as follows: one call for two new kics in 2014 on the themes 'healthy lifestyle and active ageing' and 'raw materials'; one call for two new kics in 2016 on the themes 'food4future' and 'value-added production' and one call for a new kic in 2018 on 'urban mobility'.

in writing. the 'programme for social change and innovation' proposed by the european commission brings together three existing programmes - progress, eures and the microfinance facility - in a new programme. the current progress funding instrument supports the development and coordination of eu policy in the fields of employment, social protection and social inclusion, working conditions, anti-discrimination and equal opportunities for women and men. the role of the eures network is to provide information, advice and placement services (coordination of job offers and applications) to mobile workers and employers, and in general to all citizens who want to benefit from the right of free movement. the progress microfinance facility was established in 2010 and facilitates access to microcredit for the creation and promotion of microenterprises. the instrument does not finance micro-enterprises directly, but allows selected microcredit lenders to provide a higher number of loans. i believe that the programme should be fully transparent so that the revenues and payments generated by a particular financial instrument are reallocated to that instrument.
in writing. − the 'programme for social change and innovation' proposed by the european commission from 2014 onwards will bring together three existing programmes - progress, eures and the microfinance facility - into a new programme, which will result in a weakening of their measures and objectives. the programme is allocated eur 958,10 million, but it is important to increase the total budget by 5% because, in a time of economic crisis and need for consolidation in the member states, social and employment programmes are becoming of central importance. the progress sub-programme should continue to ensure that the largest share of funding is allocated to the areas of social inclusion, social protection and poverty reduction. in view of the increasing problems faced by young people in the labour market and the increasing youth unemployment, it is essential that at least 10% be used to tackle youth unemployment. as regards the eures sub-programme, funding for specific mobility programmes, cross-border partnerships, and the training and qualification of eures staff should be ensured. the adequate funding of the microfinance and social entrepreneurship sub-programme should also be ensured.
