in writing. i voted in favour of this programme, which aims to empower and support the social and employment policies of the member states. it will help to promote voluntary economic mobility in europe, provide one-to-one support for crossborder workers, promote initiative projects to combat poverty and social exclusion, and provide micro-credit to the most vulnerable so that they can set up their own businesses and support social innovation. i strongly support these initiatives. this programme provides a clear and coherent framework and has thus been linked to a number of broader issues affecting quality of employment, poverty reduction and social inclusion. in this time of crisis, we must put all the chances on our side in order to create a more just and united europe. i am confident in the capacity of the recent instruments adopted by the european union to contribute to these objectives, and in particular this programme for social change and innovation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of creating the programme for social change and innovation. by combining the programmes progress, eures, and micro-financing, the programme for social change offers a more direct instrument for the commission to use in its effort to fight poverty and safeguard social protections. close to 99% of the new businesses opened in the eu are small businesses with a third of the owners formerly unemployed. it is quite clear then that promoting small business growth with tools such a micro-lending and social inclusion can go a long way to addressing the very real issue of the eu’s unemployed youth. with over 20% of young adults currently unemployed and with no sign of a substantial remedy in sight, the institutions must maintain and expand their focus on those methods that have shown results, namely micro-financing and small business development. the collection of administrative activities should provide streamlining and focus for these three programmes, to help them better reach their goals and promote further development throughout the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing a european union programme for social change and social innovation. the programme should contribute to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives, in particular the poverty reduction and employment objectives. to this end, the programme should support the implementation of strategic initiatives, paying particular attention to the european platform against poverty and social exclusion, the agenda for new skills and jobs and the 'youth on the move' initiative, as well as the youth opportunities initiative. in particular, the programme should contribute to the identification, analysis and scaling up of innovative solutions and their practical application through social policy experimentation, in order to assist member states, where necessary, to increase the efficiency of their labour markets and further improve their social protection and inclusion policies. the programme should also pay particular attention to the territorial dimension of unemployment, poverty and social exclusion, in particular the growing inequalities that exist within and between regions, between rural and urban areas, as well as in cities.
in writing. − the european union's policy on the environment and climate change has improved significantly in recent years, reflected in the actual improvement in the state of the environment in the eu. however, at european level, there are still many challenges to be addressed, which is why i welcome the establishment of the special funding programme for environment and climate policies life. it is intended to act as a catalyst for change in policy development and implementation by providing and disseminating solutions and best practices to achieve environmental and climate objectives. i am confident that this programme will also successfully address some of the key challenges facing the union: halting and reversing the decline in biodiversity, improving resource efficiency, and addressing environmental and health concerns.
in writing. − the risks associated with environmental degradation and climate change are some of the most profound and very long-term challenges facing the european union today. combating climate change and strengthening the union's resilience to the associated risks must be a key priority of our political efforts. in the period 2007-2013, life+ has proven to be such a specific financial instrument. as the only separate union financial instrument targeting these areas, it has proven over the years to be an indispensable part of the union's effort to combat climate change and environmental degradation. life+ has repeatedly been evaluated as a highly successful programme. its high european added value and significant catalytic effect were highlighted. the continuation of the life+ programme in the future, for the period 2014-2020, is indispensable in my view, as it is essential to substantially strengthen the programme, also in terms of financial support.
in writing. − over the past 20 years, life has achieved considerable success as a means of addressing the environmental and climate challenges facing european citizens. the commission's proposed life share of the general eu budget of 0,3% is disproportionately low in relation to the challenges and opportunities of the transition to a sustainable, low-carbon, resource-efficient and biodiverse society. in its resolution on the eu biodiversity strategy, the european parliament expressed its disagreement with the proposed funding for the new life programme and considered that the challenges addressed in the biodiversity and nature conservation plan require a substantial increase in the funding allocated to the life programme. today's vote in favour of an adequate budget for the life programme is a strong signal that the eu is serious about its environmental and climate commitments. i believe that european solidarity must play an important role in supporting member states and regions with a low project selection rate in trying to achieve a higher quality of environmental projects and thus increase the absorption rate of funds.
in writing. − i believe that the commission should propose a method for monitoring the long-term success of projects, especially in the field of nature and biodiversity.
in writing. − i voted for the life programme in support of vital projects to protect the environment and to assist the implementation of eu legislation. i welcome the co-financing of projects to improve nature protection, waste management, and water and air quality, as this should lead to direct and long-lasting positive impacts on human health.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation establishing a programme for environment and climate policy (life) because the programme will contribute to the achievement of a low-carbon, resource-efficient and climate-resilient economy. the life programme has two sub-programmes with three priority areas each: -the environment sub-programme with the priority areas: environment and resource efficiency; nature and biodiversity; environmental governance and information. - and the sub-programme for climate policy with the priority areas of climate change mitigation; adaptation to climate change; climate governance and information. the financial envelope for the implementation of the life programme for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 3 456 655 000 in current prices, broken down as follows: - eur 2 592 491 250 shall be allocated to the sub-programme for environment; - eur 864 163 750 shall be allocated to the sub-programme for climate policy. union funding shall be provided through: grants; procurement contracts; contributions to financial instruments, in accordance with the provisions on financial instruments laid down in regulation (eu) no 966/2012, in particular articles 139 and 140 thereof, and in accordance with pronounced operational requirements laid down in specific union acts; or any other type of intervention necessary to achieve the general objectives.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the amended proposal for a regulation establishing an action programme for taxation in the european union for the period 2014-2020 (fiscalis 2020) and repealing decision no 1482/2007/ec. it will actively strengthen the functioning of taxation systems in the internal market, while contributing to the progressive removal of existing barriers and distortions in the internal market. the operational objectives and priorities of the programme are: -to implement, improve, operate and support european tax information systems; -to support administrative cooperation activities; -to strengthen the skills and competences of officials in tax administrations; -strengthening the understanding and implementation of union law in the tax field; -supporting the improvement of administrative procedures and sharing good practice in the administrative field. the financial envelope for the implementation of the programme is set at eur 223 366 000 in current prices. the union's financial support for the activities referred to in article 7 shall take the form of grants, public procurement contracts and reimbursement of the costs of the external experts referred to in article 4. the countries participating in the programme are the member states, the acceding countries, the candidate countries and potential candidate countries as well as the partner countries under the european neighbourhood policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because customs cooperation is essential to enhance security at the borders of the european union. the exchange of good practices between the competent authorities of the member states can also lead to a more effective fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. technical capacity building will be required in the period ahead, including support to participating countries in the acquisition and maintenance of equipment and the development of human skills. by preventing cross-border fraud, on the one hand, revenues to national budgets can be increased and, on the other, adequate protection of european citizens is ensured.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing an action programme for customs in the european union for the period 2014-2020 (customs 2020) and repealing decision no 624/2007/ec. customs authorities face complex challenges on a daily basis and effective cooperation between union customs authorities has become increasingly important. this regulation establishes a multiannual action programme 'customs 2020' with the aim of improving the functioning of the customs union. the programme shall cover the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2020. the financial envelope for the implementation of the programme for the period 2014-2020 is set at eur 522 943 000. the annual appropriations shall be authorised by the european parliament and the council within the limits of the multiannual financial framework. the general objective of the programme is to support the functioning and modernisation of the customs union with a view to strengthening the internal market through cooperation between the participating countries, their customs authorities and their officials. the specific objectives are to support customs authorities in protecting the financial and economic interests of the union and the member states, including the fight against fraud and the protection of intellectual property rights, to enhance safety and security, to protect citizens and the environment, to improve the administrative capacity of customs authorities and to strengthen the competitiveness of european businesses.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the deadlines for transposing and implementing the directive on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of insurance and reinsurance (solvency ii) needed to be amended to avoid a situation of prolonged legal uncertainty and to ensure the legal continuity of the current solvency provisions. the supervisory authorities and insurance and reinsurance undertakings should also be given a period of time to prepare for the application of the solvency ii package. last but not least, the alignment of that directive with the omnibus ii directive was necessary to ensure uniform application and to create an appropriate framework in the field.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal to amend directive 2009/138/ec on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of insurance and reinsurance (solvency ii) as regards its date of transposition and application and the date of repeal of certain directives. directive 2009/138/ec provides for a modern, risk-based system for the regulation and supervision of insurance and reinsurance undertakings in the union. that system is essential to ensure the safety and soundness of the insurance sector so that it can provide sustainable insurance products and support the real economy by encouraging long-term investment and added stability. in order to avoid imposing unduly burdensome legislative obligations on member states under directive 2009/138/ec and subsequently under the new supervisory architecture provided for in the omnibus ii proposal, the date for transposition and the date of application of the directive is postponed, allowing sufficient time for supervisors and insurance and reinsurance undertakings to prepare for the application of the new architecture. the proposal sets 31 january 2015 as the date for transposition and 1 january 2016 as the date for application of the directive. the proposal also amends articles 310 and 311 accordingly by setting a new date for the repeal of solvency i (1 january 2016).
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the state of play of the doha development agenda and preparations for the ninth wto ministerial conference. the doha round negotiations were launched in 2001 with the objectives of creating new trade opportunities, strengthening multilateral trade rules and addressing current trade system imbalances, with the needs and interests of developing countries, and in particular least developed countries, at the heart of the negotiations. the wto ministerial meetings to conclude the doha round reached a deadlock at the end of july 2008, but the 9th wto ministerial conference will take place in indonesia from 3 to 6 december 2013. i consider it important to discuss and remove barriers to trade and investment affecting the services sectors, including ict and telecommunications, professional and business services, financial services, e-commerce, construction, retail and distribution. i also believe that technology transfer can be a driver for growth and trade and welcome the resumption of negotiations on the extension of the information technology agreement, which increases both the range of products covered and the number of participating countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the low rate of economic growth and the high unemployment rate, especially among young people, require a coordinated approach. we need strong measures in the short, medium and long term to facilitate and strengthen entrepreneurship at eu level. it is worrying that economic uncertainty is discouraging eu citizens from taking the initiative to work independently. therefore, there is a need to step up efforts to provide incentives in this regard and to develop a culture of attractiveness to entrepreneurship. the european union can and must complement member states' actions in this area by means of cooperation, exchange of best practice, advice and ongoing assistance. last but not least, i believe that the member states, and the commission, must constantly assess measures to favour tax breaks for small and medium-sized enterprises that employ young people.
in writing. − i support the proposal that the revival of entrepreneurship in europe be linked to the commission's industrial policy activities and coordinated efforts to improve the entrepreneurial culture in europe. european statistics show that the number of eu citizens considering working independently in the current context of economic uncertainty is decreasing. as such, europe needs to explore all possibilities to adopt specific measures and targets to make entrepreneurship attractive again, including for skilled and experienced workers and especially in sectors of strategic importance for the union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the entrepreneurship 2020 action plan: revitalising entrepreneurship in europe. we invite the commission to strengthen support, advice and assistance measures for enterprises, in particular for the smallest enterprises, and also to promote the creation of clusters, business networks and business associations that support the development of competitive advantages, benefit from the shared management of human resources and lead to increased competitiveness. we propose that member states could request additional funds from the european globalisation adjustment fund and the european social fund to provide support and advice for setting up a business, and not just to justify the continued relocation of businesses. we call on member states to grant a two-year grace period for newly established businesses in respect of social security contributions and a three-year grace period for all taxes in advance, so that in the first three years businesses only pay taxes on the profits actually generated. the system must be fully transparent to prevent any abuse. we also ask the commission to ensure that member states reduce the timeframe for granting concessions and other approvals required for setting up a company to one month.

in writing. this resolution is a further step in the fight of the european parliament and the socialists and democrats for the european union to strengthen the social dimension of its economic and monetary union. the current situation is worrying. unemployment in the union now stands at an alarming 26.6 million, and youth unemployment is at unprecedented levels, with an average of 23% for the union as a whole. since 2007, poverty rates in the union have increased and household incomes have decreased, with the result that 24.2% of the european population is now at risk of poverty or social exclusion. this situation is intolerable. it is necessary to insist that social considerations be placed at the heart of european integration. the social dimension of emu is to guarantee social security and a sufficient standard of living for all, and european citizens must therefore be aware that the union is capable of promoting social progress. finally, more support is needed for the voluntary mobility of workers in order to make the most of the union's employment potential.

member of the commission. − madam president, first of all i would like to thank the rapporteur, ms fraga, and the committee on fisheries for their work on this proposal. but i would also like to thank the committee on budgets and the committee on development who have given support to this proposal. so it is not only the fisheries committee but also the budgets and development committees that are supporting this proposal. i would like to remind you that two years ago this house rejected our proposal referring to a possible agreement with morocco on fisheries. but this house also asked me to negotiate a new agreement. you asked the commission to negotiate a new agreement, and of course you put conditions on these new negotiations: economic profitability, environmental sustainability and compliance with international law. so i can say to you that the agreement we have reached with the moroccan authorities is in full accordance with these conditions you have already set. i took parliament’s message on board and i negotiated. it took me 18 difficult months to reach this agreement. and let me be clear: i think that this is the best possible agreement we can have, and no other agreement will be possible if parliament decides to reject it. of course it is up to you to decide, but i would like you to know that if you decide to reject it there will be no other agreement in place. but i really think that this agreement fulfils your demands and concerns. let me explain why. this agreement is economically profitable. this is also understood and underlined by parliament’s committee on budgets. fishing possibilities increase by 33%, eu taxpayers’ payments decrease by 30% and the eu fleet is expected to benefit by up to eur 100 million per year. we have to think about the social consequences of this agreement and that is why the social partners – both sides, the ship-owners and the workers – strongly support this agreement. the trade union etf, the european transport federation, has come to me strongly supporting this agreement. this agreement is also environmentally sustainable: the protocol contains clear legal obligations for sustainable exploitation, based on scientific assessment, providing certainty that only the surplus will be fished. so this is what we asked for: only the surplus will be fished. finally, the protocol is compliant with international law. let me explain this a little bit further. first i would like to make one point very clear: no legal authority until now – including the united nations, the european court of justice or the legal service of any of the eu institutions (commission, council, and parliament) – has ever said that an agreement with morocco covering western sahara is illegal. nobody. what they do say – and rightly so – is that such an agreement must fulfil certain conditions; in particular, referring to this fisheries agreement, that fishing activities must benefit the local population. these are the conditions we have to meet, and may i also say that, if we had legal advice saying that any agreement with morocco would be illegal, then no agreement referring to the western sahara could be adopted by this parliament. i would like to remind you that we already have an agreement with morocco, including the western sahara territory. you have voted for trade and other agreements referring to this territory. and i think that this is the only way to keep working with morocco, unless you think that we have to end our relations with this country. of course it is up to you to decide. i would also like to underline that there is a human rights clause within the protocol. i would also like to underline that this agreement is better, absolutely better, than the agreements you have voted for before. why? because we have introduced a very detailed reporting obligation on morocco. morocco must report on the economic and social benefits, for example on employment and investments. but they also have to report on the geographical distribution of all sectoral support projects. so we can see whether the local population can benefit from our taxpayers’ money. i may also say to you that, if we have any doubts, we can also ask our delegation in morocco to carry out fact-finding missions. so there are a lot of safety clauses referring to all your concerns. i have listened to your concerns, the concerns of parliament and i have done my part. of course i can understand that your concerns perhaps go further than fisheries and this agreement, but i would like to underline that realistically this is the best agreement we have. i think that the best way for the european union to go in the interests of all the moroccan population, including all territories’ populations, is to keep in contact with morocco and come to an agreement.

on behalf of the ppe group. we all know that there are serious shortcomings in the implementation of national roma integration strategies in the member states of the union. the question here and now is whether member states are serious about making efforts to improve the situation of roma and are prepared to take the first steps in a long process to do so. positive change is very difficult to hope for in the short term, but the foundations for future success should be laid now. money is only one of the important factors in dealing with problems effectively: we very often see that the funds available do not reach the beneficiaries and we also see serious irregularities in the monitoring of programmes. it is also important that the geographical balance be maintained between the member states: not only the focus on communities concentrated on the periphery of large cities, but also the problems of roma living in rural areas. in particular, there are some astonishing insights that in romania, the western and central regions of the country do not need to be looked at in this respect, because the real problems are in the south and east. we must say emphatically that this is not so. in the case of romania, roma communities are present throughout the country and unfortunately in similarly difficult social conditions. the commission has an important role to play in the implementation of these strategies, as improving the situation of roma communities is a common responsibility and a european issue that cannot be seen as the responsibility of a few member states alone.
madam president, the european roma integration strategy was drawn up in 2011, followed by the national reports in 2012 and a first report by the european commission and the council in 2013. these initiatives create a solid basis in the process of solving roma problems. however, i do see the inadequacy of the gender approach, which means that there is a need to focus the analysis in this direction, which is practically the aim of the report we are going to vote on tomorrow. roma women are known to live in a deeply patriarchal, traditionalist society, where economic dependence, domestic violence, limited access to education, early marriage and pregnancy have consequences on their health, personal fulfilment and social status. the european roma integration strategy must address the integration of roma women separately, which can reduce discrimination against them in general, as well as within their own community. in my view, the strategy should focus on cooperation between member states to avoid tensions, exchange of good practices and cross-border solutions, given the traditional mobility of these ethnic groups, and also provide for concrete measures to involve non-governmental organisations, but also the ethnic groups themselves, in solving this complex european problem of the european integration of the roma. answer to a question asked under the 'blue card' procedure. it's a delicate matter. moreover, in romania there have been numerous concrete measures by which such early marriages are practically not legal. there is talk of engagement, there is talk of other such measures, but it is very true that, in view of the best interests of the child, such marriages are not permitted in my country. this means that the legislation is basically the same as the european one. the problem is that we have to know these traditions very well, because they exist. we have to try, through education, as it's been said here, especially, to bring about change within the community, which basically leads to this idea of communication, of talking to these ethnicities.
in writing. following the poor progress made by member states in implementing national roma integration strategies, the european parliament resolution of 12 december calls on the member states and the european commission to create an effective mechanism at eu level for the implementation and evaluation of national roma integration strategies. the resolution also calls for the active involvement and empowerment of roma people in the development and management of roma inclusion strategies and policies, with the commission tasked with establishing a mechanism to monitor and take firm action in the event of violations of roma fundamental rights. education plays an important role in the process of roma integration, and the resolution calls on states to facilitate access to education for roma children and to provide the necessary infrastructure for teacher training to prevent school dropout. the involvement of ngos in the education process can ensure access for roma to mentoring programmes and vocational training courses that allow access to the labour market. an integrated approach to the use of european and national funds, as well as the involvement of civil society, local and regional authorities, would ensure the success of national roma integration strategies in urban and rural communities.
mr president, in the context of today's international anti-corruption day, i draw attention to the fact that the socialist government in romania continues to obstruct justice and the fight against corruption. the 2014 budget brings significant cuts to the main institutions in the field of justice. ani will lose 10,3 million lei compared to this year, or 34,2%, contrary to the recommendations of the cvm commission. the budget of the ministry of justice is reduced by 94 million lei compared to last year, and that of the public ministry is reduced by 41 million lei compared to 2013. in addition, the ponta government has a minister being sued by the dna and several deputies and senators are protected by the parliament through usl majority decisions.
mr president, on 1 january 2014, after seven long years, the transitional barriers will be lifted on the labour markets in all member states. in britain, a vicious media campaign has created the false expectation of an allied romanian and bulgarian invasion. british officials have even hinted that new restrictions could be introduced by britain. this is simply false and dangerous as it encourages public disapproval of the rights enshrined in the european treaties. the so-called debate in britain would be hilarious if it were not shameful, and i regret that this house did not find worthy of debate the implications of the british attitude to the completion of the single market.
i call on the european parliament to get involved in establishing a strict control of the opinion poll market at continental level, with exemplary penalties for offenders. we cannot talk about democracy and free elections if they are tainted by blatant fraud. ladies and gentlemen, i said those two phrases in this room on march 12, 2012. but i spoke, i heard. since then, there have been parliamentary elections in my country, romania, which have also been stolen. on 25 may 2014, elections will also be held for the european parliament. i have no doubt that these will be stolen as well. the mechanism is simple, like in a stupid movie. the secret services run everything with the approval of the yankee masters of the penal colony called romania, and the undercover officers of this new securitate have made their own lying polling institutes and television stations. some european officials turn a blind eye. what's the point of elections? how effective is the european parliament?
in writing. the fight against organised crime requires a coherent response from the european union in the field of judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters. with a budget of €472 million for the period 2014-2020, the justice programme will extend the application of member states' laws and policies and will contain simplified administrative procedures and harmonised rules. funding from the justice programme will be targeted at concrete results. one of these is to meet the eu's target of training 700,000 legal practitioners by 2020. access to the programme's funds will be open to public agencies and private bodies in the member states and candidate countries wishing to participate in the justice programme. it is important that public procurement under this programme is protected and that olaf investigates suspected fraud with european money.
rapporteur for the opinion. − mr president, the civil protection mechanism as a fundamental role is a key solidarity-based instrument for a european rapid response to a wide spectrum of crises. both the opinion of the committee on foreign affairs and our report on the solidarity and mutual defence clauses supported the general approach of the proposal, which consists in transforming the current ad hoc system into pre-planned disaster management while respecting the leading role and primary responsibility of member states in civil protection. the committee on foreign affairs welcomed the increased focus on prevention and preparedness and highlighted the importance of shared risk assessment and contingency planning. a need to ensure consistency with the implementation of the solidarity clause is clearly underlined in our document and in the final report we are debating today. a significant point in the foreign affairs committee’s opinion was the need to reach an adequate balance between the imperative of rapid response on the one hand, and coherence of eu external relations on the other. finally we appreciate the constructive approach and support of commissioner kristalina georgieva and the representatives of the eeas.
the recent typhoon that caused widespread disaster in the philippines is a tragic reminder of the increased incidence of extreme weather events caused by climate change. extreme weather will cause more and more such devastating events in the future. while we know these events will increase in frequency and intensity, we cannot predict when they will occur. this is why it is all the more important to be prepared for such situations, to be able to react quickly and effectively, and the union civil protection mechanism will help us in this regard. the agreement that has been negotiated with the council will significantly improve the current mechanism, ensure better risk assessment, increased public awareness, improved coordination and communication, increased operational capacity. so we are not just talking about flimsy steps or superficial progress in the best direction. we are talking about real improvements, based on a strengthened european solidarity, and they can really help save lives.
madam president, commissioner, i consider it very important that local and regional authorities are involved in emergency assistance and civil protection operations. at the same time, cross-border regions must step up their cooperation in order to coordinate joint intervention actions. the harmonisation of emergency codes across all member states through the new mechanism contributes significantly to the rapid detection and early warning of disasters and will allow for common prevention and response measures. increasing mobility in emergency situations by creating a system of alternative transport routes can improve access to emergency assistance, in particular in remote or limited areas. the on-the-spot intervention modules, supported by volunteer teams, in less populated areas have demonstrated a rapid response capability in the field of civil protection. the preparation and coordination of voluntary actions by teams of experts contributes to increasing the capacity to intervene. i congratulate the reporter on her excellent work.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because i believe that improving the functioning of the judiciary is essential for romania, especially in the context of the existence of the cvm for my country. therefore, the exchange of good practices, information sessions or other forms of cooperation between european judicial frameworks could be a solution to make the system more efficient in my country as well. the objectives must be to ensure the application of european law but also to guarantee access to justice for our citizens. long and exhausting trials must become the exception rather than the rule. and the professionalism and impartiality of the magistrates be a certainty. this will also increase the degree of trust in the judiciary and ultimately in the authorities.
in writing. i voted in favour of this programme, which funds actions at european level that contribute to the further establishment of a european area of justice based on mutual recognition and trust, in particular by promoting judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters. i welcome its adoption, as the actions it funds have the potential to foster mutual trust between member states and to improve cross-border cooperation, the development and dissemination of best practice in the field of justice. the justice programme for the period 2014-2020 is expected to have a significant impact on judicial cooperation in the eu, by funding a number of concrete actions, such as analysis, training, mutual learning and cooperation activities. the programme should promote support for networking activities at european level between specialised bodies and entities, as well as national, regional and local authorities and ngos. finally, i am pleased that, in the implementation of all its actions, the programme seeks to promote equality between women and men and the rights of the child, in particular through child-friendly justice.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation establishing the 'justice' programme for the period 2014-2020. in the process of developing a european area of justice, i consider it particularly important to guarantee the rule of law and an independent and efficient judiciary and to respect fundamental rights and common principles such as non-discrimination, gender equality, effective access to justice for all. the 'justice' programme has a budget of eur 377 604 million and aims to: - facilitate and support judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters - 30% of the financial envelope; - support and promotion of judicial training, including linguistic training on legal terminology, in order to foster a common legal and judicial culture - 35% of the financial envelope; - facilitating effective access to justice for all, including promoting and supporting the rights of victims of crime, while respecting the right of defence - 30% of the financial envelope; - support for drug policy initiatives in the areas of judicial cooperation and crime prevention which are closely linked to the overall objective of the 'justice' programme - 5% of the financial envelope. the commission shall adopt annual work programmes in the form of implementing acts.
in writing. − i supported the report because the programme can play a very important role in combating discrimination. we all see populist parties gaining ground amid the crisis. and often these parties are based on messages that encourage discrimination against foreigners. as a romanian, i know the difficulties faced by my fellow citizens in many states. what worries me is that in some of these countries, the very authorities are encouraging these trends. that's why i think the program should be based primarily on information campaigns that combat discrimination.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the new programme now focuses on promoting the rights associated with european citizenship, the principles of non-discrimination, equality between women and men, children's rights, data protection and consumer and business issues. the 'rights and citizenship' programme has its origins in the simplification and rationalisation of funding instruments, being the successor of the three current daphne iii programmes, progress (which funds actions related to gender equality and the anti-discrimination section) and fundamental rights and citizenship.
in writing. − the establishment of the 'rights and citizenship' programme for the period 2014-2020 is the natural follow-up, and the necessary response, to combat a number of dangerous phenomena, which have been accentuated in the recent period by the consequences of the economic and social crisis. i am talking about xenophobia, racism, anti-semitism, discrimination, including gender discrimination, exclusion, intolerance. these phenomena are in flagrant contradiction with the union's founding values, with the principles that guide us, with the interests of european citizens. we also need to be aware of the rise in social violence, the problems of young people and women, the decline in trust in democracy and its political institutions. the programme under discussion is primarily aimed at european citizens, raising their awareness of the effects of these phenomena and their rights and obligations. this programme is an important step towards building a genuine european citizenship. this is why i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the 'rights and citizenship' programme for the period 2014-2020.
in writing. − given that the european union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, and that these values are common to the member states in a society characterised by pluralism, non-discrimination, tolerance, justice, solidarity and equality between women and men, i consider that all persons are entitled to enjoy within the union the rights conferred on them by the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) and by the treaty on european union (teu).
in writing. i voted in favour of this programme establishing the resources for the european union to finance actions in the field of equality and citizenship. the general objective of the programme is to contribute to the further development of an area for the promotion, protection and effective implementation of equality and human rights as enshrined in the treaties of the european union and the charter of fundamental rights, as well as in the international conventions on human rights to which the union is a party. for the period 2014-2020, the programme will notably finance a number of concrete actions that should have a real impact on the ground, in particular with the actors most involved in the field of fundamental rights and local citizenship. these actions will consist of analysis, mutual learning, cooperation, awareness-raising and dissemination activities, support to key actors whose activities contribute to the achievement of the objectives of the programme, such as regional and local authorities and ngos, including through action grants or operating grants.
in writing. − the 'rights, equality and citizenship' programme follows the three previous programmes in this field: fundamental rights and citizenship, daphne iii and the 'diversity and the fight against discrimination' and 'equality between men and women' parts of the employment and social equality (progress) programme. the ambitious objectives of the programme are to promote greater protection of children's rights and the rights deriving from union citizenship. furthermore, as the proposed amendments to the original draft resolution underline, the main indicators for measuring the achievement of these objectives should be adapted to measurement standards which can actually be functional to the proper implementation of the programme and thus useful for checking the progress of the programme and any critical points.
in writing. − the 'rights and citizenship' programme 2014-2020 is key to upholding the european fundamental rights which came into law with the lisbon treaty. given the abuses against citizens' rights based on discrimination based on sex, race, ethnic origin, religion or sexual orientation, we need to ensure that we protect european citizens by providing legislative, executive and information support. the funding of such a programme is necessary to ensure its success and effectiveness for the purpose for which it is proposed. if we do not tackle xenophobia, homophobia and other forms of intolerance, we risk jeopardising the very foundations of the european union. moreover, violence against vulnerable groups such as children, young people and women cannot be addressed without coordinating the efforts of ngos with those of national and international authorities. in this context, personal data can also be discussed, which must have a uniform legal framework in all member states. the year 2013 is the year of the european citizen. we have to show them that they won't be forgotten once the theme changes!
in writing. − the rights and citizenship programme aims to promote the rights deriving from european citizenship, with particular regard to the fight against discrimination. at the same time, we must be able to respond to the fact that many european citizens feel that they can only enjoy the rights of european citizenship if they study, work and settle in another member state, whereas the majority of them are not. as regards fundamental rights, the provisions of the charter of fundamental rights are binding only on the eu institutions and on the application of eu law by the member states, and cannot be relied upon by reason of the actions of the member states. if this were to change - and this would obviously require a treaty change - the institution of european citizenship would also have a much greater significance for citizens and confidence in the european institutions would increase.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the adoption of the regulation establishing, for the period 2014-2020, the programme 'rights, equality and citizenship' with a financial envelope for its implementation of eur 439 473 000 and the following specific objectives: - promoting the effective application of the principle of non-discrimination on grounds of sex, racial or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation and respect for the principle of non-discrimination; - preventing and combating racism, xenophobia, homophobia and other forms of intolerance; - promoting and protecting the rights of persons with disabilities; -promoting equality between women and men and developing an inclusive approach to it; - preventing and combating all forms of violence against children, young people and women, and violence against other groups at risk, in particular those at risk of violence in close relationships, and protecting the victims of such violence; -the promotion and protection of the rights of the child; - contributing to the highest level of protection of privacy and personal data; -promote and improve the exercise of the rights attaching to union citizenship; - ensuring that citizens, as consumers or entrepreneurs in the internal market, can exercise their rights under union law, in the light of projects financed under the consumer protection programme.

in writing. − regulation (ec) no 55/2008 provides for the introduction of autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova, by eliminating all customs duties on industrial products and improving access for agricultural products to the european union market. pursuant to that regulation, the autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova apply until 31 december 2015. its application after 1 january 2013 is also conditional on the successful completion of certain procedures within the world trade organisation. it is important to ensure the continuity of trade flows from the republic of moldova until 31 december 2015 and it is also necessary to provide legal certainty to economic operators so that they can continue to import in accordance with the regulation on autonomous trade preferences. it is also important to provide that the autonomous trade preferences apply without interruption until the expiry date laid down in regulation (ec) no 55/2008.
in writing. − the european union's economic relationship with the republic of moldova is very important to the latter, especially in the context of its complicated relations with the russian federation, one of its most important trading partners. regulation (ec) no 55/2008 provides for the introduction of autonomous trade preferences (atps) for the republic of moldova by eliminating all customs duties on industrial products and improving access of agricultural products to the european union market. the current proposal, for which i voted, aims to ensure continuity of trade flows from the republic of moldova until 31 december 2015 and to provide legal certainty to economic operators so that they can continue imports, giving a solid basis to these relations, predictability and security.
in writing. − welcomes the decision to liberalise imports of wine from the republic of moldova into the european union, which will thus be able to be exported in unlimited quantities to the european union as from 1 january 2014, especially since 45,7% of the total exports of the republic of moldova are destined for the eu; on the other hand, it is important that the adoption of this report takes place shortly after the signing of the association agreement with the eu, an agreement which creates the necessary conditions for the diversification of the markets for moldovan producers. in addition, the implementation of the provisions of the association agreement with the eu will bring the republic of moldova closer to european values and facilitate its economic integration and political association with the community.

in writing. − welcomes the amendment of regulation no 55/2008 introducing autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova with a view to liberalising imports of moldovan wine as from 1 january 2014. the european parliament's vote comes at a key moment after the initiation of the eu-moldova association agreement, which also aims to create a deep and comprehensive free trade area. pending the entry into force of the association agreement, scheduled for 2015, the eu must deliver on its promises and urgently liberalise imports of wines from moldova by removing them from annex 1 to regulation 55/2008. it is well known that the ban on exporting moldovan wines to russia, which is in fact a traditional market for moldovan products, blocks its economic development. given that the agricultural sector represents 40% of the moldovan economy and employs a quarter of the workforce, the process of liberalising european wine imports from moldova should take place as a matter of urgency.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation introducing autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova. in the framework of the european neighbourhood policy, the eu-moldova enp action plan and the eastern partnership, moldova has adopted an ambitious programme of political association and further economic integration with the union. in addition, moldova has already made significant progress in regulatory approximation with a view to convergence with union legislation and standards. negotiations for a new association agreement, including the establishment of a deep and comprehensive free trade area between the union and moldova, started in january 2010 and were completed in july 2013. that agreement provides for the full liberalisation of bilateral trade in wine. in order to support moldova's efforts under the enp and the eastern partnership and to ensure an attractive and reliable market for its wine exports, it is necessary to liberalise imports of wine from moldova into the union without delay. in order to ensure the continuation of trade flows from moldova and legal certainty for economic operators, it is necessary that the autonomous trade preferences apply without interruption until the expiry date set out in regulation (ec) no 55/2008. it shall apply from 1 january 2014.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because the health and safety of workers at the workplace is of particular importance. the convention on the safety of chemicals at work is a very useful instrument that outlines the principles to be followed to achieve a high level of safety at work. employers have a responsibility to prevent the exposure of employees to chemicals that could endanger their health. workers must also comply with safety standards at work to prevent accidents. i therefore believe that the ratification by all member states of those parts of the convention on the safety of chemicals at work which fall within the competence of the european union should take place as soon as possible.
in writing. − convention no 170 on chemicals, adopted on 25 june 1990 at the 77th session of the international labour conference, entered into force on 4 november 1993. the aim of the convention is to prevent and reduce occupational diseases and accidents caused by chemicals, but the convention will also improve the protection of people and the environment. the provisions of chemicals convention no 170 address issues relating to: establishing an assessment of chemicals, obtaining information by employers from their suppliers, providing information to workers, the need for appropriate preventive measures and establishing protection programmes for workers. the european union is committed to promoting the decent work agenda, both internally and in its external relations. labour standards are a central element of the concept of decent work. the ratification of ilo conventions by member states therefore sends an important signal as regards the coherence of the union's policy to improve global labour standards. it is therefore necessary to remove at eu level any legal obstacles to the ratification by member states of those conventions, the content of which is not a cause for concern from the point of view of the existing union acquis.
in writing. − i consider this convention to be an important instrument for the protection of workers, the environment and society in general, with a view to ensuring health and safety at work.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft council decision authorising the member states to ratify, in the interest of the european union, the 1990 international labour organisation convention on the safety of chemicals at work (convention no 170). i consider the protection and improvement of workers' health and safety to be an important issue and support the promotion of decent working conditions for all, both inside and outside the union. member states have an obligation under union law to harmonise laws, regulations and administrative practices relating to classification, packaging and labelling and it is therefore important that they ratify the convention in the interest of the union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because the fight against crossborder organised crime must be a priority, both of the european union and of the member states. illegal trade in firearms is a major source of income for international organised crime groups. and very often these weapons and ammunition end up being used by terrorist groups. i too believe that firearms should be marked at the time of manufacture so that the country of origin and the manufacturer of the firearm can be identified. i also believe that the exchange of information between the signatory parties can reduce the phenomenon of cross-border trafficking in firearms. the application of this protocol will lead to an increase in the level of security for citizens of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol against the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition, additional to the united nations convention against transnational organized crime. the convention is the first comprehensive instrument to combat transnational organised crime and illicit trafficking in firearms. i welcome the vote on this resolution because the signing of this protocol would make it possible to prevent and combat illicit trafficking in firearms by better controlling weapons through their marking, import and export authorizations, and by strengthening cooperation and the exchange of information between the states parties. in particular, it is very important that the exchange of information between the parties to the convention be strengthened. we will only be able to combat effectively all forms of trafficking such as arms trafficking if member states cooperate even more than criminal networks. finally, it should be stressed that the protocol enhances the security of european citizens without, however, harming the legal users of firearms.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol against the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition, supplementing the united nations convention against transnational organized crime. the un international convention against transnational organized crime, adopted on 15 november 2000, is the first global instrument to combat transnational organized crime and the illicit trade in firearms. three protocols specify the convention, providing for specific measures to combat specific offences. the protocols concern, respectively, trafficking in human beings, smuggling of migrants and the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms. the european community signed the protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms in january 2002. the protocol aims to prevent, combat and eradicate the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition. it also provides for measures to confiscate weapons which have been the subject of illicit manufacture or trafficking and measures to prevent the illegal reactivation of deactivated firearms. each state party to the protocol also undertakes to retain for at least 10 years the firearms information necessary for their tracing and identification.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because, in order to ensure compliance with the rules of the international trade organisation, the union had to negotiate adjustments to compensate for the increase in customs duties due to the enlargement of the community bloc. the increase of tariff quotas is the most common practice used by the union in such cases. this ensures that the accession of romania and bulgaria to the european union and, at the same time, the application by these two states of community rules on trade, does not affect previous agreements and does not cause trade damage to the partners of the two states.
in writing. − with the accession of bulgaria and romania, the european union has expanded its customs union. consequently, the eu was obliged under wto rules (article xxiv (6) of gatt 1994) to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating rights on the schedules of commitments of any acceding member with a view to agreeing on a mutually advantageous adjustment to compensate for the increase in the consolidated duties and the significant losses associated with it. in general, eu enlargement is a positive factor for wto members. if the countries that joined the wto had higher tariffs than the eu, the wto members would benefit. otherwise, when acceding countries have lower customs duties than the eu and are obliged to increase their customs duties, the eu compensates for the difference. so, in general, the wto member countries have a lot to gain.
in writing. − i believe that eu enlargement is a positive factor for the members of the world trade organisation (wto) and that a trade war between wto members would be in no one's interest, especially in the current context of the global economic recession.
in writing. − the accession of romania and bulgaria to the eu meant that the two countries were included in the customs union of the european union. the eu therefore had to open negotiations with the world trade organisation members on the list of commitments of romania and bulgaria with a view to agreeing mutually advantageous adjustments to compensate for the increase in the consolidated customs duties and the significant losses associated with it. the commission also found that the chinese exporting producers had not provided any evidence that the measures were in line with the requirements of the basic regulation. as is known, the eu-china compensation agreement mainly concerns garlic, mushrooms, chocolate, bakery products and biscuits. given that the eu has already concluded similar compensation agreements with cuba, brazil, australia, new zealand, argentina and the united states, the 2012 eu-china agreement should be approved by the european parliament.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the people's republic of china pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions in the schedules of the republic of bulgaria and romania in the course of their accession to the european union. on 29 january 2007, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with certain other member states of the world trade organisation under article xxiv (6) of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 in the context of the accession to the european union of the republic of bulgaria and romania. the negotiations were concluded and on 31 may 2012 the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the people's republic of china pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions in the schedules of the republic of bulgaria and romania in the course of their accession to the european union was initialled.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft decision on the conclusion of a revised memorandum of understanding with the usa on the import of beef from animals not treated with certain growth promoting hormones and on the increased duties applied by the usa to certain eu products. in 2009, the eu and the us signed a memorandum of understanding that opened the possibility of eliminating all us trade sanctions on eu agricultural products following the wto dispute over hormones in beef in exchange for a zero duty tariff quota on high-quality beef derived from cattle not treated with growth-promoting hormones. under the second phase of the mou, the eu increased the quota for high-quality beef to 45,000 tonnes and the us suspended all trade sanctions on eu products following the hormone dispute between august 2012 and august 2013. as the parties were unable to move to phase three of the mou, the mou expired on 1 august 2013. as the current memorandum provides for the maintenance of the obligations of the parties until 1 february 2014, this decision proposes to extend the second phase until 31 july 2015 in order to give the parties more time to move to the third phase.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation because the partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of côte d'ivoire is a relatively old one and is of importance to both parties, especially in the context of almost all ivorian tuna production being exported to the european union - some 55 000 million tonnes per year. the agreement is therefore economically justified and in line with the objectives of the european union's fisheries policy. last but not least, it should be noted that this agreement provides numerous jobs for both parties, in a context where they are essential for economic growth in the areas concerned.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft decision on the conclusion of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of côte d'ivoire (2013-2018). this new agreement is based on the results of an ex-post evaluation of the protocol between the eu and côte d'ivoire on a fisheries partnership agreement covering the period july 2007 to june 2013. the assessment carried out in june 2012 by independent experts and financed by the commission shows that, from the outset, the agreement was economically justified, reasonable, balanced and effective. the eu and côte d'ivoire are privileged partners, especially in the fisheries sector, since almost all ivorian tuna production is exported to the eu. this represents an average of about 55 billion tons per year. the partnership agreement provides for fishing opportunities to be allocated to two categories of vessels, namely 28 freezer tuna traps and 10 french and spanish floating longliners. the european parliament supports this agreement, but will nevertheless remain vigilant about the quality of the aid granted to the ivorian employment sector. we also call on the commission to strengthen controls on the effective use of the funds lost and on illegal fishing.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, the exceptional geographical situation of the canary islands being an obstacle to their development. in this respect, the proposed import duty reductions, as well as the whole set of specific measures for the outermost regions, will help this area to overcome the structural difficulties it is facing. the extension of the existing autonomous tariff quotas for a further period of 7 years is therefore a natural step, offering economic operators a long-term perspective to reach a level of activity that would allow the stabilisation of the economic and social environment on the islands.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation opening and providing for the administration of autonomous tariff quotas of the union for the import of certain fishery products into the canary islands from 2014 to 2020. the canary islands are among the outermost regions of the european union for which special measures may be provided for, in accordance with article 349 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, in order to overcome the economic disadvantages which these regions face as a result of their geographical location. the exceptional geographical situation of the canary islands in relation to the sources of supply of fishery products essential for domestic consumption entails costs that represent a significant burden for this sector. the negative effects of this natural handicap can be remedied by temporarily suspending customs duties on imports of the products concerned from third countries. the proposed import duty reductions, in combination with other specific measures for the outermost regions, will help the canary islands to overcome the structural difficulties they are facing. the government of the kingdom of spain has requested the extension of the measures provided for in council regulation (ec) no 645/2008 of 8 july 2008 opening and providing for the administration of autonomous community tariff quotas for imports of certain fishery products into the canary islands which expire on 31 december 2013.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on unlocking the potential of cloud computing in europe given the economic potential of the cloud to increase europe's global competitiveness, and the fact that it can become a powerful tool for economic growth and employment. we call on the commission to take the lead in promoting standards and specifications in support of privacy-friendly, reliable, highly interoperable, secure and energy-efficient cloud services as an integral part of a future union industrial policy. reliability, security and data protection are necessary to enhance consumer confidence and competitiveness. we consider digital skills among all citizens to be of particular importance and urge member states to develop concepts on how to promote the safe use of internet services, including cloud computing services. we stress that the development of cloud services risks, in the absence of or in the case of insufficient availability of broadband infrastructure, to amplify the digital divide between urban and rural areas, which will make it increasingly difficult to achieve territorial cohesion and regional economic growth.
