in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the opinion on the evaluation report on berec and the office. the body of european regulators for electronic communications (berec) was established to help define the technical and policy guidelines for the completion of the internal market, with a dual objective: to give regulators as much independence as possible and to improve the consistency of their implementation of the regulatory framework at european level. i consider that the completion of the internal market is a continuous process, best facilitated by improving regulation in individual national markets, and the most robust and sustainable way to achieve this (ensuring that regulatory decisions are considered legitimate within national markets) is through the 'bottom-up' approach currently represented by berec. we recommend that the commission and the member states ensure adequate funding for both berec and the national regulatory authorities. they also argue that the necessary cooperation, coordination and informal aspects of governance take time to develop fully. berec should act in the interest of european citizens and therefore mechanisms related to accountability to the european parliament, which is the only directly elected institution to represent the interests of european citizens, should be strengthened.
in writing. − i have voted today in favour of the berec report, because i believe it covers very well all the issues that are either not working or could be working better within the agency. the report acknowledges that berec, like any other agency in times of financial constraint, is faced with limited resources. however, it also gives valuable feedback on what still needs to be done to improve the efficiency and relevance of its activities. i believe that the relationship between berec and the national regulatory authorities should be better defined and the duties and tasks within the agency should be clearly demarcated. moreover, the independence of the office from all interested stakeholders and its members should be respected with consistency. not lastly, i also think that timely debate at the development stage of the work programme with all interested stakeholders should be a priority and better communication should be ensured, so that stakeholders can engage more efficiently and in a more timely way with the agency. because all these issues have been taken on board in what i see as a very balanced report, i have wholeheartedly voted today in favour of this report.
in writing. − i supported this text and welcome the fact that the reform of the common fisheries policy will include greater decentralisation of decisions, at a level closer to those involved. among the objectives mentioned, romania prioritises support for coastal and small-scale fisheries and freshwater aquaculture. sustainable exploitation of resources cannot be achieved without clear measures to reduce the environmental impact of fishing activities. the promotion of the coastal and small fleet supports such measures because of the benefits to the local community and the environment. last but not least, i should like to point out that the commission's proposal to reduce the european quota for cod by 15% will directly affect my country, and in the black sea only romania and bulgaria are subject to these quotas. we need to encourage the other riparian states to get involved.
in writing. − the reform addresses the biggest and most persistent problem of the common fisheries policy, which is overfishing. the council of the european union is obliged to act sustainably in its annual decisions on the volume of catches. overfishing should be stopped by 2015 to the extent possible, in order to allow fish stocks to recover. it is specified that a postponement to a later date (at the latest by 2020) is only allowed if the economic and social sustainability of the fleets concerned is seriously affected. in future, therefore, all stocks must be managed on the basis of the principle of maximum sustainable yield. member states will have to allocate fisheries resources to fishermen on the basis of objective and transparent criteria. these criteria must be of an environmental, social and economic nature. this can benefit those fleet segments that demonstrate that they can create above average jobs and that they affect the environment below average. the european parliament has sought greater transparency not only in the allocation of quotas but also in the data collected by member states on the state of stocks, which must be made available to all interested parties, subject to compliance with data protection provisions.
in writing. − i believe that the fundamental objectives of the fisheries policy are being met.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting the regulation on the common fisheries policy (cfp), amending council regulations (ec) no 1954/2003 and (ec) no 1224/2009 and repealing council regulations (ec) no 2371/2002 and (ec) no 639/2004 and council decision 2004/585. the scope of the cfp shall include the conservation of marine biological resources and the management of fisheries targeting such resources. in addition, it shall cover market and financial measures taken in support of its objectives, freshwater biological resources and aquaculture activities, as well as the processing and marketing of fishery and aquaculture products, where such activities take place in the territory of the member states or in union waters, including by fishing vessels flying the flag of third countries and registered in third countries, or by union fishing vessels, or by nationals of member states, without prejudice to the primary responsibility of the flag state, taking into account the provisions of article 117 of the united nations convention on the law of the sea of 10 december 1982.
in writing. − i supported this text because the rules on the common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products are of particular importance from the point of view of consumer protection. i therefore welcome the fact that food information for them will be at the heart of this regulation. given the increasing variety of fishery products, it is important to allow consumers to make informed choices. they should therefore have access to clear information on the origin and method of production. at the same time, it is necessary to ensure that imported products entering the eu market comply with the same marketing requirements and standards that union producers must comply with.
in writing. − i believe that this amendment should take into account the need to regulate the provision of information on gear types, as regards products obtained from wild caught fish species.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the council's first reading position with a view to adopting the regulation on the common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products, amending council regulations (ec) no 1184/2006 and (ec) no 1224/2009 and repealing council regulation (ec) no 104/2000. the regulation adopted establishes a common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products ('common market organisation') which contains the following elements: trade organisations; marketing standards; consumer information; competition rules; market knowledge. since fish stocks are common resources, their sustainable and efficient exploitation can in certain cases be better achieved by organisations composed of members from different member states and regions. it is necessary to encourage the possibility of setting up producer organisations and associations of producer organisations at national or transnational level, based on biogeographical regions, as appropriate. those organisations should take the form of partnerships aiming at the development of common and binding rules and ensuring a level playing field for all parties involved in fishing. when such organisations are set up, it is necessary to ensure that they remain subject to the competition rules laid down in the adopted regulation.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the european union must play a leading role in the responsible management of resources of all kinds. this report is a step forward in our efforts to exploit our fisheries resources sustainably and rationally. we are also talking about alignment with the objectives of the common fisheries policy. addressing the vulnerability of deep-sea stocks with caution, as well as banning certain fishing methods that could destroy the ecosystems in which they operate, are measures that will considerably reduce the impact of fishing on the environment. furthermore, measures to reduce unwanted catches of deep-sea species should be strengthened. finally, i believe that holders of fishing authorisations should be encouraged to actively participate in the assessment of the stocks of species on the ocean floor.
in writing. − the deep-sea fisheries in the north-east atlantic are characterised by two very different practices, on the one hand, traditional coastal fleets using paragates in portugal and, on the other, large nomadic trawlers operating mainly under the french or spanish flag. in total, deep-sea species account for around 1% of the quantities landed in the north-east atlantic. i voted in favour of this report because it fully supports the commission's proposal which has the potential to ensure the sustainability of both commercially exploited and accidentally caught deep-sea species and to prevent significant adverse effects on vulnerable marine ecosystems. the draft report aims to strengthen the commission's proposal in the following key areas, among which i would like to mention: identifying deep-sea species and the most vulnerable species; identifying and protecting vulnerable marine ecosystems; establishing an annual assessment of fleet capacity by member states; the obligation to carry out an impact assessment before issuing or renewing fishing authorisations for deep-sea gears; financial assistance for the transition to more sustainable fishing gear.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation laying down specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters in the north-east atlantic and repealing regulation (ec) no 2347/2002. the objectives of the adopted regulation are: - to ensure the sustainable management and exploitation of deep-sea species, while reducing the impact of deep-sea fishing activities on the marine environment; - prevent significant adverse effects on vulnerable marine ecosystems and ensure the long-term conservation of deep-sea fish stocks; - improve scientific knowledge of deep-sea species and their habitats; - implement technical measures on fisheries management recommended by the north east atlantic fisheries commission (neafc). - to minimise and, where possible, prevent by-catches; - apply prudential and ecosystem-based approaches to fisheries management and ensure that the measures taken by the union for the sustainable management of deep-sea fish stocks are in line with the resolutions adopted by the united nations general assembly, in particular resolutions 61/105 and 64/72.
in writing. - i voted for this report because natural and man-made disasters have multiplied and worsened in recent years, with disproportionate effects on member states but also on developing countries. effective ways of improving europe's ability to deal with unforeseen events can reduce the costs to the union's economy and the obstacles to growth. despite reservations in some member states, solidarity with those who are suffering is more important than bureaucratic obstacles or national reticence. in this context, through another instrument, the solidarity fund, my country is receiving financial assistance to cover the damage caused by the drought in the summer of 2012. we must not overlook the international dimension of this civil protection mechanism which was recently activated for the philippines, which was badly affected by tropical cyclone haiyan.
in writing. − the number and severity of natural and man-made disasters have increased significantly in recent years and climate change is expected to trigger major disasters in the future. civil protection remains the responsibility of the member states and the purpose of european legislation is to support and complement the actions of the member states and to promote cooperation and consistency. it is therefore important to further promote existing guidelines on risk assessment and mapping as well as on host country support, to make clearer reference to future guidelines presented in order to improve the comparability of member states' risk management plans and to harmonise the definition of host country support with that used in the eu guidelines. the union mechanism should promote continued regional cooperation in the field of exchange of knowledge and good practices as well as in training programmes. the eu's funding of assets and the establishment of the european emergency response capability in the form of a voluntary grouping are also important steps towards a better and more reliable european disaster response system.
in writing. − the establishment of a european civil protection mechanism is an idea that i have advocated, and which responds to real needs, namely a rapid, effective, coherent response in cases where this intervention is required. we all agree that, for example, extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and more destructive, and the number of victims is increasing. where these phenomena are of a cross-border nature, common procedures and proper coordination of the intervention teams' efforts are needed. i also called for the establishment of a european civil protection body to which all member states would contribute and which would be equipped with the necessary means for a very rapid first response. that is why i voted in favour of adopting the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on a union civil protection mechanism. it would mean a better capacity to manage the risks faced by civil protection mechanisms, in the spirit of solidarity between member states.
in writing. − i believe that the union and the member states should coordinate their respective support programmes in order to increase the effectiveness and efficiency of providing support and policy dialogue, in accordance with the established principles on strengthening operational coordination and for harmonising policies and procedures.
in writing. − natural and man-made disasters are an inevitable reality. climate change is causing a series of natural disasters that cannot be identified with precision. crimes caused by acts of terrorism, nuclear or radiological accidents have left hundreds of thousands of people vulnerable. the european union needs to have a civil protection mechanism in place in such situations to be able to react effectively and avoid a mass spread of panic. each member state has a safeguard mechanism which must be subject to a common standard in order to provide all union citizens with an immediate response in emergency situations. furthermore, we need to coordinate with humanitarian aid experts and exchange good practices on lessons learned in interventions to ensure concrete results. the regional dimension must also be integrated into the civil protection mechanism as many member states in the same region are exposed to similar risks. the commission's responsibility to set up the emergency response centre (erc), which is a central element of the mechanism, should therefore have a functional basis for all member states in the event of a disaster.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on a union civil protection mechanism. the union civil protection mechanism (the 'union mechanism') aims to strengthen cooperation between the union and the member states and to facilitate coordination in the field of civil protection with a view to improving the effectiveness of systems for preventing, preparing for and responding to natural and man-made disasters. the union mechanism shall promote solidarity between member states through practical cooperation and coordination. the protection to be provided by the union mechanism shall cover in the first place persons, but also the environment and tangible property, including cultural heritage, against: - all types of natural and man-made disasters, including the consequences of terrorist acts; - technological, radiological or environmental disasters; - marine pollution and acute health emergencies occurring within or outside the union. in the event of the consequences of terrorist acts or radiological disasters, the union mechanism may cover only preparedness and response actions. the financial envelope for the implementation of the union mechanism for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 368 428 000 in current prices.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. irresponsible actions by financial market participants have undermined the confidence of all actors, and in particular of citizens, and measures to regain that confidence are particularly important for economic growth. to this end, we need financial reforms that embody a high degree of responsibility and prudence, with a view to eliminating irresponsible lending and borrowing practices. i believe that this directive will provide a high level of protection for buyers of real estate within the eu and at the same time provide a legal framework that ensures the responsible functioning of the mortgage market.
in writing. − the financial crisis has made it clear that irresponsible behaviour by market participants has serious effects on the stability of the financial system. the loss of credibility of market participants directly affects the european union's sustainable growth strategy, calling into question the union's ability to achieve its proposed 2020 targets. loans in a foreign currency without fully understanding the currency risks involved have been to the detriment of the consumer, creating problems in the internal market for credit agreements. this type of loan was sometimes aggressively promoted, giving the buyer a false illusion that it could "beat the market". given the significant role that mortgages play for households in the union, i believe that we need stricter regulations for creditors and credit intermediaries. consumers who take out a credit agreement for residential property should be made aware of all the benefits and risks to which they are exposed throughout the life of the credit, not just for a short period of time.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the directive on credit agreements for residential property. taking out a mortgage loan is one of the most important financial decisions in a person's life, as it involves a financial commitment that can last for many decades. the eu mortgage market is considerable: in 2008, the balance of mortgage loans for housing in the eu27 amounted to almost eur 6 trillion, which is about 50% of eu gdp. many european citizens have lost confidence in the financial sector, loans have become increasingly difficult for borrowers to repay, and the number of defaults and foreclosures has increased. the approved directive provides a common framework for certain aspects of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to contracts covering consumer credit secured by mortgages or otherwise related to residential immovable property. the directive also provides for the obligation to carry out a credit assessment before granting a credit as a basis for the development of underwriting standards in relation to residential immovable property in the member states, as well as for certain prudential and supervisory requirements, including for the establishment and supervision of credit intermediaries, appointed representatives and non-banking institutions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it was necessary to align the regulations in this area with the regime established after the adoption of the treaty of lisbon. for the least developed countries, the union has established a preferential trade regime to promote trade and economic development in those countries. parliament's involvement in the delegated act procedure is particularly important and gives the european legislator a democratic lever to scrutinise the european commission's decisions. last but not least, the adoption of the report will ensure greater coherence of the legislative act proposed by the european commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on imports of rice originating in bangladesh. this regulation is part of the union's common commercial policy, which must respect the objectives of the union's development cooperation policy as set out in article 208 of the treaty, in particular the eradication of poverty and the promotion of sustainable development and good governance in developing countries. as such, it should also be in line with the requirements of the world trade organisation (wto), in particular the decision on differential and more favourable treatment, reciprocity and enhanced participation of developing countries (the 'enabling clause') adopted by the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) in 1979, under which wto member states may grant differential and more favourable treatment to developing countries. this regulation recognises the right of small farmers and rural workers to a decent income and to a safe and healthy working environment and considers respect for that right to be fundamental to the achievement of the general objectives of granting trade preferences to developing countries and in particular to the least developed countries.
in writing. − the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) is a key tool for reducing eu industrial emissions in a cost-effective way. since the start of the second marketing phase in 2008, emissions have been reduced by more than 10%. this decrease is largely due to the slowdown in economic growth, which has caused a reduction in economic activities and production. by the end of 2011, a surplus of 955 million emission allowances had been accumulated, and this surplus is expected to increase. because emissions allowances are being supplied in quantities far in excess of demand, the price of carbon has decreased. this decrease in the carbon price has become a factor in reducing incentives for investment in low-carbon technologies and increasing the risk of the eu being stuck in high-carbon infrastructure. the commission should adapt the auction calendar. it is important that the decision to adapt the auction calendar is executed only once in the third phase of the eu ets trading. this short-term measure should be considered as an option ensuring the stability of the eu ets pending the adoption of the necessary long-term structural measures.
in writing. − the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) established by directive 2003/87/ec has created the world's first major carbon market and sets a price for carbon at eu level. the decision amending directive 2003/87/ec provides that where an assessment of individual industrial sectors indicates that no significant impact on sectors or subsectors exposed to a significant risk of carbon leakage is foreseen, the commission may, in exceptional circumstances, adapt the calendar for the period referred to in article 13 (1) from 1 january 2013 in order to ensure the proper functioning of the market. the commission shall apply a single adjustment of this type to a maximum of 900 million allowances. i am against arbitrary and unpredictable interventions in the carbon market because i believe that they can negatively affect both the carbon market and the industry. i also believe that artificially raising the price of carbon will cause electricity prices to rise, carbon dioxide emissions to shift, and unemployment to rise. that is why i did not support the legislative resolution on the proposal for a decision amending directive 2003/87/ec by clarifying the provisions on the greenhouse gas emission allowance auction timetable.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which i consider to be impactful in improving resource efficiency. i am of the opinion that the council regulation does not take into account the commission communication on 'a resource efficient europe', namely the transformation of the eu economy into a 'circular economy', based on a recycling society, with the aim of reducing waste generation and using waste as a resource. the commission has also concluded that the proposed criteria for the elimination of waste paper are not sufficient to ensure the recycling of paper. recycling brings benefits both economically and socially, and also for improving the quality of life through a clean environment.
in writing. − i supported the european parliament resolution opposing the adoption of the council regulation on the definition of the criteria for determining whether recovered paper is no longer waste pursuant to article 6 (1) of the waste directive 2008/98/ec. the commission has not correctly assessed the impact of the proposed regulation on paper recycling, the waste paper value chain, waste paper shipments and the overall environmental effects of the draft regulation. i consider that stimulating the growth of global trade in this paper which is claimed to 'not fall within the waste category' by circumventing environmental and health protection guarantees would not only have an additional negative impact on the environment during transport, but could also lead to a decrease in the recycling rate of paper in europe due to the reduced availability of waste paper, so that the paper producer may have to substitute the product at least partially by increasing the production of virgin fibres in europe, which implies higher energy consumption and higher co2 emissions, which would again contravene the criterion of avoiding harmful effects on the global environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report and i would like to point out that although we have a roma strategy, its implementation at member state level is lacking. in this context, roma women face several forms of discrimination. moreover, now that the election campaign is in full swing, roma have become real targets for the authorities in some countries. the principle of free movement is systematically violated. those who use roma as a campaign theme should do so in a constructive way. they should show the electorate what they have done to integrate this community and not seek illegal solutions to their continued expulsion or discrimination.
in writing. − the issue of roma integration has been a constant focus of the european parliament and the european institutions, as well as national governments. we must note both the recent efforts and achievements, the awareness of the seriousness of the roma ethnic problems, and the obstacles that still exist in the way of implementing some of the policies designed to solve them. there are obstacles of a different nature, and i think we still have to take that particularity into account. i voted in favour of the resolution on gender discrimination in the case of the roma ethnic group because it addresses one of the most serious problems faced by members of this ethnic group. discrimination against roma women is a sad and hard-to-remove reality. there needs to be a change in culture both within the ethnic group and in the way institutions address this issue. i have noted with satisfaction some of the proposals in the resolution, which directly concern roma women, and which, if applied consistently and in good faith, can change their lives for the better. i also welcome the proposals for measures to actively combat poverty among roma women, social diseases, illiteracy and to increase education.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the gender aspects of the european framework for national roma integration strategies. i think this is a very important topic, because it allows one of the many aspects of the roma integration issue to be approached through the perspective of those who perhaps suffer most from the precarious socioeconomic situation in which too many roma europeans currently live. empowering roma women is one of the aspects that should be given special attention in eu strategies, so that they can take control of their lives, becoming visible agents of change in their communities and having their voices heard to influence policies and programmes that affect them. strengthening the socio-economic resilience of roma women, i.e. their ability to adapt to the rapidly changing economic environment, by saving and preventing the decline of assets, is a crucial point that, if properly implemented on the ground in conjunction with local authorities, could have concrete positive effects.
in writing. − free movement and mobility within the eu has brought the issue of the roma community, one of the largest ethnic groups, numbering some 12 million people, to the attention of many member states. roma accuse themselves of often being victims of discrimination and social exclusion, living in poverty, with limited access to social and health services, and decent housing. the first phenomenon, and it's particularly dangerous, is generalization. when we talk about roma, we often fail to mention that a good number of them are perfectly integrated and lead normal and respectable lives in society. the second aspect is their identification as criminals, also with a degree of generalization. and here we have a distortion of the truth, by omission or lack of clarification. it is not specified what percentage of the entire roma community falls under the heading 'crimes', nor the nature of the crimes. it should be noted that roma are not the big criminals anywhere in the eu, but perhaps small criminals, but these deviations from the law are heavily publicized. improving living conditions and combating discrimination against roma is a collective responsibility at european level. the mere transfer of responsibilities from one member state to another only prolongs the integration of this ethnic group.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on gender issues in the context of national roma integration strategies. the risk of poverty for roma women exceeds that of roma men and roma families with four or more children are at a higher risk of poverty in the eu. roma integration is a european issue, which must be addressed at european level and not only through national roma integration strategies. we call on the commission and the member states to create a specific guidance and school support system for roma youth, through public education and social services, from pre-school to university, with particular attention to gender issues. we call on member states to develop specific programmes for roma girls and young women to continue primary, secondary or higher education, and to establish special actions for adolescent mothers and early school leavers and to support their continued education by subsidising their entry into the labour market and providing on-the-job training. we call on member states to combat territorial segregation, forced evictions and homelessness faced by roma men and women and to establish effective and transparent housing policies.

in writing. − in an increasingly globalised world, europe must promote new european industrial policies, of which a sustainable automotive industry is an important component. it can and must play a central role in the european economy. this requires member states to implement appropriate structural reforms. coordination of these reforms will lead to increased competitiveness, for example by supporting research and innovation, skills development, retraining, reducing indirect costs, improving labour flexibility through social dialogue, and reducing red tape and payment delays.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the cars 2020 resolution: towards a strong, competitive and sustainable motor industry in europe because it supports the commission's action plan to put the automotive industry at the heart of economic growth. the report highlights important aspects of the automotive industry such as innovation, technology and human resource optimisation, encouraging investment in the sector, while also analysing the repercussions in terms of production and demand. the resolution also calls on the member states to stimulate investment, and stresses that in the context of the economic and financial crisis, a robust internal market covering external markets is needed to cope with competition inside and outside the european union.
in writing. − europe is the world's largest producer of motor vehicles. the european automotive industry accounts for over 12 million direct and indirect specialised jobs. however, the european car industry is going through a difficult period, with sales of new cars in the eu having fallen by 40% over the last six years. at the same time, the demand for cars in emerging markets is continuously on the rise. the low production costs and the need to adapt to the demands of these economies contribute to the increase in the number of relocations with disastrous effects for the union, both economically and socially. i support the commission's initiative to support the competitiveness and sustainability of the motor vehicle sector because i am convinced of the need for a joint action plan to relaunch the european automotive industry. the achievement of the proposed objectives must take into account aspects such as: innovation capacity, employment, the specialisation of workers or the guidelines on european mobility. in the last ten years, an important production chain for the automotive industry has developed in western romania, which supplies components for most european car brands. supporting the production clusters is the main condition for achieving the ambitious targets of cars 2020.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on cars 2020: towards a strong, competitive and sustainable motor industry in europe. i welcome the commission's cars 2020 initiative which aims to increase the role of the automotive industry in the european economy. in developing future policies for the sector, the commission should take into account the entire motor vehicle sector, in particular subcontractors and distribution and after-sales service undertakings. i believe it is essential to maintain and strengthen coherent and dynamic research, manufacturing, production, value and innovation chains in the eu geared towards the production of sustainable cars. i stress the importance of maintaining and strengthening the manufacturing base in europe both for ensuring a decent living for european citizens and for strengthening european industry in order to recover and develop economically. we call for coordination at eu level to step up the fight against the import of counterfeit car parts and stress the importance of respecting the principle of technological neutrality in the choice of standards to protect the investments of first-time market entrants and thus encourage innovation in the car manufacturing sector. we also call on the commission to develop cross-cutting roadmaps covering the development of the energy sector, the transport sector and the ict sector.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because volunteering strengthens civic skills and provides an important experience that can be used in professional life. i also want to stress the importance of promoting volunteering activities, especially among pupils, students and other categories of young people. volunteering can contribute to the economic development of local communities, and the benefits can be felt indirectly across the national economy. i too support the strengthening of the community framework for volunteering. the exchange of information and good practices can thus achieve a higher level of convergence between member states, in particular as regards the participation of european citizens in volunteering activities.
in writing. − the situation of volunteering in the european union is marked by an average involvement rate of 30% according to the eurobarometer of november 2010, with 13 countries above this average, including the netherlands, denmark and sweden, where involvement exceeds 50% of the population. the profile of volunteers at european level indicates a higher degree of activism of citizens with a high socio-economic level and around 20 years of schooling, people active in the labour market and who show a strong interest in public life. the value of volunteering is identified in two major dimensions: the individual development of the people involved in volunteering activities and the development of communities and society as a whole. the contribution of volunteering to individual development is reflected in the acquisition of knowledge, skills and abilities transferable to the labour market, in the potential of volunteering as a lifelong learning opportunity, in the cultivation of social skills such as trust, tolerance, self-esteem, respect for diversity. the contribution of volunteering to community development is reflected in solving local problems by complementing the financial contribution with the work of volunteers, facilitating social cohesion by bringing people together for a common purpose, facilitating social integration and combating the risk of social exclusion of vulnerable social groups.
in writing. − 2011 was the european year of volunteering, to celebrate and promote the commitment of volunteers and volunteer organisations and to help address the challenges facing the field, such as the shrinking number of participants and their tendency to abandon long-term commitments in favour of specific short-term projects. volunteering is increasingly becoming an opportunity to learn and acquire qualifications and skills 'on the job'. a european skills passport has been introduced, which provides an overview of volunteers' skills, allowing them to be recognised for both professional and educational purposes. member states and the commission should establish a single point of contact in the form of a service responsible for volunteering policy. the european year of volunteering has had several positive results and proves how important it is to continue in the same direction to ensure that volunteering does not just remain the focus of a single year-long campaign in a sector of strategic importance to the eu, but becomes a key element of eu policies on social cohesion and culture.
in writing. − i believe that volunteering has an immediate impact on society, as it promotes solidarity between generations and supports active ageing and civic participation throughout life, thus contributing to the goal of social inclusion.

in writing. - i voted for this report. volunteering should be seen as an opportunity to learn and to acquire professional and interpersonal skills. in 2011, the european year of volunteering, over eur 14 billion was invested in events and projects to promote volunteering activities. over 1,600 organizations participated and over 2 million volunteer hours were logged. but things don't have to stop there. unfortunately, there are major discrepancies between member states in legislation on volunteer rights and the way volunteering is organised. there are more and more people who want to volunteer in other member states, but they face legislative barriers. i therefore ask the commission to propose a common european approach to volunteering practices, which will be rapidly transposed into national legislation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on volunteering and volunteering activities in europe. i voted for paragraph 17 which underlines that volunteering, increasingly widespread among both young and old, promotes intercultural learning as well as a sense of european identity and solidarity between generations, and supports active ageing and civic participation throughout life. i also voted for paragraph 32 where we call on member states to implement the provisions of directive 2004/114/ec on the conditions of admission of third-country nationals for the purposes of studies, pupil exchange, unpaid vocational training or voluntary service and to simplify or even eliminate visa procedures for persons wishing to engage in voluntary activities, in particular in the framework of the european neighbourhood policy. we stress that unfortunately, bureaucratic barriers at national level continue to limit opportunities to engage in volunteering activities, which are not yet legally recognised to a sufficient extent in some member states. given the existence of different cultural traditions and practices, there are major discrepancies between member states as regards the legislation applying to volunteering, the rights of volunteers and the way in which these activities are organised.
mr president, unfortunately the vilnius summit was a failure. in its first ever geostrategic confrontation with russia, the eu was defeated. the credibility of the eastern partnership has crumbled and the developments which followed prove that our approach was wrong. from now on, the eu must understand that its enlargement and association with its neighbours are primarily about its own security, not about their transformation; that enlargement and association are a geostrategic exercise; that values cannot flourish before we win the geostrategic contest; that enlargement and association are a process of synthesis between western and eastern european cultures, traditions and security sensitivities; that the eu must transform itself while asking others to transform; that the eu is not the only alternative as at least some countries have other alternatives; and that the eastern european states striving to join the eu must not only reform their internal systems, but pay the price for decoupling from the old soviet imperial structures. therefore, the philosophy of our eastern policy must be changed. the negotiations with ukraine, but also with azerbaijan and others, should restart immediately, so that the association agreement with ukraine can be signed during the next eu-ukraine summit. finally, financial means must be put in place to facilitate the decoupling of ukraine and other neighbouring states from their old geopolitical and geo-economic ties. if we want to change this unfortunate trend, we must learn the lessons of the vilnius summit and not fool ourselves with flattering conclusions.

in writing. in the context of discussing the conclusions of the vilnius eastern partnership meeting, i think it should be stated that the enlargement of the european union is a logical and necessary process for the future of the european project. i cannot agree with those who see enlargement as a threat to the cohesion of the union as a whole. the price of stopping enlargement would be much higher than the costs of enlargement of the union, both in economic and social terms and in terms of security. the eu has the resources to support enlargement, to fight poverty and to reduce the development gap between the different european countries. the rich nations of europe have no reason to feel threatened by the potential flows of economic migrants from the candidate countries. it is a fact that the first to leave are the professional elites in these countries, who are filling the demand for labour in sensitive areas in the rich countries. it is in the interests of the old eu states to invest in the new member countries because as employment in these countries increases, the flow of migrants will decrease. we need a coherent plan and the political will to do that.

in writing. at the third eastern partnership high-level meeting in vilnius, lithuania, the parties reviewed progress in concluding new association agreements between the eu and certain partner countries. the countries that are part of the eastern partnership are armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, moldova and ukraine. the association agreements with georgia and moldova were initialled at the meeting, and will help to create deeper political and economic relations between the eu and these two countries. the agreements will include complex and comprehensive free trade areas, a free trade area covering both goods and services (comprehensive free trade area) and involving a high degree of legislative convergence (deep free trade area). i particularly welcome the initialling of the association agreement between the eu and the republic of moldova, romania's neighbour. the eu is thus extending its sphere of influence to the east, and moldovan citizens will soon be able to enjoy the benefits of belonging to the european family. the republic of moldova is thus taking a historic step for its citizens. i believe that in the future romania will be able to support the republic of moldova in the process of integration into the european union, both in negotiations and in the transposition of european legislation into national legislation.
president-in-office of the council. − madam president, i am delighted to be able to participate in this afternoon’s debate. this discussion takes place exactly two years after the commission tabled its proposals for the package of seven external financial instruments. today is particularly significant in that it paves the way for a vote in parliament and for the subsequent entry into force of these financing instruments. it is important that the external financial instruments package for the period 2014-2020 is approved in good time so as to be operational from the beginning of next year. the union’s external activity needs a solid and clear financial framework that offers an effective basis for programming and implementation for the commission/eeas activities. at the same time, the instruments must be flexible enough to adapt swiftly to developments and changing political and economic circumstances. the proposed package allows for an efficient use of available resources and the most effective impact on the eu’s external action. we have sought maximum coherence and complementarity between the different instruments, as well as the creation of synergies between the external financial instruments and other eu policies. as a result of our negotiations we will have a simplified regulatory environment, and will have provided for easier access to union assistance by partner countries and regions, civil society organisations, smes as well as other stakeholders. the lithuanian presidency has taken forward this work, based on the excellent progress made by earlier presidencies. our aim has always been to bring the whole package to a mutually satisfactory conclusion by the end of this year. the negotiations have been lengthy and not always easy. we have to devote much time to discussions on the overall structure of the instruments, and in particular the issue of delegated acts and some other horizontal issues such as the possibility of reviewing the instruments at mid-term. at the same time, very significant efforts have been made on each individual instrument in order to reach an outcome which is acceptable to all our institutions. i am therefore particularly pleased to confirm that the permanent representatives committee last week endorsed the entire external financial instruments package, and i look forward to a positive vote here in the european parliament. of course this outcome would not have been possible without considerable flexibility from both sides. i am therefore grateful to parliament for demonstrating such a constructive attitude, even when the positions of our two institutions looked far apart. i would particularly like to pay tribute to the work of the chair of the committee on foreign affairs, mr elmar brok, and the chair of the committee on development, ms eva joly. i would also like to thank the rapporteurs for the specific instruments – mr berman (dci); mr bütikofer (ifsp); mr kukan (eni); shadow rapporteurs for the time and expertise which they have brought to the dossier. last but not least, i would like to thank the commission and eeas for their contribution and for their many positive suggestions which were key to helping us reach such a balanced outcome. in adopting the external financial instruments package, the european union will be equipping itself with a comprehensive set of instruments covering a whole range of policies related to its external action. the package will meet immediate, urgent and unforeseen needs as well as more strategic, long-term imperatives, enhancing partner countries’ ownership of their development processes and ensuring the sustainability of eu external aid.

member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank all the rapporteurs for the quality of the report. todayʼs very important discussion to be followed later by a vote on the package of neighbours. secondly, there is consensus that we should support political reforms as well as economic, social and territorial development. the overall funding, which is roughly equal to the current seven years, and not higher. to make the most of these resources we will differentiate between partners and we will strictly implement the incentive-based approach. the majority of funds should go to partners with high ambitions for cooperation with the european union, that are committed to reform and with whom we share a value base.

member of the commission. − mr president, the domestic workers convention of the international labour organization, which recently entered into force, comes at an opportune time, both to improve working conditions for workers amongst the most vulnerable and to contribute to an inclusive economy. with decent conditions, domestic work is able to provide job opportunities and potentially better life conditions for women, low-skilled and migrant workers. on the side of the users, it helps provide quality care, personal and household services and a better balance between family life and work. yet most domestic workers too often remain in the informal sphere and are excluded from labour rights, social security and sometimes even fundamental rights. states ratifying the ilo domestic workers convention are required to take measures to ensure fair and decent working conditions, prevent abuse, ensure equal treatment, protect against discrimination, offer decent living conditions, and provide easy access to complaint mechanisms. there is already a body of union legislation in most matters covered by the convention. overall, the convention and eu legislation share the same approach. eu law is more protective and detailed in some areas and the convention in others. the purpose of the draft council decision submitted to the consent of parliament is to remove any legal impediment to ratifying the ilo domestic workers convention no 189. it will authorise member states to ratify the convention, should they so wish, for the parts of the convention falling under union competence. there are already three council decisions to authorise ratification of other ilo conventions, and this plenary today voted its consent to a similar proposal regarding the chemicals convention no 170, the report by ms steinruck. the implementation of the ilo domestic workers convention is in line with the eu commitment to decent work and the eu strategy to combat trafficking in human beings. the decision to ratify the convention will, however, remain in the hands of the member states. several of them have expressed their intention to do so. the commission is satisfied that the council approved the general approach regarding this proposal in june, and it welcomes the draft recommendation submitted to this plenary session of the european parliament for debate.

the reporter. − commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to thank both my shadow rapporteurs and the european commission for their cooperation. i also thank the economic and social committee for the opinion which i have tried to take into account in the preparation of my own report. by its proposal of 12 june 2013, the european commission proposed to extend the automatic exchange of information between tax administrations of the member states of the european union as part of the intensified fight against tax evasion. under this proposal, dividends, capital gains, all other forms of financial income and account balances will be added to the list of categories subject to automatic exchange of information within the european union. this would make it possible to set up the largest system of its kind in the world in the european union. the proposal, together with the european union's existing directive on taxation of savings and the existing directive on administrative cooperation, which the current proposal aims to amend, will allow member states to exchange as much information as they have committed to exchange with the united states under the us tax compliance and offshore accounts law, known as facta. i also fully support the commission's proposal and consider that it is in line with both the action plan on tax fraud and tax evasion and the european parliament's position expressed in its report on combating tax fraud, tax evasion and tax havens. in times of crisis, when european citizens often face tax increases, it is vital to address issues of tax fraud and evasion. it causes an estimated loss of €1 trillion per year, which is a cost of around €2 000 per year for every european citizen. the directive also responds to requests from several member states for the conclusion of a so-called european union facta, following bilateral agreements between some member states and the united states of america. the proposal is also in line with and complements initiatives at oecd, g8, g20 and global level. to better respond to the challenges of today, we have proposed some improvements, in particular in terms of data protection and privacy. i consider that the exchange of information should respect the existing data protection legislation of the european union, in particular in view of the sensitivity of this issue and recent international developments. i also consider that, once this directive enters into force, the commission should negotiate, on behalf of the european union, agreements with third countries on the automatic exchange of information on the model of the european union's trade policy. in practice, the negotiations with the united states on facta would, i believe, have been more advantageous for the european union and the member states if the commission, with a mandate from the member states, had been the negotiator on behalf of the european union. at the same time, member states should ensure the effective application of the directive by mobilising all necessary human, technological and financial resources, taking into account the volume and complexity of the information subject to automatic exchange. last but not least, i believe it is necessary for member states to use sanctions to obtain this much needed information. i also want to advocate the swift adoption and implementation of the proposal, in line with the timetable proposed by the commission, because the european union has the opportunity to be a leader in setting a global standard for the automatic exchange of information. i therefore regret the position of the ppe group, which is trying to water down the commission's proposal. the automatic exchange of information is an effective way of fighting tax evasion, and amendment no 17 is damaging to the commission's proposal and to the credibility of the european parliament. it is contradictory to speak of an automatic exchange of information and at the same time to insert the statement 'if this information is available'. i understand the reasoning behind the amendment, but i cannot understand the support of the whole ppe group for this direction and therefore i will not support this amendment.

in writing. − this proposal for a directive, concerning the so-called 'pericles 2020' action programme on exchanges, assistance and training for the protection of the euro against counterfeiting, strengthens the current framework for the fight against counterfeiting of the euro. the proposal for a directive introduces a minimum penalty of six months' imprisonment for the production and distribution of counterfeit coins and, in parallel, a maximum penalty of eight years for individuals in the case of distribution of coins with a value of at least eur 5 000.
in writing. − in the first half of 2013, eur 317 000 in counterfeit euro was detected across the european union. this represents an increase of 26 % in comparison to 2012 for the same period. until now, the pericles programme has played an important role in avoiding large-scale counterfeiting which would entail damaging consequences for the eu economy and endanger the stability of the euro and ultimately the stability of all european currencies. with a budget of over eur 7.3 million for the next seven years, pericles 2020 will continue fostering transnational cooperation for the protection of the euro both within and outside the european union. i welcome in particular the fact that the renewed programme seeks the greater involvement of eurojust and of the members of the judiciary working on the fight against euro counterfeiting in its future activities. in the same way as cigarette counterfeiting and smuggling, euro counterfeiting schemes are designed by and benefit organised crime networks at the expense of eu citizens. together with hercule iii, pericles 2020 will help disrupt the activities of organised crime networks and protect the licit economy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation establishing an exchange, assistance and training programme for the protection of the euro against counterfeiting (the 'pericles 2020' programme). the 'pericles 2020' programme shall actively encourage and involve enhanced transnational cooperation for the protection of the euro within and outside the union and with the union's trading partners, also paying attention to those member states or third countries with the highest rates of counterfeiting of the euro. the financial envelope of the programme is eur 7 344 000 (current prices) and is open to the participation of the following groups: - staff of agencies engaged in detecting and combating counterfeiting (in particular police forces and financial administrations, depending on their specific tasks at national level); - staff of the intelligence services; - representatives of national central banks, mints, commercial banks and other financial intermediaries (in particular with regard to the obligations of financial institutions); - magistrates, specialist lawyers and members of the judiciary in this field; - chambers of commerce and industry or other comparable structures capable of providing access to small and medium-sized enterprises, retailers and cash-in-transit companies. for the implementation of the programme, the commission shall adopt annual work programmes.

in writing. - i voted for this recommendation because at least 53 million people, mostly women and girls, are employed as domestic workers. they make a substantial contribution to the global economy and generate 7.5 percent of the salaries of employed women globally. such activities are among the least protected and often opaque forms of work. of the 2.6 million domestic workers in the eu, 89% are women and 50% are migrants, thus vulnerable. by promoting basic labour standards, we will extend the basic rights of these workers and take a step forward in the fight against trafficking in human beings. i can therefore only welcome the fact that the way is now open for the member states to ratify the convention in a very short time. last but not least, i express the hope that a considerable number of countries in the world will follow suit.
in writing. − states that ratify ilo convention 189 on decent work for domestic workers must ensure decent working conditions with social rights and prevent abuse, violence and child labour in the home. the main objective of the convention is to recognise the value of domestic workers and to provide a number of safeguards, such as: defining a domestic worker as a person engaged in domestic gainful activity in an employment relationship; establishing a minimum age for domestic workers; equal treatment for domestic workers and workers in general in terms of normal working hours, overtime compensation, daily and weekly rest periods and paid annual leave and social security protection, with respect for maternity; coverage by the minimum wage for domestic workers where such coverage exists and remuneration established without discrimination on the basis of sex, etc. states should ensure that domestic workers who work for several employers and are usually paid by the hour or day benefit from the same social protection as other workers and pay their social security contributions. it is important to ensure that their salaries are at least equivalent to the national minimum wages laid down by national legislation.
in writing. − considers it necessary for the signatory states to adopt measures aimed at respecting, promoting and raising awareness of fundamental principles and rights in the field of labour (freedom of association and of association, recognition of the right to collective bargaining, elimination of all forms of forced or compulsory labour, effective abolition of child labour and elimination of discrimination in employment).
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the home has been neglected for too long, its economic and social importance has been overlooked. most domestic workers belong to vulnerable groups such as girls, women, migrants, members of disadvantaged communities and children. protecting them is a challenge for the authorities responsible, especially when they come from another country without receiving a work contract before crossing the border. furthermore, domestic abuse is common and easy to cover up. we have to be responsible for those who stay at home or in other people's homes, or we're rightly accused of hypocrisy. the lack of legislation to protect domestic workers by means of effective labour inspection measures, enforcement and sanctioning of breaches of the measures adopted is a disgrace to a democratic union that prides itself on defending human rights. there are over 2.6 million people in the eu who, without our efforts, will be left exposed to risks that can often cost them their lives. thank you!
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft council decision authorising the member states to ratify, in the interest of the european union, the 2011 international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers (convention no 189). most of the rules under the 2011 international labour organisation (ilo) convention no 189 on decent work for domestic workers are largely covered by the union acquis in the areas of social policy, combating discrimination, judicial cooperation in criminal matters and asylum and immigration. the provisions of the convention on the protection of migrant domestic workers potentially affect the free movement of workers an area falling within the exclusive competence of the union. the council should therefore authorise member states which are bound by union law on minimum requirements in the field of working conditions to ratify the convention in the interest of the union.

in writing. − the partnership and cooperation agreement between the republic of armenia and the european communities entered into force on 1 july 1999. armenia has actively participated in the european neighbourhood policy since 2004 and in the eastern partnership since its launch in 2009. this draft recommendation addresses the participation of the republic of armenia in union programmes following its express request in april 2012. the protocol contains a framework agreement on the general principles for the participation of armenia in union programmes and includes standard provisions forming part of such protocols for the enp countries. participation in each programme therefore requires the drafting of a memorandum of understanding (mou) to be signed by both parties. in addition, the participation of the enp countries shall only concern those union programmes whose status and objectives allow such participation. the conclusion of the protocol will allow for the gradual opening up or enhanced participation of armenia in certain union programmes, providing an opportunity to further promote cultural, educational, environmental, technical and scientific links, intensifying people-to-people contacts and sectoral cooperation, in addition to strengthening political relations through the eastern partnership and the conclusion of the association agreement.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft decision on the conclusion of a protocol to the eu-armenia partnership and cooperation agreement on a framework agreement between the eu and the republic of armenia on the general principles for the participation of the republic of armenia in union programmes. the partnership and cooperation agreement between the republic of armenia and the eu entered into force in 1999. armenia has actively participated in the european neighbourhood policy since 2004 and in the eastern partnership since its launch in 2009. the protocol contains a framework agreement on the general principles for the participation of armenia in union programmes. participation in each programme shall be subject to the drawing up of a memorandum of understanding (mou) to be signed by both parties. the participation of armenia shall only concern those union programmes whose status and objectives permit such participation. armenia shall contribute financially to the specific programmes in which it participates. the financial implications differ according to the programme and are specified in the mou. the conclusion of the protocol will allow for the gradual opening up or enhanced participation of armenia in certain union programmes, providing an opportunity to further promote cultural, educational, technical and scientific links, intensifying people-to-people contacts and sectoral cooperation, in addition to strengthening political relations through the eastern partnership and the conclusion of the association agreement.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a council decision amending decision 2002/546/ec as regards its period of application. council decision 2002/546/ec of 20 june 2002 adopted pursuant to article 299 (2) of the ec treaty authorises spain to apply, until 31 december 2011, exemptions or reductions from the 'arbitrio sobre importaciones y entregas de mercancías en las islas canarias' ('the 'aiem') for certain products manufactured locally in the canary islands. on 16 november 2010, spain submitted to the commission a request for an extension of the period of application of decision 2002/546/ec by two years, so that its expiry date coincides with that of the regional aid guidelines 2007-2013. council decision 895/2011/eu of 19 december 2011 amended decision 2002/546/ec by extending its period of application until 31 december 2013. on 28 june 2013, the commission adopted new regional aid guidelines for the period 2014-2020. given that those guidelines enter into force on 1 july 2014, it is justified to extend the period of application of decision 2002/546/ec, as amended by decision 895/2011/eu, by six months in order to coincide with the expiry date of those guidelines.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because i too agree that eu development aid should be better coordinated. it is not normal that in times of crisis we should redouble our efforts and thus waste a lot of money unnecessarily. on the other hand, i believe that assistance should focus more on financing education and health in developing countries. i believe that in these areas coordination would be essential and would lead to concrete results. more use should also be made of the traditional links that some member states have with developing countries. and the aid should be coordinated by those eu members with a more developed distribution network and contacts in the beneficiary countries.
in writing. − recent estimates in the 'non-europe' cost report show that some €800 million could be saved annually by reducing transaction costs if the eu and its member states focused their aid efforts on fewer countries and activities. a further eur 8.4 billion could be saved annually if country allocations were fully coordinated and focused solely on poverty reduction. in view of this, i voted in favour of the legislative resolution containing recommendations to the commission on the coordination of eu donors on development aid. a coordinated action by the eu as a whole, in particular through the establishment of a committee composed of representatives of the commission, the council and the european parliament, has an added value that, in terms of policies and financial leverage, is greater than the sum of the individual actions of its 28 member states and the commission. we call on the commission to present, preferably by 31 december 2015 and in any event no later than the first half of 2016, a proposal for an act on eu donor coordination on development aid, pursuant to articles 209 and 210 tfeu, following the adoption and implementation of a roadmap.

in writing. − i believe that any debate on the external action of the european union must start with the establishment of a set of effective, flexible and adaptable instruments, capable at the same time of achieving the objectives of this approach: the promotion of democracy and the rule of law, respect for international law, effective protection of universal human rights, respect for human dignity and solidarity. equally important is the development of a clear and effective system for assessing the impact of eu financial assistance in implementing these principles. it is also necessary to ensure complementarity between the european union's external action policies and instruments.
in writing. − the proposed regulation will serve as a horizontal framework, in line with the objectives of the simplification agenda for the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, providing unified and harmonised rules for the geographical instruments of the eu's external action. the eu financial instruments are not intended to replace those of the member states or to substitute for private funding or other eu financial interventions. the commission seeks to ensure the coherence and complementarity of the funds, in order to create budgetary synergy by sharing its resources and expertise with those of its partners. innovative financial instruments have a multiplier effect on the eu budget by facilitating and attracting other public and private funding for projects of interest to the eu, but this should not be at the expense of the fair use of eu funds. in the same context, budgetary considerations should also strike the right balance to better align the eu's internal policy objectives with its external objectives, by streamlining initiatives such as the europe 2020 strategy or those in the field of democracy, the rule of law, human rights, entrepreneurship and environmental protection.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because i too want more coherence in the union's external action. funds for non-eu countries should focus mainly on supporting justice reforms. energy projects and projects aimed at combating discrimination should also not be neglected. i am confident that through the external financial instruments the union will become a reference point for the neighbourhood and beyond. i also stress the importance of monitoring how the funds are spent. it is very important that our citizens know that money is being used correctly and leads to concrete results. the annual report will therefore play a special role in showing where improvements can be made in the spending of funds.

in writing. − globally, the european union has assumed an important role through its external policies, focused on conflict prevention and peacekeeping. these objectives, which derive from the fundamental principles of the european union, must, however, be pursued in a coherent and effective manner, by means of appropriate instruments. the variety of factors that can pose direct or indirect threats to the european union and its citizens makes the development of such institutional instruments all the more important. they must contribute to the development of the capacity for rapid reaction, crisis management or the impact of natural phenomena. they must ensure the effectiveness of the union's external policy and act in a complementary manner to policies and instruments with medium- or long-term effects.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation establishing the stability instrument. it will contribute to stability and peace and provide, for the period 2014-2020, direct support for the union's external policies by improving the efficiency and coherence of union action in the field of conflict prevention, crisis preparedness, crisis response and peacebuilding, as well as in addressing global and trans-regional threats. the financial envelope is eur 2 338 719 000. in accordance with the approved regulation, the union shall take measures of development cooperation, as well as measures of financial, economic and technical cooperation with third countries, regional and international organisations and other state and civil society actors. civil society actors include non-governmental organisations, organisations representing indigenous peoples, professional groups and local initiative groups, cooperatives, trade unions, organisations representing economic and social interests, local organisations (including networks) active in the field of decentralised regional cooperation and integration, consumer organisations, women's and youth organisations, educational, cultural, research and scientific organisations, universities, churches and associations or religious communities, the media and all non-governmental associations and private and public foundations likely to contribute to the development of external or internal policies.

in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy is one of the most important ways in which the european union can exert its political influence in the geographical area close to its borders. at this level, there are many factors that need to be taken into account by european decision-makers: organised crime, human trafficking, the flow of migrants. all these factors justify the need for an active neighbourhood policy. but this cannot be achieved without the right tools to deliver the solutions and the results that are expected. the european neighbourhood instrument must generate political and economic incentives capable of giving substance to this major policy of the european union. without factors capable of promoting institutional transformation and policy change, the european union's neighbourhood cannot become the area of prosperity we all want.
in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy aims to create an area of prosperity and good relations with the eu's neighbouring countries. the general objective of the eu's neighbourhood policy is to extend the area of freedom, democracy and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms to the countries in the eu's neighbourhood. this policy can be seen as an investment in the future of the eu and covers 16 partner countries to the east and south of the eu's borders. within the framework of the european neighbourhood policy, the union offers neighbouring countries a privileged relationship based on a mutual commitment to respect and promote the values of democracy and human rights, the rule of law, good governance, employment, human capital development, social protection and the principles of the market economy and sustainable development, with a particular focus on strengthening civil society. gender equality, combating discrimination, social justice, social inclusion and workers' rights should be a cross-cutting objective of all actions undertaken under this regulation. the union should support partner countries in their efforts to create jobs and improve employability, address labour market issues and develop social policies.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european neighbourhood instrument, which directly supports the union's external policy and plays a key role in strengthening its relations with its neighbourhood countries. as part of this policy, the union offers its neighbours a privileged relationship based on a common commitment to the values of democracy, respect for human rights, the rule of law and good governance, as well as the principles of a market economy and sustainable and inclusive development. it is important that the european neighbourhood policy also provides a framework for enhancing the mobility of persons, in particular through the facilitation of visa procedures and, on a case-by-case basis, through visa liberalisation. the union's support through this instrument shall be defined in partnership with beneficiaries in the preparation, implementation and monitoring of union support, including with national and local authorities as well as civil society organisations. this is a positive sign that this instrument is aimed at achieving concrete results in collaboration with the political and civil actors on the ground.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation establishing the european neighbourhood instrument. article 8 of the treaty on european union provides that the union is to develop privileged relations with neighbouring countries with a view to establishing an area of prosperity and good neighbourliness, based on the values of the union and characterised by close and peaceful relations based on cooperation. the adopted regulation establishes a european neighbourhood instrument (eni) with a view to making further progress towards the achievement of an area of shared prosperity and good neighbourliness involving the union and the following countries and territories: the following entries for the countries listed in annex i to the treaty on european union are deleted: within this area of shared prosperity and good neighbourliness, special relations based on cooperation, peace and security, mutual accountability and a common commitment to the universal values of democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights, in accordance with the treaty on european union, will develop. the financial envelope available for the implementation of the regulation approved for the period 2014-2020 is set at eur 15 432 634 000 in current prices. up to 5% of the financial envelope shall be allocated to cross-border cooperation programmes.
