in writing. − accession to the european union is a process of strong political and institutional transformation and is membership of an organisation based primarily on adherence to a set of principles. at the same time, the accession process must guarantee an effective transition to participatory democracy in the candidate countries, support the building of strong anti-corruption mechanisms and open and transparent public institutions. building the rule of law is an imperative, but one that must be undertaken with determination. the benefits of enlargement strengthening the european area of solidarity and security are clear. they cannot be achieved, just as the process of transformation of the member states cannot be achieved in the absence of effective instruments capable of ensuring compatibility between the identity and interests of the candidate state and those of the european union.
in writing. i welcome the vote on the european parliament resolution on the instrument for pre-accession assistance, which i voted in favour of. assistance to the candidate countries, which is expected to amount to almost eur 11 billion for the period 2014-2020, is a strong support for the union's enlargement policy, particularly towards the western balkans and turkey. the enlargement strategy is based on consolidation, conditionality and communication, combined with the union's capacity to integrate new members. the accession process is based on objective criteria and on the application of the principle of equal treatment of all candidate countries, each of which is to be judged on its own merits. progress towards accession depends on each candidate's respect for the union's values and its capacity to undertake the necessary reforms to bring its political, institutional, legal, administrative and economic system into line with the union's rules, standards, policies and practices. i am pleased that this instrument also provides for targeted and more flexible assistance, which gives more responsibility to local authorities, and to reward the progress made by the candidate countries in implementing reforms.
in writing. − mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the proposal for a regulation on the ipa ii pre-accession facility and its focus on a more effective and targeted reform process. i believe that in the pre-accession process the european union should not reinvent the wheel. the best examples of the challenges that arise and need to be addressed in the reform process are found in the experience of the states that joined in the 2004 and 2007 waves. i therefore welcome the importance attached by ipa ii to strengthening the rule of law, including by combating corruption and organised crime, and the focus on public administration reform and good governance. the latter two will be key conditions for the use of the structural funds after accession. and as political and administrative reform goes hand in hand with economic development, i welcome funding for the thematic priorities on employment, including youth employment, fostering competitiveness and strengthening the business environment. last but not least, i would also like to mention the importance of developing civil society, research capacities and information technology. thank you!

in writing. − one of the most important objectives of the european union's development policy is to combat poverty. poverty and the collateral effects of low living standards are at the root of some of the most important economic, political and social challenges facing the world's states and societies. in these circumstances, i believe that, although external aid provided by the european union remains one of the most important instruments of development policy, there is a need for more effective coordination between the actions of the union and the member states and for greater transparency in relations between the union and the partner countries. while the union remains the main global contributor in this area, there is a need to build a framework capable of harmonising national policies with european ones, thus ensuring a high level of complementarity and cooperation.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation establishing a financing instrument for development cooperation. the fight against poverty remains the primary objective of the european union's development policy as set out in chapter 1 of title v of the treaty on european union and chapter 1 of title iii of part five of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, in line with the millennium development goals (mdgs) and other internationally agreed development commitments and targets endorsed by the union and its member states in the united nations and other relevant international fora. the financial reference amount for the implementation of the adopted regulation for the period 2014-2020 shall be eur 19 662 million. the funding will be made available through two multiannual allocations covering only the first four years and the last three years respectively. this funding will be reflected in the indicative multiannual programming of these instruments, in line with the identified needs and priorities of the countries concerned. the amounts allocated may be revised in the event of major unforeseen circumstances or major political changes, in line with the eu's external priorities.

in writing. − the egf was set up to provide the eu with a tool to show solidarity and support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in global trade patterns caused by globalisation. the fund was subsequently extended to include workers made redundant as a direct result of the global financial and economic crisis. in 2009-2010, 82% of egf applications were based on criteria related to the 'crisis derogation' and, in the same period, 10% of redundant workers in the eu accessed the fund. the commission's proposal to include the notion of unexpected crisis in the regulation is therefore welcome, as it allows the fund to respond to the real needs of workers made redundant. i believe that the european union needs a return to growth with a dynamic job creation agenda. the egf may help to achieve these objectives by supporting workers made redundant when they seek employment, improve their skills or re-skill or wish to pursue self-employment, in line with the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. − the egf was set up to provide the eu with a tool to show solidarity and support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in global trade patterns caused by globalisation. the maximum amount proposed for the seven-year period (2014-2020) is eur 3 billion, with a maximum annual use of the fund of eur 429 million. the eu needs economic growth with a dynamic job creation agenda. the egf may help to support workers made redundant when they seek employment, improve their skills or re-skill or wish to pursue self-employment, in line with the eu 2020 strategy. the evaluation of the fund reported a re-employment rate of 48,1% and in most cases this rate increased over the medium term. one of the most common criticisms of the egf is that it reacts too slowly. it is important to improve the speed of this fund by further limiting the deadlines. member states should make every effort to ensure that they respond to planned or announced redundancies as soon as possible and that they start applying the measures as soon as they submit applications to the fund.
in writing. − in the previous european seven-year programme, we were already able to appreciate the added value of the european globalisation adjustment fund. the maximum amount for the next 7 years has been set at eur 3 billion, with a maximum annual drawdown of eur 429 million. the fund is intended for fixed-term and temporary workers, owners and managers of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and self-employed persons. we believe that more could be done in this spending area too, especially in view of the allocation of these resources, which are intended to protect those who lose their jobs and seek to be relocated. however, we welcomed the proposal as amended and we consider the egf to be a fundamental instrument, especially in the context of the economic crisis we are going through.
in writing. − the revised european globalisation adjustment fund for the period 2009-2013 has been a real help to a significant number of european citizens who have lost their jobs as a result of the financial crisis that hit europe. the european union has managed to overcome the crisis period, but unfortunately the labour market is still fragile. labour absorption rates are still not at pre-crisis levels, and we cannot predict when they will return. i therefore consider it important that the eu continues to be involved in helping workers made redundant as a result of the cuts associated with the economic crisis. i support raising the maximum co-financing threshold of the fund and extending eligibility in terms of access to the fund to smes, self-employed workers and farmers, categories de facto excluded from the range of possible beneficiaries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) (2014-2020). the egf enables the union to show solidarity with workers made redundant and can provide support to beneficiaries in small labour markets or in exceptional situations, in particular with regard to collective applications involving small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), even if the number of redundancies is below the normal threshold for mobilising the egf. the adopted regulation applies to applications from member states for financial contributions from the egf for actions concerning: - workers made redundant and self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major structural changes in the pattern of world trade due to globalisation, as demonstrated by a substantial increase in imports into the union, a profound change in trade in union goods or services, a rapid decline in the union market share in a sector or the resulting relocation of activities to third countries, provided that the redundancies have a strong negative impact on the local, regional or national economy; - workers made redundant and self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of the global financial and economic crisis and as a result of regulation (ec) no 546/2009 and a new global financial and economic crisis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. standards for the automatic exchange of information differ from country to country and bilateral or multilateral agreements in this area have not proven effective. if my country were to collect all the taxes and fees it has, it would have budget revenues as a percentage of gdp above the european average. i therefore agree that taxation and the exchange of information on taxation should be discussed at eu level. i would like to express my position on the clause on the availability of certain information. i am of the opinion that such a clause is not appropriate in the context of this directive. i say this because states must have an equal share in this exchange of information. and any exceptions to this may give rise to abuse, affecting the overall objective of the proposal.
in writing. i abstained in the final vote on this report on the automatic and compulsory exchange of information in tax matters because of the adoption of a regressive and very problematic amendment introduced and adopted by the conservatives in the european parliament, which has seriously weakened the scope of the text. the purpose of this directive is to extend the automatic exchange of information between european tax administrations, with the aim of strengthening the fight against tax evasion. the amendment introduced by the conservatives will leave it to member states to decide in their national law which categories of information will be subject to the obligation to exchange tax information automatically. this possibility for member states greatly weakens the scope of this text, even though tax evasion is considered to be one of the major problems today and has contributed to the worsening of the financial crisis. however, it is important that the socialist and democratic group has succeeded in making the exchange of information between tax authorities compulsory. the strengthening of european tax policy must be achieved through the automatic exchange of information. the introduction of exceptions to this principle by the conservatives is a negative sign in the fight against tax evasion, which must be uncompromising.
in writing. − every year, eur 1 trillion is lost to tax evasion and avoidance in the eu. in 2011, the size of the shadow economy was estimated to be around eur 2.4 billion. this represents 19.2 % of the unionʼs gdp. last april, offshore leaks disclosed details of 130 000 offshore accounts and the tax justice network estimated that eur 16 to 25 trillion are hidden in offshore places. these facts are straightforward and show that fighting tax fraud needs to be further reinforced at eu level and cooperation among member states improved and deepened. the commission’s proposal to extend the scope of the already existing eu automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation agreements to dividends, capital gains, other financial income and account balances represents a positive step forward. i expect the council and the member states to commit to their statement of 2 march 2012 advocating for increased levels of cooperation in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion and to support the commission’s amended proposal.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation establishing a community system for the registration of carriers of radioactive materials. the adopted regulation establishes a community system for the authorisation and registration of carriers of radioactive materials based on directive 2008/68/ec and directive 96/29/euratom. it shall apply to any carrier transporting radioactive materials by road, rail and inland waterway within the community, from third countries to the community and from the community to third countries. a transitional period of one year shall apply from the date of entry into force of the regulation in order to allow all carriers to apply for and obtain a registration certificate under the adopted regulation. during this transitional period, the provisions of directive 96/29/euratom and directive 2008/68/ec shall apply. i voted for amendment no 54 which prohibits the transport of radioactive materials in a convoy carrying explosive materials. i also voted for amendment no 53, which states that when applying for registration, the applicant must prove that he has the financial means to pay compensation for any damage in the event of an accident involving the convoy for which he is responsible, in accordance with the 'polluter pays' principle.

thank you, mr president, and thank you to mr klute for this report. access to a bank account for the many is just another dimension of economic and social inclusion. i had a good chat with mr klute, who was interested to know what the specific problems are in the south-eastern member states of the european union. in that conversation, i told mr. klute that in these countries, as a rule, the banking system, most of the banking assets are owned by foreign banks in the developed member states. our problem in these countries is not so much opening a bank account as managing to maintain it, because in these countries and in my country, romania, banks practice a multitude of fees and a level of fees that practically exclude for many citizens the possibility of opening and maintaining a bank account. these are fees that these banks do not dare to practice in the member states where they are based. that is why i think that in the european union we will have to do more in this direction, for decent fees for opening and operating bank accounts.
in writing. we often speak of the free movement of persons within the eu as a fundamental freedom in the eu. this freedom becomes a frustration if citizens who choose mobility face all sorts of problems in their daily lives, including access to a bank account. this is particularly true for young people who are studying in a member state other than their home member state and who have difficulty opening an account without an address in that country. having a payment account with basic functionalities is something absolutely indispensable in everyday life, for receiving salaries, for paying rent and so on. the whole world is going through a process of dematerialization, card payments have become widespread, and in the last few years, smartphone payments have also been developed. i do not think that in such a context we can afford to leave certain categories of the population without access to payment accounts, either because of their financial situation or because of the administrative problems generated by settling in another eu country. in order to trust banks, consumers also need more transparency regarding the fees charged for the various financial services offered.
president draghi, you personally, together with the european central bank, have saved the euro, and for that we thank you. but i would now like to raise an issue of concern to the member states outside the euro area. in order not to generalize, i will give the example of romania. as you know, over 80% of banking assets in romania are owned by parent banks in euro area member states. what's happening now? we are seeing a year-on-year increase in npls, following the credit boom towards the end of 2008. these banks are sitting with non-performing loans on their balance sheets year after year and we are simply seeing the parent banks withdraw money from the new deposits made from the savings of the population and businesses in romania. in other words, while credit is practically not declining, because non-performing loans are not removed from balance sheets, the parent banks are putting tremendous pressure on their romanian subsidiaries to withdraw the credit flows they granted during the boom. i would like to see this issue brought to the attention of the european central bank next year when the assets of the major banks in the euro area are assessed.
president draghi, the european union has not emerged from the crisis as long as its economic and monetary policies are not geared to combating unemployment and stimulating domestic demand, as christine lagarde pointed out yesterday. unlike the united states, which has made progress on the path to economic recovery, the european union does not have a central bank that acts directly to stimulate economic growth. the ecb's monetary policy measures are welcome. however, i believe that the bank should consider using unconventional measures such as capital injections, public debt financing and spending programmes in the fields of innovation, education, transport infrastructure, technology and also to contribute to the development of small and medium-sized enterprises. finally, i would like to stress that i believe the mandate of the bank must include two important components: price stability and, equally, full employment.
member of the commission. - mr president, allow me to make this statement on behalf of my colleague, commissioner algirdas šemeta, who was unable to be present. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission thanks the european parliament for its active and decisive role in the fight against tax fraud and evasion and aggressive tax planning. today you are calling on the commission to launch a study on the possible introduction of indicators as a basis for measures to reduce tax fraud and evasion and aggressive tax planning. the commission supports the introduction of standard indicators which will make it possible to take more precise and timely action against this phenomenon. but to develop such indicators we absolutely need the support of the member states. they are the ones who have to develop their indicators. harmonisation at european level will then be possible once these indicators have been developed at national level. there is currently no harmonised measure of the underground economy, nor any even more complex estimate of the tax gap. given the differences between member states in the availability of tax data, their tax systems and their tax administrations, member states must first develop national estimates of the tax gap before we can then make this estimate at european level. once these national estimates are made, indicators at union level based on national data can be developed. so first we need to agree on common definitions. the commission services shall support this process by providing national administrations with platforms for the exchange of good practice on the harmonisation of the methodology for calculating this tax gap. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, you also ask for a set of objectives to be introduced quickly. first of all, let me emphasize that the term 'tax gain shortfall' covers a wide phenomenon encompassing different issues. for example, undeclared work, vat fraud, bankruptcies or aggressive tax planning also contribute to the loss of tax revenue. to identify measurable and tangible targets for reducing the tax gap and to develop policies accordingly, we therefore need, in addition to a numerical estimate, to understand the nature of the gap for each type of tax. for example, the commission recently commissioned a study to quantify the vat shortfall. this study was published in september 2013. the vat gap amounts to eur 193 billion per year for the period 2006-2011. that being said, we cannot conclude that vat fraud amounts to such an amount since this shortfall in vat does not only include fraud and evasion. there are other reasons too, including unintentional errors and bankruptcies. however, the findings of this study are an important basis for the discussion on the size of the vat gap and on the methods for reducing it. several member states have, following the publication of this study, initiated a process to assess their vat gap. in conclusion, the commission considers that the european parliament's requests are a step in the right direction but that much work remains to be done. the member states must first do the work internally. the commission is then open to considering the harmonization of these indicators. finally, the setting of quantified targets will have to take account of all the factors of the fiscal shortfall.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal to amend directives 2006/112/ec and 2008/118/ec as regards the french outermost regions, in particular mayotte. the european council, by its decision 2012/419/eu amending the status of mayotte in relation to the eu, decided that mayotte will have, as from 1 january 2014, the status of an outermost region within the meaning of article 349 tfeu instead of an overseas country and territory within the meaning of article 355 (2) tfeu. the proposal aims to ensure that it is treated in the same way under the two directives (directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of value added tax and directive 2008/118/ec on the general arrangements for excise duties) as soon as it becomes an outermost region. the proposal is to apply to mayotte the same status applied for many years to guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique and réunion. it clarifies the status of the french part of saint martin without changing it. the proposal does not affect the situation of other french outermost regions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the draft council directive amending council directive 2010/18/eu as a result of the change of status of mayotte. as from 1 january 2014, mayotte ceases to be an overseas territory and becomes an outermost region. this proposal follows the examination of the request by the french authorities to amend the union acquis by postponing the implementation of directive 2010/18/eu implementing the revised framework agreement on parental leave concluded by businesseurope, ueapme, ceep and the etuc and repealing directive 96/34/ec. the french request to postpone the implementation until 31 december 2018 is justified in view of the special economic situation of the new overseas department of mayotte, which requires a gradual alignment of mayotte's legislation with french and european legislation, as well as a gradual increase in social rights, in order to avoid the economic destabilisation of the island that could result from a non-progressive increase in social rights, and to ensure the gradual achievement of equal treatment in the specific field of parental leave. on this basis, it is proposed to amend directive 2010/18/eu to grant france a deferral of the implementation of the directive in mayotte.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the preparations for the european council meeting (19-20 december 2013). they argue that the intensification of economic cooperation should be accompanied by a mechanism based on incentive measures. we believe that any additional funding or instruments, such as a solidarity mechanism, should be an integral part of the eu budget, but remain outside the ceilings agreed in the multiannual financial framework (mff). i believe that member states should commit to supporting a european defence industrial and technological base (edtib). closer coordination of national defence budget planning (possibly through the establishment of a 'european semester' devoted to defence issues) and closer cooperation across industrial sectors (harmonisation of standards and certification of defence equipment) could lead to a robust edtib. , able to overcome fragmentation and increase the creativity and capacity of european industry sectors. we call for new incentives and support measures for the defence industry, alongside a commitment to the development of key defence technologies and systems (fiscal incentives, financial support for research and development and the institutionalisation of synergies between civilian and military capabilities).
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report and i would like to point out that multilevel governance is not differentiated governance. but the two concepts are often confused, and countries like romania suffer the most. i am in favour of deeper integration, but it must be for all countries and not create a two-speed europe. as regards the possibility of creating an unemployment insurance fund for the euro area countries, i must say that a two-speed europe could be envisaged. basically it would provide a safety net in addition to some states. i know that such a measure can only be implemented after the treaties have been amended, but i would like to draw attention to the fact that these proposals discriminate against the states which have not yet adopted the euro.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the multi-level governance of the european union as it provides a welcome orientation for the union's activities. i believe that the eu must move towards full employment. it will also have to be endowed with a minister of finance and with its own resources. at the same time, the troika must be subject to democratic control.
in writing. − throughout the process of european integration it has been found that differentiated integration is sometimes a necessity for overcoming crises. the recent economic and financial crisis confirms this, and this report could not be more timely. economic and monetary union needs ambitious initiatives, such as banking union or fiscal and budgetary coordination, to work properly. however, it seems to me particularly important that initiatives for deeper integration should be taken within the existing institutional framework and based on the community method. the use of intergovernmental agreements to resolve possible crises is an outdated method that bypasses the democratic control of parliament. differentiated integration can also bring problems for eu unity. this is also reflected at ep level in decisions on the euro area. the creation of a subcommittee on such issues is inappropriate as it would exclude meps from the countries that will join the euro, who represent the general european interest as much as other meps. unfortunately, both opt-outs and differentiated membership of the euro and the schengen area complicate things for citizens, and sometimes differentiation is an obstacle to their rights. if we want citizens to embrace and identify with the european project, it is essential to maintain its coherence.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the constitutional problems of a multi-level administration of the european union. we believe that a strengthened budgetary capacity is needed, based on specific own resources and supporting growth and social cohesion in the union budget, aiming at correcting imbalances, structural divergences and financial emergencies that are directly linked to monetary union, without undermining the traditional functions of the union budget to finance common policies. i believe that a balance between employment policy and economic policy is necessary for a positive development of the eu, in accordance with articles 121 and 148 tfeu. the treaties also provide that the promotion of employment and the guarantee of adequate social protection must be taken into account when defining and implementing the union's policies and activities. we call for the establishment of employment and social indicators to complement fiscal and macroeconomic indicators, and for the preparation of reports on the state of structural reforms, in order to ensure an adequate and efficient level of social investment and, therefore, the sustainability of the european social model of a european social union in the long term.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i too agree that there is sometimes a need for more transparency in the european decision-making process. indeed, the adoption of the 2014-2020 budget was a difficult process and has brought to light various problems in relations between the european institutions. on the one hand, the european council provides the union's general guidelines and plays a very important role in adopting the multiannual budget. on the other hand, parliament represents the will of the citizens and therefore has democratic legitimacy. and with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, parliament's role in adopting the budget has increased greatly. in future, a balance will have to be found that does not delay the adoption of such important acts as the union budget.
in writing. − i believe that the president of the european council and the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy should be invited, together with the president of the commission, to participate once a year in a general debate on the internal and external situation of the union.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the european parliament's relations with the institutions representing national governments. we believe that, in the light of the experience gained over these four years, there is a need to improve the working relationship between the european council and the parliament. this could take the form of either a joint statement, an interinstitutional agreement or an exchange of letters. we call for parliament to be involved in good time whenever the european council initiates an action plan or a procedure likely to include a legislative dimension, in order to decide in cooperation with parliament in a form appropriate to each case. i argue that the president of parliament should participate fully in european council meetings when interinstitutional matters are being discussed. the european parliament and the european council would adapt their rules of procedure accordingly, to specify the election of their representatives and the manner in which they obtain a negotiating mandate and report on the negotiations.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution because we are all witnessing the dramatic change in the european landscape. whether we're talking about intensive land use and urban development or road and energy infrastructure, natural habitats and biodiversity are inevitably suffering. that is why i believe that green infrastructure is a potential solution to these problems. moreover, we're talking about investments that benefit the environment, the economy, and create new jobs. green infrastructure is also a desirable for romania which has a rich heritage of rare habitats and species that need adequate protection. that's why i think it's essential to provide solutions that work for nature, not to support initiatives that work against it. this will help to reduce the negative impact of grey infrastructure development on biodiversity.
in writing. − i believe that the development of eco-infrastructures must be supported by sound data and in-depth knowledge, and i encourage the commission, in collaboration with the european environment agency, member states and other stakeholders, to ensure that the union strengthens its capacity for mapping and evaluating ecosystems and associated ecosystem services and that this information and knowledge is taken into account appropriately, including in the planning and implementation of eu co-funded projects.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on green infrastructure exploiting europe's natural capital. green infrastructure can play a particularly important role in cities, where an increasing proportion of the population now lives. they can provide services such as air filtration, temperature control and mitigation of 'heat island' effects, recreation areas, flood protection, rainwater collection and flood prevention, groundwater repair, restoring or halting biodiversity loss, mitigating extreme weather events and their effects, improving citizens' health and improving the overall quality of life, including by providing accessible and affordable areas for physical activities. i believe that investing in green infrastructure is also an investment in public health. also, reducing risks associated with natural disasters such as floods or forest fires is a positive outcome of creating or rebuilding ecological infrastructures, such as natural floodplains, forested areas, wetlands, etc., which can increase resilience to disasters and contribute to adaptation to climate change, significantly reducing the costs imposed on society. i support the development of a strategy to set priorities for green infrastructure projects in europe and believe that more cross-border interregional strategies and projects are needed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report and believe that a low inflation environment is the best contribution monetary policy can make to creating favourable conditions for growth. that is why i welcome the decisions taken by the european central bank in 2012. they have been instrumental in stabilising the banking sector and breaking the link between banks and the public sector. i cannot fail to note, however, that the effects of the crisis and unfavourable economic conditions are still problems with serious repercussions on eu growth and recovery. in addition, the demand for liquidity from the banking system has increased, which means that the degree of dependence of the banking system on the intervention of the central bank is increasing.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the work of the european central bank because i believe that the ecb must use direct measures, such as capital injections or spending programmes, to stimulate economic growth in the european union. the bank should also consider supporting small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the annual report of the european central bank for 2012. i believe that in order to reduce risks, improve the stability of the banking system and avoid the emergence of 'too big to fail' institutions, the possibility of a complete separation of investment banks from deposit banks could be considered. i believe that the 'troika' should be replaced by a system in which the commission, accountable to the european parliament, is placed at the centre of the mechanism with the programme countries, the eurogroup is included in the decision-making process, the ecb provides expertise and the imf makes recommendations when necessary. the european parliament is concerned about the transfer of risk from distressed banks and governments to the ecb's balance sheet as a result of the ecb's decision to buy 'unlimited' amounts of short-term government debt. the long-term refinancing operations (ltros) do not provide a fundamental solution to the crisis. we consider that, while they have ensured a healthy easing of tensions in distressed financial markets, the monetary policy instruments used by the ecb since the beginning of the crisis have demonstrated their limits in terms of their ability to stimulate growth and improve the labour market situation. we ask the ecb to consider other measures.
in writing. - i supported this resolution because the union continues to lose €1 trillion a year to tax fraud. we are talking about a fight that must be waged first at national level, and then consolidated at european level. romania loses 54 million euros every day because of tax evasion. moreover, the underground economy accounts for almost 30% of gdp. if my country were to collect all its taxes and duties, it would have a budget revenue as a percentage of gdp above the european average. but the ponta government's fiscal policies are paradoxical: taxes and fees are rising while budget revenues are falling. furthermore, i wonder what we can expect from a prime minister who declares that a fundamental institution of the rule of law, the constitutional court, supports tax evasion.
in writing. − fighting tax evasion and tax avoidance at european level is undoubtedly and rightfully among parliamentʼs top priorities. in the last few months, we have adopted several reports on this issue, including the report on the fight against fraud, tax evasion and tax havens, the report on a common system of value added tax and a quick reaction mechanism against vat fraud or even the report on the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation adopted yesterday. tax fraud, tax evasion and tax avoidance cost european taxpayers around eur 1 trillion every year and this is only an estimate. it is time to act and tackle this issue in a comprehensive, consistent and concerted manner. tax base harmonisation between member states is the best way to avoid tax avoidance. however until this is achieved and implemented in practice, better coordination and cooperation among member states would already produce substantial improvements. in this respect, a commission study developing indicators for measuring tax fraud and tax avoidance would be a good basis for further strengthening coordination and cooperation between all 28 member states. at the end of the day, no member state can benefit from fiscal dumping.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 12 december 2013 on a call for a measurable and binding commitment to combat tax fraud and tax evasion in the eu. an estimated eur 1 trillion of potential tax revenues is lost annually to tax fraud and evasion in the eu. the scale of tax fraud and evasion undermines citizens' confidence in the fairness and legitimacy of public administrations and their tax systems. i believe that any revenue gains would give member states a better chance to balance their budgets and increase their disposable income to promote investment, growth and employment, which are crucial factors in a sustainable eu exit strategy. we call on the commission to introduce a set of concrete targets for reducing tax harm at european and national level, with the main objective of reducing tax harm by 2020. we propose that these objectives be included in the europe 2020 strategy, where appropriate, and we invite the commission to examine whether they could be given a clear role in the european semester.

on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, in china the removal of organs from donors without prior and free consent is happening today in front of our eyes. chinese doctors have testified in this parliament and before the us congress that they have harvested organs from live people. international reports show that, of 100 000 organ transplants in china in the last 10 years, more than half have come from falun gong. since 1999 the chinese government party has sent hundreds of thousands of practitioners to their death. the government launched a nationwide persecution to eradicate the traditional and peaceful spiritual practice of falun gong. this follows the principles of truth, compassion and tolerance. in china, organ harvesting has become basically a booming business. for kidney and liver transplants, the waiting time in europe is several years. in china it is one to four weeks. this shows that china has a huge bank of living people from whom organs can be removed at any time. we must save innocent people from being killed in china at any time for their organs. the eu must impose sanctions on … (the president cut off the speaker)
in writing. – i want to support the need for full reconciliation in sri lanka and i believe the european union is fully behind the government of that country when it wants to bring its citizens back together. i welcome the efforts made on reconstruction and the commission established in august this year, as well as the successful first round of elections taking place in the northern provinces. i believe the resolution by the alde group should be seen as a step forward and as support for the post-conflict reconstruction phase. no one has the right to give any ultimatums or warnings to a government that is trying its best to get a war-torn country back on track, but we appreciate the need for actions being undertaken to address many of the issues left behind by the war. either way, the way forward for a prosperous and peaceful sri lanka is through fully implementing reconciliatory measures, promoting human rights and personal liberties and ensuring there are no further recriminations and tensions within the various ethnicities and religious minorities in the country.
in writing. – the current rsp on the situation in sri lanka proves once more the double standards of developed states towards the less developed ones. it is a demonstration of the prevalence of concealed interests, a rush to forward hidden political agendas rather than to offer support to a country in difficulty. by scolding sri lanka for not completely eradicating its historical problems and by setting impending deadlines for it to do so, we are condemning its efforts and we are undermining its ability to ever surpass its difficulties. by pressurising sri lanka, we oversimplify and even disrupt the process of post-conflict reconciliation (which is in fact a lengthy procedure that could last over several generations) and we send misleading messages which delay the already ongoing developments in the country. we must acknowledge the progress accomplished so far, as this represents essential proof that sri lanka is striving to improve the human rights situation, freedom of press, the integration of idps and the overall welfare of its population, among other matters. all these reforms must be further encouraged and the eu must offer support and not criticism.
